body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.03338, 'Embedding of sub-stochastic matrices'] A sub-stochastic matrix\/ $M\in\cM_{d,\leqslant}$ can only be
  embeddable when it satisfies\/ $\det (M) > 0$. Then, one has\/
  $M = \ee^Q$, with a sub-stochastic generator\/ $Q$, if and only if
  the unique extension of\/ $M$ to\/ $M_{\mathsf{c}}$ is embeddable
  with a stochastic generator in $\mathsf{c}$-block form, where the
  latter then is the unique extension\/ of\/ $Q$ to\/
  $Q_{\mathsf{c}}$.

[Theorem thm:intro_local_stats of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let \((x,y)\in \mathcal D_c^\circ\setminus \mathscr A\). In the rough region, let \(\zeta_*=\Omega(x,y)\), and in a frozen, quasi-frozen or smooth region, let \(\zeta_*\) be any point in the corresponding component \(A_{(x,y)}\subset \Sigma(\mathbb{R})\setminus \bm \alpha\). If \((x,y)\in \mathcal F_{(\alpha,\beta)}\), assume in addition that
\[
(x,y)\notin \bm l_{e(\alpha)}\cup \bm l_{e(\beta)}.
\] 
For a black vertex $\mathsf b$ and a white vertex $\mathsf w$ of $\mathsf C$, let
\[
\mathsf b_n:=\mathsf b+(j_n,k_n),
\qquad
\mathsf w_n:=\mathsf w+(j_n,k_n)
\]
denote their translates in $\mathsf C_n$. Then
\[
\mathsf K^{-1}_{\mathsf b_n,\mathsf w_n}\rightarrow \mathsf A^{\zeta_*}_{\mathsf b,\mathsf w}
\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,
\]
uniformly over $\mathsf b$ and $\mathsf w$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: cf. Theorem~\ref{thm:inverse_convergence}

[Theorem thm:speed.FPP of arXiv:2411.02046, 'Speed of Convergence and Moderate Deviations of FPP on Random Geometric Graphs'] Let $d \geq 2$,~$\lambda > 0$ and $r>r_c(\lambda)$, and consider first-passage percolation on the random geometric graph on~$\R^d$ with parameters~$\lambda$ and~$r$, with passage times satisfying~(equation A1 of the paper) and~(equation A2 of the paper) above. 
Then, there exists $c'>0$ and a finite constant $\upvarphi>0$ such that, almost surely, for~$t$ large enough, we have
    \begin{equation} 
	    \left(1-c'\frac{\log(t)}{\sqrt{t}}{}\right) B(o, \upvarphi) \subseteq \frac{1}{t}H_{t} \subseteq \left(1+c'\frac{\log(t)}{\sqrt{t}}{}\right) B(o, \upvarphi).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quantitative shape theorem for FPP on RGGs

body:
[Lemma 23 (Uniform bounds for the Malliavin derivatives of $F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)$) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume that Assumptions \ref{ass:smooth},
\ref{ass:second-malliavin-uniform}, \ref{ass:coeff-level-new}(i)(ii),
and \ref{ass:first-malliavin-uniform} hold, let $ \hat{\omega} $ be given by
\eqref{eq:def-omega-second-malliavin}, and let
$\varphi\in C_b^2\left(\R^d\right)$.
Then, there exists a constant $C>0$, depending only on
$\omega$, $m$, and $\varphi$, such that for all $N\ge 1$, all
$0 \le s,r \le t$, all $j,k\in\left\{1,\dots,N\right\}$ and all
$\alpha,\beta\in\left\{1,\dots,m\right\}$,
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{D_s^{j,\alpha}F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)}^4
\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt{N}} e^{-\hat{\omega}\left( t-s \right)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{D_r^{k,\beta}D_s^{j,\alpha}F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)}^4
\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt{N}}
e^{-\hat{\omega}\left( t-\min\left\{ r,s \right\} \right)}
\left(
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{j=k\right\}}+\frac1N
\right).
\end{equation}
title: Uniform bounds for the Malliavin derivatives of $F_t^N\left(\varphi\right)$

body:
[Theorem thm:flat-transport of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $R$ be bounded and restrict to laws with $\log f$ bounded on
		$R$. Then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item wherever $\rho_{\max} < 1$ the splitting
			$T_{f}\mathcal{D}_{+} = V_{f}\oplus\mathcal{H}_{f}$ holds and
			$d\pi$ maps $\mathcal{H}_{f}$ isomorphically onto the base, by the
			marginal formula
			\begin{equation}
				d\pi\big(E_{f}(a,b)\big)
				= \Big(f_{1}\cdot(a + Pb)(F_{1}),\;
				f_{2}\cdot(b + P^{*}a)(F_{2})\Big)
				
			\end{equation}
			and invertibility of the block operator with entries
			$I, P, P^{*}, I$; the Ehresmann curvature of the connection
			vanishes identically, brackets of horizontal fields being
			horizontal by Lemma~(lem:involutive of the paper);
			\item the leaves are global horizontal sections:
			$\pi$ restricted to a leaf is a bijection onto the base, and
			parallel transport of $f$ to target marginals $(g_{1},g_{2})$ is
			the Csisz\'ar $I$-projection of $f$ onto the target Fr\'echet
			class~[csiszar1975], the unique separable tilt of $f$ with
			those marginals, characterized by the Pythagorean identity
			\begin{equation}
				D\big(h \,\Vert\, f\big)
				= D\big(h \,\Vert\, f^{\rightarrow}\big)
				+ D\big(f^{\rightarrow} \Vert\, f\big)
				\qquad\text{for all $h$ in the target class};
				
			\end{equation}
			\item iterative proportional fitting is the alternation of the two
			derangetropy coordinate moves that match one marginal at a time; it
			converges to the parallel transport~[csiszar1975,ruschendorf1995],
			and its linearization at the limit law contracts, per full cycle, at
			exactly the rate $\rho_{\max}^{2}$ of the limit, the squared
			cosine of the principal angle between the two rank subspaces, by von Neumann's
			alternating projection theorem~[deutsch2001];
			\item there is no holonomy paradox: transport to fixed target
			marginals is order-independent by the uniqueness in part (ii),
			while the finite-update commutator of the
			display~(equation eq:gaussian-curvature of the paper) compares transports based at
			different intermediate laws; its coefficient is an order defect of
			the modulation groupoid, not a holonomy of the connection.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Flatness, and Sinkhorn as parallel transport

[Lemma 11 (Discrete approximation lemma) of arXiv:2606.27774, 'Variational Formulas for the Spectrum of\\ Block Wishart Matrices'] Fix $\alpha \in(0,\infty)$.
   For any compactly supported probability measure $\nu\in\cuP(\sa{k}{\C})$, 
   and all $\eps > 0$,  
   there exists a measure $\nu^\up{\eps}$ and a set $\cC^\up{\eps} \subseteq \C^{k\times k}$ 
   such that the following hold:
   \begin{enumerate}
       \item
       
       $\cC^\up{\eps} \subseteq \supp(\nu)$, has finite cardinality, and 
       
       $$
       
       \sup_{\bY \in \supp(\nu)} \inf_{\bT \in \cC^\up{\eps}} \|\bT - \bY\|_\op \le \eps\, .$$
       \item
       
       The measure $\nu^\up{\eps}$ is supported on $\cC^\up{\eps}$, with weights
       $p_\eps(\bT) =\nu^\up{\eps}(\{\bT\})$ satisfying:
       \begin{equation}
       \nu^\up{\eps} :=\sum_{\bT \in \cC^\up{\eps}} p_\eps(\bT)\delta_{\bT},\quad\quad \sum_{\bT\in \cC^\up{\eps}} p_\eps(\bT) = 1 ,\quad\quad 
       p_\eps(\bT) > 0 \quad\forall \bT \in \cC^\up{\eps}.
       \end{equation}
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
       \item
       
       Recall the definition of $w_k$ from Eq.~\eqref{eq:wk-def},
       and let, for $\eps >0$,
       $w_k^\up{\eps}$ denote
       the free element 
       defined by Eq.~\eqref{eq:wk-def} with $\nu$ replaced by $\nu^\up{\eps}$,

       Then for any $\bU \in\cU_-(\alpha,\nu)$,
        there exists $\eps_0(\bU) >0$ such that for all $\eps < \eps_0(\bU)$,
       \begin{equation}
        w_k^\up{\eps}  - (\bU \otimes \id_\cA) \succ 0.
       \end{equation}

       \item 
       For any $\bU \in\cU_- (\alpha,\nu) \cap \cU_-(\alpha,\nu^\up{\eps})$
        \begin{equation}
            \|\hat \bS_\up{\alpha,\nu}(\bU)  - \hat \bS_\up{\alpha,\nu^\up{\eps}}(\bU)\|_\op \to 0
        \end{equation}       
        as $\eps\to 0$.

      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
   \end{enumerate}

\[
    \pr(M_n\geq d\mid K_n=k)=\pwend{k}{d}.
\]
In the standard sequential construction of a uniform permutation, the
indicators that $m$ starts a new cycle are independent
$\operatorname{Bern}(1/m)$ random variables. After marking, the indicators
for $m\geq 2$ are independent $\operatorname{Bern}(1/(2m))$ random
variables. Proposition~\ref{prop:p-walk} now gives
\eqref{eq:p-walk-Wendel-mixture}.

CAMPAIGN RESULT [independently checked proof; E0095-BLOWUP v3; no novelty claim]. Let m>=8 be divisible by4, k a positive even integer, and G=C_m[empty_k] the graph with vertices (x,i), x mod m and 0<=i<k, having all edges between neighboring cycle clusters and none within a cluster. Its degree is d=2k and lambda_2(L_G)=d(1-cos(2pi/m)). A new-edge perfect matching attaining absolute SRW gap 2/(d+1) exists if and only if d sin^2(2pi/m)>=2. When this holds, put a=m/2-1 and pair (x,i) with (ax mod m,i) if ax!=x, otherwise pair within the fixed cluster by i xor1. This is a globally absolute-gap optimal matching. It gives exact threshold-sharp examples m8,d4 and m12,d8. Taking d_m=4ceil(1/(2sin^2(2pi/m))), k=d_m/2, gives optimal examples with base lambda_2->1, asymptotically attaining the necessary threshold d-sqrt(d(d-2)) as degree grows. Below the condition this statement does not compute the optimum gap, and it does not identify a fixed-tolerance total-variation minimizer. For each fixed m,k satisfying the condition, this construction is also TV-optimal to leading high-accuracy order: its t_mix(epsilon) and the minimum over all matchings are both log(1/epsilon)/[-log((d-1)/(d+1))]+O(1) as epsilon decreases to zero, so their ratio tends to one. Constants may depend on the fixed graph.

For k>=2 labeled points in R^3, a differentiable map on an open subset of R^(3k) whose output is only a common translation of one fixed labeled k-point template has derivative rank at most 3, hence zero determinant. Its image is contained in a 3-dimensional affine subspace and has zero 3k-dimensional Lebesgue measure. A finite union over label permutations is also null. Such a map on a positive-volume bad set cannot meet the positive-Jacobian premise of the Gibbs repair-area-formula bound; repairs retaining full-dimensional displacement freedom are not ruled out.

For $R, A, B$, as defined above, assume we know that w.h.p.\ under $\pi^0_{\Lambda}$, all of $R$ lies in the exterior of $\mathfrak{L}_{n-1}$ (for $n = 1$, there is no assumption, since in the setting of (thm:1 of the paper), w.h.p.\ $\mathfrak{L}_0$ does not exist). Then, there exists a $\pi^0_{\Lambda}$-measurable distribution on connected regions $Q\subset R$ with marked boundary conditions $\xi$ satisfying  (it:LB-Q-simp-conn,it:LB-dist-Q-R-bdy,it:LB-Q-bc-arc of the paper)
        below, such that the following holds. If $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_1$ is the area of the interior of $\mathfrak{L}_n$ intersected with~$Q$, and $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_2$ is the area above the $(H+1-n)$ level line in $Q$ under $\pi^\xi_Q$, then $\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_1 \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal A}_2$ w.h.p.\ under $\pi^0_{\Lambda}$.

            \item  The boundary conditions $\xi$ assigns height $H-n$ on the straight line between $A$ and $B$, and $H+1-n$ on the remainder of $\partial Q$.

\end{align}
At the restart, \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian,
\(\BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds, and
\begin{align}
        b^+&\leq\tfrac12 b,                                      \\
 \|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
        &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b,                                      \\
        d_{\TT^2}(r^+(1))&<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}}.                    
\end{align}
In particular, these estimates imply the qualitative conclusion
\eqref{eq:one-block-theorem-conclusion}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 44 (Reflection-invariant formal descent) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] Let $\cO$ be a complete DVR with $2\in\cO^\times$, let
$a\in\cO^\times$, and set $x_a=a+a^{-1}$.  Let $F_a$ and
$F_{a^{-1}}$ be integral germs on the residue disks of $a$ and $a^{-1}$,
compatible under $z\mapsto z^{-1}$.  If the two disks coincide, assume
that the germs also agree after recentering.

Then the two germs descend uniquely through $X=z+z^{-1}$.  If
$\bar a^2\ne1$, the descended germ lies in $\cO[[X-x_a]]$.  If
$\bar a=\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, it lies in
$\cO[[X-2\varepsilon]]$.

[Dfn 123 (L\'evy--Prohorov convergence of derivatives) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. By passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $\nu_N$ converges in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric to a limiting measure $\nu$. Since $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ almost everywhere, we immediately conclude that 
	\[\nu((s,t])
	=-\Big[ p'(t)-p'(s)\Big]
	\]
for almost all $s,t$. Now recall that $p'$ denotes the derivative of $p$ from the right, so in particular $p'$ is right-continuous: this implies that the above equality holds for all $s,t\in[0,1]$. For this form of convergence, we hereafter say for short that \textbf{$(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric.}
title: L\'evy--Prohorov convergence of derivatives

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.00449, 'First-order phase transitions in the hard-core model'] \label[theorem]{thm:arytreedynamics}
    Let $f_{d,\lambda}:[0,\infty]\to[0,\infty]$ be the function with $f_{d,\lambda}(\infty)=0$ and $f_{d,\lambda}(r) = \lambda(1+r)^{-d}$. Then, for all integers $d\ge 2$, the following hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For all $\lambda>0$, $f_{d,\lambda}$ has exactly one fixed point $r^*$.
        \item If $0<\lambda < \lambda_c(d+1)$, then $r^*$ is an attracting fixed point of $f_{d,\lambda}$ whose basin of attraction is $[0,\infty]$.
        \item If $\lambda > \lambda_c(d+1)$, then $r^*$ is a repelling fixed point and there exist $r^0 < r^* < r^1$ such that $\{r^0,r^1\}$ is an attracting periodic orbit of $f_{d,\lambda}$ whose basin of attraction is $[0,\infty]\setminus\{r^*\}$. More precisely, if $r\in [0,r^*)$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_{d,\lambda}^{\circ 2n}(r)=r^0$, and if $r\in(r^*,\infty]$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty}f_{d,\lambda}^{\circ 2n}(r)=r^1$.
        \item We have
        \[ \lim_{\lambda\downarrow \lambda_c(d+1)}|r^1-r^0| = 0. \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.00449

[Definition def:thermo-conv of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Consider a family of microscopic semigroups $(P_t^\varepsilon,\pi^\varepsilon)$ with macroscopic limit $(\bar P_t,\bar\pi)$, and let
$\mathcal{F}^\varepsilon,\mathcal{I}^\varepsilon,\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon,\sigma^\varepsilon$ and $\bar\mathcal{F},\bar\mathcal{I},\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}},\bar\sigma$
be the associated thermodynamic functionals defined in (def:sigmas-single of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Level I (free-energy convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{free-energy convergence} on \(t\) if
\[
\mathcal{F}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\mathcal{F}(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level II (weak thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{weak thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits free-energy convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\mathcal{I}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\mathcal{I}(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level III (liminf thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{liminf thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits weak thermodynamic convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon(t)
\;\ge\;\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}(t),\qquad
\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\sigma^{\varepsilon}(t)
\;\ge\;\bar\sigma(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level IV (strong thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{strong thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits liminf thermodynamic convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}(t),
\qquad
\sigma^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\sigma(t).
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Four levels of thermodynamic convergence

[Teorema 25 (Quasi-invariance principle) of arXiv:2506.11937, 'Random rotational invariance of integration by parts formulas within a Bismut-type approac'] Let $ (X,W)$ be a weak solution to a non-explosive $ SDE_{\mu,\sigma}$ and let $ (X',W')=(P_T(X),P_T(W))$ be the transformed process via the finite stochastic transformation $ T=(\Phi, B, \eta,h)$, where $ h$ is a predictable stochastic process that forms a non-explosive vector field for $SDE_{\mu,\sigma}$. If $T$ is a (finite) symmetry of $SDE_{\mu,\sigma}$, then, for any fixed time $ t \in [0,T]$ and for any measurable and bounded function $ g$, the following quasi-invariance principle holds: \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}[g(X)]=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}}\Bigg[g(X') \exp\Big(\int_0^t h_{\alpha}(X_s,s) dW^{\alpha}_s - \frac{1}{2}\int_0^t h_{\alpha}^2(X_s,s)ds\Big) \Bigg]
\end{equation}
title: Quasi-invariance principle

body: Let A be a Hermitian n by n matrix. For any nonzero vector x in C^n, the Rayleigh quotient of x with respect to A is R_A(x) = (x* A x) / (x* x). R_A is homogeneous of degree 0 (R_A(c x) = R_A(x) for any nonzero scalar c), so it is determined by the direction of x alone, and its range over all nonzero x is contained in the interval between the smallest and largest eigenvalues of A. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis]
title: Rayleigh Quotient

[Lemma MaximalInequalityUnderMixing of arXiv:2412.01635, 'On the Weak Convergence of the Function-Indexed Sequential Empirical Process and its Smoot'] Let $\mathcal H$ be a set of Borel maps $\mathcal X \to \mathbb R.$ Assume there exist $\lambda, \tau > 0$ and an even integer $\nu \geq 2$ such that 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] $\zeta(\alpha^X, \lambda, \nu) = \sum_{s = 1}^\infty s^{\nu-2} \alpha^X(s)^{\lambda/(2+\lambda)} < \infty,$
		
		\item[(ii)] $\E{\left|h(X_{t,n}) - \E{h(X_{t,n})}\right|^{l \frac{2+\lambda}{2}}} \leq \tau^{2+\lambda}$, for all $h \in \mathcal H$, $l = 2,...,\nu$ and $1 \leq t \leq n, n \in \mathbb N.$ 
	\end{itemize}
	
	Then there exists a constant $C \geq 0$ that only depends on $\nu$, $\lambda$ and the mixing coefficients such that for each $n \in \mathbb N$ and $1 \leq i \leq j \leq n$, with $m = j-i+1$, we have 
	$$ \sup_{h \in \mathcal H} \norm{S_{n,i,j}(h)}_{L_\nu} \leq C \sqrt{m} \max\left\{m^{-\frac12}, \tau \right\}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma MaximalInequalityUnderMixing of arXiv:2412.01635

[Definition eq:MF1 of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting'] Consider $A_{l,i}$ and $D_{l,i}$  Poisson processes of intensity $\lambda\rm{dx}$ and Poisson processes of intensity $\rm{dxdy}$ respectively, each being independent in $l,i$. The initial condition
\[
\left(q_i^{(MF1,l)}(0)\right)_{l\geq 1,\;0\leq i\leq N-1}
\]
is assumed to be invariant in law under translations of the index $i$ on the
discrete torus.
Define $Q^{MF1}=(q^{(MF1,l)}_i)_{l \in \mathbb{N}_*, i \in [1,N]}$
    \begin{align}
q_i^{(MF1,l)}(t)
&=
q_i^{(MF1,l)}(0)
+
A_{l,i}[0,t]
\nonumber \\
&\quad
-
\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb R_+}
\mathbf 1_{\{q_i^{(MF1,l)}(z^-)>0\}}
\mathbf 1_{\{u\leq \mu^{MF1}(z^-)\}}
\,D_{l,i}(\mathrm du,\mathrm dz),
\end{align}
where  $\mu^{MF1}(z)=B\log_2(1+\frac{1}{1+\mathbb{P}(q_1^{(MF1,1)}(z)>0)\xi_N})$.

body:
[Cor 25 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ be the function from Lemma~\ref{l:F.iii.sqrtk.Lip}. As stated therein, $\E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ does not depend on the choice of $\cB \in \scB(\lambda,\mu)$, so we denote this quantity simply $\E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k)$. We then have
        \[\P\bigg(
    \Big|F^{\riii}(k,\cB) - \E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k)\Big|
    \ge \frac{\epsilon'}{10}
    ;\cE_{\gd}
    \bigg) \le e^{-ckN}\]
for any fixed partition $\cB \in \scB(\lambda,\mu)$.

\begin{proof}
From Lemma~\ref{l:F.iii.sqrtk.Lip},
the function $\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ is $O((kN)^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz, and therefore concentrates around its mean $\E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k)$ with failure probability $e^{-ckN}$ (by Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}). On the event $\cE_\gd$, the functions
$\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$
and $F^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ coincide,
so the claim follows.
\end{proof}

[Lemma lem:TLD2 of arXiv:2608.29657, 'Hypocoercivity of Tempered Bouncy Particle Samplers for Heavy-Tailed Targets'] Let~(ass:sigmabounds of the paper) hold. Then we have the following.\\
    (I) For $g \in C_b^2({\mathbb R}^d) \cap \mathrm{Dom}(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma)$, we have
    $\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma g = {\mathcal L}_\sigma g$  $\mu$-a.e.  Moreover, $C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d) \subseteq \mathrm{Dom}(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma)$ and $C_c^\infty({\mathbb R}^d)$ is a core of $(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma, \mathrm{Dom}(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma))$.\\
    (II) If $f,g \in C_b^2({\mathbb R}^d) \cap \mathrm{Dom}(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma)$ then  $\langle f, (-\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma) g \rangle_{L^2(\mu)} = \langle \nabla_x f, \sigma^2 \nabla_x g \rangle_{L^2(\mu)} = \langle (-\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma  )f, g \rangle_{L^2(\mu)}$. Moreover, if~(ass:wpi of the paper) also holds then $\langle \nabla_x g, \sigma^2 \nabla_x g \rangle_{L^2(\mu)} \leq m^{-1}\|\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma g\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2 $.\\
    (III) For $g \in C_b^{1}({\mathbb R}^d)$ we have $(m - \bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma)^{-1} g \in C_b^{2} ({\mathbb R}^d) \cap \mathrm{Dom}(\bar {\mathcal L}_\sigma)$. Moreover, if~(ass:wpi of the paper) holds, then the inequality $\|(m - \bar{\mathcal L}_\sigma)^{-1} g \|_{L^2(\mu)} \leq (2m)^{-1} \| g\|_{L^2(\mu)}$ holds for all $g \in L_0^2(\mu) \cap C^1_b({\mathbb R}^d)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem Lnetw of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] The matrix $M(t)$ in (equation eq:Tmat of the paper) has a decomposition \begin{equation} 
 M(t)
 =
 X_{i_1}(t)\cdot X_{i_2}(t)
 \cdots
 X_{i_N}(t) \cdot 
 D(t) 
\end{equation}
where $D(t)$ is a diagonal matrix with each entry a positive Laurent monomial in the $t$-parameters, and each $X_i(t)$ is the triangular matrix $I + m_iE_{i+1,i}$ where $m_i$ is a positive Laurent monomial in the triangle $t$-parameters.

Moreover, the unipotent matrix $L_\rho(P)$ for (equation eq:Lfactor of the paper) is obtained by conjugating $M(t)\cdot D(t)^{-1}$ by a diagonal matrix involving the shear parameters $e:=e_\rho(x,P)$. In particular, it is the weight matrix of a transparent weighted planar network whose non-constant edge-weights are positive Laurent monomials in $t$ and $e$.
title: Lem Lnetw of arXiv:2608.27939

[Lemma lem:GetIntoi of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with $p_0=1$ such that, for all positive integers~$x$, $W_x \le (6/\lambda)^x$. 
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer and suppose that bin~$i$ is a bottleneck. 
Let $U = (U^A,U^B,U^C)$ be the under-backoff process with birth rate~$3\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$.
Let $T = i \lceil  \exp((\log i)^{2/3} ) \rceil$.
Then 
with probability at least 
$  W_i^{-6/7}  $,
for all $t\in [T]$, 
$\mathbf{s}^{U^A}(t)$ and $\mathbf{s}^{U^B}(t)$ are both non-empty
and there is a $T^U\in [T]$ such that $\mathbf{b}_i^{U^C}(T^U)$ is non-empty
and for every $t\leq T^U$, $\bigcup_{k\in [i]} 
\mathbf{b}_k^{U^C}(t)  $ is non-empty.

  exists, is called the \emph{parent} of $x$, and denoted by $\hat{x}$.
  Conversely, the \emph{children} of $x$ are the vertices in
  $S_{1}^{\pp -}(x)$. The elements of $S_{1}^{\pp -}(\hat{x})$ are called
  the \emph{siblings} of $x$. The set of siblings of a vertex $x$ is denoted
  by $\Sib(x)$ and is empty if $x$ has no parent. The set of smaller
  siblings is
  \begin{equation*}
    \Sib^{-}(x) = \Sib(x) \cap \{y \in \vertices \col y \prec x\}.
  \end{equation*}
title: Definition 23 of arXiv:2604.11682

[Definition def:saturated of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(\varphi\) be a semiflow on a compact manifold \(N\). A subset \(W\subset N\) is called (\(\varphi\)-)/saturated/ if for every point \(p\in W\), the entire flowline through \(p\) is contained in \(W\).

If, in addition, \(W\) is a \(I\)-bundle \(F\times I\) and the \(\varphi|_{W}\) is orbit equivalent to a product flow on \(F\times I\), then \(W\) is called \emph{product saturated}.
title: Saturated subset

		$K$-light vector $t$ supported on $\mathcal I^c$ with $\|t\|_2=1$, with

	$$
	\inf_{\substack{\supp h\subset\mathcal I\\
	\|h\|_1\le d^{2/3}}}

	Consequently, the same conclusion holds with $\mathcal L_X^*$ in place

body:
[Definition 30 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $m\ge 2$ and $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. For a subset $A$ of $\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, we consider the restriction
$$\mu_{X;A}:=\mu_X|C_m\times A:C_m\times A\rightarrow\mathbb N\cup\{0\}$$
of $\mu_X$ to $C_m\times A$; so $\mu_X=\mu_{X;\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket}$. If $A=\{b\}$, let $\mu_{X;b}:=\mu_{X,\{b\}}$.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} For $m\ge 2$ (resp.\ $m\ge 3$) we say that $\mu_{X;A}$ has exceptional $+1$ (resp.\ $-1$) jumps or that $\mu_{X;A}$ has jump type $1$ (resp.\ $-1$) if there exists $b\in A\cap\llbracket 1,p^s-1\rrbracket$ such that the function $\mu_{X;b}$ is non-constant and for each such $b$, $\mu_{X;b}$ attains its maximum (resp.\ minimum) at precisely one element of the source.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} We say that $\mu_{X;A}$ has jump type $0$ if either $m=2$ and it does not have jump type $ 1$ or $m\ge 3$ and it does not have jump types $-1$ or $1$. 

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} We say that $\mu_{X;A}$ has regular $\pm 1$ jumps if for each $b\in A$ the function $\mu_{X;b}$ is non-constant, attains its maximum at two or more elements of the source, and attains its minimum at two or more elements of the source.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} For $m=2$ (resp.\ $m\ge 3$), we fix an $s$-tuple $(\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_{s-1})\in\{0,1\}^s$ (resp. $(\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_{s-1})\in\{-1,0,1\}^s$). We say the multiplicity function $\mu_X$ has jump type $(\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_{s-1})$ if for each $j\in\llbracket0,s-1\rrbracket$, $\mu_{X;A_{s,j}}$ has jump type $\epsilon_j$.

\smallskip
{\bf (5)} We call the $2s$-tuple 
$$(\l_{0,0},|\mathbb J_{X;0}|,\l_{1,0},|\mathbb J_{X;1}|,\ldots,\l_{s-1,0},|\mathbb J_{X;s-1}|)\in(\mathbb N\cup\{0\})^{2s} $$
 as the multiplicity type of $\mu_X$.

Status: complete candidate proof, author-checked in two analytic formulations; no independent review and no claim of established novelty. Current-literature search is incomplete. Do not count as a promoted original solution.

Source: Hasebe and Ueda, *Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions*, ALEA 15 (2018), 353–374, Problem 3.3; archived arXiv1710.08240v2, PDF p.6. The PDF carries the arXiv revision date14 September2018 and a manuscript header4 November2021; retain that discrepancy. Primary links: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.08240 and https://alea.math.cnrs.fr/articles/v15/15-15.pdf . The source defines S(0,t) to have variance t, and D_mu to be support diameter.

The source proves the sufficient constant4 and asks for the optimal universal C in t>=C D_mu^2. Its paragraph says the symmetric Bernoulli law on{-1,1} has threshold t=4 and diameter2, then prints2<=C<=4. Those preceding numbers imply the lower bound C>=1. The candidate upper bound below is a separate argument, not a conclusion drawn from that arithmetic inconsistency.

## Candidate theorem

If mu is a compactly supported probability measure on R with support diameter D, then mu free-convolved with the centered semicircle law of variance t is unimodal whenever t>=D^2. The optimal universal constant in the source's normalization is therefore C=1.

When D=0 the measure is a point mass and the assertion is immediate. Henceforth D>0. No symmetry, density, or non-atomicity of mu is assumed.

## An elementary moment inequality

Let Q be a probability law of a centered real variable X supported in an interval of length D. Write a=E_Q X^2 and b=E_Q X^4. Then

\[
 a\le D^2/4,\qquad b+3a^2\le D^2a.
\]

For the first inequality, if the supporting interval is[l,h], then E[(X-l)(h-X)]>=0 gives a<=-lh, and -lh<=D^2/4 because l+h has a real square. For the second, let X' be an independent copy. Pointwise, (X-X')^4<=D^2(X-X')^2. Taking expectations and using E X=0 gives2b+6a^2<=2D^2a. This derivation checks both the coefficient3 and the use of the diameter rather than radius.

Equality a=D^2/4 forces l=-D/2,h=D/2 and Q to put equal mass on the two endpoints: equality in E[(X-l)(h-X)]>=0 forces endpoint support, and centering fixes the weights.

## Cauchy-profile lemma

For R>0 define

\[
 F_R(u)=\int\frac{d\mu(x)}{(x-u)^2+R^2}.
\]

Claim: F_R has no local minimum with value at most1/D^2.

Take any stationary point u of F_R with F_R''(u)>=0. Put y=R^2>0 and

\[
 Z=\int ((x-u)^2+y)^{-2}\,d\mu(x),\qquad
 dQ(x)=Z^{-1}((x-u)^2+y)^{-2}\,d\mu(x).
\]

Differentiation under the integral is justified by R>0 and compact support. Stationarity says E_Q(X-u)=0. With a=E_Q(X-u)^2 and b=E_Q(X-u)^4, the preceding moment inequalities apply. The second derivative is

\[
 \frac{F_R''(u)}{2Z}
 =E_Q\frac{3(X-u)^2-y}{(X-u)^2+y}
 =3-4y E_Q\frac1{(X-u)^2+y}.
\]

Jensen's inequality and F_R''(u)>=0 imply

\[
 \frac1{a+y}\le E_Q\frac1{(X-u)^2+y}\le\frac3{4y},
 \qquad y\le3a.
\]

The normalization of Q gives an exact reciprocal-profile identity:

\[
 \frac1{F_R(u)}
 =\frac{E_Q[((X-u)^2+y)^2]}{E_Q[(X-u)^2+y]}
 =\frac{b+2ay+y^2}{a+y}.
\]

Consequently

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1{F_R(u)}-D^2
 &\le\frac{y^2+2ay-3a^2-D^2y}{a+y}\\
 &=\frac{(y-3a)(y+a)+(4a-D^2)y}{a+y}\le0.
 \end{aligned}
\]

The first inequality uses b<=D^2a-3a^2; the final two summands are nonpositive because y<=3a and4a<=D^2. In particular, F_R(u)>=1/D^2.

The equality case matters for the endpoint t=D^2. If F_R(u)=1/D^2 and F_R''(u)>=0, then the two final nonpositive terms both vanish: y=3a and4a=D^2, since y>0. Equality in the variance bound forces Q to be symmetric Bernoulli on u plus/minus D/2. On these two points the reweighting denominator is equal, so mu is the same symmetric Bernoulli law. Writing c=D/2 and s for displacement from its midpoint, with R^2=3c^2, gives

\[
 F_R(u+s)=\frac{s^2+4c^2}{s^4+4c^2s^2+16c^4},
 \qquad
 F_R(u+s)-\frac1{4c^2}
 =-\frac{s^4}{4c^2(s^4+4c^2s^2+16c^4)}<0\quad(s\ne0).
\]

Thus the only possible equality point is a strict maximum, not a local minimum. Every local minimum therefore has value strictly greater than1/D^2, proving the claim including equality.

## Unimodality via Biane's density parametrization

For fixed t>=D^2 and fixed R>0, the equation F_R(u)=1/t has at most two solutions. Indeed, if there were three solutions u1<u2<u3, then either F_R dips below1/t somewhere in[u1,u3], producing an interior local minimum below that level, or F_R>=1/t throughout that interval, making u2 a local minimum at that level. Both alternatives contradict the Cauchy-profile lemma because1/t<=1/D^2. The analytic function cannot be identically constant on an interval, since F_R tends to0 at infinity.

Now use exactly the density framework stated in source Section2.2 and Lemma3.1. Define v_t(u)>=0 by

\[
 \int\frac{d\mu(x)}{(x-u)^2+v_t(u)^2}=\frac1t
\]

where its positive solution exists, setting v_t=0 elsewhere. Biane's real homeomorphism psi_t satisfies

\[
 p_t(\psi_t(u))=\frac{v_t(u)}{\pi t},
\]

where p_t is the continuous density of mu free-convolved with S(0,t), analytic wherever positive. Each positive density level p_t=a corresponds to F_(pi*a*t)(u)=1/t, and therefore has at most two points. Source Lemma2.2, equivalently Lemma3.1, now gives unimodality. All source assumptions match: mu is compactly supported, t>0, and the semicircle parameter is variance.

## Sharpness

Let mu be symmetric Bernoulli on{-c,c}, c>0, so D=2c. For c^2<t<4c^2, the positive solution at the symmetry center has v_t(0)^2=t-c^2. Implicit differentiation at0 yields

\[
 v_t''(0)=\frac{3c^2-v_t(0)^2}{v_t(0)(c^2+v_t(0)^2)}
 =\frac{4c^2-t}{t\sqrt{t-c^2}}>0.
\]

Thus v_t has a positive strict local minimum at0, and the density under the homeomorphism psi_t does as well. It is not unimodal. For any proposed C<1, choose t strictly between max(C,1/4)D^2 and D^2. Then t>=CD^2 but unimodality fails. This proves the lower bound C>=1 independently of the source's printed inequality.

## Second analytic check and remaining review obligations

The same moment computation can be applied directly at critical points of v_t. At such a point, the profile's first derivative vanishes and the sign of v_t'' equals the sign of F_v-fixed''. The calculation above says a nonnegative second derivative would force t<=D^2. Hence for t>D^2 every critical point of v_t is a strict maximum, giving the same threshold. The equality analysis in the Cauchy-profile proof closes the boundary without appealing to weak closure of unimodal laws.

The load-bearing points to challenge are the Q-normalization identity, the centered fourth-moment inequality, the direction of Jensen, and the equality case at t=D^2. [Lemma lem:robust of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] Fix $s\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. Let $T\ge 100$ and put
\[
\eta=\frac{1}{10s\sqrt{T}}.
\]
Let $G$ be an
$N$-vertex $r$-regular graph satisfying
$\lambda(G)\le\eta r$. Then every set $S\subseteq V(G)$ with
$|S|\ge N/s$ contains a set $U\subseteq S$ with $|U|>N/(3s)$ such that
$G[U]$ is a $(1/(10s),T)$-expander.

body:
[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_k)\in\mathcal P_{d,k}^{\rm lc}$. Then $X$ has finite
moments of all orders and $\Sigma^d(X)$ is well defined. Moreover, if
$X_m=(X_{m,1},\ldots,X_{m,k})\in\mathcal P_{d,k}^{\rm lc}$ converges in
distribution to $X$, then, for every $p\ge1$,
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\sup_{m\ge1}
\mathbb E\bigl[|X_{m,j}|^p\bigr]<\infty.
\]

kernels.  Any two minimal graded presentations of this terminal are related
by a unique grade-preserving unitary between their primitive supports.  The
unitary intertwines the one-leg flattenings, the weighted Fock evaluation,
and every finite block-pairing contraction diagram.

If epsilon_1, ..., epsilon_N are pairwise independent Rademacher variables and a_1, ..., a_N are real, then E[(sum_i a_i epsilon_i)^2] = sum_i a_i^2.
each epsilon_i is -1 or 1 with probability 1/2
epsilon_i and epsilon_j are independent for i != j
the a_i are deterministic reals

body:
[Theorem thm:CSP_measure_initial of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Suppose Assumptions (asp:sigma of the paper) and (asp:coefficients of the paper) hold,
and let $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and $\lambda\in[1,2)$ be the constants in
Assumption (asp:sigma of the paper).
Let $\mu_0$ be a nonnegative $\mathcal F_0$-measurable random Radon
measure on $\mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
    \mu_0\in L_2\bigl(\Omega;H_2^{-1/2-\kappa}(\mathbb{R})\bigr)
    \qquad\text{for every }\kappa\in(0,1/2),
\]
and assume one of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (i)] if $\lambda=1$, then $\mathbb{E}[\mu_0(\mathbb{R})]<\infty$;
\item[\rm (ii)] if $\lambda\in(1,2)$, then there exists
$q>\frac{\lambda-1}{2-\lambda}$ such that
$\mathbb{E}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(1+x^2)^{q/2}\,\mu_0(\mathrm{d} x)<\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (a)] {\rm(Existence)} There exists a nonnegative solution $u\in C((0,T];C_{\rm tem})$ of (equation eq:SPDE of the paper).
\item[\rm (b)] {\rm(Compact support)} If, in addition,
Assumption (ass:shifted_uniqueness of the paper) holds, then every
nonnegative solution $u\in C((0,T];C_{\rm tem})$ of (equation eq:SPDE of the paper) has compact support at every $t\in(0,T]$, almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Existence and CSP for measure-valued initial data

body:
[Lem 164 ($\bar{\bx}$ is Lipschitz) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $\bar{\bx}\equiv \bar{\bx}(q_d)$
 as in \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}, so it is measurable with respect to
 $\cG(q_d)$. Then
		\[
		\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2
		\le \frac{Nq_0}{q_d} \le N\,.\]
and the centered random vector $\bar{\bx}  -\E\bar{\bx}$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $L^{O(1)}$.

\begin{proof} 
Recall $\chi(p)=\E R(p)$ with $R(p)$ as in \eqref{e:p.corr.overlap}, and $q_d=\chi(p_d)$. Note that
	\[
	\frac{\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N}
	= \frac{\|\E\cA(\bG)\|^2}{Nq_d}
	= \frac{\chi(0)}{q_d} 
	\le \frac{\chi(p_0)}{q_d} = \frac{q_0}{q_d}\le1\,,
	\]
which proves the first claim. Next note that we can write
	\[
	\sqrt{q_d}\bar{\bx}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}}{=}
	\E\bigg( \cA
	\Big(\sqrt{p_d}\bar{\bG} +\sqrt{1-p_d}\bG'\Big)
	\,\bigg|\,\bar{\bG}\bigg)\,,
	\]
where $\bar{\bG} = \bG(q_d)/\sqrt{p_d}$ and $\bG'$ are independent $M\times N$ matrices, each with i.i.d.\ standard gaussian entries. Since $\cA$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $p_d/q_d \le L^{O(1)}$ by \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound}, it follows that $\bar{\bx}$ is $L^{O(1)}$-Lipschitz with respect to $\bar{\bG}$. The claim then follows using Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $\bar{\bx}$ is Lipschitz

[Lemma LIL of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Let $ \{ x(j) : j \in \mathbb{N} \} $ be a sequence of i.i.d.\ nonnegative random variables with mean~$ 1 $ and coefficient of variation $ c_{x} < \infty $. Then,
	\[  
	\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{\sup_{1\leq j \leq n} \big( \sum_{i = 1}^{j}x(i) - j \big)}{\sqrt{2 n \log\log n}} \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} - \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{\inf_{1\leq j \leq n} \big( \sum_{i = 1}^{j}x(i) - j \big)}{\sqrt{2 n \log\log n}} \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} c_{x}.
	\]
	Let $ \{ N(t) : t \geq 0 \} $ be the associated renewal process, given by $ N(t) = \max\{ j \in \mathbb{N}_{0} : \sum_{i = 1}^{j} x(j) \leq t \} $. Then,
	\[  
	\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{\sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} (N(t) - t)}{\sqrt{2 T \log\log T}} \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} - \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{\inf_{0 \leq t \leq T} (N(t) - t)}{\sqrt{2 T \log\log T}} \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} c_{x}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma LIL of arXiv:2505.04942

[Definition 7 (Hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] Let $ H_n(\lambda_n, \mu_n;  \nu_n)$ denote the set of all discrete concave functions $h_n:T_n \ra \R,$ (which,  following Knutson and Tao \cite{KT1},  we call hives)
such that \ben \item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(0,  i) = \sum_{j = 1}^i \la_n(j).$
\item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(i,  n) = \sum_{j = 1}^n \la_n(j) + \sum_{j = 1}^i \mu_n(j).$
\item $\forall i \in [n]\cup\{0\},\quad h_n(i,  i) = \sum_{j = 1}^i \nu_n(j).$
\een
Let $|H_n(\lambda_n, \mu_n;  \nu_n)|$ denote the ${n-1 \choose 2}-$dimensional Lebesgue measure of this hive polytope.
title: Hive

    The same bound holds if $\mathbf{X}$ is replaced by the stationary
    $n$-line $\lambda$-tilted ensemble $\mathbf{X}_n \sim \mathcal{L}_n^\lambda$, for any $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:phase-transition of arXiv:2602.19192, 'Bakry--\'Emery Curvature of the Fractional Laplacian\\ via Fractional Brownian Covariance'] \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For all $\gamma \in (0,1]$:
  $\kappa(\gamma) := \lim_N \kappa(\gamma,N)$
  exists and satisfies $\frac{1}{2} \leq \kappa(\gamma) \leq 1$.
  (For $\gamma < 1$, the lower bound is conditional on the
  Z-matrix property; see Lemma~(lem:kappa-lower of the paper).)
\item For all $\gamma \in (0,2)$ with $\gamma \neq 1$:
  $\kappa(\gamma) < 1$.
\item At $\gamma = 1$: $\kappa(1) = 1$
  (Theorem~(thm:cauchy of the paper)).
\item Consequently, $\gamma = 1$ is the unique global maximizer
  of $\kappa(\gamma)$ on $(0,2)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 4 (Behavior of geodesics) of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $D$ be a weak geodesic CLE$_4$ metric coupling in the sense of \Cref{def:weak_axioms}. Let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a deterministic simply connected domain. Then:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, every $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic $P$ connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ is such that $\{D_{\Gamma_{U}}^{U}(\SCL_1,\SCL): \SCL \in \Gamma, \ \SCL\cap P([0,1]) \neq \emptyset\}$ forms a dense subset of the interval $[0, D_{\Gamma_{U}}^{U}(\SCL_1, \SCL_2)]$.
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, every $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic $P$ connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ has the property that the subset $\{P(t) : t \in [0,1],\ P(t) \notin \bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma_U} \SCL\}$ of $\overline U$ is of Hausdorff dimension zero. 
			\item Almost surely, for each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, no $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ touches $\partial U$. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Behavior of geodesics

Then for all $t,s\in T_N$ with $|t-s|<b^{-L}$,

[Corollary 51 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] The support of every ordinary Lascoux polynomial $\Omega_\alpha$ is
$M^\natural$-convex, and
\begin{equation}
 \Supp(\Omega_\alpha)=\Newt(\Omega_\alpha)\cap\ZZ^n.
\end{equation}
The positive-parameter polynomial $\Omega_\alpha^+(x;\beta)$ has saturated
Newton polytope in $\ZZ^{n+1}$.  Thus Conjecture~5.6 of
Monical--Tokcan--Yong holds.

[Prop propinftyinfty of arXiv:2604.19184, 'Growing random planar network with \\oriented branching and fusion\\'] There exists  a constant $C$ such that for any  measurable function  $f: \mathcal X \rightarrow \mathbb R_+$ with support in $\mathbb R_+^3$  and such that $\parallel f \parallel<\infty$ and for any $t\geq 0$,
  $$M_tf(\infty,\infty, 0) \leq C\parallel f \parallel (1+t)^2$$  and 
  $$ \big\vert M_tf(\infty,\infty, 0) -t^2\Pi(f) \big\vert\leq  C\parallel f \parallel t.$$
Moreover,  the measure  $\Pi$ on $\mathbb R_+^3$  satisfies
$$\Pi(dL,d\ell,da)=g(L,\ell)dLd\ell \delta_L(da)$$
where its density 
 $g$ with respect to Lebesgue measure for the first and second coordinate writes 
\begin{align*}
 g(L,\ell)=\sum_{k\geq 1} \frac{(k+1)}{((k-1)!)^2} \left( ke^{-(k+1)L-k\ell} +\frac{1+k}{k}e^{-(1+k)L-(1+k)\ell}\right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop propinftyinfty of arXiv:2604.19184

[Lemma L:Int-4 of arXiv:2606.23865, 'Uniform-in-time Gaussian fluctuations for multiscale nonlinear stochastic systems via Mall'] For $0 \le u \le s \le w \le r \le t$, let the term $\mathcal{J}_4(t;\varepsilon,\eta)$ be defined as follows:
\begin{multline*}
\mathcal{J}_4(t;\varepsilon,\eta)  \triangleq  K \int_{u=0}^t \int_{s=u}^t \int_{w=s}^t \int_{r=w}^t  (\varepsilon+ \eta + \sqrt{\varepsilon \eta})^2 e^{-2 \alpha (t-u)} e^{-\alpha(t-w)} e^{-\alpha(t-r)} e^{-\frac{\lambda}{\eta} (r-w)} \\
\times  e^{-\frac{\lambda}{\eta} (w-s)}     dr \thinspace dw \thinspace ds \thinspace du.  
\end{multline*}
Then, there exists a time-independent positive constant $K$ such that
$$ \mathcal{J}_4(t;\varepsilon,\eta) \le K \thinspace \eta^2 \thinspace (\varepsilon+ \eta + \sqrt{\varepsilon \eta})^2 .$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L:Int-4 of arXiv:2606.23865

[Proposition 130 (Pointwise commutator estimates involving $\angLie$ ; \cite{abbrescia2022emergence}*{Prop.\,14.5}) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $1 \leq N \leq \Ntop$ be an integer, and let $\varphi$ be a scalar function. 
	For any $\Singletan \in \Tanset$ (see definition \eqref{E:COMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}),
	iterated commutators can be bounded pointwise as follows
	on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \tander^N] \varphi
			\right|
			& \lesssim 
			\auxbootsmall \left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right| 
			+ 
			\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_1,\,N_2\leq N}} 
				\left|\tander^{[2,N_1]}\controlvars \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}},
			\\
			\begin{split}
				\left|[\muX, \tander^N]\varphi \right|,
				\,
				\left|
				[\Singletan, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi
				\right|
				& \lesssim
				\left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right| 
				+ 
				\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_1,\,N_2\leq N}} 
					\left|\tander^{[2,N_1]} \badcontrolvars \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}
				 
				\\
				& \ \
				+ 
				\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N \\ N_1 \leq N-1}} 
					\left|\tander^{[1,N_1]} \muX \wavearray \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}.
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	In particular, 
	for any $\Singletan \in \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	we have the following pointwise estimates
	on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|[\Singletan, \tander^N] \varphi \right| 
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\auxbootsmall \left| \tander^{[1,N]}\varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq \Ntop - 11,
			\\
			\left|[\muX, \tander^N]\varphi \right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim \left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right|,
			& 
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq \Ntop - 12.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	Moreover, the following pointwise estimates hold:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;2}] \varphi
			\right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\muX, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi 
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\left| \comdersmall^{[1,N];1} \varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq 5,
			
			\\
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;3}] \varphi
			\right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\muX, \comder^{N;2}] \varphi 
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\left| \comdersmall^{[1,N];2} \varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq 4.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	Finally, if $\upxi$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form or an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent type $\binom{0}{2}$-tensorfield 
	and $\Singletan \in \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	then the following estimates hold:
	\begin{subequations}
\begin{align} 
\left|
	[\angLie_{\Singletan}, \angLie_{\tander}^N] \upxi 
\right|_{\gtorus} 
&
\lesssim 
\auxbootsmall \left| \angLie_{\tander}^{\leq N} \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}  
+ 
\underbrace{\sum_{\substack{N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_2\leq N}} 
\left|\tandersmall^{[2,N_1]} \controlvars \right| 
\left|\angLie_{\tander}^{[1,N_2]}  \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}},
	\\
\begin{split} 
\left|
	[\angLie_{\Singletan}, \angLie_{\comder}^{N;1}] \upxi 
\right|_{\gtorus} 
&
\lesssim 
\left| \angLie_{\tander}^{\leq N} \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}  
+

[Prop 10 of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Every finite $\F_p[t]$-module $G$ admits a unique decomposition
\begin{equation}
G\cong \bigoplus_{f\in S} G_f,
\end{equation}
where only finitely many summands are nonzero, and $G_f$ denotes the $f$-primary submodule of $G$.

Moreover, for each $f\in S$, there exists a unique partition
\[
\l^{(f)}=(\l^{(f)}_1,\l^{(f)}_2,\ldots)\in\Y
\]
such that
\[
G_f\cong \bigoplus_{j\ge 1}\F_p[t]/(f^{\l^{(f)}_j})
\]
as $\F_p[t]$-modules. Equivalently, if $f_1,\dots,f_r\in S$ are the distinct irreducible polynomials such that
$G_{f_i}\neq 0$, then
\[
G\cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^r\bigoplus_{j\ge 1}\F_p[t]/(f_i^{\l^{(f_i)}_j}),
\]
and the collection of partitions
\[
\l^{(f_1)},\dots,\l^{(f_r)}
\]
is uniquely determined by the $\F_p[t]$-module isomorphism class of $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 10 of arXiv:2609.01413

body:
For each N let theta_N be a unit vector in R^N, Y_t iid with law P_N, and L_N(x;Y) a loss on the unit sphere S^(N-1). Let its population loss be Phi_N(x)=E L_N(x;Y)=phi(m_N(x)), where m_N(x)=x.theta_N and the same function phi:[-1,1]->R is used for every N. The spherical stochastic gradients exist almost surely; assume explicitly that E grad_S L_N(x;Y)=grad_S Phi_N(x). Let H_N(x;Y)=L_N(x;Y)-Phi_N(x). For constants C_1,iota>0 independent of N, assume sup_x E[(grad_S H_N(x;Y).theta_N)^2]<=C_1 and sup_x E||grad_S H_N(x;Y)||^(4+iota)<=C_1 N^((4+iota)/2). For a fixed integer k>=1, suppose phi is C^(k+1) on [-1,1], phi_prime(m)<0 for 0<m<1, phi^(ell)(0)=0 for 1<=ell<k, phi^(k)(0)<0, and sup_[-1,1]|phi^(k+1)|<infinity. Starting independently of the samples, use online spherical SGD X_tilde_t=X_(t-1)-(delta_N/N) grad_S L_N(X_(t-1);Y_t), X_t=X_tilde_t/||X_tilde_t||. Here alpha_N>0 and delta_N>0, and there are M_N=alpha_N*N fresh-sample updates (M_N integer). The initial law mu_N is uniform on the hemisphere {x in S^(N-1):x.theta_N>=0}. If k=1 assume alpha_N->0 and delta_N=O(1); if k=2 assume alpha_N/log N->0 and delta_N=O(1); if k>=3 assume alpha_N/N^(k-2)->0 and delta_N=O(alpha_N^(-1/2)). Then max_(0<=t<=M_N)|m_N(X_t)|->0 in probability and in L^p for every finite p>=1. Thus these subcritical fresh-sample online updates cannot weakly recover the teacher. For k>=3 the sample threshold is N^(k-1), while the matched known upper guarantee in this source has extra logarithms. The lower bound is for the stated algorithm and step regime; it is not an information-theoretic lower bound for all estimators or for data reuse.
all explicitly stated fixed-profile, spherical-gradient, fresh-sample, and moment assumptions
hemispherical uniform initialization independent of samples
the stated k-dependent subcritical alpha and step-size bounds

body:
Let zeta(s) = sum_{n >= 1} n^{-s} for Re s > 1, continued meromorphically to the whole complex plane with a single simple pole at s = 1. Its zeros at the negative even integers are called trivial; all other zeros lie in the strip 0 < Re s < 1. The Riemann hypothesis asserts that every non-trivial zero has real part exactly 1/2. It is open (Riemann 1859). Equivalent forms: pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x) for the prime-counting function; and |sum_{n <= x} mu(n)| = O(x^{1/2 + epsilon}) for every epsilon > 0. The zeros have been verified numerically to lie on the critical line up to height 3 x 10^12 (Platt and Trudgian, 2021).
the hypothesis itself is a conjecture; the meromorphic continuation, the pole at s = 1, the trivial zeros, the location of the other zeros in the critical strip, the stated equivalences, and the numerical verification are theorems

body:
[Theorem 2 (The Cauchy stability of finite-energy  Einstein areal flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider one of the three Einstein--matter models in \autoref{theo-main-results} with $\Tbb^2$ symmetry on~$\Tbb^3$.
In the Einstein--Navier--Stokes case, assume that the model is admissible and torus-adapted, and that its matter stress tensor~$T_\chi$ obeys the coercive stress condition in \autoref{def-Tchi-coercive}.
In the Einstein--Euler case, we use the conventions $T_\chi=T_{\rm E}$, $\vNumb_\chi=\vNumb_\Jbb$, and $\zeta=0$.
Prescribe\footnote{Equivalently, prescribe a signed areal time~$t_0$ and initial data $(\mathring\Phi,\mathring\Psi,\mathring\zeta)$ for the \JKL{} formulation of the areal flow, together with the conformal modulus of one symmetry orbit.}
 an initial data set $(\mathring g,\mathring k,\mathring\Jbb,\mathring\zeta)$, consisting of a Riemannian metric, second fundamental form, fluid momentum, and relaxation field (absent for the Einstein--Euler model) satisfying Einstein's constraint equations and invariant under two commuting Killing fields $Y,Z$ with closed orbits, and assume that the orbit area constant and equal to $|t_0|\neq 0$.

Consider a regular Cauchy development $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ on $\Tbb^3\times[t_0,t_1]$ of these initial data for the chosen Einstein--Euler or Einstein--Navier--Stokes model in the areal foliation, with an areal time interval $I = [t_0,t_1] \subset \RR\setminus\{0\}$.
\bei
\item Assume that the initial spatial volume, the initial energy norm~$\mathcal E(t_0)$, and the bounded-variation norm of $\mathring\Psi=(\mathring\ell,\log\mathring\Omega,\mathring\Kpar)$ on~$\Tbb^3$ are bounded by a constant~$\mathcal I_0$.

\item In the future-contracting regime, assume that the conformal length has a positive lower bound $\mathcal L_{\min}$ on $I$; in the future-expanding regime, this lower bound is $\mathcal L_{\min}=\mathcal L(t_0)>0$, which is part of the initial data controlled by~$\mathcal I_0$.

\item Assume either that the fluid velocity is orthogonal to the symmetry orbits or, more generally, that the parallel momentum per particle is uniformly bounded in the sense that~\eqref{intro-parall-perpart-bounded} holds at $t=t_0$ for some constant $C^\parallel>0$.
\eei
Then the following Cauchy stability properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}

\item The parallel momentum per particle remains uniformly bounded at all times by~$C^\parallel$ in the sense that~\eqref{intro-parall-perpart-bounded} holds on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$.

\item There exists a constant
\be
C=C\bigl(\mathcal I_0,t_0,t_1,\mathcal L_{\min}^{-1},C^\parallel\bigr)
\ee
such that the $L^2$ norms of~$\Phi$ and bounded-variation norms of~$\Psi$ on areal time slices (constant~$t$) and on timelike slices orthogonal to the areal foliation (constant~$x$ in the \JKL{} formulation) are controlled as
\bel{equajKD93}
\aligned
& \sup_{t\in I}\bigl(
\|\Phi\|_{L^2(\Tbb^3,\dVtrois)}
+ \|\Psi\|_{\BV(\Tbb^3)}
\bigr)
\\
& + \sup_{x\in\Sbb^1}\bigl(
\|\Phi\|_{L^2(\Interval\times\Tbb^2,\dVundeux)}
+ \|\Psi\|_{\BV(\Interval\times\Tbb^2)}
\bigr)
+\int_{I\times\Tbb^3}\!\!\mathfrak d_*\,\dVuntrois
\leq C.
\endaligned
\ee
Here, $\dVuntrois,\dVtrois,\dVundeux$ are volume forms of the (Lorentzian) metric~$g$ and of (Riemannian) induced metrics on spatial and temporal slices.

\item The last term in \eqref{equajKD93} represents the total non-negative production measure and vanishes for the Einstein--Euler system.  For the particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes system it is the produced particle number density $\mathfrak d_*=\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}$, while for the dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes system it is the dissipated mass-energy density $\mathfrak d_*=\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}/(-n_\alpha\beta^\alpha)$.

\item Moreover, these conclusions allow vacuum, arbitrarily large mass-energy density, and arbitrary finite rapidity. For the two Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems, the constant $C$ is independent of the relaxation rate map~$\mathscr B$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Cauchy stability of finite-energy  Einstein areal flows

$F_N(q)=\sum_{n\geq0}a_{N,n}q^{n}$ have nonnegative coefficients.  Suppose that
on an open interval $I\subset(0,1)$,
\[
  F_N(q)\longrightarrow F(q)=\sum_{n\geq0}a_{n}q^{n}<\infty,
\]
and $a_{n}\geq0$ for every $n$.
Then $a_{N,n}\to a_{n}$ for every fixed $n$.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let (X_{m,n})_{0<=m<n} be a doubly indexed family of random variables satisfying subadditivity X_{m,n} <= X_{m,k} + X_{k,n} for m<k<n, stationarity, that the joint law of (X_{m+1,n+1})_{m<n} equals that of (X_{m,n})_{m<n} under a measure-preserving shift, and integrability, E[X_{0,1}^+] < infinity together with a lower bound such as E[X_{0,n}] >= -cn preventing a trivially degenerate -infinity limit. Then X_{0,n}/n converges almost surely and in L^1 to a random variable X, equal to lim_n E[X_{0,n}]/n = inf_n E[X_{0,n}]/n, and X is almost surely constant if the underlying shift is ergodic rather than merely measure-preserving. This is the random, non-i.i.d. generalization of Fekete's lemma, which is its deterministic special case, and of the classical ergodic theorem, which is its additive special case, and it is the fundamental tool establishing existence of limiting growth rates in first-passage percolation (the time constant), longest increasing subsequence problems, and last-passage percolation, with the closely related Furstenberg-Kesten theorem giving Lyapunov exponents for random matrix products via an analogous but distinct subadditive argument. It does not give the value of the limit X, only its existence as an abstract limit or infimum, and does not by itself give a rate of convergence or determine whether X is almost surely constant unless ergodicity, not merely stationarity, of the shift has been separately established. Typical failure: Invoking Kingman's theorem to conclude the limiting growth rate is deterministic without separately verifying ergodicity of the underlying probability-preserving transformation, checking only stationarity; stationarity alone gives convergence to a possibly random limit X that can be a genuine mixture over ergodic components, so asserting a single deterministic time constant or growth rate without checking ergodicity is a common gap, especially in models built from a mixture of environments. Canonical reference: Kingman, 1968, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B; Kingman, 1973, Annals of Probability; Steele, Probability Theory and Combinatorial Optimization, 1997, SIAM.
subadditivity of the doubly indexed array X_{m,n} under the relation X_{m,n}<=X_{m,k}+X_{k,n}
joint stationarity of the array under the shift (m,n) -> (m+1,n+1)
integrability, E[X_{0,1}^+]<infinity, together with a lower bound preventing a degenerate -infinity limit
for an almost-surely-constant limit: ergodicity, not merely measure-preservation, of the underlying shift
title: Technique: Kingman's Subadditive Ergodic Theorem

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\delta>0$ and $\alpha\in [-2,2]$. For every $\nu>0$, there exists a $\Phi\in (0,1/10)$ such that with probability at least $1-\nu$, for all points $x,y\in B_{\Phi}(-1)$, $x',y'\in B_{\Phi}(1)$ and all $D_h$-geodesics $\Gamma_{x,x'},\Gamma_{y,y'}$, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\geq \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}-\delta$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}( (\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'}) \cap \cT^\alpha_h)\geq  \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}_{\alpha}-\delta$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{LQG}}( (\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\cap \cT^\alpha_h)\geq \Delta^{\mathrm{LQG}}_{\alpha}-\delta$,
  \item 
  $\chi(\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\leq \chi +\delta$,
  \item 
  $\chi'(\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\geq \chi'-\delta$,
  \item 
  $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}(\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\geq \alpha_{\mathrm{max}}-\delta$,
      \item 
      $\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}(\Gamma_{x,x'}\cap\Gamma_{y,y'})\leq \alpha_{\mathrm{min}}+\delta$.
  \end{enumerate}

    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 2$, and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) =O(d_G(x,y))^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha > 1 + 1/d$.
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$ be sufficiently large.
    
    Then there exists $A = A(G,J) > 0$ such that

        \right)
        \le
        \exp
        \left(
            -
            \beta k ^{(d-1)/d}
            /
            A
        \right).

[Theorem 38 ($\mathscr{S}_R$ properties) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $f \in \mathcal{B}_R^n$ \eqref{BRTR}. Let $\emptyset \neq G = G^1 \times \cdots \times G^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, with all $G^k$ closed. Then 
\begin{align}
   \mathscr{S}_R(f,G) &= (\mathscr{S}_R(f_1,G^1),...,\mathscr{S}_R(f_n,G^n)) \\
   &= \Big(\sup \big(G^1 \cup (-\infty, \inf G^1]\big)_{\leq \widetilde{X}_1},..., \sup \big(G^n \cup (-\infty, \inf G^n]\big)_{\leq \widetilde{X}_n}\Big) 
   \end{align}
has the following properties. 
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item $\mathscr{S}_R(f,G) \in \mathcal{T}_R(f)$
\item $\forall k$, $P(\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k) \geq t) = f_k \big( \inf \big(G^k \cup (-\infty, \inf G^k]\big)_{\geq t} \big), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}$ (employing the convention\footnote{This is natural because $f_k \searrow 0$ by definition of $\mathcal{B}_R$.} $f_k(+\infty) = 0$)
\item $\mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)$ are right continuous
\item $\mathscr{S}_R(f,G)$ is the unique element of $\mathcal{N}^n$ which satisfies (ii) and (iii)
\item $\forall s_k \in (0,1), \ \mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s_k) \in G^k \cup (-\infty, \inf G^k]$
\item $\forall s_k \in(0,1), \ \mathscr{S}_R(f_k,G^k)(s_k) \leq \widetilde{X}_k(s_k), \ k=1,...,n$
\end{enumerate}
\begin{proof} 
(iv) is an application of lemma~\ref{uniquenessneat}. (v) and (vi) follow immediately by \eqref{SRXkeq} and since $G^k$ are closed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let n,m be positive integers with m<=n, and [n]={1,...,n}. For b in {0,1}^n define S0={i:b_i=1}. Independently sample Y1 uniformly from [n]^m, and put S1=Unique(Y1), A=S0\S1 and B=S1\S0. If |A|>=|B|, choose a uniform random injection sigma:B->A and replace each occurrence of a in B by sigma(a). Otherwise choose a uniform random injection tau:A->B and replace each occurrence of tau(a) by a. Call the resulting string Y. All injection choices use fresh private randomness conditional on b,Y1. If b is uniform on {0,1}^n, then Y is exactly uniform on [n]^m. For every b,Y1 and every permitted injection, |S0 symmetric_difference Unique(Y)|=abs(|S0|-|S1|). Thus the coupling has a uniform binary-vector marginal and a uniform length-m string marginal; independence of these two marginals is not asserted.
Positive integers1<=m<=n. Uniform binary b and independent uniform Y1 for the uniformity conclusion.
Uniform injections conditional on their domain and codomain; the support identity itself is deterministic.

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] For any $0 <\gamma < \frac{2q}{q-1}$, the distributions $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_t \circ (\widetilde{L}_t)^{-1}$ under the Gibbs measure \eqref{eq:self-gibbs-measure} satisfy an LDP in $\widetilde{\mathcal{X}}_{\le 1}(\mathbb{R})$ with good rate function
    \[
    \mathcal{I}_{1, q, \gamma}^{\mathrm{Gibbs}}(\xi) = \begin{cases}
    \mathcal{I}(\xi) - \left( \sum_{i \in I} \| \psi_i \|_{2q}^{2q} \right)^{\gamma / q}  + \rho_{1, q, \gamma} & \text{if } \mathcal{I}(\xi) < \infty\\
    \infty & \text{otherwise},
    \end{cases}
    \]
    where $\mathcal{I}(\cdot)$ and $\rho_{1, q, \gamma}$ are defined in \eqref{eq:rate-function} and \eqref{eq:self-tilted-var}, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:gs-subgaussian of arXiv:2608.09465, 'Balancing fractional Brownian motion'] Given $u_1,\ldots,u_n\in\mathbb R^m$ with $\|u_i\|_2\leq\zeta$, there is a randomized polynomial-time algorithm returning $\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma_i u_i$ is $(\sqrt{40}\,\zeta)$-subgaussian. Consequently, for every symmetric convex body $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ of Gaussian measure at least $1/2$, there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathrm{alg}}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma_i u_i\in (c\zeta)\cdot\mathcal K\right\}\geq\frac12.
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We say that a real probability measure
$$m\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$$
is the classical version of another measure, called its free version, or its liberation
$$\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$$
when the classical cumulants of $m$ coincide with the free cumulants of $\mu$.

Let A_1, ..., A_m be events, N the number that occur, 1 <= k <= m, and S_r = sum over r-element I of P(intersection of A_i, i in I), with S_r = 0 for r > m. If S_k > 0, then P(N >= k) >= S_k^2 / sum_{j=0}^k c(k, j) S_{2k - j}, with c(k, j) = (2k - j)!/(j! ((k - j)!)^2). The denominator is also the sum, over ordered pairs (I, J) of k-element sets, of P(intersection of A_i, i in I or J). For k = 1 this is the Chung-Erdős inequality. No independence is assumed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:71bd73e400b00d5bb781adcb9df8b8f0329907f58bd3fa3bc1a7cb627a4f1c22","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/71/71bd73e400b00d5bb781adcb9df8b8f0329907f58bd3fa3bc1a7cb627a4f1c22.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:06f7cb816a20bfd98c74c8dc9cb5ed834d0b7655847882b22837239cc8b3a9ab","bundle_entry_key":"one-seed-tilted-balanced-c-global-margin","bundle_id":"population.relu-one-seed-tilted-balanced-c-global-margin","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:relu-two-point-one-seed-tilted-balanced-c-global-margin","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# One seed plus tilted balanced C neurons creates the missing seed
Claim w733-T363-020 v1; kind moved; target2; proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

## Precise statement
Use the bias-free, fully trained two-layer ReLU network on x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels+1, summed exponential or logistic loss, and ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially every neuron is positive-output A (x1-only), positive-output C (both-active), or strictly dead with arbitrary output. At least one A and one C are present, and no B (x2-only) is present. For every C neuron w=(u,y), assume u<=0 and v^2>=u^2+y^2. Assume E=f1-f2>0 initially. Then a global absolutely continuous flow exists, and every such flow enters strict B at a finite time and subsequently reaches the global normalized margin sqrt17/16 with convergent normalized parameter direction. The reflected statement exchanges x1 and x2 and reverses u. These are scale-invariant sufficient subcones, not entire activation-pattern labels.

## 1. Continuation and the invariant until B appears
Claim017 section1 constructs global absolutely continuous flows for positive-live networks, without requiring both permanent seeds for that construction. Its bounded-norm-on-bounded-time argument and its null-boundary-level-set argument apply here unchanged. Claim019 gives E>0 and u<=0 up to the first strict B entry; positive A stays A, dead neurons stay dead, and C cannot enter A. All live outputs increase. The invariant v^2-||w||^2 is constant, so each C retains v>=||w||. These statements hold along every global absolutely continuous continuation; uniqueness at grazing contacts is not required.

We prove finite B entry by contradiction. Suppose no strict B entry ever occurs. Then all original C neurons remain in the closed C cone forever, their boundary contacts have measure zero, and the C equations hold almost everywhere. In particular v(t)>=v(0)>0. Put a=||x1||=sqrt17/4, c=x1.x2=-15/16, ai=-ell_prime(fi)>0, Ii(t)=integral_0^t ai(s) ds, and T=I1+I2. Since E>0, a1<=a2 and I1<=I2.

For total parameter squared norm N, Ndot<=2a(a1+a2)N. If T were bounded on infinite physical time, N and both predictions would be bounded; exponential and logistic ai would then remain bounded below by a positive constant. This contradicts bounded T. Hence T tends to infinity and I2>=T/2 tends to infinity.

## 2. A dissipative weighted variable for C
For one C neuron set q1=(w.x1)/a>=0 and s=v+q1. Then v<=s<=2v because 0<=q1<=||w||<=v. The C cone estimate from claim016 gives z2=w.x2<=2||w||/sqrt17<=2v/sqrt17. Almost everywhere the exact C equations yield

 sdot=a*a1*s+a2*(z2+(c/a)*v)
      <=a*a1*s-(7/(4sqrt17))*a2*v
      <=(a*a1-b*a2)*s,  b=7/(8sqrt17)>0.

Here c/a=-15/(4sqrt17); no approximation enters these constants. Gronwall implies
 s(t)<=s(0) exp[a I1-b I2].
Since n=v^2+||w||^2<=2v^2<=2s^2, summing over C gives
 N_C(t)<=C0 exp[2a I1-2b I2], C0=2 sum_C s_j(0)^2.

## 3. The clock contradiction
For the permanent A sector, its exact hyperbolic solution gives
 H_A=alpha exp(2a I1)-beta exp(-2a I1), alpha>beta>=0.
Consequently H_A>=H_A(0) exp(2a I1), so
 N_C/H_A <= (C0/H_A(0)) exp(-2b I2) ->0.
If I1 were bounded, the bound for N_C would force N_C->0, contradicting v_j(t)>=v_j(0)>0 for any C neuron. Thus I1->infinity and H_A->infinity. Only C contributes to point2, and its cone estimate gives f2<=N_C/sqrt17. Since f1>=H_A, this implies
 E=f1-f2>=H_A-N_C/sqrt17 ->infinity.

For exponential loss a1/a2=exp(-E)->0. For logistic loss, f2>=0 implies a1/a2<=2exp(-E)->0. For every epsilon>0 there is t_epsilon after which a1<=epsilon*a2; integrating and using I2->infinity gives limsup I1/I2<=epsilon. Hence I1/I2->0. It follows that a I1-b I2->-infinity. The bound in section2 now forces every C s_j(t)->0, again contradicting s_j>=v_j>=v_j(0)>0. Therefore the assumption of no finite strict B entry is impossible.

## 4. Global-margin consequence and limits
Take a finite time after the first strict B entry, away from the null boundary contact sets. There is a permanent positive A seed and a permanent positive B seed; all other live outputs are positive. Apply claim017 from that state. Its conclusion is normalized margin sqrt17/16 and convergence of the normalized parameter direction along every global absolutely continuous continuation. Reflection proves the symmetric theorem. Common rescaling of every initial parameter by any sigma>0 preserves all hypotheses, including E>0; thus the result applies at sigma=1e-6.

This is a subcone result and does not classify every initial A/C pattern. It changes no whole-orbit labels: the remaining unknown count stays2713. Claims017 and019 and this claim all await independent review. The hardest new step is the two-clock contradiction in section3; grazing continuation is inherited from the unaudited claim017. No formal certificate, independent audit, or literature novelty is asserted. Primary setup: Vardi-Shamir-Srebro arXiv2110.02732v4, Theorem3.2 and AppendixC.3.

## 5. Exact Gaussian mass of the sufficient subcone
Assume all coordinates are independent N(0,sigma^2). Put p=atan(1/4)/pi, q=1/4-p/2. A+ has probability q; strict dead with arbitrary output has probability p. For C require the strict version u<0 and v>||w||. This C event has probability e=p(1-1/sqrt2)/4: in spherical coordinates about the positive v axis its polar angle is in (0,pi/4) and its hidden azimuth lies in (pi/2,pi/2+atan(1/4)). The sphere-area fraction is atan(1/4)(1-1/sqrt2)/(4pi).

The conditional A law is V=|N(0,1)|, independent hidden radius R Rayleigh(1) and angle Phi uniform(-atan4,atan4); its point1 contribution is V R(cos Phi+sin Phi/4). The conditional C law has independent radius rho distributed chi_3, t uniform(1/sqrt2,1), and phi uniform(pi/2,pi/2+atan(1/4)); V=rho*t, U=rho*sqrt(1-t^2)*cos phi, Y=rho*sqrt(1-t^2)*sin phi. These are Gaussian conditional laws at unit scale.

For integers h,k>=1 define the exact finite-dimensional integral
 K_hk=P[sum_(j=1)^h V_j R_j(cos Phi_j+sin Phi_j/4) > sum_(j=1)^k (-2 U_j V_j)],
using independent A and C conditional variables just specified. It is positive, since a nonempty open set has arbitrarily small negative C horizontal coordinates and positive A contributions. This is a definition by an explicit integral, not a closed-form evaluation or certified numerical estimate.

With d=m-h-k, the exact Gaussian probability of the theorem's two reflected, disjoint strict subcones is
 P_m=2 sum_(h,k>=1,h+k<=m) [m!/(h!k!d!)] q^h e^k p^d K_hk.
All scales sigma>0 have the same probability because the dominance inequality is homogeneous of degree2. These subcones are disjoint from claim017's initial-two-seed family of mass H_m, so H_m+P_m is an exact sufficient-family mass, hence a lower bound for the total global-convergence probability. This is not a total basin probability and does not resolve all activation patterns. body: For an n by n random matrix A with iid mean-zero sub-Gaussian entries, the smallest singular value satisfies P(s_min(A) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= C eps + c^n: square random matrices are typically invertible with s_min of order n^{-1/2} (Rudelson-Vershynin), resolving the quantitative invertibility problem behind Spielman-Teng smoothed analysis. For tall m by n matrices with m >= (1 + delta) n, s_min is of order sqrt(m) - sqrt(n-ish) with exponential concentration. The proofs decompose the sphere into compressible vectors (close to sparse - handled by nets and tensorization) and incompressible vectors (reduced to distance-to-subspace and small-ball estimates via the Berry-Esseen or Littlewood-Offord theory of anti-concentration).

metadata_json: {"artifact_digest":"sha256:b25fea35f4311de349420169b38a1814fabb9e4a598c855d19295e672eab67e9","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b2/b25fea35f4311de349420169b38a1814fabb9e4a598c855d19295e672eab67e9.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f63d5cd8c88e7a9dc411e46d70a07cedaa1104c3f26aba9ba5ba1376335dfce0","bundle_entry_key":"2608-26084-lemma-110-generating-iff-free-boolean-al","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s3_110","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-20260907/bundle_s3_110.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2608-26084-lemma-110-generating-iff-free-boolean-al","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: Denote by~$\\beta_A\\colon A\\to\\bool{A}$ the order embedding into the free Boolean algebra of~$A$, with~$\\boolrec$ the unique morphism of Boolean algebras such that $\\boolrec\\circ \\beta_A= i$. It suffices to show~$\\boolrec$ is bijective. body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.28528, 'Strong solutions of SDEs with critical discontinuities in diffusion coefficients'] Let $d \geq 3$. Assume that the diffusion coefficients $\sigma \in [L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})]^{d \times d}$ satisfy the uniform ellipticity condition: for every $t \in \mathbb R$
$$
\sigma(t,\cdot) \sigma(t,\cdot)^{\top} \geq \kappa I \quad \text{a.e.\,on $\mathbb R^{d}$ for some fixed $\kappa>0$}
$$
and have \textit{form-bounded} derivatives, i.e.\,condition \eqref{nabla_sigma} holds.

We also impose the following auxiliary condition on the time-dependence of $\sigma$:

\begin{itemize}

\item[{\rm ($\mathbf{H}$)}] 
$$
\sup_{y \in \mathbb R^d}\|\sigma(t,\cdot)-\sigma(s,\cdot)\|_{L_{\rho_y}^2(\mathbb R^d)} \leq C|t-s|^\gamma \quad t,s \in \mathbb R, |t-s| \leq 1
$$
with the H\"{o}lder continuity exponent $\gamma \in ]0,1]$.
\end{itemize}

Let  $$\sigma_n \in \big[L^\infty(\mathbb R, C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^d))\big]^{d \times d} \cap [C_{\text{unif},\loc}^\gamma(\mathbb R,L^2_\rho(\mathbb R^d))]^{d \times d}$$ be a sequence of bounded matrix fields having bounded  derivatives in the spatial variables, $$\|\sigma_n\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})} \leq \|\sigma\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})}, \quad \sigma_n\sigma_n^{\top} \geq \frac{\kappa}{4}I$$ such that 
$$
\sigma_n \rightarrow \sigma \quad \text{ in $[L^\infty_{\loc}(\mathbb R,L^2_{\rho}(\mathbb R^d))]^{d \times d}$},
$$
and that satisfy \eqref{nabla_sigma} and ${\rm (\mathbf{H})}$ uniformly in $n$, i.e.\,with the same parameters $\nu$, $c_\nu$ and $C$, $\gamma$. It is not difficult to see that the spatial mollification of $\sigma$ produces such $\{\sigma_n\}$, see Appendix \ref{approx_app}. By the classical theory, for each $n$, there exists a pathwise unique strong solution $X_{r,t}^{x,n}$ to the approximating equation
\begin{equation} 

X_{r,t}^{x,n}=x + \int_r^t \sigma_n(s,X^{x,n}_{r,s})\, dW_s,
\end{equation}
considered on the same (fixed) complete probability space  $(\Omega,\{\mathcal F^W_{t}\}_{0 \leq t \leq T},\mathcal F^W,\mathbf{P})$.

Then, if the form-bound $\nu$ of $|\nabla \sigma|$ in \eqref{nabla_sigma} is smaller than a certain constant that only depends on the dimension $d$, the ellipticity constant $\kappa$ and $\|\sigma\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^{1+d})}$, the following are true:

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] There exists a subsequence $\{\sigma_{n_k}\}$  and a continuous random field $X$ such that, for every $N \geq 1$,
$$
\sup_{0\leq r\leq t\le T, |x|\le N} |X_{r,t}^{x,n_k}-X_{r,t}^x| \rightarrow 0 \quad \mathbf{P}-a.s.,
$$
where $X^x_{r,t}$ is a strong solution of SDE \eqref{sde1_}
on $(\Omega,\{\mathcal F^W_t\}_{0 \leq t \leq T},\mathcal F^W,\mathbf{P})$.

\medskip

    \item[(ii)] The operators
    \[
    P_\sigma^{r,t}f(x) := \mathbf{E}[f(X^x_{r,t})], \quad f \in C_\infty, \quad r,t \in [0,T], r<t,
    \]
    constitute a backward Feller propagator on $C_\infty$, 
and, furthermore, if $\{\sigma_n\}$ additionally satisfies
$$
\nabla a_n \rightarrow \nabla a \quad \text{ in } L_{\loc}^2(\mathbb R,L^2_\rho(\mathbb R^d)),
$$
where $a=\sigma\sigma^{\top}$, $a_n=\sigma_n(\sigma_n)^{\top}$ (once again, mollifying $\sigma$ in the spatial variables produces this convergence, see Appendix \ref{approx_app}), then
$$
P_\sigma^{r,t}=s\mbox{-}C_\infty\mbox{-}\lim_n P_{\sigma_n}^{r,t} \quad \text{loc.\,uniformly in $r,t \in [0,T]$, $r<t$.}
$$
There is no need to pass to a subsequence of $\{\sigma_n\}$. In this sense, the law of $X^x_{r,t}$ does not depend on the choice of the subsequence in {\rm (\textit{i})}.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
