body: [Lem 1st_step_ancestral of arXiv:2510.18856, 'Evolution of recursive trees with limited memory'] Fix $k\geqslant 1$ and let $n=n_1>n_2>\dots> n_k\geqslant j(n-1)$. Then, for $\beta=1/2$ and $D_n$ the distance from $1$ to the highest branchpoint in the subtree of $\mathcal{T}_n$ spanned by $1,n_1,n_2,\dots, n_k$, it holds that $n^{-1/2}D_n\stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} 4X_{k-1}$ where $X_{k-1}$ is distributed as $U^{1/(4k(k-1))}$ for $U$ a $\operatorname{uniform}[0,1]$ random variable. Moreover, jointly, $n^{-1}L(T)\stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} X_{k-1}^2$.

[Lemma lem:4 of arXiv:2509.10225, 'Phase Transitions for Elephant Random Walks \\ with Two memory Channels'] Fix $i \in \{1,2\}$. Let $p \neq 7/8$ be such that $- \frac{1}{2} \leq \lambda^{(1)}_p\left(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(p)}\right) < 0$. Then there exists a finite random variable $\boldsymbol{\Delta}^{(i,p)}$ such that \begin{align}\frac{{\boldsymbol{\nu}^{(i)}_p\left(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(p)}\right)^\top}\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{n+1}\left(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(p)}\right)}{n^{\lambda^{(1)}_p\left(\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{(p)}\right)}} \stackrel{a.s.}{\to} \boldsymbol{\Delta}^{(i,p)}.
\end{align}
title: Lemma lem:4 of arXiv:2509.10225

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, The maximal Kemeny constant of an n-vertex graph (2026) proves that for simple random walk on a connected simple graph with n vertices Kemeny's constant is at most n^3/54 + (37/8) n^(5/2), and that two complete graphs of order floor(n/3) joined by a path attain the leading term, so the maximum over connected n-vertex graphs is asymptotic to n^3/54. This proves the Kemeny-constant assertion of Open Problem 6.13 of D. Aldous and J. A. Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs; the relaxation-time assertion of the same problem was proved by Aksoy, Chung, Tait and Tobin. The same argument gives (1 - 1/r) n^3/54 + O(n^(5/2)) for the maxima over K_{r+1}-free graphs and over graphs of chromatic number at most r. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/maximal-kemeny-constant (commit 33503b469849); ResearchGate record 414471140. Not refereed.
title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 6.13, Kemeny-constant assertion, proved: the maximal Kemeny constant of an n-vertex graph is asymptotic to n^3/54 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/maximal-kemeny-constant)

[Lemma lem:independent-eigenvalues-lattice-induction of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $(X,\mu)$ be an ergodic probability-preserving Borel
$\mathbb R^d$-space. If its Koopman representation has $d$
linearly independent eigenvalues
\[
    \xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
then $(X,\mu)$ is lattice-induced. In particular, when $d=1$, a single nonzero Koopman eigenvalue implies that the action is lattice-induced.

body:
Let M be a compact Riemannian manifold and let f be a C^{1+a} diffeomorphism of M for some a > 0 (that is, Df is Holder continuous with exponent a). Let mu be an f-invariant Borel probability measure, and for mu-a.e. x let lambda_1(x) > ... > lambda_{k(x)}(x) be the Lyapunov exponents with the Oseledets splitting. Write E^s(x) for the sum of the Oseledets subspaces with NEGATIVE exponent, d_s(x) = dim E^s(x), and lambda^s(x) = the largest negative exponent at x. Fix a small eps > 0.

Then for mu-a.e. x with d_s(x) > 0 there exist a measurable function r(x) > 0 and an embedded C^{1+a} disk W^s_loc(x) of dimension d_s(x), contained in the ball of radius r(x) around x and TANGENT TO E^s(x) at x, such that:
 (i) for all y in W^s_loc(x) and all n >= 0,  d(f^n x, f^n y) <= C(x) e^{(lambda^s(x) + eps) n} d(x, y), with C(x) measurable and finite; in particular limsup (1/n) log d(f^n x, f^n y) <= lambda^s(x) < 0;
 (ii) f( W^s_loc(x) ) is contained in W^s_loc(f x);
 (iii) x -> W^s_loc(x) is measurable, and the size is TEMPERED: r(f^n x) >= r(x) e^{-eps |n|} for all n, so the disks may shrink along the orbit but only subexponentially;
 (iv) on each Pesin block Lambda_l the constants C, r and the estimates are uniform and the disks vary continuously in the C^1 topology with the base point.
The global stable manifold W^s(x), defined as the increasing union over n >= 0 of f^{-n}( W^s_loc(f^n x) ), is then an injectively immersed C^{1+a} submanifold consisting of points whose forward orbit converges exponentially to that of x. The unstable statement follows by applying this to f^{-1}.

SHARP EDGES. (1) The Holder hypothesis on Df is NOT cosmetic: the theorem is false for merely C^1 diffeomorphisms -- Pugh constructed a C^1 diffeomorphism (in dimension 4) with non-zero exponents for which the conclusion fails. The Holder exponent is what makes the nonlinear remainder in Lyapunov charts small enough to run the graph transform against a chart size that shrinks subexponentially. (2) r(x) CANNOT be taken uniformly positive: it is only tempered, and any argument that needs a uniform size must work on a Pesin block and pay for the fact that the block is not invariant. (3) Nothing is asserted at points where all exponents are >= 0, or in directions with ZERO exponent. (4) The family of stable manifolds is measurable, not continuous, on the whole space; continuity holds only along Pesin blocks. (5) Absolute continuity of the stable lamination (needed for Pesin's entropy formula and for ergodic components) is a FURTHER theorem, also requiring C^{1+a}; it is not part of this statement and must be cited separately.
M is a compact Riemannian manifold; f is a C^{1+a} diffeomorphism of M with a > 0 (Holder derivative)
mu is an f-invariant Borel probability measure
the conclusion is stated at mu-almost every point having at least one negative Lyapunov exponent
eps > 0 is fixed small relative to the largest negative exponent; C(x) and r(x) are measurable, r tempered
no claim is made at points with only non-negative exponents, in zero-exponent directions, or about absolute continuity of the lamination
title: Pesin's stable manifold theorem (non-uniformly hyperbolic local stable manifolds)

body: [Lemma lem_1 of arXiv:2412.03774, '{ Refining Concentration for \\Gaussian Quadratic Chaos with\\ Applications in Sonar and C'] Let $m\geq1$ be an integer. For every $0<b<1$, the smallest $a$ (tightest upper bound) for which~((gen_ineq1 of the paper)) holds is $a=\theta_m(b)$ as defined in~((theta_func of the paper)). Equivalently, for every $a>\frac{1}{m+1}$, the largest $b$ for which the inequality in ((theone of the paper)) holds is $\theta_m^{-1}(a)$ where $\theta_m^{-1}(\cdot)$ is the inverse function to $\theta_m(\cdot)$.  Conversely, if $a\leq \frac{1}{m+1}$, there exists no $b>0$ such that ((theone of the paper)) holds.
title: Lemma lem_1 of arXiv:2412.03774

body:
[Theorem thm:state-dependent kernels of arXiv:2509.02996, 'Group-averaged Markov chains: mixing improvement'] Assume $P\in \mathcal{S}(\pi)$. Let $G$ be any finite group acting on $\mathcal{X}$. Under Assumption (assum:pi and G of the paper), without assuming any group invariance of $\pi$, the arguments in the following results still hold for $P_{la}$, $P_{ra}$ and $(P_{la})_{ra}$ defined in this subsection (with $P_{da}$ in the original results replaced by these three kernels):
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item Improvement of multiplicative spectral gap: Theorem (thm:singular value improvement of the paper) (assuming $P$ is compact) and Corollary (cor:larger group is better of the paper).

        \item Improvement of asymptotic variance: Theorem (thm:asympvar improvement of the paper) (assuming $P$ is compact) and Remark (remark:asympvar QP=PQ=QPQ of the paper) (both assuming $P$ is reversible).

        \item Pythagorean identities: Theorem (thm:pythKL of the paper) (assuming $P$ and $M$ admit a transition density w.r.t. $\mathfrak{m}$ at any starting state $x$) and Theorem (thm:pythHS of the paper) HS part (assuming $P$ is a HS operator). Precisely, we have
        \begin{align}
        	D_{KL}^\pi(P\|M) &= D_{KL}^\pi(P\|(P_{la})_{ra})+D_{KL}^\pi((P_{la})_{ra}\|M), \quad  M\in \mathcal{LI}(G)\cap \mathcal{RI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi), \\
        	D_{KL}^\pi(P\|M) &= D_{KL}^\pi(P\|P_{la})+D_{KL}^\pi(P_{la}\|M), \quad  M\in \mathcal{LI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi),\\
        	D_{KL}^\pi(P\|M) &= D_{KL}^\pi(P\|P_{ra})+D_{KL}^\pi(P_{ra}\|M), \quad  M\in \mathcal{RI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi),
        \end{align}
        and 
        \begin{align}
            \left\lVert P-M \right\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 &=\norm{P-(P_{la})_{ra}}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2+\norm{(P_{la})_{ra}-M}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2, \quad M\in \mathcal{LI}(G)\cap \mathcal{RI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi),\\
            \left\lVert P-M \right\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 &=\norm{P-P_{la}}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2+\norm{P_{la}-M}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2, \quad M\in \mathcal{LI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi),\\
            \left\lVert P-M \right\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 &=\norm{P-P_{ra}}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2+\norm{P_{ra}-M}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2, \quad M\in \mathcal{RI}(G)\cap \mathcal{S}(\pi).
        \end{align}

        \item Comparable mixing times: Theorem (thm:mixing time equivalence within QP,PQ,QPQ of the paper).
    \end{enumerate}
title: Theorem thm:state-dependent kernels of arXiv:2509.02996

body:
[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.24167, '\bf On the stability of rarefaction for stochastic viscous conservation law'] Assume $X(t)\in C^1(\mathbb R_+,\mathbb R_+)$ and satisfies that
    $$
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\dot{X_t} \leq X_t^\alpha+t^{-\beta}, \\
\int_0^t X_s d s \leq C (1+t)^p,
\end{array}\right.
$$
where $\alpha>2$ and $0\leq p<(\alpha-2) \big( \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\wedge \frac{1}{\alpha-1} \big)$. Then we have the sharp decay estimate $$X(t)=O\big(t^{-( \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\wedge \frac{1}{\alpha-1} )}\big).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2606.24167

body:
[Theorem thm:er-critical-window-winner-selection of arXiv:2608.06159, 'Majority Dynamics on Resampled Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs:\\[0.5ex] Gaussian Winner '] Under Assumption~(ass:connectivity of the paper), retain the preceding choices of
\(K\) and \(h_N\), and fix \(C_0>0\). Consider deterministic initial
configurations satisfying
\begin{align}
x_0
\coloneqq
\Delta_0\sqrt{\frac{2b\log N}{\pi N}},
\qquad
|x_0|\le C_0.

\end{align}
Uniformly over all such configurations, the blue- and red-unanimity
probabilities at time \(T_{N}+3\) satisfy
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
\P\left(
\gR_{T_{N}+3}=\emptyset
\,\middle|\,
\rvy_0
\right)
&=
\Phi(x_0)+O\left(\mathfrak r_N(C_0)\right),
\\
\P\left(
\gB_{T_{N}+3}=\emptyset
\,\middle|\,
\rvy_0
\right)
&=
\Phi(-x_0)+O\left(\mathfrak r_N(C_0)\right).

\end{align}
\end{subequations}
In particular, the approximation error vanishes,
\(\mathfrak r_N(C_0)=o(1)\), and the time horizon satisfies
\(T_{N}+3=(1+o(1))\log N/\log\log N\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Critical-window winner selection

[Definition 2 (Cell complex) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] Let ${\bf E}^d$ be an affine space. A {\bf cell} is a convex piecewise linear
polyhedron $S\subset {\bf E}^d$ whose relative interior lies in some affine subspace
${\bf E}^i\subset {\bf E}^d$. We write $S^m$ for a cell of dimension $m$. A {\bf convex cell complex} $Y$ in ${\bf E}^d$ is a finite collection
$\mathcal F=\{S\}$ of cells such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item for each $S^m\in\mathcal F$, its boundary $\partial S^m$ is a union
    of $F^j\in\mathcal F$ with $j<m$, where $\{F^j\}$ are called the faces of $S^m$.
    \item if $F^j,S^m\in\mathcal F$ with $j<m$, and $F^j\cap S^m\neq\varnothing$,
    then $F^j\subset S^m$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Cell complex

[Lemma 173 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider a tiling model as above and choose $C>0$. Assumed that all the involved rescaled by $\N$ parameters of the model are smaller than $C$. Further assume that equations \eqref{eq_trapezoid_restriction_2} are non-contradictory, that each segment $[\hat a'_h,\hat b'_h]$, $h\in[H]$ contains at least one band of the simplified equilibrium measure $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ of length at least $C^{-1}$, and that the bands of $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ are at distance at least $C^{-1}$ from the endpoints of the segment. Then for $\N$ large enough (depending on the constant $C$), both the equilibrium measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and the simplified equilibrium measure $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}$ have one band per segment. Furthermore, Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic}, \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}, and \ref{Assumptions_analyticity} hold for the associated discrete ensemble. And, for any $\delta > 0$ there exists a constant $C_2 > 0$ depending only on $\delta > 0$ and the constants in the assumptions such that, for any $h \in [H]$ and $z \in \amsmathbb{C}$ at distance at least $\delta$ from $[\hat{a}_h',\hat{b}_h']$ we have
\[
\big|\Gm_{\mu_h}(z) - \Gm_{\tilde{\mu}_h}(z)\big| \leq \frac{C_2}{\N^2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 173 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Lemma lem:forward-meeting of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] Under Assumption (assumption:markovchain of the paper), there exists $\rho \in(0,1)$ and,
for each $x,y\in\mathcal X$, a coupling $(X_t^x,X_t^y)_{t\ge0}$ of
two copies of the chain started at $X_0^x=x$, $X_0^y=y$, such that the
meeting time $T^+(x,y):=\inf\{t\ge0: X_t^x=X_t^y\}$ satisfies
\[
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(T^+(x,y)>k\bigr)
  \lesssim
  \bigl(V(x)+V(y)\bigr)\rho^k,
  \qquad k\ge0.
\]
Consequently, for every $p\ge1$ there exists $C_{p}<\infty$ with $  \mathbb{E}\bigl[T^+(x,y)^p\bigr]
  \le C_{p}\bigl(V(x)+V(y)\bigr).$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:forward-meeting of arXiv:2601.08184

\end{equation}

\[ 
\lambda (t) := c_0 \exp \left( - \dfrac{ \varepsilon c (1- e^{ - \delta t } ) }{\delta  }  \right)  \ \text{ and }\ 
G(t, \xi ) := \dfrac{ \exp \left( - a \xi e^{- \delta t } \right)  }{ 1+\exp \left( - a \xi e^{- \delta t } \right) }

where $a \geq 0$,  $ \delta \geq |\Omega_c | \left( \max_{ k \in \Omega_c } M(e_k) \right)^2  $ and  $c\geq \dfrac{a |\Omega_c | \min_{ k \in \Omega_c } ( \alpha_k M(e_k )) }{2}$.

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2608.21312, 'Interface between competing random walks on a cycle'] Let $S_n$ be the ATD walk as in~\eqref{eq:ATD walk}. Then there are constants $q_1,q_2>0$ and intervals $[x_1, x_2], [y_1, y_2]$ with $y_1 > x_2+1$ such that, for every integer $m\ge1$,
\[
  \pr\left(-x_2m^2\le  S_m\le -x_1m^2\right)\ge q_1
\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad
  \pr\left(y_1m^2\le  S_m\le y_2m^2\right)\ge q_2.
\]

[DRAFT: T407-LOW-003 v2, proof unaudited; not independently checked; priority unestablished.] Candidate theorem: there are absolute constants c,epsilon_0>0 such that for each integer d>=2, learning H_d={sign(a^T U b):U in O(d)} from IID independent standard Gaussian a,b in R^d to disagreement risk epsilon<=epsilon_0 with success probability at least 3/4 requires at least c d^2/epsilon labeled examples, even for randomized improper learners. Hence an orthogonally equivariant learner of the fixed balanced quadratic target sign(sum_(i<=d)x_i^2-sum_(i>d)x_i^2) under N(0,I_(2d)) needs the same order, including for expected disagreement risk after constant adjustments. The candidate proof uses a local packing with disagreement Omega(t) but conditional binary-label entropy <=100t after a common signed-permutation conjugation; no disjointness of disagreement regions is assumed. This concerns noiseless binary classification only and does not settle joint all-layer CNN training.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] There exists a closed surface \(\Sigma_2\) of genus two, unit-speed
Teichm\"uller geodesics
\(
  X_t^{(n)}\in\mathcal T(\Sigma_2),
\)
simple closed curves \(\alpha_n\), and intervals
\(I_n=[r_n,s_n]\) with
\(
  0<r_n<s_n,
  s_n-r_n\to\infty,
\)
such that
\[
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_0^{(n)}}(\alpha_n)\ge \frac13,
  \qquad
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_{-2}^{(n)}}(\alpha_n)\le e^{-4}.
\]
Moreover, there are constants \(0<m<M<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such
that
\[
  m
  \le
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_t^{(n)}}(\alpha_n)
  \le
  M
\quad (t\in I_n).
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Exit-time lower bound from effective resistance: compare the exit time from B(N) with the commute time. Result: The commute-time identity gives E^0_h tau_{B(N)^c} >= c R_eff(0, B(N)^c) pi(B(N)) where pi is the reversible measure (volume of the Liouville measure of the box). The volume is N^{psi... } of order N^{2 + 2 beta^2 g ...} in the notation of the notes, i.e. N^{psi(beta)} up to N^{o(1)} by the LQG volume estimates, and R_eff(0, B(N)^c) >= (log N)^{1/2 - o(1)} ... the resistance lower bound available is only polylogarithmic. Hence E tau >= N^{psi(beta)} times a polylog, which is the right exponent, but the problem asks for a bound on tau in probability, not in expectation, with a (log T)^{1/2+delta} correction. Converting expectation to probability needs concentration of the exit time, and the exit time is not concentrated at fixed environment because the walk can be trapped near the maximum: the trapping time at the deepest well has a heavy tail. The exponent statement (T^{1/psi(beta)+o(1)}) follows from the expectation bound plus Markov's inequality in one direction; the precise correction is out of reach with the resistance route. Key identity: E tau_B(N) >= c R_eff(0,B(N)^c) mu_h(B(N)) with mu_h(B(N)) = N^{psi(beta)+o(1)}. Obstruction: Exit-time concentration fails at fixed environment because of trapping at deep wells; the polylog correction is a trapping statement, not a resistance statement.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2512.02661, 'Worst-case mixing estimates for Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers'] Let $X_t$ and $\Lc{i}_t$ be continuous stochastic processes which take values in $D$ and $\bbR_{\geq 0}$, respectively.
	Then, $X_t$ is called \emph{a reflected Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers $B_i$ and local times $\Lc{i}_t$} if the following properties hold with probability one:
	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2.5em, label = (\roman*)]
		\item
		      $
			      \intd X_t =  \intd W_t +  \sum_{i=0}^{\nb} s_i(\Lc{i}_t) \vec{n}_i(X_t) \bb1\{X_t \in B_i \}\intd \Lc{i}_t.\nonumber
		      $
		\item For $i \leq {\nb}$, $\Lc{i}_t$ is nondecreasing, satisfies $\Lc{i}_0 =0$, and increases at time $t$ if and only if $X_t \in  B_i$.
		      That is,
		      \begin{align}
			      \Lc{i}_t = \int_0^t \bb1\{X_r\in B_i \}\, \intd \Lc{i}_r.\nonumber
		      \end{align}
		\item For $i \leq {\nb}$, if $s_i(\Lc{i}_t) = +1$ then $X_t$ is on the positive side of $B_i$.
		      Similarly, if $s_i(\Lc{i}_t) = -1$ then $X_t$ is on the negative side of $B_i$.
	\end{enumerate}
	The process $X_t$ may also be referred to as a \emph{snapping-out Brownian motion}.

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03669, 'Volterra Integral Reduction \\ for Boundary Diffusion Problems'] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:smooth}--\ref{ass:func} and~\ref{ass:potential}, 
for each fixed $y$, the function $t\mapsto \partial_x f(t,y^+)$ 
is the unique solution in $C[0,T]$ of the following Volterra integral equation 
of the second kind with a weakly singular kernel
\begin{equation}

\alpha(t,y)\,\partial_x f(t,y^+)
=
\partial_x g(t,y)
+
\int_0^t
k(t,s)\,
\frac{\gamma_0(t-s,y)}
{(t-s)^{1/2}}\,
\partial_x f(s,y^+)\,ds,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
\alpha(t,y) = 
\frac{\sigma^2(y)+k(t,t)}
{\sigma^2(y)}, \qquad
\gamma_0(\tau,y) =
\tau^{1/2} r_0(\tau,y,y)
-
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}
{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma^2(y)},
\end{equation}
and $r_0(\tau,y,y)$ is a continuous implicit function satisfying 
$r_0(\tau,y,y)=O_K(\tau^{1/2})$ uniformly on compact sets.

[Defn def Mixing of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] Let $G$ be a group acting on a probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $r\geq 2$ be an integer. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item [(1)] We say that the action of $G$ on $(X,\mu)$ is {\bf mixing of order $r\geq 2 $}, if for all $f_1,...,f_r \in L^{\infty}(X,\mu)$, and for all $g_1,g_2,\dots, g_r \in G$ we have 
$$
\bigg| \int_{X}\prod_{i=1}^r ( f_i\circ g_i){\rm{d}} \mu- \prod_{i=1}^r  \int_{X}f_i{\rm{d}} \mu\bigg| \to 0  \qquad\mbox{as $\min_{\ell\neq k} \, d(g_\ell,g_k)\to \infty$}.
$$

\item [(2)] We fix an $G$-invariant sub-algebra $\mathcal A$ of $L^{\infty}(X,\mu)$, and a family $N = (N_s)_{s\in \mathbb{N}}$ of semi-norms on $\mathcal A$. Then we say that the action of the group $G$ on  $(X,\mu)$ is {\bf exponentially mixing of order $r$} with respect to $d$ and $(\mathcal A,N)$, if there exist $\delta_r > 0$ and an integer $s_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $s > s_r$, $f_1,...,f_r \in  \mathcal A$ and $g_1,\dots,g_r\in G$, 
$$
 \bigg| \int_{X}\prod_{i=1}^r ( f_i\circ g_i){\rm{d}} \mu- \prod_{i=1}^r  \int_{X}f_i{\rm{d}} \mu\bigg|  \leq C {\rm e} ^{-\delta_r d_r(g_1,..,g_r)} \prod_{i=1}^r N_s(f_i) 
$$
for some finite constant $C=C(s,r)$. In this case, $\delta_r>0$ is called {\bf the rate of mixing}. 
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem RPD_L_n of arXiv:2607.12061, 'Models for species evolution with random deaths'] Let $f^\dagger_c = \tfrac{qr}{p}$ and suppose $p>q$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If \( f < f^\dagger_c \), then $|\mathcal{B}(f)| = \infty$ a.s. and $\mathbb{E}(B_{i+1}-B_i) \leq  \frac{f^\dagger_c}{f^\dagger_c-f} <\infty$ for all $i$.  
\item[(ii)] If $f=f^\dagger_c$ then $|\mathcal{B}(f)|=\infty$ a.s.  and $\mathbb{E}(B_{i+1}-B_i) \to \infty$ as $i \to \infty$.
\item[(iii)] If \( f > f^\dagger_c \), then $|\mathcal{B}(f)| <\infty$ a.s.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 3 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] Let  $\cH$ be an         $n$-dimensional Hilbert space. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For any invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A$, the system $\{Ae_k, (A^{-1})^Te_k\}_{k=1}^n$ forms a  biorthogonal system in $\R^n$. 
        \item Given a  linearly independent set of vectors $\{E_k\}_{k=1}^n$ in an 
        $n$-dimensional Hilbert space $\cH$, there exist unique vectors $\{F_k\}_{k=1}^n$ such that $\{E_k, F_k\}_{k=1}^n$ is a  biorthogonal system in $\cH$. 
        \item For a  biorthogonal system $\{E_k, F_k\}_{k=1}^n$ in an 
        $n$-dimensional Hilbert space $\cH$, the Euclidean norm of each $F_k$ satisfies
        \begin{equation}
            \|F_k\|_2=\frac{1}{\mbox{dist}(E_k, H_k)}, \qquad k=1, \dots, n,
        \end{equation}
        where $H_k=\mbox{span}\{E_i\}_{i\neq k}$ denotes the subspace spanned by all $E_i$ except $E_k$, and $\operatorname{dist}(E_k, H_k)$ is the Euclidean distance from $E_k$ to $H_k$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 3 of arXiv:2604.12233

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.27569, 'Laplace and Dolbeault operators on Sasakian manifolds'] (formulas stated in \cite
{Schmude2014LaplaceOpsSasakiEinstMflds} for Sasakian-Einstein case) The
following identities hold on a Sasakian manifold $(M^{2n+1},g,\xi )$
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\left\{ \partial _{C},\xi \lrcorner \right\} =\left\{ \overline{
\partial _{C}},\xi \lrcorner \right\} =0,\left\{ \partial _{C}^{\ast },\eta
\wedge \right\} =\left\{ \overline{\partial _{C}}^{\ast },\eta \wedge
\right\} =0$

\item $\left\{ \partial _{C},\eta \wedge \right\} =\left\{ \overline{
\partial _{C}},\eta \wedge \right\} =L,\,\,\left\{ \partial _{C}^{\ast },\xi
\lrcorner \right\} =\left\{ \overline{\partial _{C}}^{\ast },\xi \lrcorner
\right\} =\Lambda $

\item $\overline{\partial _{C}}\partial _{C}+\partial _{C}\overline{\partial
_{C}}=-2L\mathcal{L}_{\xi }$

\item $\overline{\partial _{C}}^{\ast }=\ast \partial _{C}\ast \left(
-1\right) ^{\deg },\qquad \partial _{C}^{\ast }=\ast \overline{\partial _{C}}
\ast \left( -1\right) ^{\deg }$

\item $0=[L,\partial _{C}]=[L,\overline{\partial _{C}}]=[\Lambda ,\overline{
\partial _{C}}^{\ast }]=[\Lambda ,\partial _{C}^{\ast }]$

\item $\left[ H,\partial _{C}\right] =-\partial _{C}-L(\xi \lrcorner )$

\item $[\Lambda ,\overline{\partial _{C}}]=-i\partial _{C}^{\ast }+i\eta
\wedge \Lambda +H(\xi \lrcorner )$

\item $[\Lambda ,\partial _{C}]=i\overline{\partial _{C}}^{\ast }-i\eta
\wedge \Lambda +H(\xi \lrcorner )$

\item $[\overline{\partial _{C}}^{\ast },L]=i\partial _{C}-iL(\xi \lrcorner
)+\eta \wedge H$

\item $[\partial _{C}^{\ast },L]=-i\overline{\partial _{C}}+iL(\xi \lrcorner
)+\eta \wedge H$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 15 of arXiv:2608.27569

[Thm restate of pnkt and nu of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $c\in\mathbb{R}$ be an absolute constant. Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(m_N)_{N\ge 1}$ and $(l_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers, such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $m_N,l_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$.
\item $n_N=m_Nl_N$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}n_N=\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
For all $N\ge 1$, let $t_N=\frac{n_N}{2}(\log n_N-\frac 12\log l_N+c)$. Let $P_{n_N}^{*t_N}$ be defined as in (defi: Pnk and its convolution of the paper), and $\nu_{n_N}^{t_N}$ be defined as in (defi: construction of nu of the paper). Let $\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash \nu_{n_N}^{t_N}$ be their induced probability measures over $\sim_{l_N}\backslash\mathfrak{S}_{n_N}$. Then, we have
$$\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log n_N(d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash\nu_{n_N}^{t_N}))\le -1.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm restate of pnkt and nu of arXiv:2604.23890

[Definition Recursive good block of arXiv:2607.22908, 'Epidemic Phase Transitions in the Zero-Range Process'] A scale-$k$ block $B$ is \emph{good} if, for each of its $3^d$ output interfaces $\Out(B, v)$
  (where $v \in \{-1, 0, 1\}^d$), the following connectivity event holds: there exists a subset of input
  sub-interfaces $\mathcal{A}_{in}(B, v) \subseteq \mathcal{L}(\In(B))$ of size $|\mathcal{A}_{in}(B, v)| \ge \frac{3}{4}
  \ell_{k-1}^d$ such that, for every $V \in \mathcal{A}_{in}(B, v)$, there exists a target set $\mathcal{T}_V(B, v)
  \subseteq \mathcal{L}(\Out(B, v))$ of size $|\mathcal{T}_V(B, v)| \ge \frac{3}{4} \ell_{k-1}^d$, such that $V$ is
  connected to each target $W \in \mathcal{T}_V(B, v)$ by a chain of good scale-$(k-1)$
  sub-blocks contained entirely within $B$.
title: Recursive good block

    $f\mapsto P_Df(z)$ is the harmonic measure with pole at $z$, that is,
    $$
	    P_Df(z) = \int_{\partial D}f(w) d\omega_z(w).
    $$

body: In physics and thermodynamics, the ergodic hypothesis says that, over long periods of time, the time spent by a system in some region of the phase space of microstates with the same energy is proportional to the volume of this region; i.e., that over long periods of time all accessible microstates are equiprobable.
title: Ergodic hypothesis

body: Axiom of choice (AC): For every set I and every I-indexed family (S_i) of nonempty sets, there exists an I-indexed family (x_i) such that x_i is an element of S_i for every i in I. Equivalently: every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function, i.e. a function f defined on the family with f(S) in S for each member S; equivalently, the Cartesian product of any family of nonempty sets is nonempty. The axiom asserts existence rather than providing a construction. It was formulated in 1904 by Ernst Zermelo in order to prove the well-ordering theorem, and it is independent of the other Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms (Goedel 1938, Cohen 1963).
title: Axiom of choice

[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Let \(n\ge1\), \(\ell\ge0\),
\(I\in\mathcal D_\ell([0,1])\), and let \(J\subset I\) be a dyadic child.  Then
\[
    \mathbb E\left[
        X_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell)
        \mid
        \mathcal F_\ell
    \right]
    =
    0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
    |X_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell)|
    \le
    C|c_J(\xi,d,\ell)|L_nT_{\ell+1,n}
\]
almost surely, and
\[
    \mathbb E\left[
        |X_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell)|^2
        \mid
        \mathcal F_\ell
    \right]
    \le
    CL_n|c_J(\xi,d,\ell)|^2M_IT_{\ell+1,n}.
\]

[Cor jointap of arXiv:2412.00610, 'Joint Poisson Convergence of Monochromatic Hyperedges in Multiplex Hypergraphs'] Fix $d\geq 3$. Suppose  the elements of a set $A_n \subseteq [n]$, with $|A_n| \rightarrow \infty$, are colored independently and uniformly at random with $c_n$ colors such that the following holds: For all $3 \leq r \leq d$, there exists a constant $\lambda_r \geq 0$ with  
    \begin{align}
    \lim_{n \to \infty}\bE W_r(A_n) = \lim_{n \to \infty}\Var W_r(A_n) = \lambda_r. 
    \end{align} 
      Then, as $n \rightarrow \infty$, 
    $$\left(\begin{array}{c}
        W_3(A_n) \\
       	\vdots \\ 
	W_d(A_n) 
        \end{array}\right) \dto \left(\begin{array}{c}
            Z_3 \\ 
            \vdots \\ 
            Z_d
            \end{array}\right), $$
      where $Z_3 \sim \Pois(\lambda_1), \ldots, Z_d \sim \Pois(\lambda_d)$ are independent.  \hfill $\Box$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.01268, 'Resultant multiplicity via projective degrees\\ and applications to tensor eigenvalues'] Assume that $I\neq (0)$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        For each $\ell\geq 1$, for which $Y_{\ell-1}\neq\varnothing$, the element $g_\ell$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R/J_{\ell-1}$.
        Moreover, \begin{equation}
        
        J_\ell = \left( J_{\ell-1}+(g_\ell) \right) : I^\infty.
                \end{equation}
                Consequently, $Y_\ell$ is the closure of $(Y_{\ell-1}\cap \cZ_{\PP}(g_\ell))\setminus X$.
        \item 
        If $\operatorname{ht}(I)\geq r$ (equivalently, if $\codim X\geq r$), then $g_1,\dots,g_r$ is a regular sequence.
        In this case, we have $y_\ell=d^\ell$ for every $\ell< r$.
        \item 
        Let $Z$ be an irreducible component of $X$ of codimension $r$, let $\fp$ be its generic point, and \[
        S \coloneqq \mathcal{O}_{\PP^{n-1},\fp}
        \] be the corresponding local ring.
        Then, $S$ is a regular local ring of dimension $r$ with $g_1,\dots,g_r$ forming a regular sequence, and a system of parameters.
        Moreover, for every $0\leq j<r$  \[
        J_j S = (g_1,\dots,g_j) S.
        \]
        Consequently, the multiplicity of $Y_{r-1}\cap\cZ_{\PP}(g_r)$ along $Z$ is  \[
        \lambda\coloneqq \length_{S}\left(S/(g_1,\dots,g_r)S\right) < \infty,
        \] and \[
        \lambda \geq \mult_Z(X).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Mainthm thm:density of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $d\ge1$ and $r>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \emph{(Positivity, uniformly in $\lambda$.)} For every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ there is
  $\bar\eta=\bar\eta(\mu,r,d)>0$ such that
  \[
    \eta_c(\lambda,\mu)\ \ge\ \bar\eta(\mu,r,d)\qquad\text{for every admissible }\lambda\in(0,\infty] ,
  \]
  that is, for every $\lambda\in(0,\infty]$ when $\mu<\infty$ and for $\lambda=\infty$ when
  $\mu=\infty$. Equivalently, the infection started from a single particle dies out almost surely
  at every intensity below $\bar\eta$, whatever the infection rate.
\item \emph{(Finiteness at $\lambda=\infty$.)} For every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ and every $d\ge1$,
  $\eta_c(\infty,\mu)<\infty$.
\item \emph{(The Boolean bound, $d\ge2$.)} For $d\ge2$ and every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$,
  \[
    \eta_c(\infty,\mu)\ \le\ \eta_c(\infty,\infty)\ \le\ \eta_c^{\mathrm{B}} ,
  \]
  so the critical density at infinite infection rate is bounded above by the critical intensity of
  the static Boolean model, uniformly in the recovery rate.
\end{enumerate}
In particular $\eta_c(\infty,\mu)\in(0,\infty)$ for every $d\ge1$ and every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$.
That is, the instantaneous infection dies out almost surely for $\eta<\eta_c(\infty,\mu)$ and
survives with positive probability for $\eta>\eta_c(\infty,\mu)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 31 ($n$-admissibility) of arXiv:2606.19115, 'Finite free perpetuities'] We say that a pair $(A_n,B_n)$ is $n$-admissible if there exist $\kappa_n\in\N$, $\mathcal{I}_n\subset \{1,\dots,\kappa_n\}$ and
independent random variables $D_1,\dots,D_{\kappa_n}$ satisfying
$\E[|D_i|^n]<\infty$ for each $i$, such that
\[
(A_n,B_n)\stackrel{d}{=}_n
\left(
\prod_{i\in\mathcal{I}_n}D_i,\,
G_{\mathcal{I}_n,\kappa_n}(0,D_1,\dots,D_{\kappa_n})
\right),
\]
that is, $A_n$ is the slope and $B_n$ is the intercept of the
random affine map $G_{\mathcal{I}_n,\kappa_n}(\cdot, D_1,\ldots,D_{\kappa_n})$.

body:
[Cor main scheme of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $X$ and $Z$ are smooth separated schemes, of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, and there is a projective contraction $f : X \to Z$ morphism whose exceptional $E$ is {a smooth Cartier divisor}.
    Moreover, suppose there is a {smooth closed subscheme $Y \subseteq Z$}, such that $f^{-1}(Y) \simeq E$ set-theoretically, and $f : X \setminus E \xrightarrow{\sim} Z \setminus Y$.
    Then $f$ is a blowup along smooth center $Y$, i.e., $X \simeq \operatorname{Bl}_{Y} Z$.
    In particular, $f|_{E} : E \to Y$ is a projective bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_{X}(E)|_{E} \simeq \mathcal{O}_{E}(-1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor main scheme of arXiv:2609.04023

Every path to ne1 crosses E_r, so sum_(e in E_r)p_e>=1. Independence and Cauchy-Schwarz give E|Gamma intersect Gamma'|=sum_e p_e^2 >= sum_(r=0)^(n-1)1/(8r+4) >=(1/8)log(2n+1). body:
[Definition def:rational-point-dimensions of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] Fix an optimal oracle prefix-free Turing machine \(V\) whose outputs are rational
points in \(\mathbb Q^n\).  For an oracle \(A\subseteq\omega\) and
\(q\in\mathbb Q^n\), define
\[
K^A(q)
=
\min\{|p|:V^A(p)=q\}.
\]
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\omega\), define
\[
K^A_r(x)
=
\min\{K^A(q):q\in\mathbb Q^n,\ |x-q|<2^{-r}\}.
\]
Define the effective Hausdorff and packing dimensions of \(x\) relative to
\(A\) by
\[
\dim_e^A(x)
=
\liminf_{r\to\infty}\frac{K^A_r(x)}{r}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Dim_e^A(x)
=
\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{K^A_r(x)}{r}.
\]
For nonempty \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), put
\[
\dim_e^A(E)
=
\sup_{x\in E}\dim_e^A(x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Dim_e^A(E)
=
\sup_{x\in E}\Dim_e^A(x).
\]
title: Definition def:rational-point-dimensions of arXiv:2608.29561

[Lemma 7 (The stopping-time meaning of ucp) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For adapted càdlàg processes \(X^{(m)},X\) in a separable metric space,
the following are equivalent on every compact time interval:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item \(\sup_{t\le T}d(X^{(m)}_t,X_t)\to0\) in probability;
\item for every sequence of possibly \(m\)-dependent stopping times
\(\tau_m\le T\), one has
\(d(X^{(m)}_{\tau_m},X_{\tau_m})\to0\) in probability.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a matrix $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$ the following conditions are equivalent, and if they are satisfied, we say that $A$ is positive:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A=B^2$, with $B=B^*$.

\item $A=CC^*$, for some $C\in M_N(\mathbb C)$.

\item $<Ax,x>\geq0$, for any vector $x\in\mathbb C^N$.

\item $A=A^*$, and the eigenvalues are positive, $\lambda_i\geq0$.

\item $A=UDU^*$, with $U\in U_N$ and with $D\in M_N(\mathbb R_+)$ diagonal.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:informal of arXiv:2411.09516, 'Sharp Matrix Empirical Bernstein Inequalities\footnote{NeurIPS 2025 Poster}'] Let $ \mathbf{X} _1,\dots ,  \mathbf{X} _n$ be symmetric matrices with eigenvalues in $[0,1]$ and common conditional mean $ \mathbf{M}  =  \mathbb E [  \mathbf{X} _i |  \mathbf{X} _1,\dots,  \mathbf{X} _{i-1} ]$. 
    For an appropriate weighted average $\hat  \mathbf{M} _n$ of $ \mathbf{X} _1,\dots,  \mathbf{X} _n$ and an appropriate sample variance proxy $v_{n,\alpha} =v(\alpha,  \mathbf{X} _1,\dots,  \mathbf{X} _n) > 0$,
    \begin{equation}
     \mathbb P \left( \lambda_{\max}(\hat \mathbf{M} _n -   \mathbf{M} ) \geqslant \sqrt{\frac{2 \log(d/\alpha) v_{n,\alpha}} {n}}   \right) \leqslant \alpha.
\end{equation}

    Further, if $\{ \mathbf{X} _i\}$ have a common conditional variance $ \mathbf{V} $, $v_{n,\alpha}$ converges almost surely to 
    $\| \mathbf{V}  \|$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem new of arXiv:2411.04238, 'Holomorphic jump-diffusions'] Let $X=(X_t)_{t\in [0,T}$ be an $S$-valued jump-diffusion with characteristics $(b,a,K)$ and extended generator $\mathcal A$.  Assume that $b_j,a_{ij}\in\mathcal O(S)$, $K$ is a kernel with holomorphic jump size, and let $F$ be the corresponding non-negative measure on the measurable space $E$. 
Let $G$ satisfy (equation eqnG of the paper) and
for each $h\in H(P_G^d(0))$, $z\in P^d_{R(S)+\varepsilon}(0)$, and $y\in E$ set $\mathcal D(J)$ and $Jh$ as in (equation eqnDJ of the paper).
Set 
 \begin{align*}
     \mathcal{V}&\subseteq\{h\in H(P^d_G(0))\colon e^h\in \mathcal D(J)
     \text{ and } P^d_{R(S)+\varepsilon}\ni z\mapsto Je^h(z,\cdot)\in L^1(E,F) \text{ is continuous}\},
\\  \mathcal{V}^*&:=\{\mathbf{u}\in \mathcal{S}^* \colon h_\mathbf{u}=h|_{{P}^d_{R(S)}(0)},  \ h\in \mathcal{V}\}.
 \end{align*}
Then $X$ is an $S$-valued $\mathcal{V}$-affine-holomorphic process and for all $\mathbf{u}\in\mathcal{V}^*$, $$\mathcal{A}\exp(h_\mathbf{u})=\exp(h_{\mathbf{u}})R(h_\mathbf{u})|_S,$$ where $R:\mathcal{V}^*\rightarrow \mathcal{S}^*$ is given by
\begin{align}
    R(\mathbf{u})&:= \sum_{|\beta|=1}\mathbf{u}^{(\beta)}\ast \underline{\mathbf{b}}^{\beta} 
    +\sum_{|\beta_1|,|\beta_2|=1}\frac{1}{(\beta_1+\beta_2)!}\underline{\underline{\mathbf{a}}}^{\beta_1+\beta_2}\ast ({\mathbf{u}^{(\beta_1)}}\ast\mathbf{u}^{(\beta_2)}+\mathbf{u}^{(\beta_1+\beta_2)})\\

[Definition 17 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] a) A function $\psi: E \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be \emph{$c$-convex}, if there is a function $\zeta: E \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x \in E$ 
$$
\psi(x) = \sup \{ \zeta(y) - c(x,y): y \in E  \}.
$$
b) We define the set of all 1-Lipschitz functions with respect to $c$ as 
$$
\mathcal{L}_1(E,c) := \{ f: E \to \mathbb{R}: f(x) - f(y) \le c(x,y) \mbox{ for all } x,y \in E  \}.
$$
c) For a $c$-convex function we define the \emph{$c$-transform}
$$
\psi^c(x) := \inf \{ \psi(y) + c(y,x): y \in E  \}.
$$

[Corollary cor:distribution of cumulative arrivals of arXiv:2412.06452, 'Time-dependent queue length distribution in queues fed by $K$ customers in a finite interv'] For $(t,k) \in (0,T) \times \{1,2,\ldots,K\} \cup [T,\infty) \times
\{K\}$ and $0 < x_1 \leq x_2 \leq \cdots \leq x_k \leq t$, we have

\begin{align}
\lefteqn{
\Pr[X_1 \leq x_1, X_2 \leq x_2, \ldots, X_k \leq x_k \mid A(t)=k]
}\qquad
\notag
\\
&=
\Pr[
\widehat{X}_1 \leq x_1, \widehat{X}_2 \leq x_2, \ldots,\widehat{X}_k \leq x_k
\mid 
\widehat{A}(t)=k
].

\end{align}

In particular, for $t \geq T$,

\begin{align}
\lefteqn{
\Pr[X_1 \leq x_1, X_2 \leq x_2, \ldots, X_K \leq x_K ]
}\qquad
\notag
\\
&=
\Pr[
\widehat{X}_1 \leq x_1, \widehat{X}_2 \leq x_2, \ldots,\widehat{X}_K \leq x_K
\mid \widehat{A}(t)=K]
\nonumber
\\
&=
\Pr[
\widehat{X}_1 \leq x_1, \widehat{X}_2 \leq x_2, \ldots,\widehat{X}_K \leq x_K
\mid \widehat{A}(T)=K].

\end{align}

Let X_1,...,X_n be independent real random variables with bounded densities, M(X) the essential supremum of the density of X, and U_1,...,U_n independent with U_i uniform on [-1/(2M(X_i)), 1/(2M(X_i))], so that M(U_i) = M(X_i). Then M(X_1 + ... + X_n) <= M(U_1 + ... + U_n), and the right side is the value at 0 of the density of U_1 + ... + U_n. With Ball's cube slicing this gives: if M(X_i) <= K and sum a_i^2 = 1, the density of sum a_iX_i is at most sqrt(2)K, which is sharp.

Assumes: independence; each X_i has a bounded density; real-valued summands (R^d version: Madiman-Melbourne-Xu)

body: For the crossing event f_R of the square [0,R]^2 in critical percolation on Z^2 and on the triangular lattice, Ent(f_R) = H(S(f_R)) <= C I(f_R) = O(R^2 alpha_4(R)), and likewise H(P(f_R)) <= C I(f_R) for the pivotal set - Kalai's Conjecture 8 (Three puzzles, ICM 2018, Section 3.3.2), equivalently open problem 1 of Garban-Pete-Schramm 2010 (arXiv:0803.3750, Section 11). Route: encode a random subset A of the square by a quadtree (one bit for empty, four bits per hit dyadic square), so H(A) <= 1 + 4 sum_{k >= 1} E|A_{2^k}| + C_0 E|A_1| with A_r the set of r-squares hit; the finest term is E|A| = I(f); for each coarser scale GPS Lemma 3.2 gives P[S cap B != 0] <= 4 P[four alternating arms from B] (because P[S cap B != 0] = E[Var(f | bits outside B)]), and the same holds for P with no constant; summing over the r-squares with the boundary handled by half-annulus arm events, the scale sum is geometric because the four-arm exponent is strictly less than 2 (alpha_4(r,R) >= (r/R)^{2-eps}). General principle: FEI holds for every Boolean function on a planar array whose spectral sample satisfies sum_{k >= 1} E|S_{2^k}| = O(E|S|).

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C009 v1. Fix alpha>=1 and C>sqrt(2). For m=ceil(alpha*d), iid real Gaussian sensing vectors, a fixed unit signal x_*, and f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2, with probability tending to one there exists a sample-dependent x0 with 0<||h||<1/10, h=x0-x_*, and max_i |a_i^T h|<=C sqrt(log d)||h||, but h^T grad f(x0)<0. Thus every positive GD step strictly increases its squared error. Construction: write A=[g,B], select v_i=g_i 1_{K<=g_i^2<=K+1}, choose fixed K>=16 alpha with q=E[G^2 1_{K<=G^2<=K+1}]<=1/(1000 alpha), and set h=-(3 alpha/(2m)) B^T v in the signal-perpendicular coordinates. Exact Gaussian conditioning gives predictions s=-t_d v+||h||(I-uu^T)xi, with t_d tending to 3/2 and ||h||^2 tending to 9 alpha q/4. The radial derivative tends to -(9/16)q4+(9/2)alpha q+(243/16)alpha^2 q^2<-4 alpha q. Initial relative incoherence follows from Gaussian maxima plus a fixed deterministic shift. This is an asymptotic obstruction to a uniform pointwise contraction lemma. It does not prove nonconvergence, defeat a rate allowing transient amplification, or produce an all-time-incoherent trajectory. Independent review pending; no specialist novelty asserted.

[Lemme decompocun of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$, and $F \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}([0,R_{\max}] \times \mathbb{R})$. The process defined in Section~(sec:inductive of the paper) verifies that, for all $t \in [0,J_{\infty} \wedge \tau_{\exp})$,
\begin{align*}
F(R_{t},\langle \mu_{t}, \varphi_{t} \rangle) = & \hspace{0.1 cm} F(R_{0},\langle \mu_{0}, \varphi_{0} \rangle) \\
    & + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t} \bigg[ \rho(\mu_{s},R_{s}) \partial_{1}F(R_{s},\langle \mu_{s}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) + \langle \mu_{s}, \Phi_{s}(R_{s},.) \rangle \partial_{2} F(R_{s},\langle \mu_{s}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \bigg] \mathrm{d}s} \\
    & + \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathcal{U} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+} } \mathbb{1}_{\{u \in V_{s-} \}} \mathbb{1}_{\{h \leq b(\xi^{u}_{s-})\}}  \bigg( F(R_{s},\langle \mu_{s-}+ \delta_{x_{0}} + \delta_{\xi^{u}_{s-}-x_{0}}-\delta_{\xi^{u}_{s-}}, \varphi_{s} \rangle)} \\
    & \hspace{4cm}- F(R_{s}, \langle \mu_{s-}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \bigg) \mathcal{N}(\mathrm{d}s,\mathrm{d}u,\mathrm{d}h) & \\
     & +
    \displaystyle{\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\mathcal{U} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+} } \mathbb{1}_{\{u \in V_{s-} \}} \mathbb{1}_{\{h \leq d(\xi^{u}_{s-})\}} }\bigg( F(R_{s},\langle \mu_{s-}-\delta_{\xi^{u}_{s-}}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \\
    & \hspace{4cm}- F(R_{s}, \langle \mu_{s-}, \varphi_{s} \rangle) \bigg) \mathcal{N}'(\mathrm{d}s,\mathrm{d}u,\mathrm{d}h),
\end{align*}
with $\Phi$ associated to $\varphi$ as in (equation eq:Phidef of the paper).

body: [Definition of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] Given an oriented (respectively unoriented) graph $G=(V,E)$ and a partition $\pi\in \mathcal{P}(V)$. We let $G^{\pi}=(V^{\pi},E^{\pi})$  be the oriented (respectively unoriented) graph obtained after identifying vertices of $G$ into the same block of $\pi$. The vertices of $G^{\pi}$ are the blocks of $V$ while its edges are given by $([u]_{\pi},[v]_{\pi})$(respectively $\{[u]_{\pi},[v]_{\pi}\}$) whenever $(u,v)$(respectively $\{u,v\}$) is an edge of $G$. If $e=(u,v)$ is an edge of $G$, we denote by $e^\pi=([u]_\pi,[v]_\pi)$  the corresponding edge of $G^\pi$. We call $G^{\pi}$ the \textit{quotient graph} of the graph $G$ with respect to $\pi$. See Example (Example: Quotient graph of the paper) for an example of a quotient graph.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomi'

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2608.04853, 'Minimal-Norm Extensions of Stationary Kernels on Subgroups of Locally Compact Abelian Grou'] Given two bounded operators $T_0:\mathcal{N}(H) \to \mathcal{N}(G)$ and $T_1:L^2(H) \to L^2(G)$ such that $T_0 f =T_1f$ for all $f \in \mathcal{N}(H)$, where the equality is understood in $L^2(G)$, there exists a bounded operator $T_\theta:\mathcal{N}(H)_{\theta} \to \mathcal{N}(G)_\theta$, such that $T_0f=T_\theta f$ for all $f \in \mathcal{N}(H)$ and
\begin{align*}
\Vert T_\theta \Vert_{\mathcal{N}(H)_\theta \to \mathcal{N}(G)_\theta } \leq \Vert T_0 \Vert_{\mathcal{N}(H) \to \mathcal{N}(G)}^{1-\theta} \cdot \Vert T_1 \Vert_{L^2(H) \to L^2(G)}^{\theta}. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For the Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3, write the window sum over W = [k0, k0 + L) as sum_{k in W} F_K(k) = 2^{-(K+1)} (L + Err(k0)) exactly, with P = 3^{K+1}; the square-integrability target needs Err <= C L at the octave position k0 = L = R = (3/2)^K, which gives E(R) << R^{-0.7095}, summable with room. Averaging k0 uniformly over Z_P gives E[Err] = 0 exactly and Var_{k0}(Err) = sum_{eps != 0} c_eps^2 |G(nu_eps)|^2 exactly, G(nu) = sum_{j<L} e(j nu/P): distinct eps give distinct nu mod P by the dissociateness lemma (3^{K+1} divides such a combination only if every coefficient, in {0, +-1, +-2}, vanishes). The identity matches the variance over every window of a full period to six printed digits at K = 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, and the measured Var(Err/L) = 1.90, 2.15, 2.54, 2.91, 3.28 there is linear in K (slope about 0.1767), i.e. logarithmic in R. It reduces exactly: sum_eps c_eps^2 = (3/2)^{K+1}, the normalised weights make the coordinates i.i.d. with P(0) = 2/3 and P(+-1) = 1/6, i.e. eta = B - B' with B ~ Bernoulli(p), p = (1 + 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.7886751 (checked to 3e-17 against the product law at K = 4, 6, 8), so the second moment is the correlation integral of the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 with this p. That auxiliary is exactly L^2-critical: the exponent governing an L^2 statement, log(p^2 + (1-p)^2)/log(2/3), equals 1 because p^2 + (1-p)^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p) = 2/3, equivalently the octave main-term exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2) is 0 - which is why the variance grows like a logarithm rather than a power. The consequence is favourable: a typical Err of order L sqrt(K), and R^{-0.70951} sqrt(log R) is still summable over octaves. The entropy-dimension ratio H(p)/log(3/2) = 1.2719 (against 1.7095 unbiased) is not the right comparison - the two exponents coincide only for the unbiased measure. The bound cannot be uniform in the window position: over a full period the median Err/L is -0.34, the 90th percentile +1.19 and the 99th +6.4, stable in K; the maximum grows like (4/3)^K (13.0 to 134.4 for K = 6..14, from windows meeting the peak at the origin, a trivial growth), and about 11 pct of all positions have Err > L at every K tried, while the octave position sits near -0.94. A proof must use where the octave sits.

 \abs{Z_j-Z_{j-1}}\leq H

\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{P}(Z_N-Z_0\geq t)
 \leq \exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2NH^2}\right).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:ricci-soft-threshold of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Work in the packetless subfiber and suppose the Ricci residual component
has no independently token-bearing hard resource covered by
(lem:ricci-internal-hard of the paper).  Resolve every internal hard
full-centered packet into all-Weyl and mixed children.  The all-Weyl
token-bearing children and, by
(lem:ricci-mixed-closed-hard of the paper), every nonzero mixed child fall
under that lemma.  Thus the retained soft family contains no packet
child.  Let $o$ be the number of unfused
$\mathsf S^\pm$ singleton supernodes and $v$ the total number of
$\mathsf V$ singleton supernodes in all maximal consecutive runs of the
Ricci component.  Put
\[
 \Delta_0=o+\frac v2.
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12n}$}
\]
If $\Delta_0\ge f_R$, where $f_R\in\{1,2\}$ is the number of root-hit
fundamental circuits, then this complete subfiber satisfies the shell
bound on the right of (eq:3.3.1w-12k of the paper).

body: [Thm higher-dims of arXiv:2411.14336, 'Finding the root in random nearest neighbor trees'] For the $d$-NN model with $d \in \mathbf{N}$, $d \geq 2$, for all $n \in \mathbf{N}$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a $O(n^2 + n(1/\varepsilon)^{1/(\log \log (1/\varepsilon))})$-time embedded root finding algorithm that returns a confidence set $H(\varepsilon,n)$ of size satisfying $|H(\varepsilon, n)| \leq \exp\bpar{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log\log(1/\varepsilon)} + d \log\log(1/\varepsilon)}$. Additionally, there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that it is information-theoretically impossible to provide a confidence set whose size satisfies $|H(\varepsilon, n)| \log \left( {|H(\varepsilon, n)|}{d^{-1/d}}\right) \leq c \log(1/\varepsilon)/d.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

STATUS: proof (unaudited); own-work draft. Jointly trained scalar head and factored attention p=kq have open positive-three-dimensional-measure inferior-selection basins for arbitrary n>=2 distinct two-token examples and every fixed eta>0. In the stated sign regions all parameters escape, factors are O(sqrt(log |v|)), loss tends to zero, and actual (v,k,q)-normalized margins are Gamma_-<Gamma_+. The complete finite stationary set is a saddle curve v=0,kq=p_bar, with one zero tangent and opposite-sign normal Hessian eigenvalues.

# Target 1: joint head, key and query training retains open inferior basins

Version 1. Proof unaudited. Own work; global novelty unestablished.

## Statement

Let n>=2, b_i,kappa_i>0 and 0<a_i<b_i. Set
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s),
L(v,k,q)=mean_i log(1+exp(-v h_i(kq))).
Train all three scalar parameters by simultaneous Euclidean GD, at any fixed eta>0.
Write r_min=min_i atanh(-a_i/b_i)/kappa_i<0.
The following nonempty open subsets of R^3 are forward invariant:

 B_-={v<0,k>0,q<0,kq<r_min},
 B_+={v>0,k>0,q>0}.

The simultaneous sign reversal (k,q)->(-k,-q) supplies two more invariant regions.
On B_-: v->-infinity, k->+infinity, q->-infinity, kq->-infinity,
L->0, and (v,k,q)/sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2)->(-1,0,0).
On B_+ the three coordinates tend to +infinity and the normalized limit is
(1,0,0). The normalized minimum signed margins, defined here as
min_i v h_i(kq)/sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2), tend respectively to
Gamma_-=min_i(b_i-a_i) and Gamma_+=min_i(b_i+a_i).
The largest attainable limiting normalized margin is Gamma_+; Gamma_+>Gamma_-.
Consequently the inferior basin has positive three-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
These are invariant-region results, not a classification of all initializations.

The two-token cross-attention and genuine first-token self-attention embeddings
in proofs/004 and 006 remain exact after replacing their attention parameter p
by kq. Thus the claim includes distinct examples and both labels.

## Exact updates and invariance

For s=kq put g_i=1/(1+exp(v h_i(s))),
F=mean g_i h_i(s), G=mean g_i h_i'(s)>0. The exact simultaneous updates are

 v_+=v+eta F, k_+=k+eta vqG, q_+=q+eta vkG.

In B_-, F<0, vq>0 and vk<0. Each sign is therefore preserved and the
product becomes more negative. In B_+ all increments are positive, since
s>0 and h_i(s)>a_i>0. No restriction on eta is needed.

Analyze either branch using positive variables u,w,r. On B_- take
u=-v,w=k,r=-q, x=wr=-s, t_i(x)=b_i tanh(kappa_i x)-a_i.
On B_+ take u=v,w=k,r=q,x=wr=s,t_i(x)=b_i tanh(kappa_i x)+a_i.
Both obey exactly

 Delta u=eta mean g_i t_i, w_+=w+delta r, r_+=r+delta w,
 delta=eta u mean g_i t_i', g_i=(1+exp(u t_i))^-1.

Here x,u,w,r increase, and t_i(x)>=c:=min_i t_i(x_0)>0.
Let H=max_i(a_i+b_i), M=max_i b_i kappa_i, kappa_0=min_i kappa_i.
All t_i<=H and t_i'<=4M exp(-2 kappa_0 x).

## Escape

If u remained bounded, u t_i<=u H would keep every g_i bounded below,
contradicting Delta u>=eta c mean g_i. Hence u->infinity.
If x remained bounded, min_i t_i' would have a positive lower bound d>0.
The exact product update is

 Delta x=delta(w^2+r^2)+delta^2 x.

Using w^2+r^2>=2x_0>0 and
delta/Delta u=u(mean g_i t_i')/(mean g_i t_i)>=u d/H,
we obtain Delta x>=2x_0 d u Delta u/H. The sum of u Delta u diverges
(already u>=u_0>0 and sum Delta u=infinity), contradicting bounded x.
Thus x->infinity, and the loss tends to zero.

## Factor growth is negligible relative to the head

This step is essential: it compares the margin in the actual three parameters,
not the collapsed (v,p) norm. Let D=w-r. The exact relation is
D_+=(1-delta)D. Since g_i<=exp(-c u),
0<delta<=eta M u exp(-c u)->0. Hence eventually delta<=1, and |D| is
bounded by a finite constant D_* (a finite earlier excursion is harmless).
Therefore w^2+r^2=2x+D^2<=2x+D_*^2.
Eventually delta<=1, so

 Delta x<=delta(3x+D_*^2),
 delta<=4 eta M u exp(-c u) exp(-2 kappa_0 x).

The function (3x+D_*^2)exp(-2 kappa_0 x) is bounded for x>=x_0>0.
Consequently Delta x->0, and eventually Delta x<=1. Also

 delta/Delta u<=4M u exp(-2 kappa_0 x)/c.

The mean value theorem now gives

 Delta exp(kappa_0 x)
 <=kappa_0 exp(kappa_0) exp(kappa_0 x) Delta x
 <=C (3x+D_*^2)exp(-kappa_0 x) u Delta u
 <=C' u Delta u.

Summing, using 2u Delta u<=Delta(u^2), yields
exp(kappa_0 x)<=C''(1+u^2). Thus x=O(log u), and
w^2+r^2=O(log u). In particular w/u,r/u->0. Since x->infinity and
|w-r| is bounded, both w,r tend to infinity. This proves every stated
coordinate and normalized limit.

## Margin optimality and positive measure

Endpoint limits give Gamma_+ and Gamma_-. For any parameters, let
N=sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2). If v>=0, choose an index minimizing a_i+b_i:
min_i v h_i/N<=Gamma_+. If v<0, choose an index minimizing b_i-a_i:
min_i v h_i/N<=Gamma_-. These inequalities remain valid when that
chosen signed prediction is negative. B_+ attains the larger endpoint
asymptotically. Gamma_+>=Gamma_-+2 min_i a_i>Gamma_-.
B_- is nonempty and open; for example take v=-1,k=R,q=-R with
R^2>-r_min. A sufficiently small ball around that point lies in B_-.

## Finite stationary set (flow stability, separate from the GD basin claim)

The only finite stationary points are v=0, kq=p_bar, where
mean_i h_i(p_bar)=0. Indeed v!=0 would force k=q=0 from the factor
gradients, but F(v,0)=mean_i a_i/(1+exp(v a_i))>0.
At v=0 the remaining condition is exactly the displayed mean root.
It is negative, so k,q are nonzero. Put A=mean_i h_i(p_bar)^2/4>=0,
B=mean_i h_i'(p_bar)/2>0. The loss Hessian is

 [[A,-Bq,-Bk],[-Bq,0,0],[-Bk,0,0]].

It has one zero tangent eigenvalue and eigenvalues
(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2(k^2+q^2)))/2 of opposite sign. Thus each point
on this critical curve is a saddle with one attracting and one repelling
normal direction for gradient flow. This does not assert a global
stable-manifold classification or small-step GD stability uniformly along
the noncompact curve.

Tarzanagh et al., arXiv:2308.16898, PDF pp.3-4 defines KQ-ERM with

regularization path and nuclear-norm bias. Sheen et al., arXiv:2403.08699,
source sections/preliminariesAr.tex line 17 likewise fixes the linear
prediction head; its main diagonal/general theorems concern gradient flow
and exponential loss. Neither checked scope is this joint-head logistic
arbitrary-step invariant-region statement. This is a bounded comparison,
not a claim that no such result exists elsewhere. Factor-balance identities
and nuclear-norm bias are prior work, not claimed as discoveries here.
The result does not cover matrices, multiple heads, or the full R^3 basin partition.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.14948, 'Graph alignment in sparse inhomogeneous models via self-overlap'] Let $(K_1, K_2)$ be a pair of random graphs, following a joint law $\mu$. The graph alignment problem is the following: a permutation $\sigma^* \in \Sym_n$ is chosen uniformly at random, independently from $K_1, K_2$; from the observation of the graphs $(G, H) = ((\sigma^*)^{-1}(K_1), K_2)$, we wish to recover the matching $\sigma^*$.

    In this setting, we refer to $(G, H)$ as a \textbf{correlated graph system}.

[Lemma LEM:hyp of arXiv:2412.09790, 'Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures'] Let $\left\{g_n\right\}_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ be a sequence of independent standard real-valued Gaussian
random variables. Given $k\in \mathbb{N}$, let $\left\{P_j\right\}_{j\in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of polynomials in 
$\bar{g}=\left\{g_n\right\}_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ of degree at most $k$. Then, for any finite $p\ge 1$, we have
\begin{align*}
\bigg\|\sum_{j\in \mathbb{N}}P_j(\bar{g})\bigg\|_{L^p(\Omega)}
\le (p-1)^{\frac{k}{2}}\bigg\|\sum_{j\in \mathbb{N}}P_j(\bar{g})\bigg\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem: colsum of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $n\geq 2$, $m \geq 1$, $\beta\geq 4$, and $1\leq d\le n/2$.  
      Let $M$ be an $m \times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ ones. Given $\tau>0$, consider the event
    \[
    \mathcal{E}_{(lem: colsum of the paper)}=\mathcal{E}_{(lem: colsum of the paper)}(\tau):=\set{M=\{M_{ij}\}_{i \in [m],j \in [n]}: \sum_{i=1}^{m} M_{ij}\le \frac{(1+\tau) md}{n} \ \mbox{ for every } j\le n}.
    \]
    Then for $\tau=\max{\big\{e^2, \frac{\beta n\log m}{md}\big\}}$,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}( \mathcal{E}_{(lem: colsum of the paper)})\ge 1-n\cdot m^{-\beta},
    \]   
and for $0 < \tau < 1$,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}( \mathcal{E}_{(lem: colsum of the paper)})\ge 1-n\exp\left(-\frac{md\tau^2}{3n}\right).
    \]

[Theorem 2 (Spectral zero pattern) of arXiv:2609.02590, 'Directional Optimal Sub-Gamma Scales for Infinitely Divisible Laws'] The directional scales satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \cplus(X)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nu((0,\infty))=0,
 \qquad
 \cminus(X)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nu((-\infty,0))=0.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, $\cplus(X)=\cminus(X)=0$ if and only if $X$ is Gaussian with
variance $V$.

body:
[Theorem 10 (max-domain of attraction of the constructed max-id process) of arXiv:2604.11434, 'Maxima of stationary systems of randomly time-changed L\'evy particles'] Let $\alpha$ be a mass function satisfying Assumption~\ref{asu:alpha},
  let
$(L_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a L\'evy process
satisfying Assumption~\ref{asu:levy}, and
    let $(X_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be the time-changed process in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:existence_tcp}.
    Consider the max-id process $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ defined by
\begin{align*}
  Z_t
  \ = \
  \max
  \mathfrak{P}_t
  \left(
  (X_t)_{t\ge 0}, \alpha(x)\exp(-x)\mathrm{d}x
  \right)
  \,,
\end{align*}
let
\begin{align*}
    \zeta_n(t)
    \ := \
    \max_{k=1,\ldots,n} Z_t^{(k)} - \log(n)
    \,,
    \qquad n\in\NN
    \,,
  \end{align*}
  where $((Z_t^{(k)})_{t\ge 0})_{k=1,\ldots,n}$ are i.i.d.~copies of $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$, and let
\begin{align*}
    \zeta_L(t)
    \ := \
    \max \mathfrak{P}_t((L_t)_{t\ge 0},\exp(-x)\mathrm{d}x)
    \,.
  \end{align*}
  Then $\zeta_n$ converges weakly to $\zeta_L$ in f.d.d.
  If, furthermore, $(L_t)_{t\ge 0}$ has continuous paths,
  then convergence holds in $\mathbb{D}([0,\infty))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: max-domain of attraction of the constructed max-id process

body:
Let K be a compact Hausdorff space and let A be a subalgebra of C(K, R), the algebra of real-valued continuous functions on K with the supremum norm, such that A contains the constant functions and separates points (for every pair of distinct points x, y in K there is f in A with f(x) different from f(y)). Then A is dense in C(K, R): every continuous real function on K is a uniform limit of elements of A. Complex version: a subalgebra of C(K, C) containing the constants, separating points, and closed under complex conjugation is dense in C(K, C). The classical Weierstrass approximation theorem (polynomials are dense in C([a,b], R)) is the special case A = polynomials on K = [a,b].

Let B be the uniform closure of A; B is again an algebra containing constants and separating points. Step 1: B is closed under absolute value. Hence B is a lattice: max(f, g) = (f + g + |f - g|)/2 and min(f, g) = (f + g - |f - g|)/2 lie in B. Step 2: two-point interpolation. For distinct x, y and prescribed real values a, b, separation plus constants give h in A with h(x) = a, h(y) = b (affinely rescale a separating function). Step 3: let g in C(K, R) and epsilon > 0. Fixing x, the open sets {z : f_(x,y)(z) < g(z) + epsilon}, indexed by y, cover K (y lies in its own set); take a finite subcover and let f_x = min of the corresponding f_(x,y); then f_x < g + epsilon everywhere and f_x(x) = g(x). The open sets {z : f_x(z) > g(z) - epsilon} cover K; a finite subcover and f = max of the corresponding f_x give |f - g| < epsilon with f in B (lattice operations, finitely many). Own-work draft extracted from C010 version 2 section 7; proof (unaudited), not a novelty claim. Let a finite-dimensional parameter space have a norm D dominated by sqrt(3) times a Hilbert norm H. Two adapted recurrences obey theta_(k+1)=theta_k-eta_k[G(theta_k)+xi_k], with a common deterministic nonnegative step sequence of total at most T. Both recurrences remain in a domain where D(G(theta)-G(theta'))<=kappa omega(D(theta-theta')), omega(0)=0, omega(s)=s log(e/s) for 0<s<=1, and omega(s)=1 for s>=1. Each noise is centered conditional on the joint past filtration and has conditional H second moment at most G0^2; initializations and any selected relabeling are in that past. Cross-run noise independence is unnecessary if these conditional statements hold. Suppose delta=E[D(theta_0-theta'_0)]+2sqrt(3)G0 sqrt(sum eta_k^2)<=1. Summing the updates first gives accumulated martingales M_n=sum_{k<n}eta_k xi_k with E||M_n||_H<=G0 sqrt(sum eta_k^2). Norm convexity and omega concavity then give e_n<=delta+kappa sum_{k<n}eta_k omega(e_k), where e_n=E D(theta_n-theta'_n). Discrete Bihari comparison yields e_K<=3(1+kappa T)delta^(exp(-kappa T)). This uses the integrated martingale and a concave drift modulus; it requires neither summing expected absolute one-step noises nor a Hilbert Lipschitz bound on G. The source gives this argument on an initialization-measurable good event, where the same proof applies to conditional expectations. Finite martingale checks are validation only, not a quantified theorem certificate or independent audit.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the uniform law of $[a,b]$, its even normalized central moments are given by the following formula,
$$M_k''=\frac{3^{k/2}}{k+1}$$
with the small order even normalized central moments being as follows:
$$M_2''=1\quad,\quad 
M_4''=\frac{9}{5}\quad,\quad
M_6''=\frac{27}{7}\quad,\quad\ldots$$
As for the odd normalized central moments, these all vanish.

Vardi, Yehudai and Shamir, Theorem 6.2 (arXiv:2110.03187v1, p.9): Let n>=4, let d,C be positive integers, and let x_1,...,x_n in R^d have Euclidean norms <=r and pairwise Euclidean distances >=delta>0, with labels y_i in {1,...,C}. Use normalized bounds r>=1 and delta<=1. Put R=d*n*C*r/delta and h=log_2 R. For every integer 2<=s<=floor(sqrt(n)), there is a feedforward ReLU network that exactly memorizes all labels, has width O(1), depth O(n*h*sqrt(log_2 s)/s), and at most O(d+n*h*sqrt(log_2 s)/s) nonzero parameters. The bit precision is at most a constant times s*h/sqrt(log_2 s). The parameter s is the tuning parameter called B in the source; it is not the achieved bit budget. Big-O constants are unspecified. Appendix C p.20 prints a weaker precision estimate O(s*sqrt(log_2 s)*h); the theorem display on p.9 and the stage bounds on p.17 give the denominator used here.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Suppose that $\zeta_j, 1\le j\le n$ are martingale differences with respect to the filtration $\FF_j, 0\le j\le n$. Assume that $\sigma_j^2, 1\le j\le n$ are non-decreasing positive reals bounded by 1 with
$\ev[\zeta_j^2|\FF_{j-1} ]\le \sigma_j^2$.
Introduce the notations
\begin{align*}
    M(k_1,k_2)=\sum_{j=k_1+1}^{k_2} \zeta_j, \qquad \sigma(k_1,k_2)^2=\sum_{j=k_1+1}^{k_2} \sigma_j^2, \qquad 0\le k_1<k_2\le n. 
\end{align*}
For $x\ge 0$ let 
\[
\gamma(x)=\max(x, x^{1/2}). 
\]
Then for $c$ large enough we have 
\begin{align*}
   & \pr\left(|M(k_1,k_2)|\ge c \cdot \gamma(\sigma(k_1,k_2))
   \log\big(4+\tfrac{\sigma^2(0,k_1)}{\sigma^2(k_1,k_2)}+3|\log\sigma(k_1,k_2)|\big)\text{ for some $0\le k_1<k_2\le n$}\right)\\&\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \le 2^{-\frac{c}{50}}+\pr(|\zeta_j|> \sigma_j^{1/2} \text{ for some } 1\le j\le n).
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2607.08536

Let q be a prime power, U uniform on F_q^m, and a_1, ..., a_r in F_q^m. For an index set I, the forms (a_i . U)_{i in I} are uniform on F_q^|I| (equivalently, mutually independent with each a_i . U uniform on F_q) if and only if the indexed family (a_i)_{i in I} is linearly independent, a repeated vector counting as a dependence. Consequently, for every integer k >= 1, the forms are k-wise independent with each form uniform on F_q if and only if every indexed subfamily of at most k coefficient vectors is linearly independent. Without uniformity the criterion is different: (a_i . U)_{i in I} is mutually independent if and only if the nonzero vectors among (a_i)_{i in I} are linearly independent. A zero vector gives the constant 0, independent of everything but not uniform: for q = 2 and m = 1 the rows 0 and 1 give (0, U), which is independent although the rows have rank 1.

the coefficient vectors form an indexed family, repeats allowed

body: [Definition 3 (Path, Circuit) of arXiv:1710.10644, 'Percolation without FKG'] A path on Λ is a finite sequence γ = (γ0, . . . , γn) of vertices such that for every i < n, γi is adjacent to γi+1; n is the length of γ, denoted by |γ|, γ0 is its starting point, and γn is its endpoint. A simple path is a path with pairwise distinct vertices. The inner part of γ is the set ˚γ := {γk : 0 < k < |γ|}. A circuit is a simple path such that its endpoint is adjacent to its starting point.

body:
[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.01419, 'A model of opinion dynamics evolving via a preferential attachment mechanism involving mul'] Consider the stochastic approximation process $\{Z_{n}\}$, with $Z_{n}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, given by
\begin{equation}
Z_{n+1}=Z_{n}+a_{n+1}\left\{F(Z_{n})+\Delta M_{n+1}+\delta_{n}\right\} \text{ for }n\in\mathbb{N}_{0},
\end{equation}
with prescribed $Z_{0}$ and the following assumptions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(B\arabic*), ref=B\arabic*]
\item  the map $F:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is Lipschitz,
\item  the step-size sequence $\{a_{n}\}$, of positive scalars, satisfies $\sum_{n}a_{n}=\infty$ and $\sum_{n}a_{n}^{2}<\infty$,
\item  the sequence $\{\Delta M_{n+1}\}$ is a martingale difference sequence with respect to the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{n+1}\}$, where $\mathcal{F}_{n}$ is the $\sigma$-field consisting of all information about the process up to and including epoch $n$, and $\{\delta_{n}\}$ is a sequence of additional error terms adapted to $\{\mathcal{F}_{n}\}$, such that $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a_{i+1}(\Delta M_{i+1}+\delta_{i})$ converges almost surely as $n\rightarrow\infty$, 
\item  and $\sup\{||Z_{n}||:n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\}<\infty$ almost surely, where $||\cdot||$ indicates the usual Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, almost surely, $\{Z_{n}\}$ converges to a (possibly sample path dependent) compact connected internally chain transitive invariant set corresponding to the autonomous ODE $\dot{x}(t)=F(x(t))$ for $t\geqslant 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.01419

    \begin{enumerate}

    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:original version of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},V,T)$ be a capacity preserving system, where $V$ is an upper probability. Then $V$ is ergodic with respect to $T$ if and only if for any $f\in B(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$, there exists a unique $c_f\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
	$$
	\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} f(T^{i} \omega)=c_f \text{ for }V\text{-a.s. }\omega\in\Omega.  
	$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:original version of arXiv:2411.00663

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem UniformFCLT-general of arXiv:2412.01635, 'On the Weak Convergence of the Function-Indexed Sequential Empirical Process and its Smoot'] (Asymptotic equicontinuity - general case)\\
Let $\nu > 2$ and let $\rho$ be a semimetric on $\mathcal F$. Assume the following conditions to hold: 	
\begin{enumerate}[ref = \arabic*]
\item  There exists $g: \mathbb N \times (0, \infty) \to \mathbb R$ such that for each $n \in \mathbb N$, $\delta > 0$, it holds 
\begin{equation}
\EOuter{ \norm{  S_{n,i,j} }_{\mathcal F_\delta}^\nu } \leq g^{\frac{\nu}{2}}(j-i+1, \delta), ~ \forall ~ 1 \leq i \leq j \leq n,
\end{equation}
and there is a universal index $Q_g \in [1,2^{1-2/\nu})$ such that for each $\delta > 0,$ the pair $(\nu/2, g(.,\delta))$ fulfills condition (equation MSS-ConditionM of the paper) with index $Q_g$. 

\item  There exists $h: \mathbb N \to \mathbb R$ such that for each $n \in \mathbb N$, it holds 
\begin{equation}
\EOuter{ \norm{ S_{n,i,j} }_{\mathcal F}^\nu } \leq h^{\frac{\nu}{2}}(j-i+1), ~ \forall ~ 1 \leq i \leq j \leq n,
\end{equation}
and the pair $(\nu/2, h)$ fulfills condition (equation MSS-ConditionM of the paper) with index $Q_h \in [1,2^{1-2/\nu})$.

\item  It holds $$\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{g(n,\delta)}{n} = 0.$$	

\item  There exists a constant $C_h \geq 0$ such that for each $0 < \varepsilon  \leq 1,$ it holds $$ \limsup_{n \to \infty}  \frac{h(\left\lfloor n \varepsilon \right\rfloor)}{n}  \leq C_h \varepsilon $$ (with the convention $h(0) = 0$). 
\end{enumerate}
Then (equation DEF:AEC of the paper) holds for $\tau((s,f),(t,g)) = |s-t| + \rho(f,g).$	If, in addition, $(\mathcal F, \rho)$ is totally bounded, then fidi-convergence of $\mathbb Z_n$ implies weak convergence in $\ell^{\infty}([0,1] \times \mathcal F)$.
title: Theorem UniformFCLT-general of arXiv:2412.01635

body: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.30 is answered NO for every b >= 1. For each b >= 1 and s >= 2b there is a four-state reversible chain X = (Y, V), Y a slow two-state chain whose rare state carries g = b and V a fast sign, with relaxation time tau_2 = 1 and a standardized g with ||g||_inf = b, such that P_pi(S_s <= 0) >= 1 - 4/s. At t = s the Kolmogorov distance of the normalized additive functional from N(0,1) is at least 1/2 - 4/s under any normalization, so no bound psi(b, t/tau_2) -> 0 exists. The normalized sum does tend to 0 in probability; a rare excursion carries its second moment (W^2 is not uniformly integrable). This replaces the 8 Sep claim, which fixed ||g||_inf = 2 and said the normalized sum does not vanish in probability. Posted 13 Oct 2026 as github.com/yspennstate/relaxation-time-normal-approximation 40395f2; outside audit owed.

body: In differential geometry, a Riemannian manifold (or Riemann space) is a geometric space on which many geometric notions such as distance, angles, length, volume, and curvature are defined. Euclidean space, the $n$ -sphere, hyperbolic space, and smooth surfaces in three-dimensional space, such as ellipsoids and paraboloids, are all examples of Riemannian manifolds. Riemannian manifolds take their name from German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, who first conceptualized them in 1854.

body: In algebra, the Wedderburn–Artin theorem is a classification theorem for semisimple rings and semisimple algebras. The theorem states that a(n Artinian) semisimple ring R is isomorphic to the product of finitely many ni-by-ni matrix rings over division rings Di, for some integers ni, both of which are uniquely determined up to permutation of the index i. In particular, any simple left or right Artinian ring is isomorphic to an n-by-n matrix ring over a division ring D, where both n and D are uniquely determined.
title: Wedderburn–Artin theorem

body: [Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $f$ be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ with nonnegative coefficients.  Then $f$ is Lorentzian if and only if $\Supp(f)$ is $M$-convex and every derivative $\partial^\beta f$, $|\beta|=d-2$, has a Hessian with at most one positive eigenvalue. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

STATUS: independently checked proof (exact C056v1, urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS20 Oct17:12). For the exact critical Gaussian tanh scalar chain with fixed K0>0 and Y=2L*K_L, let W solve dW=(2tW+2)ds+sqrt(2t)W dB from0 on[0,1], t=L/n, g_j,s=P_(1-s)^t(2/w)^j, D_j=g_j,0 prime(0). Let C0=lim_m[1/q_m-2m+(5/6)logm] for the deterministic tanh variance recursion. With C^t=(2t^2w-6t-5/(3w))D+(3t^2w^2-2tw)D^2+(2/3)t^2w^3D^3, define R_j=D_j*C0+integral_0^1{E[(C^t g_j,s)(W_s)]+(5/6)D_j/s}ds. The improper integral is absolutely convergent. E Y^j=m_j(t)+(5j/12)J_j(t)logL/L+R_j(t,K0)/L+o(1/L), uniformly as L grows over integers n with L/n<=c, fixed c and j. Cumulant coefficient is sum_j partial_j P_k(m)R_j. Limits: L,n joint first, continuum overlap cutoff delta->0 second, fixed-layer cutoff m->infinity last. At t=0, R_j=-j*C0/2. For linear reciprocal W, R_w=e^(2t)[C0+2t-4(1-e^(-2t))-(5/6)int_0^t(e^(-2r)m1(r)-1)/r dr]. Definitions: A_t=int_0^1 exp(tr+sqrt(2t)B_r)dr,H_t=exp(t+sqrt(2t)B_1),m_j=E A_t^-j,J_j=E[H_t A_t^(-j-1)] using the same Brownian path. q0=K0,q_(r+1)=E tanh(sqrt(q_r)Z)^2 for standard Gaussian Z. Assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian rows/layers, weight variance1/n, zero bias, unshaped tanh, fixed K0>0, fixed finite cumulant order and finite c. Remainder uniform for L->infinity and 0<L/n<=c; does not assert relative accuracy at fixed L. Scope: Independent reviewer audit pending, especially matched overlap and improved late large-q remainder. Supplies uniform little-o1/L only; no explicit numerical rate or all-orders width expansion. At nonlattice times L=floor(nt0), evaluate at t=L/n or retain the order1/n fractional-part correction; do not silently replace t by t0. Audit note: C053/C055/C056v1 PASS receipts supersede the historical pending-review metadata in the reproduced draft. No all-orders expansion or computable remainder rate is claimed.
Independent standard Gaussian rows/layers, weight variance1/n, zero bias, unshaped tanh, fixed K0>0, fixed finite cumulant order and finite c. Remainder uniform for L->infinity and 0<L/n<=c; does not assert relative accuracy at fixed L.
