Own-work auxiliary proof draft (unaudited); no novelty priority claimed. Fix any oracle O. Let P_L be given by a uniform polynomial-time O-relative evaluator of nonnegative rational weights with polynomial numerator/denominator bit bounds and positive normalizer. Suppose a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR proposal R_L has polynomial next-bit precision and P_L(x)<=D(L)R_L(x) pointwise, for an integer-valued polynomial D>=1. For every fixed positive integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR Q_L with KL(P_L||Q_L)<L^(-c). Conditional importance sampling with K=(1024 D L^(2c+2))^2 samples per position, globally shared random tapes, and one dyadic normalizer-scale exponent suffices; smoothing and output rounding bound KL by (47/120)L^(-c). Exact normalization, a sampler for P and distributional inversion are not assumed. The domination premise itself also yields nonuniform inverse-polynomial-TV sampling by bounded rejection. No common oracle with NP circuit hardness and domination proposals for all efficiently weighted laws has been constructed. This does not settle Target 2 or assert that the premise follows from IR2.
Uniform polynomial-time O-relative rational weight evaluator; known polynomial numerator/denominator bit bound; Z_L>0
Polynomial-size nonuniform O-relative AR proposal with polynomial dyadic precision and pointwise P_L<=D(L)R_L for an integer polynomial D>=1
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7f/7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e6f8938fd0964f6bdec71311b16a459f94b9a6dcb22372c6c194227f52f9e1ff","bundle_entry_key":"importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","bundle_id":"population.t410-importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"autoregressive distributions; importance sampling; oracle computational complexity; forward KL; nonuniform circuits","draft":"w739/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Polynomial domination by an AR proposal suffices for forward-KL approximation

T410-w739-C012 v1. Kind: auxiliary sufficient-condition lemma. Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). Own-work draft; no novelty priority claimed.
This is an alternative sufficient condition, not a construction of the target oracle.

## Statement and unpaid obligation

Fix an oracle O. For each integer L>=1 let P_L(x)=w_L(x)/Z_L on
{0,1}^L. The nonnegative rational weights w_L are uniformly polynomial-time
computable relative to O, not all zero, and their numerator and positive
denominator have bit lengths at most a known polynomial b(L).

Assume a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive proposal R_L:
its next-bit probabilities are exactly evaluable dyadics with common
precision B(L), a polynomial. Assume further that

    P_L(x) <= D(L) R_L(x) for every x,                         (1)

where D>=1 is an integer-valued polynomial. Then for each fixed positive
integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive Q_L
whose next-bit probabilities are dyadic and

    KL(P_L || Q_L) <= (47/120) L^(-c) < L^(-c).              (2)

Natural logarithms are used. All circuits use the same oracle O. Their
size exponent may depend on c and on the polynomial bounds. The uniform
weight evaluator is a single algorithm; the proposal and resulting Q may
have length-dependent advice. For any fixed positive real requested
exponent one can instead use its integer ceiling.

The hardest unpaid step for Target 2 is to construct ONE oracle with
NP^O not contained in P^O/poly and, for EVERY efficient-weight law, a
proposal satisfying (1). This proof supplies no such oracle or universal
proposal. It does not derive (1) from the reported IR2 result, assert
equivalence with C003's sampler/inverter criterion, or settle Target 2.

## 1. Only a short scale advice is needed

The weight representation implies 2^(-b)<=Z_L<=2^(b+L). Choose the
integer a=ceil(log_2 Z_L) as nonuniform advice and set A=2^a. Then

    Z_L <= A <= 2 Z_L,       z:=Z_L/A belongs to [1/2,1].

The signed exponent a uses O(log(b+L+1)) bits; the rational A itself has
polynomial representation length. We do NOT assume the exact rational Z
has polynomial bit length: arbitrary rational weight denominators need
not share a small common denominator.

For R(x)>0 put h(x)=w(x)/(A R(x)); set h=0 when R(x)=0. Domination
ensures P(x)=w(x)=0 on the latter set. Consequently

    0 <= h(x) <= D,          E_R h = z.

Computing h takes polynomial-size exact rational arithmetic: R(x) is a
product of L polynomial-bit dyadics, and w,A have polynomial bit length.
Hereafter L subscripts are omitted.

## 2. Conditional importance estimates and change of measure

For a prefix s of length i<L with R(s)>0, define

    a_s=E_R[h(X)|s],    b_s=E_R[h(X) 1{X_(i+1)=1}|s].

Then P(s)=R(s)a_s/z. When P(s)>0 the true next-bit probability is
p_s=b_s/a_s. Draw K independent suffix samples from R(.|s). This is an
exact ancestral sampler: each next-bit dyadic of precision B uses B fair
bits, so at most LB random bits per sample. Let ahat_s,bhat_s be the
sample means of h and h times the next-bit indicator. Define

    g_s=bhat_s/ahat_s if ahat_s>0; otherwise g_s=1/2.

We always have 0<=g_s<=1 and ahat_s*g_s=bhat_s, including the zero
denominator case because nonnegative h forces bhat_s=0 there. Thus

    a_s |g_s-p_s| <= |a_s-ahat_s|+|b_s-bhat_s|.             (3)

This follows by writing a_s*g_s-b_s as
(a_s-ahat_s)*g_s+(bhat_s-b_s). Each sample variable lies in [0,D], so
variance of each mean is at most D^2/K. By Cauchy-Schwarz its mean
absolute error is at most D/sqrt(K). Multiply (3) by R(s)/z and sum over
prefixes with P(s)>0. Since their R masses sum to at most one and z>=1/2,

    sum_s P(s) E |g_s-p_s| <= 4D/sqrt(K)                   (4)

at every position. Prefixes of zero P mass contribute zero. At an
R-null prefix output 1/2 directly; it is P-null by (1).

No sample from P, normalizer computation, or distributional inversion
was used. In particular we did not require an accuracy guarantee at
each one of exponentially many prefixes.

## 3. One polynomial table of shared tapes

At each position select K independent tapes of length LB. Use these
SAME tapes to evaluate the conditional sampler at every prefix of that
length. For each FIXED prefix its K samples have exactly the independent
law used above. Evaluations at different prefixes may be correlated;
only linearity of expectation over prefixes is used in (4).

There are L*K*L*B advice bits, not a tape table indexed by all prefixes.
For any fixed advice table, evaluation runs K ancestral samplers and
computes their exact rational sample means. Adding K polynomial-bit
rationals can increase bit length by at most a polynomial factor K;
division and the other arithmetic therefore have polynomial circuits.
This remains true when the proposal itself has nonuniform advice.

## 4. Smoothing, KL, and explicit sample count

Write eta=L^(-c), epsilon=eta/(16L), and choose the perfect square

    K = (1024 D L^(2c+2))^2.

This is polynomial for fixed c. Let q_s=epsilon+(1-2epsilon)g_s at
R-positive prefixes, so q_s is in [epsilon,1-epsilon]. Also

    |p_s-q_s| <= |p_s-g_s|+epsilon,
    (p_s-q_s)^2 <= 2|p_s-g_s|+2epsilon^2.

For Bernoulli parameters p in [0,1], q in (0,1), the inequality
log t<=t-1, applied to each nonzero P term, gives

    kl(p||q) <= (p-q)^2/[q(1-q)].                          (5)

The same formula holds at p=0,1 by the zero-mass convention. Chain rule
for forward KL, (4), and (5) yield

    E KL(P||Q) <= [8DL/sqrt(K)+2L epsilon^2]
                         /[epsilon(1-epsilon)].          (6)

Here sqrt(K)=64DL/(eta epsilon). Each of the two terms in (6) equals
eta/[8(1-epsilon)]. Since epsilon<=1/16, their sum is at most
(4/15)eta. This calculation averages over a finite, polynomial-length
random table, not over independent conditional errors along a P path.

## 5. Polynomial-bit dyadic outputs

Choose an integer t with Delta=2^(-t)<=eta epsilon/(16L), for example
t=ceil(log_2(256 L^(2c+2))). Replace q_s by

    qhat_s = floor(2^t q_s)/2^t.

Then |qhat_s-q_s|<=Delta and qhat_s>=epsilon/2, while both complementary
probabilities are at least epsilon/2. The derivative of log on this
range is at most 2/epsilon. For every fixed random table, each next-bit
log probability changes in absolute value by at most 2Delta/epsilon.
The chain rule therefore gives

    KL(P||Qhat) <= KL(P||Q)+2L Delta/epsilon
                <= KL(P||Q)+eta/8.

Use qhat=1/2 at R-null prefixes. Averaging shows

    E KL(P||Qhat) <= (4/15+1/8)eta = (47/120)eta.

Some single finite table has loss at most this average. Fix it as advice.
The resulting Qhat is a normalized AR law with polynomial-size oracle
circuits and t-bit dyadic next probabilities. This proves (2).

## Scope and validation

The proposal premise already implies NONUNIFORM approximate sampling of
P, although the proof above does not invoke such a sampler. Indeed draw
X from R and accept it with probability h(X)/D, using a fresh uniform
number in [0,1]. The acceptance probability is z/D>=1/(2D), and the
accepted law is exactly P. Rational acceptance probabilities can instead
be rounded DOWN to dyadics of mesh delta. The acceptance probability
decreases by at most delta and the accepted law changes in total
variation by at most 2D delta, provided delta<=1/(4D): if v(x) is the
unnormalized accepted mass and v'(x)<=v(x), their missing total mass e
is at most delta, and TV(v/alpha,v'/(alpha-e))<=e/alpha<=2D delta.
The rounded success probability is at least 1/(4D). Truncating after
T independent proposals adds at most (1-1/(4D))^T to the TV error.
For a requested inverse-polynomial error rho, choose dyadic
delta<=rho/(4D) and T>=4D ln(2/rho). Thus a strict polynomial-time
NONUNIFORM dyadic sampler with TV error at most rho follows. Its
normalizer-scale advice and the proposal advice need not be uniform.
This implication is an explicit limitation of the sufficient condition,
not a contradiction to it or a uniform sampling theorem for the oracle.

This proof is a sufficient-condition derivation, not a novelty claim or
an independently checked proof. Finite rational diagnostics check (3),
the prefix change-of-measure identity, and the constants, with an omitted-
denominator negative control. They do not prove the asymptotic theorem
by enumeration. No enormous K sample run is proposed or performed.
The condition (1) must be established before applying this to any
particular oracle or weight family. Target 1 C001 v2 remains subject to
independent review; Target 2 remains OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:cd6159c155b54a445d85ded8bfe2169b8fbff887b41d8a66fa0cb61f5b912613","revision_digest":"sha256:f19892a156489aea3c44cdeab77ef7112d4b9e56b7b483fe2d21b6bdf47d45f1","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C012-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T22:53:13.841333+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

\sigma_n^2(\lambda) :=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_X\otimes \mathbb{P}}\left[\left(\lambda \cdot Z_n\right)^2\right] \geq \kappa \sum_{i=0}^{q-1} \lambda_i^2 .
\]

AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. For each epsilon in (0,1), delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon) is the largest delta in (0,1] such that the following implication holds for every finite forest G, independent Bernoulli edge probabilities in [0,1], vertices o,b and nonempty relay set A: if P(o connects to A)>1-delta and P(a connects to b)>1-delta for all a in A, then P(o connects to b)>1-epsilon. A two-edge path rules out every larger delta, so delta_star is also a necessary upper bound on any proposed all-finite-graph modulus. Its sufficiency for arbitrary cyclic graphs is not asserted.

[Theorem 36 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Assume that the family of vector fields \( \{V_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^d \) is equiregular and satisfies Hypotheses \ref{h1} and \ref{1.2}. Let \( Y \) be the solution to equation \eqref{density1}, driven by a \( d \)-dimensional fractional Brownian motion \( B \) with Hurst parameter \( H \in \left(\frac{1}{4}, 1\right) \). Then, for any fixed real numbers \( 0 < a < b \), \( M > 0 \), \( \eta_1 > 0 \), and \( 0 < \eta_2 < 1/H \), there exist strictly positive constants
\[
C_1 = C_1(a, b, V, H, M, n, \eta_1, Q), \quad C_2 = C_2(a, b, V, H, M, n, \eta_2, Q)
\]
such that for all compact sets \( A \subset B_d(o,M) \),
\begin{equation}
C_2 \, \mathrm{Cap}_{Q - 1/H + \eta_2}(A)
\ \leqslant\
\mathbb{P}(Y([a,b]) \cap A \neq \emptyset)
\ \leqslant\
C_1 \, \mathrm{Cap}_{Q - 1/H - \eta_1}(A),
\end{equation}
where \( Q \) is the homogeneous dimension defined in Definition~\ref{defofhomodim}. In particular, if $Q=N$, then $\eta_2$ can be chosen to be $0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 36 of arXiv:2512.07202

[Proposition 201 (Identification of the most difficult error terms in the commuted wave equations) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\velocityarray \eqdef (v^1,v^2,v^3)$ 
be solutions to the covariant wave equations \eqref{E:COVARIANTWAVEEQUATIONSWAVEVARIABLES}. We denote the product of $\upmu$ and the RHS of the covariant wave equation satisfied by 
$v^i$ by $\mathfrak{G}_{i}$, 
i.e., 
$\upmu \Box_{\gfour} v^i = \mathfrak{G}_{i}$. \begin{subequations}  
\begin{align} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tanderY^{N-1} \Lunit v^i) 
& 
= 
\angrmd^{\sharp} v^i  \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tanderY^{N-1} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
+ 
\tanderY^{N-1} \Lunit \mathfrak{G}_{i} 
+ 
\HarmlessWave{N},	
	\\
\begin{split} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tanderY^{N-1}\Yvf{A} v^i) 
& 
= 
(\muX v^i)  \tanderY^{N-1} \Yvf{A} \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi 
+ 
(\Speed^{-2} X^A) \angrmd^{\sharp} v^i \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tanderY^{N-1} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
\\
& \ \
+ 
\tanderY^{N-1}\Yvf{A} \mathfrak{G}_{i} 
+ 
\HarmlessWave{N}. 
\end{split}
\end{align}Moreover, if $1 \leq N \leq \Ntop$ and $\tander^N$
denotes any order $N$ string of $\mathcal{P}_u$-tangent commutator
other than the ones appearing on LHSs~\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVELFIRSTTHENALLYS}--\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVEALLYS},
(i.e., if $\tander^N$ features at least two copies of $\Lunit$ or only a single $\Lunit$ but does not act first like it does in
\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVELFIRSTTHENALLYS}), 
then $\tander^N v^i$ obeys the following wave equation:
\begin{align} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tander^N v^i) 
	& = 
	\tander^N \mathfrak{G}_i
	+ 
	\HarmlessWave{N}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations}

[Definition1 Defbad of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] Fix $A,a > 0$ and $t \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p}^n}(n,g_n)$. Let $i \in \{1,\cdots,\ell_n\}$ and $e \in \partial_i t$. Fix a peeling algorithm $\mathcal{A}$. Fix $j \ge 0$ and assume that $\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e)$ is a planar triangulation with one hole. We say that step $j+1$ is $\mathbf{BAD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$ (see Figure~(badcases of the paper)) if it satisfies one of the conditions below:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $\mathcal{L}_k^{\mathrm{nsep}}$ or $\mathcal{R}_k^{\mathrm{nsep}}$ with $k \in \{0,\cdots,A-1\}$.
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $\mathcal{L}_k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{R}_k^{\mathrm{sep}}$) with $k \in \{0,\cdots,A-1\}$, and writing $t_1$ for the component filling the left hole (resp. the right hole), we have $t_1 \notin \bigsqcup_{i=0}^{a}\mathcal{T}_{k+1}(i,0)$.
     \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $(\mathcal{H}_{A+1})$.
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
 Otherwise, it is said to be $\mathbf{GOOD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$. Note that if step $j+1$ is $\mathbf{GOOD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$, then $\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j+1}(t,e)$ is again a planar triangulation with one hole.

body:
Let Z be a random finite measure on D with total mass T>0 almost surely and 0<E[T]<infinity. Put U_A=Z(A)/T. Then E[Z(A)]/E[T]-E[U_A]=Cov(T,U_A)/E[T] for each measurable A. Consequently mean normalized measure equals normalized mean measure exactly when Cov(T,U_A)=0 for every A. Independence of total mass and normalized measure is sufficient but unnecessary: three equally likely outcomes T=(1,2,3), U_first=(1,0,1) on two sites give both averages (2/3,1/3), yet T and the normalized measure are dependent. No integrability or independence claim for DGFF extremal mass is inferred from this finite example.

[Thm 7 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$ forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold with $\Lambda_F<\infty$. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Given constants $p \in (\frac{n}{2}, n]$, $\alpha\in [\frac{1}{2},1)$ and a fixed point $x_{0}\in M$. Then,  for $0 \leq r < R_{0}$ and an arbitrarily fixed point $x\in M$ satisfying that $d_{F}(x_{0}, x) \leq \Lambda_{F}^{-1}\left( R_{0}-r\right)$, there exist positive constants $D_{1}=D_{1}(n, p, \vartheta , R_{0})$ and $D_{2}=D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$, such that, when $\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}<D_{1}^{-\frac{2p-1}{p}}$, we have
\beq
&& \left(\frac{m\left(B_{\Lambda_{F}^{-1}r}^{+}(x)\right)}{m\left(B_{R_{0}}^{+}(x_{0})\right)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 p-1}} \geq  \Big[\frac{1}{4} \left(1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}\right)
e^{-\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}}\Lambda_{F}^{-\left(2 \vartheta R_{0}b(p,\alpha)+\frac{5n}{2p-1}\right)}   \nonumber \\
&& \times \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+\frac{4n-2p}{2p-1}}  -  \frac{D_{2}\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}}{1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}} \Big] \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}, 
\eeq
where
\beqn
&& D_{1}(n,p,\vartheta,R_{0}):=D(n, p) e^{\frac{2 p+1}{2 p-1} \vartheta R_{0}} R_{0}^{\frac{2p}{2 p-1}},  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ D(n, p):=\frac{n(n-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2 p-1}}(2 p-1)^{\frac{p}{2 p-1}}}{(2 p-n)^\frac{3p-2}{2p-1}},    \\
&& D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0}):=\frac{D_{1}(n,p,\vartheta,R_{0}) e^{\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}} \Lambda_{F}^{-\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}}{1-e^{-\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2p-1}}(2-\alpha)^{\frac{2p-2n}{2p-1}}\alpha^{\frac{n}{2p-1}} }, \ \ \  b(p,\alpha):=\frac{1}{(2p-1)\ln(2-\alpha)}.
\eeqn

body: [Proposition 3 of arXiv:2607.15125, '2607.15125'] The function $x \mapsto \phi(a;x)$ is analytic at $0$ for $a \in [-1,0)$ and non-analytic for $a \in (0,1]$. Moreover, for $a>0$, it is of class $C^{\lfloor 1/a \rfloor -1}$, but not smoother. The first singular term in its expansion at 0 is of order $\abs{x}^{1/a}$ when $1/a$ is not an even integer, and of order $x^{1/a}\ln(\abs{x})$ when $1/a$ is an even integer. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 3 of arXiv:2607.15125

body: [Prop Linfty_vs_weak of arXiv:2506.12171, 'The multinomial dimer model'] Suppose that $G=(V,E)\subset \Lambda$ is a finite subgraph. Then a sequence of discrete flows $(\omega_k(e))_{e\in E}$ converges to a discrete flow $(\omega(e))_{e\in E}$ as $k\to \infty$ in the sup norm topology on $E$ if and only if it converges to $(\omega(e))_{e\in E}$ in the weak topology on flows.

body:
[Conjecture 17 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] If $d=3$, $H_0=1$, and $H_1=H_2=H_3=1/2$, then
there exist constants $\mf A,\mf B\neq0$ such that
\[\msf Q_\ka(t)=\ka^2\mf A\,t^{1/2}+\ka^4\mf B\,t\log(1/t)+O_{\mbf P}(t)\qquad\text{as }t\to0.\]
More generally, if a model of the PAM requires multiple renormalization functions of decreasing order, say $\msf c_1(\eps),\ldots,\msf c_n(\eps)$, then there are corresponding
deterministic contributions of order $t\msf c_k(t)$ in the small-$t$ asymptotics of $\msf Q_\ka(t)$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 17 of arXiv:2608.18834

body:
[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2608.27218, 'Mapping class groups have a unique Polish group structure'] Let \( \Gamma \) be a locally finite connected graph of rank at least two, and let \( G \) be a closed subgroup of \( \mcg(\Gamma) \). 
		Suppose that 
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item \( G \) contains all word maps, and
			\item given a submanifold \( M \) of \( M_\Gamma \) homeomorphic to \( M_{1,2} \) with both boundary components being separating spheres and given two non-separating spheres \( S_1 \) and \( S_2 \) in \( M \), there exists an element of \( G \) with a representative in \( \mcg(M_\Gamma) \)  supported in \( M \) and mapping \( S_1 \) to \( S_2 \). 
		\end{enumerate}
		Then \( G \) has a unique Polish group structure.
		\qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 25 (Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] There are constants
\[
        K_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,\qquad \Lambda_*<\infty,
        \qquad \beta_{\mathrm{reg}}>0,\qquad C_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,
\]
depending only on \(K,N,\sigma\), with the following property.  For every
\(0<\beta_*\leq\beta_{\mathrm{reg}}\), there is a constant
\(\eta_{\mathrm{st}}>0\), depending only on \(K,N,\sigma,\beta_*\), such that the following holds.
Let \(p(\tau)\) be any parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block, for
some \(\delta_0\geq c_0\), under the standing fixed-threshold application.
Fix the torus structure used during this
stage and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Put
\[
        b:=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))}.
\]
Assume that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian,
\(\BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds, and \(b<\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).  These are
exactly the analytic start conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with
\(\Lambda=\Lambda_*\) and \(\eta=\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r(\tau)\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow
\(q(\tau)\) relative to it exist on \([1,100]\), and
\begin{align}
        |\sec_{r(\tau)}|&\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}/\tau,
                &&1\leq\tau\leq100,                               \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &<\beta_*,                                         \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.                                 
\end{align}
If
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian, \(\BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds,
\(|\sec_{r^+(1)}|\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}\), and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\|q^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
 +\|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}\\
 &\qquad\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
        \|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
        \leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart

[Lemma lem:usa-facts of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$ satisfy Condition~(cond:usa-minimax of the paper).
  Let $t \in \{0,\ldots,T-1\}$.
  Let $X:\mathcal{Y}^T\to\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and upper semi-analytic.
  Then the following hold.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item Per-round minimax duality: $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}[X \mid s] = \overline{\mathbb{E}}^* [X \mid s]$ when $t=T-1$.
  \item The map $\mathcal{Y}^t \ni s \mapsto \overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[X \mid s]$ is upper semi-analytic.
  \item The tower property of $\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*$: $\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[X \mid Y_{1..t}]] = \overline{\mathbb{E}}^* X$.
  \end{enumerate}

Abel's theorem (the Abelian direction): if the series sum a_n converges to s, then the power series f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1 and f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below. The converse is false in general: f(x) = sum (-1)^n x^n = 1/(1 + x) tends to 1/2 while sum (-1)^n diverges. Tauber's theorem (the Tauberian direction): if f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1, f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below, and n a_n -> 0, then sum a_n converges to s. Littlewood strengthened the condition to a_n = O(1/n) (Littlewood's Tauberian theorem, 1911), and Hardy and Littlewood showed that a one-sided bound n a_n >= -C also suffices. 'Abelian' theorems pass from a summability method's convergence to a weaker one; 'Tauberian' theorems go back under an extra growth condition on the terms.
Abel: sum a_n converges
Tauber: f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below and n a_n -> 0 (Littlewood: a_n = O(1/n) suffices, with a harder proof)

[Lemma 6 (Localized empirical-process bound) of arXiv:2608.22179, '\bf Token-Level Likelihood-Array Regression for Membership Inference and AI-Generated Text'] Let \(Z\) be a centered Hilbert-space feature with covariance operator \(\Gamma_Z\),
and let
\(f^\circ(Z)=\alpha^\circ+\ip{\theta^\circ}{Z}\) be any fixed score. For
\(a,b>0\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\E\sup_{\delta,h}\Big[&(P-P_n)
\left\{
\ell_Y\bigl(f^\circ(Z)+\delta+\ip{h}{Z}\bigr)
-\ell_Y\bigl(f^\circ(Z)\bigr)
\right\}\\
&-a\{\delta^2+\norm{h}_{\Gamma_Z}^2\}-b\norm{h}^2\Big]
\leq
\frac{C}{an}\{1+\mathcal N_{\Gamma_Z}(b/a)\}.
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
The supremum may be restricted to any subset of \(\R\oplus\mathcal H\). The
constant \(C\) is universal and the result does not require \(f^\circ\) to be the
true conditional log odds.

[Theorem 2 (Distance theorem for sparse simple random tensors) of arXiv:2606.24090, 'Sparsity-adaptive concentration inequalities for random polynomials'] Let \(0<\alpha\le 1\), \(p\in(0,1]\), and let
\[
     X=X^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{(d)}\in\mathbb R^{n^d},
\]
where \(X_i^{(k)}=\delta_i^{(k)}\xi_i^{(k)}\), the variables \(\delta_i^{(k)}\) are i.i.d. Bernoulli\((p)\), and the variables \(\xi_i^{(k)}\) are independent, mean zero, variance one, and satisfy  $\|\xi_i^{(k)}\|_{\Psi_\alpha}\le 1$. All variables are assumed to be mutually independent.
Set
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}:=\max_{0\le s\le d-1}(np)^{s/2}.
\]
Then for every deterministic nonzero matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n^d\times n^d}\) and every \(t\ge 0\),
\begin{align}
&\mathbb P\left\{
\left|\|B X\|_2-p^{d/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\right|\ge t
\right\}\nonumber\\
&\qquad\le 2\exp\left[
-c_{\alpha,d}
\min\left\{
\frac{t^2}{\Lambda_{n,p,d}^2\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2},
\left(\frac{t}{n^{(d-1)/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^\alpha,
\left(\frac{t}{\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^{\alpha/d}
\right\}
\right].
\end{align}
In particular, if \(np\ge 1\), then
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}=(np)^{(d-1)/2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Distance theorem for sparse simple random tensors

Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, q>=2 an integer, K>=0, u the uniform independent q-color law, and gamma_K the free ferromagnetic Potts law proportional to exp(K times the number of agreeing edges). Then D(u||gamma_K)>=|E|[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]. Equality holds on forests; for K>0 and a graph with a cycle it is strict. Thus on growing Z^d boxes at any fixed K>0, liminf D(u||gamma_K)/|V|>=d[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]>0. This is a product-law obstruction and does not establish critical discontinuity.
finite simple graph
integer q>=2
K>=0
uniform independent spins
free zero-field Potts Gibbs law

body:
[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] The following absolute continuity relationships hold:
	\begin{itemize}
	\item Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ be two disjoint non-trivial segments of $\partial \BD$. Let $\tau$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that the ball $\SCB_t(\alpha; D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ hits $\beta$. Let $X$ be a deterministically selected point (e.g., the leftmost in some parameterization) in $\beta \cap \SCB_\tau(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$. Then the law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\beta$. 
	\item Similarly, let $\tau'$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that $\SCB_t(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ hits $\SCL(0)$ and let $X$ be a deterministically selected point in $\SCL(0) \cap \SCB_{\tau'}(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$. Then, conditionally on $\SCL(0)$, the conditional law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the harmonic measure on $\SCL(0)$ seen from $\infty$ in $\BC \setminus \overline{\mathop{\mathrm{int}}(\SCL(0))}$.
	\item Furthermore, let $\tau''$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that $\SCB_t(\SCL(0); D^\BD_{\Gamma_{\BD}})$ hits $\partial \BD$ and let $X$ be a rotationally equivariant selected point on $\partial \BD \cap \SCB_{\tau''}(\SCL(0); D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ (i.e., the selection commutes with rotations of $\BD$). Then, the law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\partial \BD$ and is actually the uniform distribution on $\partial \BD$.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.04139

		variation distance $\delta$ of $\nu_x$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.14254, '2605.14254'] The process $\xi^{\lambda,z}$ is a semi-martingale and it has the following dynamic:
		\begin{equation}
			\xi^{\lambda,z}_{t}=b^{\lambda,z}_t+\lambda\,\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t\wedge\sigma_z^{\lambda} }\text{sgn}(z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_{s})\,\mathrm{d}s,\, t\geq 0,
		\end{equation}
		where $b^{\lambda,z}$ is an $\mathbb{F}^{\xi^{\lambda,z}}$-Brownian motion stopped at $\sigma_z^{\lambda}$. Here, the sgn function is defined as
		$$
		\text{sgn}(x):=\left\{\begin{aligned}
			-1, & \text { for } x<0 \\
			0, & \text { for } x=0 \\
			+1, & \text { for } x>0
		\end{aligned}\right..
		$$

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $t_n\to\infty$, $\mu\in\mathbf M(\mathbf D)$ be such that $\mu_{t_n}\overset{v}\to \mu$ and let $\Upsilon$ be a Poisson point process on ${\bf D}$ with intensity $\mu$.
    Then $\Upsilon$ and $\Upsilon_{t_n}$ are a.s.~admissible and we may write 
    $$\Upsilon=\sum_{i=1}^\infty \delta_{X_i},$$
    with $\{X_i(o)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ strictly increasing.
title: Proposition 23 of arXiv:2504.02435

In R^(k+1) let M0 be the smooth closed surface z^2+Phi(|x|^2)=1, where Phi(s)=0 for s<=1 and Phi(s)=(s-1)exp(-1/(s-1)) for s>1. Let V0 be its surface volume. Put ell=1/(2sqrt(k)), A=1/12, Q=[-ell/2,ell/2]^k, and b(t)=64t^3(1-t)^3 on [0,1], zero outside. For n>=1 put h=ell/n and partition Q into n^k cells with lower corners c_i. For every sigma in {-1,+1}^(n^k), define f_sigma(x)=A h^2 sum_i sigma_i product_j b((x_j-c_ij)/h), T_sigma(x,z)=(x,z+f_sigma(x)), Vn=area(T_sigma(M0)), and t_n=(V0/Vn)^(1/k). Let mu_(sigma,n) be exactly uniform surface probability on t_n T_sigma(M0), isometrically embedded into R^D. There are constants C,W0 depending only on k,D and this fixed base such that, for W>=W0, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG architecture with at most W charged edge weights and biases has sup_(n,sigma) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],mu_(sigma,n))<=C W^(-4/k), with depth O(W). All fixed coefficients are charged; absent edges are absent; skip connections, unrestricted real weights and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed. The exact squared-gradient graph area density is C2 across every cell face with bounds independent of n; uniformly positive C2 chart densities have uniformly C2 inverse triangular transports. Apply Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk Theorem 3.3 (arXiv:1906.09477, p.5) at r=2,d=k, then a logarithmic-size tent-map scalar-source conversion and a fixed finite chart mixture with positive-time connectors. The source-conversion coupling uses the exact smooth map Lipschitz constant, not the coding network Lipschitz constant. This is a candidate theorem only for this entire explicit packing family, not all reach-bounded C2 surfaces. No bounded-bit, efficient weight-computation, complete T339 solution or novelty claim is made.
Exactly the explicit smooth base and signed cubic-endpoint bump family in the statement; k>=1, D>=k+1; scalar uniform latent source; unrestricted real-weight sparse feedforward DAG parameter count including fixed coefficients. Analytic proof unaudited, depending on unaudited T2-007 regularity and the known Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk theorem.

[Theorem thm:ck-and-wk-enjoy-lip of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Both $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$ enjoy LIP.
  \begin{proof}
    Let $L \in \set{\textbf{CK}, \textbf{WK}}$ and suppose $L \vdash \varphi \to \psi$,
    then $\varphi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \psi$ is provable in $\mathrm{G}_L$.
    Consider the partition $\varphi;\emptyset$ of $\varphi$,
    then by Lemma (lemma:maehara of the paper), there is $\chi$ such that
    $\varphi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \chi$ and $\chi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \psi$ are provable in $\mathrm{G}_L$,
    which imply $L \vdash \varphi \to \chi$ and $L \vdash \chi \to \psi$, respectively,
    and $\mathrm{V}^\bullet(\chi) \subseteq \mathrm{V}^\bullet(\varphi) \cap \mathrm{V}^\bullet(\psi)$ for each $\bullet \in \set{+, -}$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2609.03556, 'An Effective SPDE Model for a Schr\"odinger Equation with a Fluctuating Magnetic Potential'] \label[lemma]{lem:rmse_viscous}
Assume \cref{hp:noise} and $\psi_0\in L^2(\R^d)$. There exists a unique
progressively measurable process $\psi^{\tau,\nu}$ with paths in
$C([0,T];L^2)\cap L^2(0,T;H^2)$ $\mathbb{P}-a.s.$ satisfying, for each
$\phi\in \mathscr{S}(\R^d)$ and $t\in [0,T]$,
\begin{align*}
i\langle \psi^{\tau,\nu}_t,\phi\rangle-i\langle \psi_0,\phi\rangle
&=-i\nu \int_0^t
\langle\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\Delta^2\phi\rangle ds
-\int_0^t \langle\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\Delta\phi\rangle ds\\
&\quad-2i\int_0^t
\langle \psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,A^{\tau}_s\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle ds+\int_0^t
\langle|A^{\tau}_s|^2\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\phi\rangle ds
\quad \mathbb{P}-a.s.,
   \end{align*}
   where $A^{\tau}_t$ is the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process \eqref{eq:OU_prel}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For an integral operator T_k on L^2 with kernel k, the formula tr T_k = integral of k(x,x) dx is not a definition and not automatic. (1) An L^2 kernel is an equivalence class modulo null sets, and on a nonatomic space the diagonal is a null set, so k(x,x) has no meaning at all without choosing a distinguished representative; different representatives give different 'diagonal integrals'. (2) Continuity of the kernel is not enough for trace class. Carleman's example: there are continuous 2pi-periodic functions g whose Fourier coefficients are not absolutely summable. The convolution operator (T f)(x) = (1/(2 pi)) times the integral over the circle of g(x - y) f(y) dy has the continuous kernel k(x,y) = g(x - y)/(2 pi), is normal with eigenvalues the Fourier coefficients of g and eigenfunctions the exponentials, so its singular values are the moduli of those coefficients; hence T is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, while the naive diagonal integral is the finite number g(0). (3) What does hold: if T is trace class on L^2([a,b]) and has a continuous kernel on [a,b] x [a,b], then tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx; and by Mercer's theorem, if k is continuous, symmetric and positive semidefinite on a compact interval (more generally on a compact metric space with a finite Borel measure of full support), then the associated operator is trace class, the eigenfunction series converges absolutely and uniformly, and tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx = sum of the eigenvalues. So the safe routes are positivity plus continuity (Mercer), or an independent proof of trace class plus continuity; 'the kernel is nice' by itself is not a proof.
the operator is trace class, or the kernel is continuous and positive semidefinite (Mercer) on a compact space with a finite Borel measure of full support
the kernel is a continuous representative, so that its diagonal values are defined
an L^2 kernel alone determines only a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, whose diagonal is undefined
title: Pitfall: The Trace Is the Integral of the Kernel Diagonal Only Under Extra Hypotheses

[Thm 8 of arXiv:2609.02415, 'Nef Cones of Hilbert Schemes of Orthogonal Grassmannians'] Let $m=\mathrm{min}\{\lfloor (N-1)/2 \rfloor-q,q-1\}$.
If $2<r\leq m$, there are $2$ connected components in $\mathrm{Hilb}_{P_{d,r}(t)}(OG(q;V))$. 
In particular, if $m=q-1$, for $q-1<r\leq \lfloor (N-1)/2 \rfloor-q$, there is $1$ connected component in $\mathrm{Hilb}_{P_{d,r}(t)}(OG(q;V))$.

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] For each $\kappa,\alpha, n>0$, there exists a non-negative function $\psi\in C^3[-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]$ such that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The function $\psi$ solves the ODE (Stein's equation)
    \begin{equation}
        \psi''(z)-\alpha z^3 \psi'(z)=-1,
        
    \end{equation}
    with boundary conditions $\psi'(-n^{1/4}\kappa)=\psi(0)=0$.
     \item We have $\psi'(z)\leq 0$ for all $z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]$ and $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}|\psi'(z)|<C_1$ for some positive constant $C_1$ independent of $n$.
    \item We have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}\psi(z)<C_2$ for some positive constant $C_2$ independent of $n$.
    \item  For all sufficiently large $n$ we have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]}|\psi'''(z)|=\alpha\kappa^3n^{3/4}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[

body:
[Prop p:efron-stein-classical of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X_0,X_1,\dots,X_n, Y$ be random vectors (possibly with different and/or infinite lengths) on the same probability space, such that $X_0,\dots,X_n$ are conditionally independent given $Y$.
    Write $\mathbf{X} \coloneqq  (X_0,\dots,X_n)$.
    Let $\widetilde{\mathbf{X}} = (\widetilde{X}_0,\dots,\widetilde{X}_n)$ be a conditionally independent copy of $\mathbf{X}$ given $Y$.
    Write
    \begin{align*}
        \widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k)} \coloneqq  (X_0,\dots,X_{k-1},\widetilde{X}_k, X_{k+1},\dots,X_n).
    \end{align*}
    Note that we have the equality of unconditional joint laws
    \begin{align*}
        (\mathbf{X},Y)\overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}},Y) \overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(0)}, Y)\overset{d}{=} \cdots \overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(n)},Y).
    \end{align*}
    

    Let $Z=Z(\mathbf{X},Y)$ be a square-integrable function of $(\mathbf{X},Y)$.
    Then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[\Var(Z \mid Y)]
        = \frac12
        \mathbb{E}\left[
            \left(
                Z(\mathbf{X},Y)
                - Z(\widetilde{\mathbf{X}},Y)
            \right)^2
        \right]
        &\leqslant
        \frac12
        \sum_{k=0}^n 
        \mathbb{E}\left[
            \left(
                Z(\mathbf{X},Y)
                - Z(\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k)},Y)
            \right)^2
        \right].
    \end{align*}
    In fact, the above holds almost surely with $\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,|\,Y]$ in place of $\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Efron--Stein inequality

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2607.20646, 'The Independence-Preserving Property and Planar Web Geometry'] Let $(\mu_X,\mu_Y,\mu_U,\mu_V)$ be probability measures on $(0, \infty)$ having positive continuous density.
Then $\HIp|_{(0,\infty)^2}$ preserves their independence if and only if there exist $p,q,r\in\R$ with $\max\{p, 0\} < \min\{q, r\}$ such that
\begin{alignat*}{3}
    \mu_X(\dd x)
        &\propto (1 + \alpha x)^{p}\Big(\frac{1}{1+x}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{\alpha x}{1+\alpha x}\Big)^r\frac{\dd x}{x} &
        &\propto x^{r-1}(1+x)^{-q}(1+\alpha x)^{p-r}\,\dd x,\\
    \mu_Y(\dd y)
        &\propto (1 + \beta y)^{p}\Big(\frac{\beta y}{1+\beta y}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{1}{1+y}\Big)^r\frac{\dd y}{y} &
        &\propto y^{q-1}(1+y)^{-r}(1+\beta y)^{p-q}\,\dd y,\\
    \mu_U(\dd u)
        &\propto (1 + \alpha u)^{p}\Big(\frac{\alpha u}{1+\alpha u}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{1}{1+u}\Big)^r\frac{\dd u}{u} &
        &\propto u^{q-1}(1+u)^{-r}(1+\alpha u)^{p-q}\,\dd u,\\
    \mu_V(\dd v)
        &\propto (1 + \beta v)^{p}\Big(\frac{1}{1+v}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{\beta v}{1+\beta v}\Big)^r\frac{\dd v}{v} &
        &\propto v^{r-1}(1+v)^{-q}(1+\beta v)^{p-r}\,\dd v.
\end{alignat*}

body:
[Lemma lem:commutator-transfer of arXiv:2608.22910, 'A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks'] Fix \(t\geq0\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\), and set
\[
C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}:=[\mathcal S_\ell,\mathrm{NFM}_\ell],
\qquad
C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}:=[Q_\ell,P_\ell].
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}
=W_\ell^\top C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}W_\ell
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}\|_F
\leq
\|W_\ell\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F.
\end{equation}
If \(W_\ell\) has full row rank, and \(\sigma_{\min}(W_\ell)\) denotes
its smallest singular value, then
\begin{equation}
\sigma_{\min}(W_\ell)^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F
\leq
\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}\|_F
\leq
\sigma_{\max}(W_\ell)^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F,
\end{equation}
and hence \(C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}=0\) if and only if
\(C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}=0\).

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. We define the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$, denoted by $\text{LE} (\lambda)$, in the following manner. First, set
$$ t_0 \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(0)\}.$$
For each $i \geq 1$, define
$$ t_i \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(t_{i-1}+1)\}. $$
Let 
$$n = \min\{i \, : \, t_i = m\}.$$
    Then, the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by
    $$\text{LE} (\lambda) \coloneqq [\lambda(t_0), \lambda(t_1), \ldots, \lambda(t_n)].$$
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.01748

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_k] = 0 and \text{Var}(X_k) = \sigma_k^2 < \infty. Let S_k = \sum_{j=1}^k X_j. Then for every \epsilon > 0, \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{1 \le k \le n} |S_k| \ge \epsilon \right) \le \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} \sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\text{Var}(S_n)}{\epsilon^2}.

This strengthens Chebyshev's inequality applied to S_n alone into a bound on the whole running maximum. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

[Proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $S_1\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}$
    \begin{proof}
        We may compute $S_1$ explicitly. We have, via a combinatorial identity,
        \[S_1=\frac{n-2m-3}{2^{n-2m-4}}\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}-m-2}\]
        By a special case of Stirling's estimate, we have
        \[\binom{n}{n/2}\sim 2^n(\pi n/2)^{-1/2}\] 
        This gives
        \[S_1\sim \frac{(n-2m-3)(2^{n-2m-4})}{(2^{n-2m-4})\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}=\frac{(n-2m-3)}{\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-2m-3}{\sqrt{n-2m-4}}\right)\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-2}{\sqrt{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-3}}\right)\]
        \[\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}\]
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a nonnegative random variable X, typically a count of some combinatorial structure written as X = sum_i X_i for indicator random variables X_i, the Paley-Zygmund inequality gives P(X > 0) >= (E[X])^2 / E[X^2]. Expanding E[X^2] = E[X] + sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j], the method succeeds in proving P(X>0) is bounded away from 0 exactly when the pair-correlation sum sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j] is of the same order as (E[X])^2, that is, when correlations between the indicators do not overwhelm the square of the mean. This is the standard route to existence results, such as an infinite cluster, a long crossing, or a large clique, once a first-moment computation has already established that E[X] is large or diverging, complementing the first-moment method, which by Markov's inequality only ever gives upper bounds on P(X>0). The method does not give any rate of convergence beyond the crude Paley-Zygmund ratio, gives no lower bound at all if the correlation structure is not controlled, and can produce a vacuous (near-0) bound whenever the variance is dominated by rare, strongly correlated configurations even though the mean itself is large. Typical failure: Computing a large or diverging first moment E[X] and declaring existence of the structure without bounding E[X^2]; if the indicators X_i are strongly positively correlated (a common situation for overlapping structures), the pair-correlation term can dominate (E[X])^2, making the Paley-Zygmund bound vacuous even as E[X] -> infinity, which is exactly the situation where a large first moment gives a false sense of near-certain existence. Canonical reference: Paley and Zygmund, 1932, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society; Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, fourth edition, Wiley.
a well-defined nonnegative counting or indicator-sum random variable X = sum_i X_i
a computable or boundable first moment E[X]

body:
[Lemma 3 (Replica Wick polynomial) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] For
\[
 M_{P,r}(\Sigma)
 =
 \E\prod_{a=1}^{r}P(X_a^\Sigma),
 \qquad \Sigma\in\Sym_r^{++}(\R),
\]
one has the polynomial identity
\begin{equation}
 M_{P,r}(\Sigma)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{E=(e_{ab})\\k_a(E)\leq m}}
 N(E)\,\Contr_E(P)
 \prod_{1\leq a\leq b\leq r}\Sigma_{ab}^{e_{ab}},
 
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 N(E)
 =
 \frac{\prod_{a=1}^{r}k_a(E)!}
 {\displaystyle
  \prod_{a=1}^{r}2^{e_{aa}}e_{aa}!\,
  \prod_{1\leq a<b\leq r}e_{ab}!}
 \in\N_{>0}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, every complete contraction of copies of the tensors
\(T_0(P),\ldots,T_m(P)\) is, up to the explicit positive factor
\eqref{eq:wick-multiplicity}, a coefficient of one of the polynomials
\(M_{P,r}\).

Let P be a locally finite poset, R a nonzero commutative ring with 1, and Q a subset with the induced order. Restricting an element of the incidence algebra I_R(P) to the comparable pairs of Q is a unital R-algebra homomorphism onto I_R(Q) if and only if Q is order-convex: x <= z <= y with x, y in Q forces z in Q. In that case mu_Q(x, y) = mu_P(x, y) for all x <= y in Q.

[Corollary 37 (Convergence, stated with a reference measure; Theorem \ref{thm:posdens}) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\XX$ be a set, $\XXA$ a $\sigma$-algebra on $\XX$, and $\lambda$ a
$\sigma$-finite measure on $(\XX,\XXA)$. Let
\[
  p : \XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \tau : \XX\times\XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty), \quad (x,y) \longmapsto \tau(y \mid x),
\]
be measurable, respectively $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable, and define the probability
measure $\pi$ and the Markov kernel $T$ by
\[
  \pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda,
  \qquad
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
where $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$ and $\int_{\XX}\tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$
for every $x \in \XX$. Write $\Xp := \{ y \in \XX : p(y) > 0 \} \in \XXA$ and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(the support is not left)} for every $x \in \XX$: $\ \tau(y \mid x) = 0$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX\setminus\Xp$;
  \item \emph{(positivity)} $\tau(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y) \in \Xp \times \Xp$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty} \tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} = 0 \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob .
\]
Theorem \ref{thm:posdens} of the introduction is the special case in which $p > 0$
everywhere, so that $\Xp = \XX$ and hypothesis (ii) is vacuous.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.24549, 'Persistent Cross Entropy'] A map $k:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{Z}\to(0,1]$ is called a
\textbf{similarity function} if it satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textit{\roman*})]
\item there exist a metric $\rho$ on $\mathcal{Z}$ and a strictly decreasing function
$h:[0,\infty)\to(0,1]$ with $h(0)=1$ and
$\lim\limits_{r\to\infty}h(r)=0$ such that
$$
k(u,v)=h(\rho(u,v));
$$

\item $k$ is Lipschitz in its second argument: there exists $L_0>0$ such that
$$
|k(u,v)-k(u,v')|
\leq
L_0\Vert v-v' \Vert
$$
for all $u,v,v'\in\mathcal{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2608.29148, '2608.29148'] A $\Theta$-metric $g$ on $(\ol X, [\Theta])$ is called an {\it asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) metric} with CR infinity $(M, H, J)$ if it satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  For any boundary defining function $r$, we have 
\[
\Bigl|\dfrac{dr}{r}\Bigr|^2_g=\dfrac{1}{4}\quad \textrm{on}\ M,
\]
or, equivalently, $|\nu|^2_g=4$. 
\item[(ii)] For any $p\in M$, the map
\[
L_p\longrightarrow {}^\Theta T_p \ol X, \quad Z\longmapsto [\nu_p, Z]
\]
gives the identity map on $L_p$.
\item[(iii)] For any contact form $\th$ on $M$, we have 
\[
\lambda_\th^*(g|_{L})=2h_{\a\ol\b}\th^\a\cdot\th^{\ol\b},
\]
where the right-hand side denotes the Levi form on $H$ associated with $\th$.
\end{enumerate}
We call $(\ol X, [\Theta], g)$ an {\it ACH manifold}.

body: Bond FPP on Z^2, iid weights in [a,b] (atoms allowed, geodesic uniqueness NOT assumed, canonical topmost selection). Blocks {Lambda} tile the edge set; X^Lambda is the one-block resampled passage time; U_Lambda = {canonical geodesic uses an edge of Lambda}; F_t the label-revealing filtration. With A2 = Sum_Lambda E[1(U_Lambda)(X^Lambda-X)^2], A4 = Sum_Lambda E[1(U_Lambda)((X^Lambda-X)^+)^4], Pbar(kappa) = Sum_Lambda E[P(U_Lambda|F_{1-kappa})^2]: for every kappa in (0,1), Var(X) <= kappa A2 + sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa)). The derivation consumes only the POSITIVE part of the increment, so the inequality also holds with A2 replaced by A2+ = Sum E[((X^Lambda-X)^+)^2] <= A2. Consumes no isotropy, no FKG, no continuum structure; planarity only inside the geodesic selection. Refereed 2026-08-09; the identity chain machine-checked by full enumeration on a 7-edge 3-block instance. Provenance: campaign problem/MG2B_framework_lemma_draft.md Theorem 8.1 + CRUX 6d (D7).

Finite-dimensional local corollary of van den Berg-Hetebrij-Rink parameterization theorem. Let F be a C^k map, integer k>=2, on a neighborhood of 0 in R^c x R^s, fixing 0, with DF(0)=diag(I_c,A_s) and spectral radius(A_s)<1. Then, after restricting to a neighborhood, there is a C^k center graph h with h(0)=0,Dh(0)=0 and a local C^k center map R, DR(0)=I_c, such that F(u,h(u))=(R(u),h(R(u))) wherever both sides remain local. The graph is parameterized by its center coordinate u. For k=3 this gives a C3 center graph. This assertion is a graph-existence and reduced-map theorem; it does not by itself assert a phase projection or stable foliation for nearby points.

    \item[$i)$] For any $v\in V,$ 
    $
    \nu[v\;\mathrm{ closed}]\leq \alpha \exp\left(-C \lambda^{
    n-\mathtt{gen}(v)}\right).
    $
    \item[$ii)$] For any $W,W'\subseteq V(\mathscr{T}_n^\mathtt{d})$ with no common descendants, the $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal{A}_{W}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{W'}$ are independent.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{C}_o$ denote the cluster of the root.  Then, for every $A\subseteq V_n,$ 
$$
\nu[|\mathcal{C}_o \cap A|\leq (1-\alpha C'-|A|^{-1/3}) |A| ]\leq \alpha C'|A|^{-1/3}.
$$

[Lemma lem:doubling-metric-dim of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space.
		
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (A)] (Doubling $\Rightarrow$ finite metric dimension)
Assume that there exists an integer $N\ge 1$ such that for every $x\in X$ and $R>0$, the ball $B(x,R)$ can be covered by at most $N$ balls of radius $R/2$.
Then $(X,d)$ is $(C,s)$-homogeneous in the sense of Assouad, with
\[s=\log_2 N, \qquad C=N,\]
hence $\Dim(X,d)<\infty$.
			
\item[\rm (B)] (Finite metric dimension $\Rightarrow$ doubling)
Assume that $(X,d)$ is $(C,s)$-homogeneous: for all $0<a<b$ and all $Y\subset Z\subset X$ with $\mathrm{diam\, }(Z)\le b$ and $Y$ $a$-separated, one has $\#Y\le C(b/a)^s$.
Then $(X,d)$ is doubling: every ball $B(x,R)$ can be covered by at most
\[N_0:=C\,2^{s}\]
balls of radius $R/2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Doubling $\Longleftrightarrow$ finite Assouad/metric dimension

At a product law the covariance derivative equals J_i*(r_(i+1)-r_i), with killing terms cancelling. Stationarity therefore forces all adjacent densities equal. Incoming and outgoing exterior jumps factor under the product law, giving the displayed covariance derivative. [Lem number-crossings-check of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Consider an annulus $A(x;r,2r)$. Let $\check{F}_1(\check{M})$ be the event that there are at most $\check{M}$ distinct clusters (open or closed) that cross this annulus. If there exist both an open crossing and a closed crossing of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for any open (resp.\ closed) cluster that crosses this annulus, one can find two (not necessarily disjoint) open (resp.\ closed) crossings of the annulus $\eta_c$ and $\eta_a$ that serve as the clockwise most and counterclockwise most boundaries of this cluster. 
Define the event $\check{F}_2(\check{b})$ as follows. If there are at least 2 crossing clusters of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for every open (resp.\ closed) crossing cluster of $A(x;r,2r)$, let $v$ be the endpoint of $\eta_a$ on the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$. On $\check{F}_2$, we require that there exists an open (resp.\ closed) path from $\eta_a$ to the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$ that stays at distance at least $10\check{b}r$ away from $v$. We also require the same assertion when we swap $\eta_a$ with $\eta_c$. In particular, this implies that for points $v$ that are the endpoints of the interfaces of crossing clusters at the inner boundary of $\check{A}$, no crossing clusters apart from the ones whose interface $v$ is on enter the box $B(v,10\check{b}r)$. 

The following holds for $R$ large enough. For each $\check{p}>0$, there exist $\check{M}$ large enough and $\check{b}>0$ small enough so that $$\mathbf{P}\!\left(\check{F}_1(\check{M})\cap \check{F}_2(\check{b})\right)\geq 1-\check{p}$$ for all annuli $A(x;r,2r)$ of radius $r\geq \frac{R}{\check{b}n}$.

[Lemma lem:7_probabilities_ordered of arXiv:2507.12601, 'Multi-type logistic branching processes with selection: frequency process and genealogy fo'] Let $\square\in\{+,-\}$.
    For every $L\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $K_L\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\kappa_L> 0$ such that for all $1\leq n\leq L$, $K \geq K_L$ and $0\leq i,j\leq \kappa_L K$, we have that $N\mapsto p_{i,j}^\square(n, N)$ is monotonically decreasing on $[N_K^\downarrow, N_K^\uparrow]$.
    Furthermore,
    \[
    \sup_{1\leq n\leq L} \left\vert p_{i,j}^\square(n,N_K^\uparrow) - p_{i,j}^\square(n, N_K^\downarrow)\right\vert \leq C_L\cdot \left(\dfrac{j}{K} + \dfrac{i(i-1)}{K^2}\right)\varepsilon_K,
    \]
    for all $K\geq K_L$ and some constant $C_L$ only depending on $L$.

UNREVIEWED AUTHOR PROOF, CONDITIONAL. Let G be an infinite connected bounded-degree Cayley graph with 0<p_c<1. Assume the uniform bound sup_F ||T_pc^F||_2<=M<infinity, where F is finite connected with free boundary, and let alpha=||A_G||_2. Then p_u>=p_c+eta>p_c, with eta=min{(1-p_c)/2,1/(2 alpha M)}. The bootstrap bounds the full T_q by 2M throughout this interval. Almost-sure uniqueness would force T_q(x,y)>=theta(q)^2, contradicting quadratic forms on n vertices. The uniform critical input remains unproved in general.
Independent Bernoulli bond percolation
Simple undirected graph
Infinite connected bounded-degree Cayley graph
0<p_c<1
UNPROVED IN GENERAL: uniform critical norm M<infinity

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $\rho \in L^1_\loc(I\times \R^d)$ be a weak solution of \eqref{CE}.
Let $N\subset I$ be given by Proposition~\ref{prop-CE-int} and let $s\in I\setminus N$.
Then for any $t\in \overline{I}$ the distribution
\begin{equation}
\langle \rho|_t, \fhi \rangle := \int_{\R^d} \rho(s,x) \fhi(x) \, dx + \int_s^t \int_{\R^d} \rho(\tau, x) \v(\tau, x) \cdot \nabla \fhi(x) \, dx \, d\tau,
\qquad \fhi \in \mathscr{D}(\R^d),
\end{equation}
is called the trace of $\rho$ at time $t$.
title: Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.03831

[Theorem partition of arXiv:2609.02180, 'Helly-Type Theorems for Splitting Point Sets \thanks{A preliminary version of this article'] In any dimension $d\geq 2$, one can fix a constant $b=b_d$ with the following property:

    For a finite point set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and any integer parameter $r$ that satisfies $2 \leq r < \abs{X}$, there is a partition $X = X_1 \mathbin{\dot\cup} \dotsb \mathbin{\dot\cup} X_t$ into at most $r$ parts such that $\abs{X}/r \leq \abs{X_i} \leq 2\abs{X}/r$ for all $i$, every set $X_i$ is enclosed by a simplex $\Delta_i$ and no hyperplane crosses more than $br^{1-1/d}$ of the simplices $\Delta_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matou\v{s}ek's Simplicial Partition \cite{Matouek1991EfficientPT}

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:induction}
Let $P$ be a Markov operator on a Polish metric space $(\Omega,d)$. Let $G\colon \Omega \to \Hm$ be $L$-Lipschitz
and $H \in  \Hm$. Let $\sigma_\infty(x) \coloneqq \diam \supp P(x,\cdot)$.
Then,
\[
P \tr\exp\left( H + G \right)(x) \le  \tr\exp\left(H + PG(x) + 2 L^2 \sigma_{\infty}^2(x) \Id \right).
\]
title: Lemma 15 of arXiv:2605.24445

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.11637, '\bf Uniform Local Asymptotics for L\'evy Processes with Subexponential Jumps'] For any $K\geq 0$ and $\delta_1\geq \delta_0>0$, we have  as $x\to\infty$,
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)}  \sup_{\delta\in [\delta_0,\delta_1]}   \bigg| \frac{ \nu\big(x-y+\Delta_\delta\big) }{ \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)}
 	-1 \bigg|  \to 0. 
 	\eeqlb
 	Moreover,  there exists a constant $x_0>0$ such that  
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{x\geq x_0}\sup_{y\geq  x}  \sup_{\delta\in [\delta_0,\delta_1]} 
 	\frac{\nu\big(y+\Delta_\delta\big)}{\nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)}<\infty. 
 	\eeqlb (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lma:analyticgauge of arXiv:2608.26564, 'Real ideal points, Conway spheres, and left-orderable Dehn fillings'] After shrinking $B$ and enlarging $K$ by a finite real extension, the normalizers $C_i$ in Proposition (prop:branchmodel of the paper) may be chosen so that $\Sigma_i(t) = C_i\rho_B|_{\pi_1(T_i)}C_i^{-1}$ is real analytic in the signed parameter $t$ and extends to $t = 0$ with $\Sigma_i(0) = \rho_i^B$. In addition, the projective relative conjugator admits a meromorphic representative in $t$. The resulting change of normalizers does not alter $J = \mathrm{red}(\widehat R)$ up to multiplication by a nonzero real scalar.

[Definition def:dense-grids-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let \(\alpha>1\). For \(n\ge1\), let 
\(
\Gamma_n(\alpha)\subset[1,2]
\)
be a
finite set with mesh at most \(2^{-\alpha n}\):
\[
\sup_{\eta\in[1,2]}\operatorname{dist}(\eta,\Gamma_n(\alpha))
\le
2^{-\alpha n},
\]
and with cardinality
\[
\#\Gamma_n(\alpha)\le C2^{\alpha n}
\]
for an absolute constant \(C\).
For a function 
\(
f:\Gamma_n(\alpha)\to\mathbb C
\)
and 
\(
1\le r<\infty
\),
write
\[
\lVert f\rVert_{\ell^r(\Gamma_n(\alpha))}
=
\left(\sum_{\eta\in\Gamma_n(\alpha)}\lvert f(\eta)\rvert^r\right)^{1/r}.
\]
title: Dense grids

[Lemma lem:angular of arXiv:2608.30831, 'Sharp discrete Hardy constants in dimensions three and four\\ and strict upper bounds from'] Let
\[
 F(q)=\sum_{r=1}^M c_r(q+\beta)^{-p_r},
 \qquad c_r,p_r,\beta>0.
\]
For $n\in\mathbb Z^N$ and $s=|n|^2$,
\begin{align}
 &\sum_{j=1}^N\bigl(F(s+1+2n_j)+F(s+1-2n_j)\bigr)\notag\\

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] For every pair of integers satisfying \eqref{eq:nk-range}, there is a compact
embedded rotational torus $\Sigma^n\subset\R^{n+1}$ whose homothetic
dilations form a shrinking solution of the unnormalised $\sigma_k$-curvature
flow \eqref{eq:sigma-k-flow} in the Sobolev almost-everywhere sense defined in
Section~\ref{sec:weak}.  More precisely, $\Sigma$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item The torus is smooth away from two rotational latitudes and satisfies
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S)$ there.
  \item If $\Omega$ is the bounded domain enclosed by $\Sigma$ and
  $S_{\mathrm w}$ is the weak shape operator of $\partial\Omega=\Sigma$, then
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w})$ almost everywhere with
  respect to the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal H^n$.
  \item Set $X_t=((k+1)(T-t))^{1/(k+1)}X$ and
  $\Sigma_t=X_t(M)$.  If $\nu_t$ and $S_{\mathrm w,t}$ are the outward unit
  normal and weak shape operator of $\Sigma_t$, respectively, then
  $\langle\partial X_t/\partial t,\nu_t\rangle
  =\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w,t})$ at $\mathcal H^n$-almost every point, for every
  $t<T$.
  \item Its profile curve has H\"older regularity $C^{1,1/k}$ and belongs
  to the Sobolev class $W^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<k/(k-1)$.
\end{enumerate}
If $s$ is arclength along the profile curve and $s_0$ is either singular
parameter, then the profile curve is
not $C^2$ at $s_0$, and the magnitude of its meridional principal curvature
is asymptotic to a positive multiple of $|s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor 28 of arXiv:2608.30763, 'Ultracontractivity of heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions via two-sid'] Let $B$ be defined as
$$
Bu (x) \ = \ \int_{\partial \Omega} k(x,y) u(y) \d \sigma(y)
$$
for $u \in \mathrm{L}^{2}\left( \partial \Omega \right)$ and 
$k \in \mathrm{L}^{2} \left( \partial \Omega \times \partial \Omega \right)$ satisfying
$$
\mathop{\operatorname{ess\,sup}}_{x\in\partial\Omega} \int_{\partial \Omega} \left| k(x,y) \right| \d \sigma(y) < \infty.
$$
Then $(\mathrm{e}^{-tL(A, B)})_{t \geq 0}$ is ultracontractive in $\mathrm{L}^{2}\left( \Omega \right)$ at any time $t > 0$.\\

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ffc8c49ef73f097dbcd9d8597a33ea07288b47a625998901ea82a425a8186800","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ff/ffc8c49ef73f097dbcd9d8597a33ea07288b47a625998901ea82a425a8186800.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:452ba6bbe8bae42609897f9aa18612c97d80ca3354c8d48f003d294369bc6451","bundle_entry_key":"baseline-weak-correction","bundle_id":"population.t244-rate-diagnostics-011","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-baseline-weak-correction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C030: next-order baseline generator; fourth order is necessary

20 October 2026. Target 1; kind bound; proof (unaudited).
This is ONLY the chi-square projection-ratio component of C004. It is not
the full ReLU transition, which also contains Q, flips, and arctan terms.

Let k be Bin(n,1/2). On n/3<=k<=2n/3 let S and R be independent
chi-square variables with respectively k and k-1 degrees of freedom and
M=sqrt(S/R). Off this central-k event put M=1. For fixed 0<d<K and bounded
C^5 f with bounded derivatives through order five, uniformly for u in [d,K],

    n E[f(uM)-f(u)] = 2u f'(u)+u^2 f''(u)
        +(1/n)[10u f'(u)+11u^2 f''(u)+4u^3 f'''(u)
                            +(u^4/2)f''''(u)] + O_(f,d,K)(n^(-3/2)). (B)

The exact conditional raw moments, for k large enough, are

    E M     = (k-1)/(k-2),
    E M^2   = k/(k-3),
    E M^3   = (k^2-1)/[(k-2)(k-4)],
    E M^4   = k(k+2)/[(k-3)(k-5)].                  (G)

These follow from E(chi-square_r)^z=2^z Gamma(r/2+z)/Gamma(r/2),
independence, and Gamma(x+1)=x Gamma(x). In particular the first formula
is exact; approximating its two gamma ratios separately is unnecessary.
Expansion in 1/k gives

    E(M-1)   =1/k+2/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^2 =1/k+5/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^3 =6/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^4 =3/k^2+O(k^-3).

For central binomial k,

    E[1/k; central]=2/n+2/n^2+O(n^-3),
    E[1/k^2; central]=4/n^2+O(n^-3).

For example expand around mu=n/2 with k-mu, whose odd central moments
vanish and whose second moment is n/4. The fourth central moment is O(n^2);
central-k Taylor denominators are bounded below by n/3, and the remaining
binomial tails are exponential. Thus the four mixed moments are respectively

    2/n+10/n^2+O(n^-3),
    2/n+22/n^2+O(n^-3),
    24/n^2+O(n^-3),
    12/n^2+O(n^-3).

Also E|M-1|^5=O(n^(-5/2)). To verify this last bound, split on central
S/k and R/k. There, M-1 is Lipschitz in their centered deviations and has
fifth absolute moment of this order. The chi-square exponential tails,
Holder, and higher inverse moments on central k bound the omitted part
exponentially. This is possible for all sufficiently large n, since k
then exceeds every fixed inverse-moment threshold used.

Fourth-order Taylor expansion with fifth-derivative remainder now proves
(B), including the factors 1/2,1/6,1/24. The fourth-order term is of size
1/n in the scaled generator, exactly the same order as the signed third
moment term. Therefore a derivation using only a third-order Taylor term
cannot give the complete weak 1/n correction, even before ReLU flips.

This partial expansion does not upgrade C004's full O(n^-1/2) error to
O(1/n). The unresolved pieces are the mixed baseline/flip moments and
angular geometry terms, uniformly enough to match the singular entrance.
If such a complete expansion is obtained, a time-step weak-error formula
also needs the discrete-vs-continuous semigroup correction, not only the
coefficient displayed in the one-step generator.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3d7df9f2e51673034c933127493e891f934b33deb918593bd355f53d6e87ca80","revision_digest":"sha256:f282992730d5aa78d8c74a31004934b8f1d577dbbef911eb63487680c57725d0","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C030:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma area Lemma of arXiv:2605.29095, 'Asymptotics of the number of components of random polynomial lemniscates'] [Area Theorem] [Ahlfors], [crane-polynomialpreimage] 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item Let \( f \) be a univalent (injective holomorphic) function on a domain \( D \subseteq \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \subset D \) be a measurable set. Then the area of the image \( f(K) \) is given by:
\[
\text{Area}\big(f(K)\big) = \int_K |f'(z)|^2 \, dA(z),
\]
where \( dA(z) = dx \, dy \) denotes the Euclidean area element in \( \mathbb{C} \).
\item Let \( p \) be a polynomial of degree \( n \) over \( \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \) be any measurable subset of the complex plane. Let \( n(z, p, K) \) be the number of preimages of \( z \) under \( p \) that lie in \( K \) counted with multiplicity. Then,
\begin{align}
    \int_{\mathbb{C}} n(z, p, K)\, dA(z) = \int_K |p'(z)|^2\, dA(z).
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 6 (Variance of polymer partition functions) of arXiv:2608.13359, 'Fractional moments of the Stochastic Heat Flow and\\2D Directed Polymers'] Let \(\th(N,\beta)\) be defined as in \eqref{def:theta-N-beta}.
  Then there are constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4\), such that for any \(\beta\in (0,1)\), any \(N\in \N\) and any \(R\geq 0\), we have
  \[
    c_1 \log\Bigl( 1+ \frac{N}{1+R^2}\Bigr) \, \cV\bigl( c_2\, \e^{\th(N,\beta)} \bigr)
    \leq \Var\bigl[ Z_{N}^{\beta,\w}(U_R) \bigr]
    \leq c_3 \log\Bigl( 1+ \frac{N}{1+R^2}\Bigr) \, \cV\bigl( c_4\, \e^{\th(N,\beta)} \bigr) \,,
  \]
  Note that \(\e^{\th(N,\beta)} = (1+o(1)) \e^{\alpha}\,  N \e^{ -\frac{\pi}{\sigma^2(\beta)}}\) as \(N\to\infty\) (uniformly in \(\beta\in(0,1)\)), recalling~\eqref{RN-asym}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  that by time $T_{\text{acc}} = L_0^{3/2}$, there exist at least $N = \lceil \frac{\bar{\rho}_0}{4} L_0^{1/4} \rceil$ green

  $C_{\textnormal{\tiny (C:accumulation of the paper)}}, c_{\textnormal{\tiny (c:accumulation of the paper)}} > 0$ such that
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}_{\rho_0}({E}_{1}^c) \le C_{\textnormal{\tiny (C:accumulation of the paper)}} (\rho_0 + 1) L_0^{2d} \exp\braces*{ -c_{\textnormal{\tiny (c:accumulation of the paper)}} \bar{\rho}_0 L_0^{1/4} }.
  \end{equation}

body:
[Definition infinity squared of arXiv:2608.25889, 'Slope Inequalities for the Geography Problem of Spin Symplectic 4-Manifolds'] We say that a smooth oriented $4$-manifold $M$\/ has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible smooth $4$-manifolds
that are all homeomorphic to $M$.  
We say that $M$\/ has $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible symplectic $4$-manifolds and infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible nonsymplectic $4$-manifolds, all of which are homeomorphic to $M$.  
We also say that a symmetric bilinear form has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if it is the intersection form of a 
simply connected smooth $4$-manifold with $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-property, respectively.
title: Definition infinity squared of arXiv:2608.25889

[Corollary cor:symmetric-3 of arXiv:2606.24881, 'Queues with Correlated Service Times --- the $M/M_D/c$ Model'] For $c=3$, we have,
\begin{align}
   \mu^{(1)}_{(1)} & = \mu_{(1)} + 2  \mu_{(2)} + \mu_{(3)} = \mu_i + 2 \mu_{ij} + \mu_{123}, \\
   \mu^{(2)}_{(1)} & = \mu_{(1)} + \mu_{(2)} = \mu_i + \mu_{ij}, \\
   \mu^{(2)}_{(2)} & = \mu_{(2)} + \mu_{(3)} = \mu_{ij} + \mu_{123}, \\
   \mu^{(3)}_{(1)} & = \mu_{(1)} = \mu_i, \\

body:
[Lemma L:basis-for-comparison of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $y_1 \le y_2 \in \mathbb{Z}, t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_1,t]_{\textsf{L}}$ and $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_2,t]_{\textsf{L}}$, and take $f:\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Then for any $E:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \le E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \ge x\}$. Similarly, 
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \ge E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \le x\}$.

Let $X$ be $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\mathbb{R}^M$ with covariance $\Sigma$. Split the rows into two independent parts of sizes $m$ and $n - m$ with sample covariances $S_1 = V_1\Lambda_1 V_1^T$ and $S_2$. The nonparametric eigenvalue-regularised covariance estimator is $\hat\Sigma = V_1 \operatorname{diag}(V_1^T S_2 V_1)\, V_1^T$, averaged over $K$ random splits. Then: (i) $\mathbb{E}[V_1^T S_2 V_1 \mid V_1] = V_1^T \Sigma V_1$, so each diagonal entry $v_i^T S_2 v_i$ is an unbiased estimate of the population variance in the direction $v_i$ - the Ledoit-Peche oracle $d_i^* = v_i^T\Sigma v_i$ evaluated on independent data; (ii) as $M, n \to \infty$ with $M/n \to c > 0$ and $m/n \to r \in (0,1)$, $\hat\Sigma$ is asymptotically optimal in Frobenius loss among estimators of the form $V_1 D V_1^T$ with $D$ diagonal (Lam 2016, Theorem 1); (iii) $\hat\Sigma$ is positive semidefinite and carries no bandwidth, floor or shrinkage constant beyond the split fraction (Lam recommends choosing $m$ by minimising $\|\hat\Sigma_m - S\|_F$ over a grid; $m = n/2$ is the usual default). A population direction of genuinely small variance keeps a small estimate (its held-out variance is small too); a direction whose small sample variance was a finite-sample cancellation receives the variance it actually has out of sample.
rows i.i.d. with finite fourth moments
M/n -> c > 0, m/n -> r in (0,1)
the two parts of the split are disjoint (independence of V_1 and S_2 is what carries the argument)

Let X be a compact Hausdorff space and let A be a subalgebra of C(X, R), the continuous real functions with the supremum norm, such that A contains the constant functions and separates points (for x != y in X there is f in A with f(x) != f(y)). Then A is dense in C(X, R). Complex form: a subalgebra of C(X, C) that contains the constants, separates points, and is closed under complex conjugation is dense in C(X, C). The Weierstrass approximation theorem is the case X = [a, b] with A the polynomials: every continuous real function on [a, b] is a uniform limit of polynomials.

[Defi 59 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] The string $s\in [k]_0^{K}$ is \textbf{collision-likely} (we write $s\in \CL$) if $s$ satisfies the following properties.
		\begin{itemize}
			\item The first $\alpha_{\tot}\log(N)$ digits of $s$ form a collision-likely prefix.
			\item $s[g_1]=\ileft^{(g_1)}$, $s[g_2]=\iright^{(g_2)}$. (Recall \eqref{def:ileft-right}.)
            \item $s[t]=l^{(t)}_{\Max}$ for all $t\in [\alpha_{\tot}+1,\cdots,\alpha_{\tot}+\lfloor2\rho\log N\rfloor]\backslash\{g_1,g_2\}$.
			\item For all $(i,l)\in T$, we have \[
            s \mbox{ contains } \beta_l^{(i)}\log(N) \mbox{ of } l\mbox{-digits in } \{\alpha_{\tot}+\lfloor2\rho\log N\rfloor+1\leq t\leq K: \bn^{(t)}/N\in D_i\}.
            \]
		\end{itemize}
title: Definition 59 of arXiv:2510.22783

[Defi 34 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] Let $c\colon [t_0,t_1]\to A$ be a smooth admissible curve and set $\gamma:=\pi\circ c$. Let $b\in \Gamma(\gamma^*A)$ be a smooth section along $\gamma$. Then there is a well-defined section $\mathcal{T}_c(b)\in \Gamma(c^*TA)$ defined as follows: Let $A_U\cong U\times\mathbb{A}$ be a vector-bundle trivialization such that $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ for a subinterval of $[t_0,t_1]$. Write $r_x\colon \mathbb{A}\to T_xM$ for the local representative of the anchor, \Cref{loctho}. In the trivialisation we identify
\begin{align} c(t)=(\gamma(t),a(t)),\quad b(t)=(\gamma(t),\beta(t)),  \text{ then define }  \notag\\ 
\mathcal{T}_c(b)(t) = \left( \gamma(t), a(t), r_{\gamma(t)}(\beta(t)), \frac{d\beta}{dt}(t)+C_{\gamma(t)}(a(t),\beta(t)) \right), 
\end{align} where $C$ is the local structure map from \Cref{locbrac} \eqref{loctrivrbracket}.

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] The stochastic convolution driver $Y=(Z,Z_\tau)$ has a centred Radon
Gaussian version in $\mathsf Y^+$.  Consequently, for every $\delta>0$
there is a compact set $\mathfrak L\subset\mathsf Y^+$ such that
\begin{align}
 p_{\mathfrak L}:=\mathbf P\{Y\in\mathfrak L\}>0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{y\in\mathfrak L}\|y\|_{\mathsf Y}<\delta.
\end{align}
The version in $\mathsf Y^+$ may be chosen from the same Fourier partial
sums as the canonical $\mathsf Y$ valued version, and hence the two agree
almost surely.

[Theorem KALOKAIRI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $\varrho (N)$ be a sequence of probability measures on
  $\hat{U} (N)$ such that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N} \log \text{} S_{\varrho (N)}^{U
    (N)} (u_1, \ldots, u_r, 1^{N - r}) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (u_i),
    
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is an analytic function in a complex neighborhood of $1$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $1^r$. Then the random measure
  $N^{- 1} \sum_{i = 1}^N \delta \left( \frac{\lambda_i + N - i}{N} \right)$, converges,
  as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in probability, in the sense of moments to a
  deterministic measure $\mathbf{m}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, whose moments are given
  by
  \begin{equation}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}} t^k \mathbf{m} (d \text{} t) = \sum_{m = 0}^k
    \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} (x^k
    (\Psi' (x))^{k - m}) \right|_{x = 1} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm replaceprinciple of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] [TVuniversality] 
 For every  $n\geq 1$  let $A_n, B_n$ be two random $n \times n$  matrices. 
 Assume that the following two conditions hold. 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item The sequence 
     \[\frac{1}{n} \left(\|A_n\|_{HS}^2 + \|B_n\|_{HS}^2\right)
     \]
     is bounded in probability, where $\|\cdot\|_{HS}$ denotes the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a matrix.
     \item For almost all complex number $z$,
     \[
     \frac{1}{n}\log \left|\det\left(A_n-zI_n\right)\right|-\frac{1}{n}\log \left|\det\left(B_n-zI_n\right)\right|
     \]
     converges in probability to $0$.
 \end{enumerate}
 Then $\mu_{A_n}-\mu_{B_n}$ converges in probability to $0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
