metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:844622c62e06c96b73b824de4c77570e511f717d0ec5426637ecc4bb0b48a021","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/84/844622c62e06c96b73b824de4c77570e511f717d0ec5426637ecc4bb0b48a021.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:954195ca0ea5fbedb34d3515cee6ee4ed30a69adfb4e177323269a4b8125cfec","bundle_entry_key":"claim-012","bundle_id":"population.adam-global-critical-cap-and-uncorrected-tracking-obstruction-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"deterministic adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-global-standard-initialization-convergence-at-subcritical-critical-epsilon-cap","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-012 v2; target1; kind special; independently checked proof; reviewer012v2 PASS.

STATEMENT
Let f(x)=lambda x^2/2 with lambda>0, and run scalar deterministic full-batch
Adam, corrected with the usual separate moments from time0 or uncorrected,
epsilon added OUTSIDE sqrt. Suppose m0=v0=0, eta,epsilon>0,
0<b<sqrt(d)<1, and
 eta lambda/epsilon <= 2(1+b)/(1-b).                         (1)
Then every finite initial x0 has x_t,m_t,v_t->0. If (1) is strict, x and
m decay at some geometric rate. Applied coordinatewise, the same holds
for any finite positive diagonal quadratic satisfying (1) in each channel.

At b=.9,d=.999, p=1 and H=38 I_2, scaled top curvature tends to38 for
every standard initial position, and scaled active curvature tends to38
at times when it is defined. This critical case has no tiny-start
restriction. The theorem is special progress on target1's boundary, not
a solution of p>1 or of generic supercritical p=1 tracking.

HARDEST OPEN PIECE
For a cap above38, the matrix comparison used below loses definiteness
near the edge and does not control nonlinear oscillation amplitudes.
Global critical convergence alone also does not give the ratio-coordinate
entry required by claim006 for arbitrary starts just above the threshold.

PRIMARY IDENTITY AND CONVENTIONS
Fong-Yang 2608.20638v2, Appendix F PDFpp41-43, Eq44-59, gives the adaptive
quadratic form used below for the uncorrected map. Their Proposition F.2
assumes wmax>2 and proves contraction only below W<2; it does not state
the critical/subcritical-cap theorem proved here. We use the algebraic
matrix identity, and supply the new cap inequality and bias correction.
No claim of exhaustive literature novelty is made.

Put c=(1-b)/(1+b), a=c eta lambda/2, e=epsilon-a>=0. For t>=1 use
 n_t=m_t/(1-b^t), u_t=v_t/(1-d^t)                            (2)
in the corrected case, and n_t=m_t,u_t=v_t in the raw case. If x0=0,
the state stays zero and the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise v1>0,
so u_t>0 for every t>=1. Define
 h_t=x_t+n_t/(c lambda), z_t=(x_t,h_t)^T,
 w_t=2a/(sqrt(u_t)+epsilon),
 theta_t=w_t/(2-w_t)=a/(sqrt(u_t)+e),
 P_t=diag(1,b theta_t), Psi_t=z_t^T P_t z_t.                 (3)
All these quantities are finite and P_t positive definite for t>=1,
including e=0 because u_t>0. Moreover 0<w_t<2.

CORRECTED RECURSION
For t>=1 let
 b_t=b(1-b^t)/(1-b^(t+1)),
 d_t=d(1-d^t)/(1-d^(t+1))                                  (4)
in the corrected case, and b_t=b,d_t=d in the raw case. Directly from
the moment definitions,
 n_(t+1)=b_t n_t+(1-b_t)lambda x_t,
 u_(t+1)=d_t u_t+(1-d_t)lambda^2 x_t^2,
 x_(t+1)=x_t-eta n_(t+1)/(sqrt(u_(t+1))+epsilon).
Put k_t=1+2(b-b_t)/(1-b). Exact substitution gives
 z_(t+1)=B_t(w_(t+1)) z_t,
 B_t(w)=[[1-w k_t,-w b_t],[1+(1-w)k_t,(1-w)b_t]].           (5)
Since b_t=b+O(b^t), B_t(w)=A(w)+O(b^t) uniformly for 0<=w<=2, where
 A(w)=[[1-w,-bw],[2-w,b(1-w)]].
The matrix formulas, not numerical approximations, are checked in
scripts/check_critical_matrix.py and logs/critical_matrix_exact.json.

IDEAL LYAPUNOV COMPARISON
Since u_(t+1)>=d_t u_t and e>=0,
 theta_(t+1)/theta_t
  =(sqrt(u_t)+e)/(sqrt(u_(t+1))+e) <=1/sqrt(d_t).             (6)
Choose once and for all b^2<d0<d and a finite T with d_t>=d0 for t>=T.
Then b theta_(t+1)<theta_t for t>=T.
For positive y,Y, direct multiplication gives
 E=diag(1,y)-A(w)^T diag(1,Y) A(w),
 E11=(2-w)[w-(2-w)Y],
 det E=[w-(2-w)Y][(2-w)y-b^2 w].                            (7)
Set w=w_(t+1), y=b theta_t, Y=b theta_(t+1).
The first bracket in (7) is (1-b)w>0. The second is positive by
theta_t>b theta_(t+1), using theta(w)=w/(2-w). Sylvester gives
 A(w_(t+1))^T P_(t+1) A(w_(t+1)) < P_t, t>=T.               (8)

SUMMABLE CORRECTION ERRORS WITHOUT ASSUMING BOUNDEDNESS
Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz on the raw standard-zero-moment sums gives
 |m_t| <=K sqrt(v_t),
 K^2=(1-b)^2/[(1-d)(1-b^2/d)]<infinity.                    (9)
In corrected Adam sqrt(u_t)>=sqrt(v_t) and 1-b^t>=1-b, so
 |n_t|/sqrt(u_t)<=K/(1-b); the same upper bound works in raw Adam.
Each step therefore obeys |x_(t+1)-x_t|<=eta K/(1-b).
Thus |x_t|<=C(1+t), u_t<=C(1+t)^2. Also
 u_t>=v_t>=d^(t-1)v1 for all t>=1. All constants below are finite and
may depend on this fixed nonzero initial state and the fixed parameters.
It follows from (3) that
 ||P_t||<=C d^(-t/2), lambda_min(P_t)>=1/[C(1+t)].           (10)
For e>0 the first bound is loose but still valid. Equations (5),(10)
and boundedness of A(w) on [0,2] imply
 ||B_t^T P_(t+1) B_t-A(w_(t+1))^T P_(t+1) A(w_(t+1))||
 <=C b^t d^(-t/2).
Together with (8) this gives
 Psi_(t+1)<=(1+e_t)Psi_t,
 0<=e_t=C(1+t)(b/sqrt(d))^t, sum_(t>=T)e_t<infinity.       (11)
For raw Adam the perturbation is zero; the same positive majorant is
allowed. Hence Psi_t is bounded, |x_t| is bounded, and the variance
recursion now gives a uniform bound u_t<=U for all sufficiently large t.

VANISHING VARIANCE
Fix any delta>0. Whenever t>=T and u_t>=delta,
 d0 delta<=u_(t+1)<=U, and delta<=u_t<=U.
Thus (u_t,u_(t+1)) lies in a compact set with positive lower bounds,
obeying the closed restriction u_(t+1)>=d0 u_t. On that set the matrices
in (8) have a UNIFORM strict relative gap: there is kappa_delta>0 with
 A(w_(t+1))^T P_(t+1) A(w_(t+1)) <=(1-kappa_delta)P_t.
Indeed the two brackets of (7) are strictly positive with uniform margin,
by b/sqrt(d0)<1; all matrix entries and P_t are continuous on this compact
set. The actual perturbation relative to P_t tends to zero by (11), so
 Psi_(t+1)<=(1-kappa_delta/2)Psi_t                         (12)
at all sufficiently late times with u_t>=delta.

Let L_t=product_(j=T)^(t-1)(1+e_j), a positive bounded product, and put
Q_t=Psi_t/L_t. By (11), Q_t is nonincreasing. If u_t>=delta infinitely
often, (12) forces Q_t->0, hence Psi_t->0 and x_t->0. The stable raw
variance recursion then gives v_t->0 and u_t->0, contradicting those
infinitely many visits. Therefore for every delta>0 only finitely many
u_t>=delta occur: u_t->0. The raw variance recurrence
 (1-d)lambda^2 x_t^2=v_(t+1)-d v_t
then gives x_t->0, and the stable raw first-moment recursion gives m_t->0.
This proves the global assertion.

STRICTLY SUBCRITICAL CAP
If e>0, allow u_t=0 as well in the final compact-set argument. Now
w_t<=2a/epsilon<2, and theta_t is uniformly bounded above and below on
0<=u_t<=U. Inequality theta_(t+1)<=theta_t/sqrt(d0) remains valid even
at zero. The same compact argument gives one uniform relative gap at
every sufficiently large t. Since the relative correction errors tend
to zero, Psi_t decays geometrically. Therefore so do x_t and h_t, and
n_t=c lambda(h_t-x_t), hence raw m_t, decay geometrically too.

DIAGONAL CRITICAL CURVATURE
Apply the scalar theorem independently to each diagonal channel. If all
lambda_i=2(1+b)epsilon/[(1-b)eta], every denominator tends to epsilon,
and every scaled preconditioned eigenvalue tends to theta=2(1+b)/(1-b).
Their maximum and any defined weighted active average have the same
limit. At b=.9,epsilon=eta,H=38 I_2, that limit is38. A coordinate that
starts at zero stays there and has curvature exactly38/eta; no issue
arises for the top eigenvalue. If the entire gradient is zero at a time,
the quotient defining active curvature is undefined there; the assertion
about active curvature is explicitly along times when it is defined.

LIMITS
No linear-rate assertion is made at equality e=0. Neither an explicit
uniform attraction rate nor an enlargement of claim006's supercritical
basin follows. Convergence of raw coordinates to zero does not imply
bounded ratios m/x or v/x^2. No beta2<=beta1^2 conclusion is asserted.
The proof is analytic inequalities plus exact algebra, not a floating-point
or Lean certificate. Newness of this global threshold must be checked
against further primary literature; its mathematical proof has independent reviewer012v2 PASS. No literature-priority claim is made here.


Large-start finite-run caveat: reviewer critical-cap x0=1e6 run takes order1e6 steps at roughly unit displacement in its normalization; no uniform attraction rate asserted.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.29747, 'Reduced Khovanov-Rozansky homology'] \cite{soergel1990kategorie}
In the category of Soergel bimodules $\mathrm{SBim}_n$, we have the following isomorphisms:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\B_i\B_j \cong \B_j\B_i$ for all $i, j$ with $|i-j| > 1$,
    \item $\B_i\B_{i+1}\B_i \oplus \B_{i+1} \cong \B_{i+1}\B_i\B_{i+1} \oplus \B_i$, and
    \item $\B_i^2 \cong (q+q^{-1}) \B_i$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  \int_0^\infty \mathrm{cMMSE}_\mu(t)\,dt
  &\ge
  0.05\int_0^\infty\mathrm{RD}_\mu(t)\,dt.
  
\end{align}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  b(T)\ge\frac{1}{80\pi}R(T).
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bernoulli width dominates the rate--distortion area

For bond percolation on Z^d with d >= 2: (a) p_c >= 1/(2d - 1), and in particular p_c > 0. (b) p_c < 1, and for d = 2 the Peierls contour argument gives an explicit bound: p_c^{bond}(Z^2) <= 1 - q_0 where q_0 > 0 is any solution of sum_{n >= 4} 4 n 3^{n-1} q^n < 1. The two halves use completely different mechanisms: (a) is a first-moment count on self-avoiding paths, comparing the cluster to a branching process with mean offspring (2d-1)p, and (b) is a first-moment count on DUAL CIRCUITS surrounding the origin. Note that (a) gives only a bound and not the value; the true p_c(Z^d) is strictly larger than 1/(2d-1) in every dimension, and for Z^2 the bound 1/3 is far from the exact value 1/2. Since p_c(Z^d) is nonincreasing in d - a d-dimensional slab embeds in dimension d+1 - part (b) for d = 2 gives p_c < 1 in every d >= 2 at once. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Sections 1.4 and 1.5]
bond percolation on Z^d, d >= 2
(b) uses planar duality and is stated for d = 2; higher d follows by monotonicity of p_c in d
the counting bounds are deliberate over-counts and the resulting numerical bounds are not sharp

Let z_k be an exogenous time-homogeneous Markov chain on {1,...,N}, with row-stochastic transition matrix P=(p_ij), and let H_1,...,H_N be fixed real d-by-d matrices. Consider the homogeneous recursion xi_(k+1)=H_(z_k)xi_k. Define the Nd^2-by-Nd^2 matrix L by block L_(j,i)=p_ij(H_i tensor H_i), equivalently L=(P^T tensor I_(d^2))diag_i(H_i tensor H_i), using columnwise vectorization and stacking moments by chain state. Then the following are equivalent: (i) E[||xi_k||^2 | z_0=i,xi_0=x] tends to zero as k tends to infinity for EVERY state i and EVERY x in R^d; (ii) rho(L)<1; (iii) there are C<infinity and 0<r<1 such that E[||xi_k||^2 | z_0=i,xi_0=x]<=C r^k ||x||^2 for every i,x,k. No irreducibility, aperiodicity, stationary initialization, or invertibility of H_i is required. The quantifier over all initial states matters: for a single fixed initial law, an inaccessible unstable state need not obstruct decay. In linear TD take H_i=I+alpha A_i in Hu?Syed notation (or I-alpha A_i with the opposite sign convention). This is a homogeneous second-moment stability criterion, not an assertion that noisy constant-step affine TD converges almost surely to a point.
Finite number of Markov states and finite dimension d
Exogenous time-homogeneous chain and deterministic state-dependent matrices
Homogeneous recursion, without additive forcing
Mean-square decay quantified over every deterministic initial state and vector
Departure-state matrix H_i and columnwise vectorization

body: In mathematics, the Chinese remainder theorem states that if one knows the remainders of the Euclidean division of an integer n by several integers, then one can determine uniquely the remainder of the division of n by the product of these integers, under the condition that the divisors are pairwise coprime.
title: Chinese remainder theorem

body: Theorem 3.8 (l_infinity-norm bound for eigenvectors of B~ and B). Let B and B~ be the non-backtracking operator and the reduced non-backtracking operator of a (d, k)-regular hypergraph, respectively, and let d, k be fixed. Then the following holds. (1) Let v_i be a unit eigenvector of A associated with the eigenvalue lambda_i, and let u_i, u'_i be unit eigenvectors of B~ associated with two eigenvalues mu_i, mu'_i, which are given by the solutions of mu^2 - (lambda_i - k + 2) mu + (d - 1)(k - 1) = 0.   (6) Then for all i in [n], ||u_i||_inf, ||u'_i||_inf <= ||v_i||_inf. (2) For a random (d, k)-regular [hyper]graph, let w_i, w'_i be unit eigenvectors of B associated with two eigenvalues mu_i, mu'_i given by (6) with mu_i, mu'_i not in {1, -(k - 1)}. Then, for d > k >= 3, with high probability, for all i in [n], ||w_i||_inf, ||w'_i||_inf <= ((sqrt(k - 1) + o(1)) / (sqrt(d - 1) - sqrt(k - 1))) ||v_i||_inf.

[Lemma lem:low-degree-star of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] Let $\Delta\ge3$ be an integer, put $k=\Delta(\Delta-1)$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a set of $k$ colors.  Let $G$ be a simple graph with $\Delta(G)\le\Delta$, and let $u\in V(G)$ with $t=d_G(u)\le\Delta-1$.  Every $B$-coloring of $G-S_u$ with colors
from $\mathcal C$ extends to a $B$-coloring of $G$ with colors from $\mathcal C$.

Moreover, if $uv\in E(G)$ and $G-uv$ has a $B$-coloring with colors from $\mathcal C$, then the edges $ux$, where
$x\in N_G(u)\setminus\{v\}$, may be uncolored and all edges of $S_u$ recolored to obtain a $B$-coloring of $G$ without changing the colors outside $S_u$.

[Definition 99 (Geometric $L^2$ norms) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] We define the $L^2$ weighted norms with respect to the area and volume forms introduced 
	in Def.\,\ref{D:VOLFORMS}. 
	Recall that we measure the norm of $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfields with $\gtorus$, i.e.,
	if $\upxi$ is a type $\binom{0}{2}$ $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfield, then
	$|\upxi|_{\gtorus}^2 \eqdef (\gtorus^{-1})^{\alpha \beta}(\gtorus^{-1})^{\sigma \delta} \upxi_{\alpha \sigma} \upxi_{\beta \delta}$. 
	Then for scalar functions or $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfields $\upxi$ and positive numbers $q$, 
	we define: 
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align}
			\| \upxi \|_{L_{q}^2\left(\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}\right)}
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\left( 	\int_{\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}} 
			|\upxi|_{\gtorus}^2 \, \weight^{q}
			\, \voldoublenulltori 
			\right)^{1/2},
			& 
			\| \upxi \|_{L_{q}^2\left(\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}\right)} 
			& \eqdef 
			\left( 
			\int_{\outgoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{u}{I}} |\upxi|_{\gtorus}^2 \, \weight^{q} \, \voloutgoingnullhypersurface 
			\right)^{1/2}, 
			 
			\\
			\| \upxi \|_{L_{q}^2\left(\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}\right)}
			& 
			\eqdef \left( 
			\int_{\ingoingcharacteristicsurfacetwoarg{\ubar}{J}} |\upxi|_{\gtorus}^2 \, \weight^{q}
			\, \volingoingnullhypersurface 
			\right)^{1/2}, 
			& 
			\| \upxi \|_{L_{q}^2\left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}\right)} 
			& \eqdef 
			\left( 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{I}{J}} |\upxi|_{\gtorus}^2 \, \weight^{q} \, \voldiamond 
			\right)^{1/2}.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}

Let $(K_\varepsilon)$ be an approximate identity on $\mathbb R^d$ ($\int K_\varepsilon=1$, $\sup\|K_\varepsilon\|_1<\infty$, $\int_{|x|\ge\delta}|K_\varepsilon|\to0$ for each $\delta>0$). (a) If $f\in L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ with $1\le p<\infty$, then $\|f*K_\varepsilon-f\|_p\to0$. (b) If $f$ is bounded and uniformly continuous, $f*K_\varepsilon\to f$ uniformly. (c) If $f\in L^\infty$ and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $(f*K_\varepsilon)(x_0)\to f(x_0)$. (d) If $K_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-d}K(x/\varepsilon)$ where $\int K=1$ and $|K|\le\psi$ for some radial, radially nonincreasing, integrable $\psi$, then for $f\in L^p$, $1\le p\le\infty$, $(f*K_\varepsilon)(x)\to f(x)$ at every Lebesgue point $x$ of $f$, hence almost everywhere, and $\sup_\varepsilon|f*K_\varepsilon|\le\|\psi\|_1Mf$ with $M$ the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. Part (a) fails for $p=\infty$ (each $f*K_\varepsilon$ is continuous, so an $f\in L^\infty$ with no continuous representative cannot be a uniform limit of them). The same statements hold on $\mathbb T$ with the kernels $F_N$ (Fejer) and $P_r$ (Poisson).
(K_eps) is an approximate identity in L^1(R^d): unit integral, uniformly bounded L^1 norms, L^1 mass outside every fixed ball tending to 0
(a): f in L^p with 1 <= p < infinity (p = infinity excluded)
(b): f bounded and uniformly continuous
(c): f essentially bounded and continuous at x_0
(d): dilation structure K_eps = eps^{-d}K(x/eps) with an integrable radially nonincreasing majorant of |K|

For a real symmetric block matrix M = [[A, B], [B^T, C]], M is positive semidefinite if and only if A is positive semidefinite, the range of B is contained in the range of A, and the generalized Schur complement C - B^T A^+ B is positive semidefinite (A^+ the Moore-Penrose inverse). The range condition cannot be dropped: A = 0, B = 1, C = 1 has generalized Schur complement 1 >= 0, but M = [[0, 1], [1, 1]] has determinant -1. (A. Albert, 1969.)
M is real symmetric
A^+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse of A

    	I_{k,i} := [iL_k, (i+1)L_k), \quad i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0},

    so that each scale-\((k+1)\) block $I_{k+1,i}$ consist of $\lfloor L_{k}^{\gamma-1}\rfloor$ many scale-$k$ blocks, i.e., $\#\{m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0} \colon  I_{k,m}\cap I_{k+1,i}\neq\emptyset\} = \lfloor L_{k}^{\gamma-1}\rfloor$.
    On the initial scale, we call a block $I_{0,i}$ {\em good} if $I_{0,i}\cap X \neq \emptyset$. For general $k\in\mathbb{N}$, we call the scale-\(k\) block $I_{k,i}$ {\em good} if it either
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item contains no more than one bad scale-\((k-1)\) sub-block or      
        \item if it contains exactly two consecutive bad sub-blocks, i.e., there exists \(m\) such that \(I_{k-1,m}, I_{k-1,m+1}\subset I_{k,i}\) are bad but all other sub-blocks \(I_{k-1,n}\subset I_{k,i}\) are good themselves.   
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 46 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] For every irregular, connected graph $H$ with maximum degree $\Delta \ge 2$ and all $\delta, \eps >0$, there is a constant $K$ such that the following holds.
  Suppose that either $p_H \cdot (\log n)^K \ll p \ll 1$ or $p_H \cdot (\log \log n)^K \ll p \ll 1$ and $H$ is stable.
  Then,
  \[
    \log \Pr(X\geq(1+\delta)\Ex[X]) \ge - (1+\eps)\cdot \psi_H^*(\delta+\eps),
  \]
  provided that $n$ is sufficiently large.

[Lemma fenzifenmu of arXiv:2605.27949, 'Yaglom limits of continuous-state branching processes in Brownian random environment \than'] Let $\left(X_t\right)_{t >0}$ and $\left(Y_t\right)_{t >0}$ be two families of non-negative, real-valued random variables. Assume that there exist functions from $(0, \infty)$ to $(0, \infty)$ denoted as $c_1(t)$ and $c_2(t)$, respectively, and constants $a_1, a_2 \in(0, \infty)$ such that
$$\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} c_1(t) \mathbb E X_t=a_1,\quad \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} c_2(t) \mathbb E Y_t=a_2,$$
$$

$$
\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\mathbb E\left[1-\mathrm{e}^{-z X_t}\right]}{\mathbb E\left[1-\mathrm{e}^{-z Y_t}\right]}=\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a_1 c_2(t)}{a_2 c_1(t)}.
$$

\]

\mathbb P\left(F(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\leq\alpha\right)\leq\alpha.

	Formally, at least one vertex making first appearance at step-$i$ is a gap witness-vertex for some block-step at the walk, specifically at step-$t$.

	(a) For $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, $\mathbb{Q}^\omega_\tau \in \mathscr{M}_{\gamma,\delta}(Y_\tau(\omega))$. \\

\lim_{y\to-\infty}\psi(y)=1.

Then
\[
\psi(u)\sim\psi_{\rm cl}(u)\sim\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{\Lambda\mu}{c-\Lambda\mu}\right]\bar F_I(u),\qquad u\to\infty.
\]

body:
[Theorem thm:spectral-lattice-induction of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $\eta$ be an ergodic translation-invariant point process on
$\mathbb R$ with positive intensity $\rho$ and local second
moments. If
\[
    \int_{0<|\xi|<1}
    \frac{1}{\xi^2}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi)<\infty,
\]
then the translation action of $\eta$ has a nonzero eigenvalue.
Consequently, $\eta$ is lattice-induced.

body: [Lemma of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] Fix $q \in (0,1)$, $\delta \in (0,1)$, and let $z_n$ be a sequence in $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{z_n}{n} = z > \delta + 1$. Let $B_{n}$ be the event that the rightmost geodesic for $G_{\mathrm{FS}}$ (in full-space) from $(1+ \lfloor \delta n \rfloor,1)$ to $(z_n,n)$ never uses a vertex $\omega'_{(i,j)}$ with $i \le j$. That is, $B_n$ is the event where the geodesic stays strictly to the right of the main diagonal line $i = j$. Then, there exist constants $A,\alpha > 0$ so  that $\mathbb P(B_n^C) \le A e^{-\alpha n}$.
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classificat'

body:
Let $f: M \to M$ be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of a Riemannian manifold. A compact set $\Lambda \subset M$ with $f(\Lambda) = \Lambda$ is (uniformly) hyperbolic if there are constants $C > 0$, $0 < \lambda < 1$ and, at every $x \in \Lambda$, a splitting $T_x M = E^s(x) \oplus E^u(x)$ such that (i) the splitting is $Df$-invariant: $Df_x E^s(x) = E^s(f x)$ and $Df_x E^u(x) = E^u(f x)$; (ii) $\|Df^n_x v\| \le C \lambda^n \|v\|$ for $v \in E^s(x)$, $n \ge 0$; (iii) $\|Df^{-n}_x v\| \le C \lambda^n \|v\|$ for $v \in E^u(x)$, $n \ge 0$. The subbundles are then automatically continuous in $x$, and the constant $C$ can be made 1 by changing to an adapted (Lyapunov) metric. The dimensions of $E^s$ and $E^u$ are locally constant on $\Lambda$. Either bundle may be trivial: $E^s = 0$ everywhere gives an expanding set (repeller), $E^u = 0$ a contracting set (attracting periodic orbit). The word 'uniform' matters: a set on which contraction and expansion rates exist at every point but with no uniform $C, \lambda$ (nonuniform hyperbolicity in the sense of Pesin) is NOT a hyperbolic set in this sense, and the stable/unstable manifold theorem below applies to it only in a weaker, measure-theoretic form.
f is a C^1 diffeomorphism of a Riemannian manifold M
Lambda is compact and f(Lambda) = Lambda
the constants C and lambda < 1 are uniform over Lambda
title: Uniformly hyperbolic set of a diffeomorphism

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] Let $q\ge0, p\ge2$, and let
$A\in C^1(\R_+)$ be non-negative, non-decreasing and satisfy $|A(t)|\le K(1+t^q)$,
for some constant $K>0$. Let $F\in C^2(\R)$ satisfying that 
 $F$ is non-decreasing, $F''$ is non-decreasing, and 
    $|F(x)|\le K_F(1+|x|^p)$, for some constant $K_F$.
Suppose in addition  $\int_0^\infty t^{q+p/2}\,\mu_n(\mathrm dt)<\infty$.
Then, for every $\rho\in\mbox{ConsStop}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n)$ and every
$i=1,\ldots,n$,
$$
    \E[A(\sigma_i)F(X_{\sigma_i})]
    \ge
    \E[A(\rho_i)F(X_{\rho_i})].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 8 of arXiv:2608.27374

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.17493, 'Integrals of some compound processes'] Let $T>0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $M\sim CP(\lambda, F)$, measurable real functions $g,f_1,\dots,f_n\in\mathcal{L}^1[0,T]$. For $0\le t\le T$, define
	$$Y_1(t) = \int_0^t g\big(M(s)\big) f_1(s) \dif s,\ \ \ Y_k(t) = \int_0^t Y_{k-1}(s)f_k(s)\dif s,\ k=2,\dots, n. $$
	Then, the probability law $p(t,\dif x, y)\dif y = P\{M(t)\in\dif x, Y_1(t)\in \dif y_1,\dots, Y_n(t)\in \dif y_n\}$ satisfies
	\begin{align}
		\frac{\partial}{\partial t}p(t, \dif x, y)+ g(x)f_1(t)& \frac{\partial}{\partial y_1}p(t, \dif x, y) + \sum_{k=2}^n y_{k-1} f_k(t)\frac{\partial}{\partial y_{k}}p(t, \dif x, y) \nonumber\\
		& = \lambda(t) \Big(I-C_F^{(x)}\Big) p(t, \dif x, y) , \ \ \ t\in [0,T],\ x,y_1,\dots,y_n \in\mathbb{R}, 
	\end{align}	
	subject to $p(0,\dif x, y) = \delta_0(\dif x, y)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.17493

body:
Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit pending. # Coprime alphabet/support sizes remove the saturation obstruction

T379-C019 v2: proof (unaudited), exact checks PASS; independent audit pending.
Target 1, secondary target 2. Arbitrary VC dimension and unequal known
truth counts, including saturation; conditional robust small-budget
game only. General noncoprime saturated mixtures and larger budgets
remain open here.

## Model and statement

Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K be integers with gcd(r,K-r)=1. There
are d unresolved A/S context pairs and N-2d fixed known S contexts.
Each S has all K truths; each A has an independent uniform r-subset.
The factual law chooses contexts uniformly then uniformly true within
context. Actual iid factual samples have no orientation tags. An
optional independent verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths
in each variable context, including S, without orientation labels.
Let C_x be the distinct observed-plus-certified truth union. Condition
on ANY positive-probability data outcome with j_x=|C_x|<=r in every
variable context. Thus no orientation is logically excluded. Some
contexts may have j_x=r; sibling counts and sample repetitions may
differ arbitrarily. Actual orientation likelihoods need not be equal.

Write h_i=min(j_left,j_right) and D_h=#{i:h_i=h},0<=h<=r. Put

 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)), M_h=D_h*(2-h/r-h/K)/N,
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

For every 0<=c<1/(2NrK), the proposed exact all-generator conditional
worst-world frontier under source Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY compatible
world is

 V(c)=tau_0*(T_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.          (1)

Source miscalibration is TV(g,p_Pi) using uniform coarsening of p in
exact g-probability bins. The same-data partition-supplied WORST-
ORIENTATION oracle has frontier

 O(c)=alpha_0*(Q_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+,       (2)

where alpha_h=2tau_h,A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr),Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t.
In particular A_r=0: a saturated oracle group has zero residual mass,
so its risk-one coefficient must NOT be used to infer a nonzero slope.
The exact zero-budget estimation penalty is

 V(0)-O(0)=sum_i h_i*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h_i)).              (3)

No exact endpoint, largest interval, actual-world-only calibration or
global expected minimax identity is claimed. This extends C017 to
saturation under the coprime arithmetic hypothesis, using a possibly
smaller interval. It does not contradict C016/C018's noncoprime cases.

## Discrete source-bin mass rigidity

Fix any robustly c-feasible generator g and its exact score partition
Pi. For every compatible world and every cell B, p(B) is an integer
multiple of 1/(NrK), since the original atom masses are 0,1/(Nr) or
1/(NK). This is a lattice statement about BIN MASSES; individual
coarsened atom probabilities have the additional bin-size divisor.
For two worlds w,w', uniformity within the SAME cells gives

 TV(p_w,Pi,p_w',Pi)=(1/2)*sum_B |p_w(B)-p_w'(B)|.

If any bin mass differs, the nonzero integer differences sum to zero,
so this TV is at least 1/(NrK). Triangle inequality and feasibility
instead give TV<=2c<1/(NrK). Therefore EVERY source bin mass is
world-invariant. This quantization argument itself needs no coprimality.

## Coprimality restores rigidity at a saturated sibling

For an unsaturated context j_x<r, swapping a residual true and false
candidate in a compatible A support shows that all uncertified atoms
occupy one score bin, as in C017. Consider an unequal pair with counts
s<t. The smaller context is unsaturated. If t<r both contexts already
have this property. If t=r, in any score bin let u_L be its known-L
count and epsilon_L indicate inclusion of all K-s uncertified L atoms;
let u_R be its known-R count and v_R its count outside C_R. Independent
orientation invariance gives

 (K-r)*(u_L-epsilon_L*s-u_R)=-r*v_R.

Hence (K-r)|r*v_R. Since gcd(r,K-r)=1, Bezout implies (K-r)|v_R.
Because 0<=v_R<=K-r, a cell contains either all or none of the
saturated context's outside atoms. Thus their score is also constant.
This is the step that fails for the noncoprime neutral bundles in C016.
The standard Bezout identity was returned in recall/walk004.txt,
card claim_63c5ddfd2e7e4d178b7628c572034232.

Both saturated counts r,r are already balanced; they need no expansion
and no assertion that their outside atoms occupy one score bin.

## Reduction to balanced minima

For each unequal pair both outside-known sets now occupy unique bins.
For any cell write u_x for its known-truth count and epsilon_x for
whether it contains the entire outside-known set. The A-minus-S source
contribution is (K-r)*(u_x-epsilon_x*j_x)/(NrK), so equality under the
orientation flip makes these expressions equal for the two siblings.

If the two outside-known bins differ, each contains an ENTIRE context
and none of the other context. If they coincide in B*, the number k
of known truths outside B* is equal in both siblings and at most s,
the smaller count. Retain all smaller-context truths. In the larger
context retain its k known truths outside B* and any s-k of its known
truths inside B*. Forget all other larger-context truths.

Expanding compatible supports by this forgetting preserves every source
bin mass: outside B* known counts are unchanged; in B* the A context
always has r-k truths. It also preserves each bin's false count for
each orientation: all K-r A false atoms remain in the same outside-
known bin. If entire contexts were separate bins, both facts follow
from fixed context mass 1/N and fixed false count K-r. Balanced pairs,
including r,r, are kept unchanged. This works independently across pairs.

Thus for the same g the enlarged balanced-minimum source game is still
robustly c-feasible and has exactly the same possible false masses.
The retained sets may depend on g, solely as a proof device. No claim
about their actual posterior or original sampling probability is made.

## Arbitrary-bin lower bound and construction

In the balanced comparison game average orientations fairly and
compatible supports uniformly. The mean factual law mu has density
(1/r+1/K)/(2N) on known truths, density
b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N) on uncertified atoms in count-h pairs,
and 1/(NK) in fixed S. Their artificial false probability is tau_h.
Increasing h decreases b_h and increases tau_h, including h=r.
Safe densities are >=1/(NK)>=b_h.

For the union E_h of uncertified groups at counts >=h, every inside
density is <=every outside density. In EACH cell, uniform averaging
therefore transfers mass into E_h: mu_Pi(E_h)>=T_h. Convexity of TV
over compatible worlds and robustness give TV(mu_Pi,g)<=c, so
g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+. The artificial average false risk is the layer-cake
sum tau_0*g(E_0)+sum_{h>0}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})g(E_h), which is at least
(1). The original worst risk equals the expanded worst risk and is
at least this average. Unequal actual posterior weights never enter.

For attainment select h_i known truths in each sibling, before seeing
any hidden orientation or residual support. Start at the balanced
comparison mean law; remove mass from uncertified groups in decreasing
h order, uniformly inside each count group, and transfer it to fixed S.
Each paired selected-known group and residual group has invariant p
mass under ALL original worlds. The generator is constant on each,
so exact-score mergers preserve invariance and Mis_infinity<=c.
Their false fractions are tau_h in EACH actual world; the false mass

T379-C019 v2: proof (unaudited), exact checks PASS; independent audit pending.
Target 1, secondary target 2. Arbitrary VC dimension and unequal known
truth counts, including saturation; conditional robust small-budget
game only. General noncoprime saturated mixtures and larger budgets
remain open here.

## Model and statement

Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K be integers with gcd(r,K-r)=1. There
are d unresolved A/S context pairs and N-2d fixed known S contexts.
Each S has all K truths; each A has an independent uniform r-subset.
The factual law chooses contexts uniformly then uniformly true within
context. Actual iid factual samples have no orientation tags. An
optional independent verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths
in each variable context, including S, without orientation labels.
Let C_x be the distinct observed-plus-certified truth union. Condition
on ANY positive-probability data outcome with j_x=|C_x|<=r in every
variable context. Thus no orientation is logically excluded. Some
contexts may have j_x=r; sibling counts and sample repetitions may
differ arbitrarily. Actual orientation likelihoods need not be equal.

Write h_i=min(j_left,j_right) and D_h=#{i:h_i=h},0<=h<=r. Put

 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)), M_h=D_h*(2-h/r-h/K)/N,
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

For every 0<=c<1/(2NrK), the proposed exact all-generator conditional
worst-world frontier under source Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY compatible
world is

 V(c)=tau_0*(T_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.          (1)

Source miscalibration is TV(g,p_Pi) using uniform coarsening of p in
exact g-probability bins. The same-data partition-supplied WORST-
ORIENTATION oracle has frontier

 O(c)=alpha_0*(Q_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+,       (2)

where alpha_h=2tau_h,A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr),Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t.
In particular A_r=0: a saturated oracle group has zero residual mass,
so its risk-one coefficient must NOT be used to infer a nonzero slope.
The exact zero-budget estimation penalty is

 V(0)-O(0)=sum_i h_i*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h_i)).              (3)

No exact endpoint, largest interval, actual-world-only calibration or
global expected minimax identity is claimed. This extends C017 to
saturation under the coprime arithmetic hypothesis, using a possibly
smaller interval. It does not contradict C016/C018's noncoprime cases.

## Discrete source-bin mass rigidity

Fix any robustly c-feasible generator g and its exact score partition
Pi. For every compatible world and every cell B, p(B) is an integer
multiple of 1/(NrK), since the original atom masses are 0,1/(Nr) or
1/(NK). This is a lattice statement about BIN MASSES; individual
coarsened atom probabilities have the additional bin-size divisor.
For two worlds w,w', uniformity within the SAME cells gives

 TV(p_w,Pi,p_w',Pi)=(1/2)*sum_B |p_w(B)-p_w'(B)|.

If any bin mass differs, the nonzero integer differences sum to zero,
so this TV is at least 1/(NrK). Triangle inequality and feasibility
instead give TV<=2c<1/(NrK). Therefore EVERY source bin mass is
world-invariant. This quantization argument itself needs no coprimality.

## Coprimality restores rigidity at a saturated sibling

For an unsaturated context j_x<r, swapping a residual true and false
candidate in a compatible A support shows that all uncertified atoms
occupy one score bin, as in C017. Consider an unequal pair with counts
s<t. The smaller context is unsaturated. If t<r both contexts already
have this property. If t=r, in any score bin let u_L be its known-L
count and epsilon_L indicate inclusion of all K-s uncertified L atoms;
let u_R be its known-R count and v_R its count outside C_R. Independent
orientation invariance gives

 (K-r)*(u_L-epsilon_L*s-u_R)=-r*v_R.

Hence (K-r)|r*v_R. Since gcd(r,K-r)=1, Bezout implies (K-r)|v_R.
Because 0<=v_R<=K-r, a cell contains either all or none of the
saturated context's outside atoms. Thus their score is also constant.
This is the step that fails for the noncoprime neutral bundles in C016.
The standard Bezout identity was returned in recall/walk004.txt,
card claim_63c5ddfd2e7e4d178b7628c572034232.

Both saturated counts r,r are already balanced; they need no expansion
and no assertion that their outside atoms occupy one score bin.

## Reduction to balanced minima

For each unequal pair both outside-known sets now occupy unique bins.
For any cell write u_x for its known-truth count and epsilon_x for
whether it contains the entire outside-known set. The A-minus-S source
contribution is (K-r)*(u_x-epsilon_x*j_x)/(NrK), so equality under the
orientation flip makes these expressions equal for the two siblings.

If the two outside-known bins differ, each contains an ENTIRE context
and none of the other context. If they coincide in B*, the number k
of known truths outside B* is equal in both siblings and at most s,
the smaller count. Retain all smaller-context truths. In the larger
context retain its k known truths outside B* and any s-k of its known
truths inside B*. Forget all other larger-context truths.

Expanding compatible supports by this forgetting preserves every source
bin mass: outside B* known counts are unchanged; in B* the A context
always has r-k truths. It also preserves each bin's false count for
each orientation: all K-r A false atoms remain in the same outside-
known bin. If entire contexts were separate bins, both facts follow
from fixed context mass 1/N and fixed false count K-r. Balanced pairs,
including r,r, are kept unchanged. This works independently across pairs.

Thus for the same g the enlarged balanced-minimum source game is still
robustly c-feasible and has exactly the same possible false masses.
The retained sets may depend on g, solely as a proof device. No claim
about their actual posterior or original sampling probability is made.

## Arbitrary-bin lower bound and construction

In the balanced comparison game average orientations fairly and
compatible supports uniformly. The mean factual law mu has density
(1/r+1/K)/(2N) on known truths, density
b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N) on uncertified atoms in count-h pairs,
and 1/(NK) in fixed S. Their artificial false probability is tau_h.
Increasing h decreases b_h and increases tau_h, including h=r.
Safe densities are >=1/(NK)>=b_h.

For the union E_h of uncertified groups at counts >=h, every inside
density is <=every outside density. In EACH cell, uniform averaging
therefore transfers mass into E_h: mu_Pi(E_h)>=T_h. Convexity of TV

sum tau_0*g(E_0)+sum_{h>0}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})g(E_h), which is at least

at least this average. Unequal actual posterior weights never enter.

h order, uniformly inside each count group, and transfer it to fixed S.

[Proposition 29 (Weak and strong solutions for Generalized particle systems) of arXiv:2605.23529, 'Generalized Bessel-Dunkl diffusions'] Assume \eqref{eq:example:GM-sigma-compatibility}, \eqref{eq:example:GM-dominance}, and \eqref{eq:example:GM-face-sign}.  Then, for every initial condition $x_0\in\Cc$, there exists a weak solution of the indicator equation \eqref{eq:example:GM-H-indicator}, up to its lifetime.  Moreover, all singular integrals are finite on compact subintervals of the lifetime.

    If, in addition, the block escape condition \eqref{eq:example:GM-block-escape} holds, then there exists a weak solution of the genuine equation \eqref{eq:example:GM-H-system}, and this solution is non-sticky.

    Assume moreover that one of the two uniqueness regimes in Theorem~\ref{thm:pathwise-uniq-indicator-nonsticky} holds.  Then the solution is pathwise unique in the non-sticky class.  Consequently, by Theorem~\ref{thm:strong:existence:uniqueness}, the equation has a strong solution, unique in the non-sticky class, up to its lifetime.  If the radial growth condition \ref{ass:growth:p2} holds, then the solution is global.

[Thm 2. thm: tightness in sP of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Tightness in $\mathscr{P}(S)$}] 
  Let $(\pi_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ be a sequence of random elements of $\mathscr{P}(S)$.
  Write $P_{n}$ for the underlying probability measure of $\pi_{n}$.
  Then, the sequence $(\pi_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ is tight if and only if the following conditions are satisfied.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      The sequence $(\pi_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ is tight with respect to the vague topology.
    \item 
      For each $r>0$, 
      $\displaystyle \lim_{l \to \infty} \limsup_{n \to \infty} P_{n}(W^{(r)}(\pi_{n}) > l) = 0$.
    \item 
      For each $r, \delta>0$, 
      $\displaystyle \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} P_{n}(M_{\varepsilon}^{(r)}(\pi_{n}) > \delta) = 0$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Theorem th:tukey-nonasymp of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] \textbf{(a)} Assume that $\max(d,t)\frac{m^2}{N}\leq c$ for a sufficiently small absolute constant $c>0$ and that 
    $\mathbb E\left|\dotp{X}{u}\right|^p<\infty$ for some $p>4$. Moreover, suppose that 
    \[
    \sqrt N\gg d(\log(m)+\log(d)), \quad m\gg \log^2(d) \ \text{ as } N\to\infty,
    \]
    and let $\varepsilon>0$ be arbitrary. Then
    \begin{equation}
        
    \left\|\widehat\mu_{N,m} - \mu \right\| \leq (2 + o_\varepsilon(1))\left((1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\frac{d}{N}} +
    \sqrt{\frac{2t}{N}}\right)
    \end{equation}
    with probability at least $1-4e^{-t}$, where the sequence $o_\varepsilon(1)\to 0$ as $N,m\to\infty$. 
    \\
    \noindent \textbf{(b)} Assuming only that $\mathbb E\|X\|^2<\infty$ and the condition $\max(d,t)\frac{m^2}{N}\leq c$, we have that
    \begin{equation}
        
    \left\|\widehat\mu_{N,m} - \mu \right\| \leq (2 + o_\varepsilon(1)) \left(4(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\frac{d}{N}} +
    \sqrt{\frac{2t}{N}} \right),
    \end{equation}
    with probability at least $1-4e^{-t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics – specifically, in the theory of stochastic processes – Doob's martingale convergence theorems are a collection of results on the limits of supermartingales, named after the American mathematician Joseph L. Doob. Informally, the martingale convergence theorem typically refers to the result that any supermartingale satisfying a certain boundedness condition must converge. One may think of supermartingales as the random variable analogues of non-increasing sequences; from this perspective, the martingale convergence theorem is a random variable analogue of the monotone convergence theorem, which states that any bounded monotone sequence converges. There are symmetric results for submartingales, which are analogous to non-decreasing sequences.
title: Doob's martingale convergence theorems

[Corollary 12 (Small-block cutoff profile) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] Assume $m_n=o(n)$ and $1\le m_n\le n-1$.  For each fixed \(c\in\R\), let \(k_n(c)\) be as in \eqref{eq:small-block-time}.
\[ \lambda_n = n\left(1-\frac{m_n}{n}\right)^{k_n(c)} \to e^{-c}, \qquad b_n=n-m_n\to\infty. \]
Consequently, for every fixed $p\ge1$,
\[
        \normTV{(Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*k_n(c)}-U_{n,p}}\to f_p(c),
\]
and
\[
        \sepd\!\left((Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*k_n(c)},U_{n,p}\right)\to
        \begin{cases}
        1-e^{-e^{-c}}(1+e^{-c}),&p=1,\\
        1-e^{-e^{-c}},&p\ge2.
        \end{cases}
\]
In particular the total variation cutoff location is
\[
        \frac{\log n}{\delta_n}\sim \frac{n}{m_n}\log n
\]
with window
\[
        \frac1{\delta_n}\sim\frac{n}{m_n}.
\]

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical/priority/scope reviews pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r. Each of d pairs has one arbitrary r-support A and one all-K S; N-2d other contexts are known S. The source chooses context uniformly then a truth uniformly. Observe ANY n iid untagged facts and independent uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts,ANY0<=ell<=r. Learning policies use data and independent seed only. For the conditional lemma take the uniform PRIOR on all orientations and A supports. Given full data D and output g, pair worlds are conditionally independent. In a possible A side with m=K-j outside-union atoms, its F false identities form a uniform F-subset. Sort their g probabilities; the side loss interval is the sum of F smallest through sum of F largest probabilities. Take the minimum/maximum over possible A sides to obtain pair range B_i, and S_g=sum B_i^2. With mu_g its conditional posterior mean, Pr(H-mu_g>=t|D,g)<=exp(-2t^2/S_g), likewise lower tail. S_g=0 means exact equality. This lemma allows arbitrary g and requires no calibration or coprimality. For frontier centering assume gcd(r,F)=1 and EVERY realized output has source Mis_infinity<=c in ALL compatible worlds at exact score bins,0<=c<1/(2NrK). Let beta_c(D) be the C026 native-branch conditional Bayes optimum. C026/C027 give an attaining native policy, polynomial at each fixed alphabet K0. Symmetrize LEARNING POLICIES by sibling swaps and atom permutations. For EVERY fixed world theta and0<delta<1, Pr_theta(|H(g_star)-beta_c(D)|<=sqrt(S_star*log(2/delta)/2))>=1-delta, including data, verifier and policy randomness. Native S_star=F^2*sum_whole(q_left-q_right)^2<=d*(F/K)^2/N^2. For EVERY robust policy there EXISTS a fixed world (depending on policy,delta,not data) with Pr_theta(H(g)>=beta_c(D)-sqrt(S_g*log(1/delta)/2))>=1-delta. An EVERY-world lower for arbitrary policies instead uses log(W/delta),W=(2*binom(K,r))^d. The observable posterior supplied-partition oracle O_bar(D)=E[sum_i F(r-j_Ai)/(Nr(K-j_Ai))-c*max({F/(K-j_Ai):j_Ai<r} union {0})|D] is computable by pair risk CDF products. Delta(D)=beta_c(D)-O_bar(D)>=0 gives an exact oracle-plus-decision-penalty center. Delta is not claimed equal to ordinary ERM partition error. An exact dyadic certificate uses radius squared m*S_g/2 and two-sided failure<=2^(1-m), avoiding floating logs/square roots. Concentration is standard Hoeffding; only its application/structural confidence lift is proposed as owner work. No radius-optimality, exact minimax quantile frontier, uniform-in-K efficiency or classical ERM theorem is claimed.

## Experiment and scope

Use the C026 paired experiment: d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r.
Each pair has one arbitrary r-support A and one all-K systematic S.
Other contexts are known S. Contexts and then true facts are sampled
uniformly. Observe n actual iid untagged facts and independent uniform
ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts,0<=ell<=r.
The uniform prior on orientations and A supports is a proof device,
not a new data source given to the learner. All policies below act on
the actual observed facts/certificates; no orientation labels are given.

The posterior range/concentration lemma below allows EVERY g and needs
neither calibration, coprimality nor a small budget. Centering at C026's
exact conditional Bayes optimum beta_c(D) additionally assumes coprime
r,F and pathwise source Mis_infinity<=c in all compatible worlds,
0<=c<1/(2NrK). Its efficient attainment uses C027 at each fixed K0.
Randomization is over learning policies with each realized output
robustly feasible, not an average of probability vectors.

Hardest step: the conditional Bayesian tail statement must be converted
with the right fixed-world quantifiers. A posterior probability bound
does NOT itself give the same confidence level in every fixed world.

## Exact posterior pair structure

Let C_is be the observed-plus-certified truth union, j_is=|C_is|,
and u_is the factual sample count. A side s is a possible A side iff
j_is<=r. If both are possible,

 pi_i=Pr(A is left|D)=L(u_iL,j_iL)/(L(u_iL,j_iL)+L(u_iR,j_iR)),
 L(u,j)=(K/r)^u binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell).

If one side has j>r, the other A side is certain. Given a possible
A side s, its F false atoms are a UNIFORM F-subset of its m=K-j_is
outside-union atoms. This follows because all r-supports containing
the union have identical likelihood for the full observed sequence.
Repeated observations change orientation likelihood via u but do not
distinguish supports containing all observed identities.

The prior is a product over pairs. The likelihood of the COMPLETE
observed data, including its fixed context counts and certificates,
factors over pair worlds; the context-choice factor is world-independent.
Thus posterior pair worlds are independent. This independence is
conditional on the FULL data, not a claim of independent marginal
context occupancies.

Given D and a policy seed, fix its actual generator g. For possible
A side s sort the m outside-union probabilities x_1<=...<=x_m. Set

 lo_is=sum_{k=1}^F x_k,
 hi_is=sum_{k=m-F+1}^m x_k,
 mu_is=(F/m) sum_{k=1}^m x_k.

The pair's possible false mass lies in
[a_i,b_i]=[min_possible_s lo_is,max_possible_s hi_is].
Its posterior mean is the orientation-weighted sum of mu_is.
Let B_i=b_i-a_i, S_g=sum_i B_i^2, mu_g=sum_i E[H_i|D,g].
All these quantities are observable from D,g and computable by sorting.
Known S contexts contribute no false mass.

## Concentration, with a self-contained standard proof

Conditional on D,g the random pair losses H_i are independent and
bounded in intervals of length B_i. Therefore, for S_g>0,

 Pr(H(g)-mu_g>=t|D,g)<=exp(-2t^2/S_g),
 Pr(H(g)-mu_g<=-t|D,g)<=exp(-2t^2/S_g).                (1)

If S_g=0, H(g)=mu_g in every compatible world and all tail claims
hold with radius0. Conditioning on a policy's independent random
seed does not change the posterior distribution of the world.

For completeness, if X is bounded in[a,b], the log mgf psi of X-EX
has psi(0)=psi'(0)=0 and psi''(s)=Var_s(X), variance under exponential
tilting. Every tilted law still lies in[a,b], and
Var_s(X)<= (EX_s-a)(b-EX_s)<=(b-a)^2/4, using
(X-a)(b-X)>=0. Integrating twice gives
psi(s)<=s^2(b-a)^2/8 for either sign of s. Independence adds these
log bounds; exponential Markov with s=4t/S_g proves(1).
This is STANDARD Hoeffding's inequality, not claimed as a new theorem.

Write R_delta(D,g)=sqrt((S_g/2)*log(1/delta)) for a one-sided tail.
For two-sided coverage replace delta by delta/2. These are posterior
bounds, with mu_g as center. Integer/Fraction checks can avoid all
floating exponentials: for integer m>=1, radius squared m*S_g/2
gives one-sided failure<=e^-m<=2^-m.
For a rational confidence delta, choose integer m with2^(1-m)<=delta
by integer comparisons. The exact algebraic radius sqrt(m*S_g/2)
then certifies two-sided failure<=delta without evaluating a floating
logarithm or square root.

## Small-budget simplification: only orientation uncertainty remains

Suppose c<1/(2NrK) and g is robust in every compatible world.
The source mass of each exact score bin is invariant across worlds
by the1/(NrK) source lattice and2c triangle bound. If j_is<r, swap
one true and one false outside-union atom in an A-support while fixing
all other world coordinates. They must belong to the same score bin;
otherwise that bin's source mass changes. Hence ALL outside-union
atoms in that context have the SAME g probability.

If j_is=r, the outside atoms are precisely the false set when s is A.
In both cases the pair loss conditional on its orientation is fixed.
Resolved pairs therefore have B_i=0. For unresolved pairs put
A_is=sum of false-atom probabilities if s is A: it is F*q_is when
j_is<r, and the sum over its F outside atoms when j_is=r.
Then

 H(g)=constant+sum_unresolved I_i*(A_iL-A_iR),
 I_i independent Bernoulli(pi_i) given D,
 S_g=sum_unresolved (A_iL-A_iR)^2.                     (2)

This simplification needs no coprimality. Coprimality is needed for
C026's optimal beta characterization, not for the present rigidity.

For the native C026 attaining policy, paired/resolved branches have
world-constant false counts. Only whole branches contribute(2).
Every risk-bearing native pool has source mean density<=lambda=1/(NK);
budget donation only reduces its score. Thus its whole-context score
q_is lies in[0,lambda] and

 S_star=F^2 sum_whole(q_iL-q_iR)^2<=d*(F/(NK))^2
       =d*kappa^2/N^2,  kappa=F/K.                    (3)

The known S recipient is outside the variable whole-context objects.
This bound is independent of the alphabet except through kappa.

## Correct fixed-world confidence statements

First take any conditional beta-attaining native policy and symmetrize
LEARNING POLICIES by the finite transitive group of sibling swaps and
atom permutations, as in C026. For each seed use the transformed data's
native generator and invert its labels. The mean center beta is group-
invariant. S_g is defined from the pulled-back actual generator and
the actual data, so the coverage event is equivariant.

Under the uniform prior, integrating(1) gives joint coverage at least
1-delta. After policy symmetrization the joint failure probability is
the SAME in every fixed world; therefore for EVERY fixed world theta,

 Pr_theta(|H(g_star)-beta_c(D)|
          <=sqrt((S_star/2)*log(2/delta)))>=1-delta.    (4)

The probability includes training/certificates and policy randomization.
One may replace S_star by d*kappa^2/N^2 using(3).
This is a uniform frequentist guarantee for the symmetrized estimator,
not a claim that conditional posterior coverage held in each theta.

For ANY robust policy A, C026 gives mu_g>=beta_c(D). Equation(1)
implies uniform-prior average lower coverage at least1-delta, so there
exists a FIXED world theta_A,delta such that

 Pr_theta(H(g_A)>=beta_c(D)-R_delta(D,g_A))>=1-delta.   (5)

The world may depend on the policy and delta but is selected before
data. This is the every-policy/some-world minimax quantifier.

A valid but weaker every-world lower statement for arbitrary A follows
by applying(1) with failure delta/W, W=(2*binom(K,r))^d. Prior-average
failure is<=delta/W, and each fixed world's prior weight is1/W, so its
failure is<=delta. Thus(5) holds for EVERY theta if R_delta is replaced
by R_(delta/W), meaning R with probability argument delta/W.
Symmetry avoids this log W confidence cost for the attaining policy.

## Observable oracle-plus-estimation decomposition

Let O(D,theta,c) be the same-data partition-supplied oracle from C025:

 sum_i F*(r-j_Ai)/(Nr(K-j_Ai))
       -c*max({F/(K-j_Ai):j_Ai<r} union {0}).

Define the POSTERIOR oracle center O_bar(D)=E[O(D,theta,c)|D] and
Delta(D)=beta_c(D)-O_bar(D). Both are observable, and Delta>=0:
the oracle has additional partition information and a larger feasible
class, so its loss lower-bounds any robust generator in each actual
orientation; average this inequality and use the native attainer.

The oracle expectation is polynomial-time computable. Its baseline is
a sum of pair posterior means. Its maximum-risk term is the expectation
of max_i alpha_{j_Ai}, alpha_j=F/(K-j) for j<r,alpha_r=0.
Given D, each j_Ai is either deterministic (resolved) or a two-point
distribution with probabilities pi_i,1-pi_i. Its maximum CDF is the
product of these independent pair CDFs. Sum differences over the at
most K risk levels to compute the expectation exactly.

Consequently(4) is a high-probability oracle-plus-learning envelope:

 H(g_star)=O_bar(D)+Delta(D)+error,
 |error|<=sqrt((S_star/2)*log(2/delta))

with confidence1-delta in every fixed world. The center's conditional
expected loss is exactly optimal by C026, and the uncertainty radius
is explicit/observable. Delta is a posterior decision-cost penalty,
NOT asserted equal to ordinary ERM partition-classification error.
The exact minimax QUANTILE frontier and the classical ERM target are
still open. C027 supplies a polynomial-time estimator at fixed K0.

## Exact evidence and limitations

logs/high_probability_frontier_check.json records39 games over2014
explicit compatible labeled worlds. Two nonuniform arbitrary generators
per data case check the general support-sampling lemma, including
noncoprime K4,r2 and resolved/full-support cases. Full world sums agree
with the independently computed posterior ranges, means and variances.
936 rational one-sided tail comparisons pass, with17 positive tail
controls so a checker returning no events would fail.

The16 native-policy games also check832 actual exact-score calibration
inequalities against source distributions, exact conditional mean=beta,
the native S bound, zero within-orientation support variance and the
posterior-oracle maximum CDF against full world sums. All these tests
use integers/Fraction, with dyadic confidence comparisons by squared
rational thresholds. The analytic Hoeffding bound supplies the infinite
parameter proof; finite checks do not independently prove it.

The quantifier control is deliberately separate from the native optimum:
no facts/certificates,d1,K3,r2, emit one atom. Its posterior false loss is
Bernoulli(1/6), mean1/6,S1. The upper failure at squared radius1/2 has
posterior probability1/6<=1/2, but in its one fixed false world failure
probability is1. This policy is robust only at unrestricted budget1;
it tests the invalid posterior-to-every-world implication, not a
small-budget optimality theorem. Symmetrizing POLICIES by choosing
one of six variable atoms uniformly gives failure1/6 in EACH of the
six fixed worlds. This is the confidence transfer used in(4).

The standard Hoeffding card was found via q034 and walked in walk009:
claim_6b27761ada691c48f1a11c73bee6747a8ad6608555e5527cc89c8d80592e2719.
It answers the concentration-method need; no duplicate is queued.
The proof above is self-contained. q033's result-specific cards were
unrelated. Brain wake/runtime health is degraded; recall is a method
lead rather than a verification certificate.

The high-probability upper uses C026/C027, and the oracle decomposition
uses C025's known-partition formula; those dependencies remain unaudited.
The lower is every-policy/some-fixed-world at the sharp posterior
confidence radius, or every-world with the explicit log W confidence
cost. These quantifiers cannot be strengthened by conditional averaging.
No optimality of the radius or exact minimax quantile frontier is claimed.
Classical ERM and uniform-in-K efficiency remain open. Independent
mathematical, priority and scope reviews are pending.

[Thm mss of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] Let $k$,  $m$, $n$ be positive integers such that $m\geq k$, and let $v_1,...,v_m\in \R^n$ be such that   
$$\|v_i\|^2\leq 1\quad \text{for all $i=1,...,m,$ and}\quad \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m v_iv_i^T \leq \frac{1}{k} \Id.$$
Then there exists a partition $\{T_1,...,T_s\}$ of $[m]$ for some integer $s>0$, such that for some universal constant $\tilde{C}\geq 1$, 
$$\tilde{C}^{-1}k< |T_j| <\tilde{C} k \quad \text{and}\quad   \|\frac{1}{|T_j|}\sum_{i\in T_j} v_iv_i^T\| \leq  \frac{\tilde{C}}{k} \quad \text{for each $j=1,...,s$}.$$

[Theorem 258 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Assume $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ is realized by a non-bipartite gluing graph $\mathsf{G}$. Then the vector $\boldsymbol{v} = \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_1}$ has $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit $\{\tau\,\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}\,\,|\,\,\tau \in \{\pm 1\}\,\,i \in [m]\}$, this orbit is good and has minimal size $2m = 2\,\textnormal{rank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta})$. For any $i \in [m]$ and $h \in \mathcal{H}_i$, we have
\[
T^{(h)}(\tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ccc} \tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \notin \mathcal{H}_i \\[0.6ex] - \tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_{i'_h}} && \textnormal{if}\,\, h \in \mathcal{H}_i. \end{array}\right.
\]
The spectral curve $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has genus $\mathsf{g}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = 2\,\textnormal{corank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) + 1$, and is equipped with a holomorphic involution $\varsigma : \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \rightarrow \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ sending $p$ in the $\boldsymbol{w}$-th sheet to $p'$ in the $(-\boldsymbol{w})$-th sheet such that $Z_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p) = Z_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p')$. The group $\hat{\mathfrak{G}}$ is the Weyl group of type $D_{m}$.

The bidifferential $\mathcal{B}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:Bcont} is defined on the spectral surface $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v} \otimes\boldsymbol{v}}^{[2],\circ} = \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} / (\varsigma,\varsigma)$. Its pullback $\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ to $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has biresidues \foreignlanguage{russian}{B}${}_{\boldsymbol{w}_1,\boldsymbol{w}_2} = \delta_{\boldsymbol{w}_1,\boldsymbol{w}_2} - 1 - \delta_{\boldsymbol{w}_1 + \boldsymbol{w}_2, \boldsymbol{0}}$, and is equal to
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}} - (\textnormal{id},\varsigma)^*\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}} - \frac{\dd z_1 \dd z_2}{(z_1 - z_2)^2},
\]
and we have $(\textnormal{id},\varsigma)^* \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}} = (\varsigma, \textnormal{id})^* \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}$. Here $\mathcal{L}$ is the same Lagrangian as in Theorem~\ref{thm:Omegav} and $\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}$ is the fundamental bidifferential of Section~\ref{sec:fund02}.

From the analytic continuation of first-kind functions in Proposition~\ref{Lem:Holo1form}, we get an linear isomorphism
\[
\begin{array}{ccc} \textnormal{Ker}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) & \longrightarrow & H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C})^- \\
\boldsymbol{v}' & \longmapsto & \mathfrak{u}_{\boldsymbol{v};\boldsymbol{v}'} \end{array}
\]
where $H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C})^-$ is the space of holomorphic $1$-forms that are anti-invariant under the involution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 258 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The chi law of parameters $n\in\mathbb N$ and $t>0$, appearing as
$$\chi_{nt}=law\left(\sqrt{f_1^2+\ldots+f_n^2}\right)$$
with $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ being independent, each following $g_t$, has density given by
$$\chi_{nt}=\frac{2x^{n-1}e^{-x^2/2t}}{(2t)^{n/2}\Gamma(n/2)}\,dx$$
and its moments are given by the following formula, valid for any $k\in\mathbb N$,
$$M_k=(2t)^{k/2}\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{n+k}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{n}{2}\right)}$$
with $\Gamma$ being as usual the gamma function.

The following is an archival copy of the reviewed v1 text. Its old draft/status and scoring labels are historical; the scope and status above govern this v2 edition.

## Reviewed v1 proof text

# Rare-contamination transfer by clipping (draft; not yet audited)

For any law P on R^d let P_sigma be the law of X=Y+sigma Z,
Z standard Gaussian independent of Y. Its score s_P satisfies
s_P(X)=-E[Z|X]/sigma. Consequently
E_P_sigma ||s_P||^4 <= d(d+2)/sigma^4 by conditional Jensen.

Suppose a fixed oracle a_sigma has mean squared score error at most
e0^2/sigma^2 for P at every positive sigma. Let f_sigma be its Euclidean
projection onto the ball of radius B/sigma. Projection is nonexpansive,
so
E_P_sigma ||f-s_P||^2 <= [2e0^2+2d(d+2)/B^2]/sigma^2.
Here the projection error of s_P is bounded by its fourth moment divided
by (B/sigma)^2; B>0.

Let Q=(1-eta)P+eta H for ANY probability law H, 0<eta<1. Use the same
clipped oracle f for Q. Define R_L(g)=E_{Y~L,Z}||g(Y+sigma Z)+Z/sigma||^2.
The conditional expectation identity gives
R_L(g)-R_L(s_L)=E_L_sigma||g-s_L||^2.
Also R_Q(g)=(1-eta)R_P(g)+eta R_H(g).
Because s_P minimizes R_P and R_H(s_Q)>=0,

E_Q_sigma||f-s_Q||^2
 <= (1-eta) E_P_sigma||f-s_P||^2 + eta R_H(f)
 <= [2e0^2+2d(d+2)/B^2+eta(B+sqrt(d))^2]/sigma^2.

The last inequality uses the deterministic bound ||f||<=B/sigma and
Minkowski in L2; it needs no moment assumption on H. All denoising risks
here are finite: f is bounded, s_L is an L2 conditional expectation of Z,
and Q dominates each mixture component, ensuring the cross-risks are finite.

Choose integer d>=1, 0<e<=1, e0=e/4, B=4(d+1)/e, and
eta=e^2/[4(B+d)^2]. Then eta<=1/(2d). The three error terms are at most
e^2/8, e^2/8, and e^2/4 respectively. Thus f is an e-accurate score
oracle for Q (with slack). eta is inverse polynomial for polynomial e.
Every query to f is simulated by one query to a and public clipping.
This preserves adaptive rounds and queries. No density oracle is used.

If P is in the unit ball and ||Cov(P)||op<=1/d, take
H=N(0,I/(eta d)). Then E_Q||Y||^2<=2 and kappa(Cov(Q))<=3 by C01.
Any sample law within TV r of Q is within TV r+eta of P.

The field f is jointly measurable whenever a is: Euclidean projection
onto a ball with positive continuous radius B/sigma is continuous in its
arguments. Clipping uses only public d,e,sigma, not the hidden instance.

Quantifiers: this construction applies to every fixed legal a, each fixed
instance, every sigma>0, and any H. The original oracle can be chosen
before any algorithm, so the transferred field can too. No adaptively
chosen contamination and no independence of query answers are assumed.

The denoising-risk identity above is also checked on 864 exact rational
finite-channel cases, including overlapping and disjoint mixtures, extreme
eta, oracle error, and active/inactive clipping. These finite checks support
the algebra only. The analytic Gaussian argument is the conditional Jensen
and orthogonal projection calculation above.

Clipping is essential. In one dimension take P=point mass at 0 and
H=point mass at L!=0. The exact P score is -x/sigma^2. The mixture score
is -x/sigma^2 + L*w_H(x)/sigma^2. As sigma decreases to zero,
sigma^4 E_Q_sigma|s_P-s_Q|^2 tends to eta*L^2: conditional on the
component and a fixed Gaussian Z, w_H tends to its component indicator;
dominated convergence applies since 0<=w_H<=1. Thus the unclipped
oracle does not have O(1/sigma^2) score error uniformly in sigma.

body:
[Prop smash-gl-left-Quillen of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The smash product of orthogonal spectra defines a left Quillen bifunctor 
    \[
        \cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$G$-global}\times\cat{$\bm{H}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$H$-global}\to
        \cat{$\bm{(G\times H)}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$(G\times H)$-global}.
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        To see that the pushout product axiom for cofibrations holds, it suffices to treat the case of generating cofibrations. Using that the enriched Yoneda embedding $\textbf{\textup{O}}^{\textup{op}}\to{\textbf{\textup{OrthSp}}}$ admits a strong symmetric monoidal structure, we then compute that the pushout product of $\textbf{\textup{O}}(V,-)\smashp_{\varphi} G_+\smashp (\partial D^n\hookrightarrow D^n)$ with $\textbf{\textup{O}}(W,-)\smashp_\psi G_+\smashp (\partial D^m\hookrightarrow D^m)$ (where $\varphi\colon K\to G$ and $\psi\colon L\to H$ are homomorphisms) is given by
        \[
            \textbf{\textup{O}}(V\oplus W,-)\smashp_{\varphi\times\psi}(G\times H)_+\smashp\big((\partial D^n\hookrightarrow D^n)\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}}(\partial D^m\hookrightarrow D^m)\big)_+,
        \]
        where we view $H\times K\subset {\textup{O}}(V)\times {\textup{O}}(W)$ as a subgroup of ${\textup{O}}(V\oplus W)$ via block sum. As $\textbf{\textup{Top}}$ is cartesian and $\cat{$\bm{(G\times H)}$-OrthSp}$ is topological, this is then indeed a cofibration, completing the proof of the pushout product axiom for cofibrations.

        Next, we will show that $i\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence for any cofibration $i\colon A\to B$ between cofibrant objects and any $H$-global weak equivalence $f\colon X\to Y$ between cofibrant objects; this then in particular applies to the generating (acyclic) cofibrations, proving (up to exchanging the roles of $G$ and $H$) the remaining case for the pushout product axiom. For this we consider the defining pushout
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                A\smashp X\arrow[r,"i\smashp X"]\arrow[d,"A\smashp f"']\arrow[dr,phantom,"\ulcorner"{very near end}] & B\smashp X\arrow[d]\arrow[ddr, bend left=15pt,"B\smashp f"]\\
                A\smashp Y\arrow[r]\arrow[drr, bend right=15pt,"i\smashp Y"'] & P\arrow[dr,dashed,"i\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f"{description}]\\
                && B\smashp Y\rlap.
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        By the previous proposition applied to ${\textup{triv}}_HA$ and ${\textup{triv}}_Gf$, the map $A\smashp f$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence, and likewise for $B\smashp f$. Moreover, $i\smashp X$ is a cofibration by the previous step, so that $B\smashp X\to P$ is also a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence by left properness. We conclude from $2$-out-of-$3$ that also $P\to B\smashp Y$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence, as claimed.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop smash-gl-left-Quillen of arXiv:2608.28504

[Proposition p:basiccap of arXiv:2605.20587, 'Persistence and entropic repulsion of stationary Gaussian fields with spectral singularity'] For every compact $D$,
   \begin{equation}

\text{\textup{Cap}}(D) := \Big( \inf_{ \nu \in \mathcal{P}(D) } \int_D \int_D K(x,y) d\nu(x) d\nu(y) \Big)^{-1}  = \inf \big\{ \|h\|^2_H : h \in H, h|_D  \ge 1 \big\} .
\end{equation}
Moreover if $\text{\textup{Cap}}(D) < \infty$, then optimisers on both sides of (equation e:cap3 of the paper) exist, and the optimiser on the right-hand side of (equation e:cap3 of the paper) is unique and can be represented as
\[ h = \text{\textup{Cap}}(D) \int K(\cdot,y) \, d\nu(y) , \]
where $\nu$ is any of the optimisers on the left-hand side.
title: Proposition p:basiccap of arXiv:2605.20587

[Lem 97 of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Fix $k\in\mathbb N$, $q\ge 2$, $M>0$, a decreasing function $F:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ of exponential decay at infinity, and $1\leq i,j\leq k$. Let $u_\x^{ij}(\y):=|   y_i-   y_j-(   x_i-   x_j)|$, for $\x,\y\in I^k$. Here $|   u|$ as usual denotes the Euclidean norm of $   u\in \mathbb R^d$. Let $\br_0\in \Ek$ be centered. Then there exists $C>0$ such that uniformly over all $\br \in \Ek$ and $\x,\y\in I^k$ one has $$-C\cdot d_{\mathrm{SRI}}(\br,\br_0)^{1/4} F\big(\min_{i'<j'}|y_{i'}-y_{j'}|\big)^{1/4}\le (P^{\br}-\mathrm{Id}) u_\x^{ij}(\y) \leq C ,
$$
where $P^{\br}$ is the Markov operator associated to $P_{\br}$.
title: Lem 97 of arXiv:2510.22155

body: [Lemma le:law_bubble of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Let $\eta_1,\eta_2$ be as described in Section~(se:intersections_setup of the paper). Given $\eta_1 \cap \eta_2$, pick two points in $\eta_1(\tau_1), \eta_1(\sigma_1) \in \eta_1 \cap \eta_2$ such that $\eta_1((\tau_1,\sigma_1))$ is a connected component of $\eta_1 \setminus \eta_2$. Let $\tau_2,\sigma_2$ be such that $\eta_1(\tau_1)=\eta_2(\tau_2)$, $\eta_1(\sigma_1)=\eta_2(\sigma_2)$. Then for $i=1,2$ the conditional law of $\eta_i|_{[\tau_i,\sigma_i]}$ given $\eta_{3-i}$ and $\eta_i|_{[0,\tau_i]\cup[\sigma_i,\infty]}$ is an ${\rm SLE}_{\kappa}${} in (a connected component of) $\mathbf{H} \setminus (\eta_{3-i} \cup \eta_i([0,\tau_i]\cup[\sigma_i,\infty]))$ from $\eta_i(\tau_i)$ to $\eta_i(\sigma_i)$.
title: Lemma le:law_bubble of arXiv:2507.15589

Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, let F_k, F: Ω × R × R^n → R be continuous with F_k → F locally uniformly on Ω × R × R^n, and let u_k ∈ C(Ω) be a viscosity subsolution of F_k(x,u_k,Du_k) = 0 for each k. If u_k → u locally uniformly on Ω, then u ∈ C(Ω) is a viscosity subsolution of F(x,u,Du) = 0. The same statement holds with 'subsolution' replaced by 'supersolution', and hence by 'solution'. In particular (vanishing viscosity), if u_ε ∈ C^2 solve F(x,u_ε,Du_ε) - ε Δu_ε = 0 and u_ε → u locally uniformly as ε ↓ 0, then u is a viscosity solution of F(x,u,Du) = 0.

[Proposition 8 (WKBC bridge-weighted regression and numerical consistency) of arXiv:2609.02196, 'Schr\"odinger Bridges on Lie Group Manifolds for Probabilistic Intrinsic Generation'] The population minimizer is \(\bm s^*=\nabla_{\bm\xi}\log h_t^{\beta^*}\), and
\begin{equation}
\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)
=\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T
\int\norm{\bm s(t,x)-\bm s^*(t,x)}^2
P_t^{\rm SB}(\dd x)\,\dd t.
\end{equation}
Let \(P^{\bm s,\pi_0}\) denote the controlled law with normalized control
\(\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\bm s\) and initial law \(\pi_0\). If
\(P_0^{\rm SB}\ll\pi_0\) and the relevant Girsanov exponentials are true martingales, then
\begin{equation}
\KL(P^{\rm SB}\|P^{\bm s,\pi_0})
=\KL(P_0^{\rm SB}\|\pi_0)
+\gamma T\bigl[\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)
-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)\bigr].
\end{equation}
In particular, when \(\pi_0=P_0^{\rm SB}\),
\begin{equation*}
d_{\rm BL}(P^{\rm SB},P^{\bm s,P_0^{\rm SB}})
\le
\sqrt{2\gamma T\bigl[\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)
-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)\bigr]}.
\end{equation*}
Thus the regression-to-path-law conversion has the explicit constant \(\gamma T\) and requires no auxiliary occupation-density-ratio constant.

For positive numerical factors \((f_{0,N},g_{T,N})\), the same reverse-KL argument applies to the corresponding numerical bridge and yields the path-space decomposition in Eq.~\eqref{eq:wkbc-total-error}. Under the approximation conditions in \cref{app:wkbc-implementation}, its numerical-bridge term tends to zero as the lattice, quadrature, Sinkhorn, interpolation, and initial-law approximations are refined, while its regression term vanishes with bridge-weighted risk consistency. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: WKBC bridge-weighted regression and numerical consistency

body:
[Theorem Feature-adaptive detection and recovery from
spectral certificates of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let
\(\mathcal{A = \{}A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\}\) be a degree-\(q\),
radius-\(r\) homological certificate for \(M\). Then, for
every starting point \(z \in M\) and every
\(T \geq s_{0}\),

\[\mathbb{P}_{z}\left( R_{q}(T,r) \right) \geq 1 - a_{hk}\,\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}\left( T - s_{0} \right).\]

In particular,
\(\mathbb{P}_{z}\left( H_{q}\left( \Gamma_{T}^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M) \right) \geq 1 - \delta\)
whenever
\(a_{hk}\,\Phi_{\mathcal{A}}\left( T - s_{0} \right) \leq \delta\).
If \(\mathcal{A}\) is a full homological certificate at radius
\(r\), the same bound holds for the simultaneous event
\(R(T,r)\).

[Proposition compact resolvent criterion proposition of arXiv:2606.01683, 'Singular-value gap of nonreversible Markov processes'] Let \(L\) be a
Markov generator on \(L^2(\mu)\), where $\mu$ is an invariant probability measure
on a measurable space.
Suppose that \(L\) has
compact resolvent. Equivalently, the embedding of $(\operatorname{Dom}(L), \| \cdot \| + \|L \cdot \|)$
into $L^2(\mu)$ is compact. 
Suppose further that the kernel of \(L\) consists only
of constants. Then \(L\) has a positive singular-value gap on
\(L^2_0(\mu)\):
\[
        \gamma
        :=
        \inf_{\substack{f\in\operatorname{Dom}(L)\cap L^2_0(\mu) \backslash \{0\}}}
        \frac{\|Lf\|}{\|f\|}
        >0.
\]
Consequently, the empirical-variance bounds of Corollary (main global corollary of the paper) apply.

[Theorem matching large beta effect of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $M$ is a Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfying $\sec_M\geq -K_2>-\infty$ and $u_0$ is bounded and satisfies $u_0\geq \varepsilon>0$ in some ball $B(x,R)$. The following holds for integers $p\geq 2$ and $u(t,x)$ which solves (equation eq:PAM-mild form of the paper) starting from $u_0$.
    \begin{enumerate}[label = {(\Alph*)}]
    \item If $\frac{n-2}{4}<\alpha<\frac{n}{4}$, then $$\lim_{\beta\to+\infty}\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{1}{\beta^{\frac{2}{4\alpha-n-2}}}\frac{\ln\mathbb{E}[\abs{u(t,x)}^p]}{t}\geq Cp(p-1).$$
    \item If $\alpha=\frac{n}{4}$, then $$\lim_{\beta\to+\infty}\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{\ln(\beta)^2}{\beta^2}\frac{\ln\mathbb{E}[\abs{u(t,x)}^p]}{t}\geq Cp(p-1).$$
    \item If $\alpha>\frac{n}{4}$, then $$\lim_{\beta\to+\infty}\lim_{t\to+\infty}\frac{1}{\beta^2}\frac{\ln\mathbb{E}[\abs{u(t,x)}^p]}{t}\geq Cp(p-1).$$
    \end{enumerate}
    The $C>0$ is different in each of the above inequalities and depend on $\alpha,n,K_2$ and $R$.

\]

[Lemma lem:spectral-factor-rescaled of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Assume
\[
f(\lambda)\sim c_f |\lambda|^{\alpha-1}L_0(1/|\lambda|),
\qquad
\lambda\to0,
\]
where \(c_f>0\), \(0<\alpha<1\), and \(L_0\) is slowly varying at infinity. Let
\(
q(\lambda):=f(\lambda)^{1/2}.
\)
For \(n\ge1\), define
\[
\psi_n(x)
:=
n^{-(1-\alpha)/2}L_0(n)^{-1/2}\,q(x/n)\,\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\le \pi n\}}.
\]
Then for every \(R>0\) and every \(\eta\in(0,\alpha)\) the following hold:

\smallskip

\noindent
\textup{(i)} For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,R)\),
\[
\sup_{\varepsilon\le |x|\le R}
\left|
\psi_n(x)-c_f^{1/2}|x|^{(\alpha-1)/2}
\right|
\longrightarrow0.
\]

\noindent
\textup{(ii)} There exists \(C_{R,\eta}<\infty\) such that for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
|\psi_n(x)|
\le
C_{R,\eta}|x|^{(\alpha-1-\eta)/2},
\qquad
0<|x|\le R.
\]
