[Theorem 2 (Structural representation and exact extraction) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] For every represented subsequence of \eqref{overview:eq:packet}, the
following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Roman*)}]
 \item Labeled block evaluation extends uniquely, at every physical
 weight $q$, to a unitary
 \begin{equation}
 \mathbb U_q:
 \cW_q\!\left(\bigoplus_{s\le q}\cK_s\right)
 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\cH_q.
 
 \end{equation}
 This unitary gives the direct implication in
 \eqref{overview:eq:weak-closure}; collision-null replicas give the
 converse realization and the convergence of the finite contraction
 register.

 \item Put
 \begin{equation}
 a_Q=\sum_{r=1}^{Q-1}\binom{Q-1}{r}^2\binom{2r}{r},
 \qquad
 \mu_Q=\left\lfloor\frac{Q^2+Q+1}{3}\right\rfloor.
 
 \end{equation}
 There are nested common graded modules $M^{[J]}$ such that the separated
 feedback energy and the coherently aggregated Gaussian self-plus-interface
 defect satisfy
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_Q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le\frac{a_QR^4}{J},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\mathrm{res}}(r^{[J]})+\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}}(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})
 \le\frac{\mu_Qa_QR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 Consequently, along a further subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
 F_n\Longrightarrow A_*+G_C,
 \qquad G_C\indep A_*.
 
 \end{equation}
 This factorization is quantitative and unconditional, but the active
 factor $A_*$ need not be canonical.

 \item Suppose that the packet is carried by one chaos order $q$, and let
 $\xi_a=[f_{n,a}]_{\mathcal U}\in\cH_q$.  A Gram-reduced trajectory
 admits a sufficiently slow diagonal $J(n)\to\infty$ for which
 \begin{equation}
 (A_n^{[J(n)]},B_n^{[J(n)]})
 \Longrightarrow
 \left(
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cD_q}\xi,
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cK_q}\xi
 \right).
 
 \end{equation}
 The second component is Gaussian and independent of the first.  The
 reduced feedback may be stopped after fewer than $J$ promotions with
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le \frac{d\,a_qR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 If $\kappa_{n,a}$ denotes the fourth cumulant of the $a$th component,
 then, along the represented subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
  P_{\cD_q}\xi=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \lim_{\mathcal U}\sum_a\kappa_{n,a}=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  F_n\Longrightarrow_{\mathcal U}N_d(0,\Sigma),
  
 \end{equation}
 and the finite-level characteristic-function error is bounded by a
 constant times $|t|^2(\sum_a\kappa_{n,a})^{1/2}$.

 \item For a finite mixed-degree terminal $T$, let $\cN_s(T)$ be the
 closed span of the ranges of its nonlinear one-leg flattenings of
 primitive weight $s$.  Then
 \begin{equation}
 T=\mathsf A^{\can}+\mathsf G^{\can},
 \qquad \mathsf G^{\can}\indep\mathsf A^{\can},
 
 \end{equation}
 where the covariance of $\mathsf G^{\can}$ is maximal among graded
 Gaussian factors annihilated by the complete raw one-leg nonlinear
 register.  Simultaneous extraction can fail to reach this split; a
 lexicographic, weight-by-weight extraction does reach it.
\end{enumerate}
The $J^{-1/2}$ law-level bound derived from
\eqref{overview:eq:HS-rate} concerns only the noncanonical factorization
\eqref{overview:eq:noncanonical}; no quantitative rate toward
\eqref{overview:eq:canonical} is asserted. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 242 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$ be non-zero and $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}} = (\boldsymbol{v} \otimes \boldsymbol{v}\,,\,0)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ we have $(\boldsymbol{w} \otimes \boldsymbol{w}\,,\,0) \in \mathfrak{G}^{[2]}.\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}$.
\item $\textnormal{Ker}(\pi^{\circ})$ is a torsion-free abelian group.
\item $\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is bijective if and only if $(\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}})^{-1}(\{\boldsymbol{v} \otimes \boldsymbol{v}\}) = \{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}\}$.
\item If $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has finite $\mathfrak{G}^{[2]}$-orbit, then $\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is bijective.
\item If $-\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} \in \mathfrak{G}$, then $\textnormal{Ker}(\pi^{\bullet}) = \{(\tau \textnormal{\textbf{Id}},\tau \textnormal{\textbf{Id}})\,\,|\,\,\tau \in \{\pm 1\}\}$ and the maps $\pi_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\bullet}$ and $\mathfrak{p}^{\bullet}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ have degree $2$ (examples where this is realized will appear in Theorem~\ref{thm:spcurvenonbip}).
\item If $-\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} \notin \mathfrak{G}$, then $\pi^{\bullet}$, $\pi^{\bullet}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ and $\mathfrak{p}_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\bullet}$ are isomorphisms.
\end{enumerate}

Assumptions: Iid nonconstant integer initial excess, mean zero, finite first moment; Source particle-hole/parking dynamics and resampling inequality; Full-space nearest-neighbor range; d>=3 for finite-Green asymptotic only. Limitation: Density lower constant only; no closer-hole geometry or matching density asymptotic. Novelty: KNOWN source resampling inequality; UNCHECKED separate optimized constant statement. The model is discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor synchronous parking on Z^d with stationary capacity-one holes; A_t(x) is the active-particle count and H_t(x) the unfilled-hole indicator. In the sparse law eta(x) is initially +1 and -1 each with probability p, and zero otherwise, independently across sites. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:6038d28eb971bf442bc01c3b4e93ee5444e37b0824f264f4f9c558155eaf4227","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/60/6038d28eb971bf442bc01c3b4e93ee5444e37b0824f264f4f9c558155eaf4227.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:003ee7cd411bd14e46e167b8c6d8c2748dacb1466880217907ba41819bb91206","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c22","bundle_id":"population.i0005-final-exploration-energy-and-charge-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and interacting particle systems","draft":"w661/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:parking-resampling-range-optimized-density-constant-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C22 v1: range-optimized resampling density constant

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis resampling
inequality and SRW range identity; UNCHECKED prior separate statement of
the optimized constant. This is a derived refinement, not a solution.

Let eta(x) be iid nonconstant integer-valued with mean zero and finite
first moment, in the source's parking model. Write S_t=E A_t(0), and
gamma=E|eta(0)-eta'(0)|>0 for an independent copy. Let R_n be the range
of full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor SRW through time n. Whenever

    E|R_{2t}|-1 >= 1/gamma,

the source's resampling argument gives

    S_t >= 1/[8(E|R_{2t}|-1)].

For d>=3 only, if g=G(0) is the finite full-space SRW Green value, this
implies

    liminf_{t->infinity} t S_t >= g/16.

For the sparse critical law, S_t=h_t is also the unfilled-hole probability.
In d4 this improves the constant 1/16 displayed in the source's coarse
range estimate to G(0)/16. No recurrent-dimensional finite-Green formula
is asserted, and no upper density asymptotic follows.

## 1. Primary inequality and its optimization

Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis, arXiv:2609.02820v1, Lemma 5.1 proof Step 3,
pp.18-19, retains the exact range in its resampling/cancellation count:

    4S_t >= epsilon-(epsilon^2/2)(E|R_{2t}|-1),
                        for every 0<=epsilon<=gamma.

The two resampled systems have the same mean-zero law; the expected
number of surviving discrepancy labels is bounded by their combined
active/hole density 4S_t. The source derives the displayed inequality
before replacing E|R_{2t}|-1 by 2t. We use that already proved inequality,
not an independent claim that unmatched labels are independent.

Put L=E|R_{2t}|-1. It is positive for integer t>=1. If L>=1/gamma,
the maximizer epsilon=1/L belongs to the allowed interval. Substitution
gives 4S_t>=1/(2L), proving the finite-time bound. Since the expected
range tends to infinity, its condition holds eventually for each fixed
nonconstant initial law.

## 2. Exact transient range rate

For any finite K, summing a walk's unique last visit to K through time n
over starting points gives

    sum_y P_y(T_K<=n)
       =sum_{m=0}^n sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+>m).

For K={0}, the left side is E|R_n| by path translation. In d>=3 the
right summand tends to P_0(T_0^+=infinity)=1/g. Cesaro averaging yields
E|R_n|/(n+1)->1/g. Therefore

    t/[8(E|R_{2t}|-1)] --> g/16.

Combining with Step 1 gives the liminf. The source sparse law has
gamma=4p(1-p), if an explicit law-dependent threshold is desired.

## Scope

The source's 1/16 is a law- and dimension-independent coarse constant.
The refinement depends on the full-space transient Green value and uses
the exact walk range. It does not resolve closer-hole geometry, improve
the missing Palm bound in C9, or justify a fixed-p density limit.

Primary source: arXiv:2609.02820v1 Lemma 5.1 proof Step 3. Full-space
escape/capacity normalization: Sznitman arXiv:0704.2560v3 (1.5)-(1.7).

body: FEI is equivalent to ONE inequality over Boolean gates of every arity with a measure-only potential (an arbitrary f is a single gate on n fresh variables). Exhaustively over EVERY NPN class at fan-in 2, 3 and 4 (4, 14, 222), each driven to its own maximum, plus 40 random genuine gates at fan-in 5, the largest margin any gate asks of the read-once potential is exactly the 2-input AND value 4.397420030e-03 -> constant 6.4558994, and it is attained only in the limit of dead inputs (1 dead at arity 3, 2 at arity 4, 3 at arity 5; same D and denominator in every row). Three routes closed: the per-coordinate erasure bound, the slack-free arity induction, and the clean face induction (DMIN). FEI itself still open.

body:
Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space. For 0 < p < infinity, L^p(mu) is the set of equivalence classes, under equality mu-almost everywhere, of measurable f: X -> C (or R) with ||f||_p = (int_X |f|^p dmu)^{1/p} < infinity. L^infinity(mu) is the set of classes of measurable f with ||f||_infinity = ess sup |f| = inf{ M >= 0 : mu({|f| > M}) = 0 } < infinity (the infimum is attained, so |f| <= ||f||_infinity a.e.). For 1 <= p <= infinity, ||.||_p is a norm and L^p(mu) is a Banach space; for 0 < p < 1 it is only a quasi-norm (||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p)) and d(f,g) = ||f-g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric. l^p denotes L^p of the counting measure on N (or on a set I). The conjugate (dual) exponent p' of 1 <= p <= infinity is defined by 1/p + 1/p' = 1, with 1' = infinity and infinity' = 1.

[Proposition prop:multi_extention_Asmussen of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $g: [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be non-decreasing and absolutely continuous with $g(0)=0$ and a locally finite density $g'\geqslant 0$ satisfying $\int_0^y g'(x)x^{-2}\mathrm{d} x<\infty$ for some $y>0$. Let $\bm{X}$ be a $d$-dimensional L\'evy process with L\'evy measure $\nu$ such that $\mathds{E}[g(60|\bm{X}_1|)]<\infty$ and $\mathds{E}[\bm{X}_1]=0$. Then
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}n
    \mathds{E}\big[g\big(\big|\bm{X}_{1/n}\big|\big)\big]
=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}g(|\bm{v}|)\nu(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 0-1 of arXiv:2411.05204, '\Large\bf Sample Path Properties of the Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge'] Let $(G(t))_{t\in[0,1]}$ be a centered Gaussian process for which $d(t,s):={\mathbb E}[(G(t)-G(s))^2]$ is continuous. Let furthermore   $\omega,\rho:[0,1)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous  functions with $\omega(0)=\rho(0)=0$, and $K\in[0,1]$ be a compact set. Then 
    $$\lim_{h\to 0}\sup_{\substack{t,s\in K\\ |t-s|<h}}\frac{G(t)-G(s)}{\omega(|t-s|)}\leq L\quad\text{ a.s. }\implies ~\lim_{h\to 0}\sup_{\substack{t,s\in K\\ |t-s|<h}}\frac{G(t)-G(s)}{\omega(|t-s|)}=L'\quad\text{ a.s. }$$
    for some $L'\geq 0$. Similarly, for each $s\in[0,1]$,
   $$\limsup_{t\in[0,1],\,t\to s}\frac{G(t)-G(s)}{\rho(|t-s|)}\leq L_s\quad\text{ a.s. }\implies ~\limsup_{t\in[0,1],\,t\to s}\frac{G(t)-G(s)}{\rho(|t-s|)}=L_s'\quad\text{ a.s. }$$
    for some $L_s'\geq 0$.

[Theorem th:tail_stable of arXiv:2412.06374, 'Stable and tempered stable distributions and processes: an overview toward trajectory simu'] Let $X\sim S_\alpha(\sigma,\beta,\delta)$ with $\alpha \in (0,2), \sigma>0, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$. Let $f_X$ be the corresponding density.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $\beta \in (-1,1]$, $
\mathbb{P}(X>x) \underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\sim} c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha(1+\beta)x^{-\alpha},$ and $
f_X(x) \underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\sim} \alpha c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha (1+\beta) x^{-\alpha-1}$.

\item For $\beta \in [-1,1)$, $
\mathbb{P}(X<x) \underset{x\rightarrow -\infty}{\sim} c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha(1-\beta)x^{-\alpha},$ and $
f_X(x) \underset{x\rightarrow -\infty}{\sim} \alpha c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha (1-\beta) x^{-\alpha-1},$
\end{enumerate}
where $c_\alpha= \frac{1-\alpha}{2\Gamma(2-\alpha) \cos(\pi\alpha/2)}\mathbf{1}_{\alpha\neq 1} + 
\pi^{-1} \mathbf{1}_{ \alpha = 1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2511.09280, 'Random Walk conditioned to stay above a non-flat floor: curvature effects'] Let \(\beta>0\). Let \((X_k)_{k\in\Z}\) be an i.i.d.\ sequence of \(\calN(0,\beta)\) random variables and \(S\) the associated random walk. Let \(p\geq 1\), and let \(h:[-1,1]\to [0,1]\) and \(\alpha_p\geq 0\) be given by
    \[
    	h(x) = 1-\abs{x}^p,\; h_n(k) = nh(k/n), \text{ and }\alpha_p = \frac{p-1}{2p-1}.
	\]
    Let \(\{S\geq h_n\} = \{S_k\geq h_n(k)\ \forall k =-n,\dots,n\}\), \(P_{0}^{h_n} = P(\cdot \given S_{-n} = S_n = 0, S\geq h_n)\) and \(\rS_0 = n^{-\alpha_p}(S_0-n)\).
    There exist \(C,c,c_-,c_+\in (0,+\infty)\), \(n_0\geq 1\), such that, for any \(n\geq n_0\) and \(\lambda\geq 1\),
    \[
        C^{-1}e^{-c_- \lambda^{(2p-1)/p}}
        \leq P_{0}^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_0 \geq \lambda \bigr)
        \leq Ce^{-c_+ \lambda^{(2p-1)/p}}.
    \]
    In particular, for all \(p\geq 0\) and \(r\geq 0\), there exist \(K_-\) and \(K_+\) such that, for any \(n\geq n_0\),
    \begin{gather*}
        K_- \leq E_0^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_0^r\bigr) \leq K_+
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        K_- \leq \Var_{P_{0}^{h_n}}(\rS_0) \leq K_+.
    \end{gather*}

[Proposition prop:compound_Poisson of arXiv:2510.18106, 'Law equivalence for Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics\\ driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $Z_t=\sum_{\tau_i\leqslant t}\xi_i$ be a compound Poisson process with rate $\lambda>0$ and jump law $\nu$ on $H$, independent of $W$. Suppose that the hypotheses of (cor:analytic_sufficient of the paper) hold with some $\beta\in(0,\tfrac12)$. Then Assumption~(ass:CM of the paper) holds on $[0,T]$. More explicitly,
\[
\Delta^{Jb}_{A\to\widetilde A}(t)
=\int_0^t\widetilde S(t-s)Q^{1/2}U^{A\to\widetilde A}_s\,ds,
\qquad 0\leqslant t\leqslant T,

body:
[Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\hat{Y}$ the stopped martingale defined above, we can construct a deterministic time change $\tilde{Y}$ that can be expressed as the stochastic integral
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_0^t \tilde{w}_t\,d\tilde{W}(t)
    \]
for $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$,
where
$\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)=Y(q_0)$,
$\tilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion, and $\tilde{w}$ satisfies
the constraint $\E[(\tilde{w}_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$.

\begin{proof} We will construct a  martingale $\tilde{Y}$ to essentially be the deterministic time-change of $\hat{Y}$ such that $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2]=t$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$. Then, for $t\in[\gamma(1),1]$, we will take $\tilde{Y}$ to be any martingale ending at $\pm1$ almost surely, which exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} below. To formalize the time reparametrization, since $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,\gamma(1)]$ is nondecreasing, we can define its right-continuous generalized inverse 
\[\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,.\]
As a consequence of \eqref{e:gamma.prime} we must have $\gamma(t)-\gamma(s)\le t-s$ and $\lambda(t)-\lambda(s)\ge t-s$ for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$. It  follows by combining these inequalities with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} that
    \beq
    \begin{aligned}
    s &\ge \gamma(s) \ge \gamma(1)+s-1 \ge s-4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,\\
    t &\le \lambda(t) \le \lambda(\gamma(1)) + t-\gamma(1)
    =1+t-\gamma(1) \le t+4\epsilon^{1/2}
    \end{aligned}
    \eeq
for all $s\in [q_0,1]$, and $t\in [q_0,\gamma(1)]$. It is clear from this that we must define $\tilde{Y}(t) = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))$, so that
we will have $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2] = \E[\hat{Y}(\lambda(t))^2] = \gamma(\lambda(t))=t$. Since
    \[
    \hat{Y}(\lambda(t)) = Y(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)}
        w_u \ind\{u\le\tau\} \,dW(u)\,,
    \]
by considering the change of variables $u=\lambda(s)$ it is natural to define
    \beq
    \tilde{W}(t) = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)^{1/2} dW(u)\,.
    \eeq
Then $\tilde{W}$ is a local martingale with quadratic variation
    \[
    \langle \tilde{W}\rangle_t 
    = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)\,du
    = \gamma(\lambda(t))-\gamma(q_0) = t-q_0
    \]
for all $t\in[q_0,1]$, so by the L\'evy characterization it is a standard Brownian motion on $t\in[q_0,1]$, and is progressively measurable with respect to the time-changed filtration
$\tilde{\cF}_Y(t)\equiv\cF_Y(\lambda(t))$. We then define the modified control
    \[
    \tilde{w}_s
    \equiv
    \frac{w_{\lambda(s)}}{\gamma'(\lambda(s))^{1/2} }
      \ind\{\lambda(s)\le \tau\}\,,\]
where we define $\tilde{w}_s\equiv1$ in the case $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ --- by Lemma~\ref{l:generalized.inverse.fn}, the set of such times $s$ is of measure zero. If $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ then clearly we have $\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]=1$, and otherwise 
\eqref{e:gamma.prime} gives
	\[\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]
    =\frac{\E[(w_{\lambda(s)})^2 \ind\{
        \lambda(s)\le\tau\}]}
        {\gamma'(\lambda(s))}
    = 1\,.
    \]
We can then express the desired process as
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^t \tilde{w}_s\,d\tilde{W}(s)\,,
    \]
where $\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)= Y(q_0)$. This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] There exists a graded invertible linear map $\Psi:
        T((\mathbb{R}^{d}))
        \to
        T((\mathbb{R}^{d}))$ such that for every smooth path
    $Y=(A,X)$ and any word $w\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$, it holds that
    \[
        \left\langle
            w,
            \Psi\circ\Sig{Y}_{s,t}
        \right\rangle
        =
        \left\langle
            w_k,
            \Sig{X}_{s,t}
        \right\rangle
        \int_{s<t_1<\cdots<t_k<t}
        \prod_{j=1}^{k}
        \left\langle
            w_{j-1},
            \Sig{X}_{s,t_j}
        \right\rangle
        \dd A^{\blue{i_j}}_{t_j},
    \]
    where we uniquely decompose
    \begin{equation}
        w
        =
        w_0\blue{i_1}w_1\cdots\blue{i_k}w_k,
        \qquad
        w_0,\ldots,w_k\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}},
        \quad

[Theorem 34 (Dual layer theorem) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1/2<\alpha<1$, let $\beta\ge1+2\alpha$, and let $A\ge0$. Set
\[
 h(s)=\frac{1+As}{(1-s^p)^\alpha},
 \qquad
 g(s)=\frac{1-As}{(1-s^p)^\alpha},
 \qquad 0\le s<1.
\]
Then for every $x>0$,
\begin{align}
 &x\sum_{|g|=x}\frac{(1-s^p)^{\beta+\alpha-1}}{|g'(s)|}
 +x\sum_{h=x}\frac{(1-s^p)^{\beta+\alpha-1}}{|h'(s)|} \\
 &\hspace{1in}\ge
 A\int_{\{|g|<x<h\}}s(1-s^p)^{\beta+\alpha-1}\,\dd s.
\end{align}

body:
[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] Fix $R>0$. Suppose that there is $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that $g_\varepsilon\in U$ for $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$ and that
		\[
		\log g_\varepsilon
		=\varepsilon Z+P_\varepsilon+W_\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		Z,W_\varepsilon\in\kLie,\quad P_\varepsilon\in\pLie,
		\]
		where $|Z|\le R$, $|P_\varepsilon|\le C_R\varepsilon^{3/2}$, and $|W_\varepsilon|\le C_R\varepsilon^2$. Then, for small $\varepsilon$,
		\[
		h_\varepsilon
		:=\exp(-\varepsilon Z)g_\varepsilon\exp(-P_\varepsilon)
		\]
		satisfies
		\[
		|\pr_{\pLie}\log h_\varepsilon|=O_R(\varepsilon^{5/2}),
		\qquad
		|\pr_{\kLie}\log h_\varepsilon|=O_R(\varepsilon^2).
		\]
		Consequently
		\begin{equation}
			d_{\sr}(e,h_\varepsilon)=O_R(\varepsilon).
		\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:upper_bound of arXiv:2411.11415, 'The ballistic limit of the log-Sobolev constant equals the Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz constant'] Suppose $f \in C^2(\R^d)$
has a unique global minimizer,
and that there are constants $L_0, L_1 > 0$
so that $\Delta f \leqslant L_0 + L_1\,\|\nabla f\|^2$.
For each $t > 0$, let $\mu_t  \deq  \frac{1}{Z_t}\, e^{-f/t}$.
Then
$$
\limsup_{t\to 0^+} \frac{C_{\msf{LS}}(\mu_t)}{t} \leqslant C_{\msf{PL}}(f)\,.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma l.FMEf of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider  a marking  function $\xi$ defined on  ~$\tilde{\mathcal{P}}\in\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}}$. Assume $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ satisfies~(equation e.kappa-bound-fine of the paper) for $k=p$ and $w = 2p\theta_dr^d$  for some  $r>0$.
Then for any $f \in \mathbb{B} ((\mathbb{K}')^p)$,
the functional $\psi_f(\bk\tilde{x}1p;\tilde{\mathcal{P}}\cap B_r(\bk{x}{1}{p}))$ at~(equation e.psip of the paper) admits  for $\alpha^{(p)}$ a.e. $\bk x1p \in (\mathbb{R}^{d})^p$ the following FME
				\begin{align}\nonumber
                  & \quad \mathbb{E} _{\bk x1p} \big[ f( \xi((x_1,U_1),
  \tilde{\mathcal{P}} \cap B_r(\bk{x}{1}{p})),...,\xi((x_p,U_p), \allowbreak\tilde{\mathcal{P}} \cap  B_r(\bk{x}{1}{p}))) \big] \, \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1p)
\\		&= \int_{\mathbb{K}^p}\psi_f(\bk {\tilde{x}}1p;o)\,\mathcal{M}_{\bk
  x1p}^{(p)}(\mathrm{d} \bk u1p) \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1p)\nonumber\\
		&\;+\sum_{l=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{l!}\int_{(B_r(\bk{x}{1}{p})\times \mathbb{K})^l}
 D^{l}_{\bk {\tilde{y}}1l}\psi_f(\bk {\tilde{x}}1p;o)\,
		\mathcal{M}^{(p+l)}_{\bk x1p\sqcup\bk y1l}(\mathrm{d} (\bk u1p\sqcup\bk w1l))\rho^{(p+l)}(\bk
                  x1p\sqcup \bk y1l)\,\mathrm{d} (\bk y1l)\,
		
		\end{align}
where  $\bk {\tilde{x}}1p=\bk {x,u}1p$, $\bk {\tilde{y}}1l=\bk {y,w}1l$.

body: [Definition D-norm of arXiv:2604.16206, 'Extrapolation of max--stable random fields with Fr\'echet marginals'] Let $\mathbf{Z}=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$ be a random vector with components  satisfying $Z_j\geq 0$ a.s., $\mathbb{E} Z_j = 1$, $j = 1,\ldots,n$. Then $\|\mathbf{x}\|_{D(\mathbf{Z})}:= \mathbb{E}\left(\bigvee_{j=1}^n \lvert x_j \rvert Z_j \right),$  $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n,$ defines the so-called \textit{D-norm}, and $\mathbf{Z}$ is called a {\it generator} of this $D-$norm.

[Lemma 37 (Diameter tightness) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let $\eps>0$, so that
$b_\eps:=\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)\in(0,\infty)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:totalmass},
Corollary~\ref{cor:conditionalmass}). Then the rescaled radius
$\sup\{|y|:y\in n^{-1}\mathcal C\}$ is tight under
$\bP(\,\cdot\mid\mu_n(\R^d)>\eps)$: for every $\theta>0$ there is
$K=K(\theta,\eps)<\infty$ with
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\
\bP\bigl(n^{-1}\mathcal C\not\subset\overline B_K\,\big|\,\mu_n(\R^d)>\eps\bigr)\ \le\ \theta .
\]
The same holds with $\mu_n(\R^d)>\eps$ replaced by $\mu_n(\varphi_0)>\eps$ for
any $\varphi_0\in\Cc$ with $\varphi_0\not\equiv0$, but only for admissible $\eps$ in the
sense of Corollary~\ref{cor:conditional}.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.03823, 'Weak rainbow saturation numbers of paths, stars and cycles'] Let  $F$  be a graph on $n$ vertices and $\ell-t$ edges with a  weakly $P_\ell$-rainbow saturated ordering $e_1,e_2,...,e_{e(\bar{F})}$, where $t\in \{0,1\}$ and $n(F)\ge \ell+1\ge 31$. Then for each $i\le \ell-2$,  there is no   $S\subseteq E(F)$ and an explicit assignment of $c$ such that all of  the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)] 
    
\item $|E(F)\setminus S|\ge i$, $| S|\ge 2-t$, 
\item $c(\{e_1,\ldots,e_i\})\subseteq c^*(E(F)\setminus S)$, and
 \item $r_c^{i}(S)\leq |S|-2+t$.
\end{enumerate}

body: Density of bilinear forms in independent vectors. If x, y in R^n are independent with coordinates of densities at most K, then x^T Z y + x^T u + v^T y + w has density at most 2 (C_RV K)^2 (2 e pi)^{1/2} min_{j >= 2} j^{-1/2} (sigma_1(Z) ... sigma_j(Z))^{-1/j} (J. Banks, J. Garza-Vargas, A. Kulkarni, N. Srivastava, Overlaps, eigenvalue gaps, and pseudospectrum under real Ginibre and absolutely continuous perturbations, arXiv:2005.08930, Corollary 2.4; Theorem 2.1 there treats matrices X, Y in R^{n x k}). The proof conditions on y: the form is linear in x with coefficient Z y + u, and E|Z y + u|^{-1} is finite once that vector has a bounded density in two or more dimensions. With rank one it fails, since E|t|^{-1} diverges for a scalar t with bounded density. In the bounded-density conjecture for x^T A x, a single hub coordinate X_h paired with its partner L = <w, X'> is exactly this rank-one bilinear case, which is why one hub needs a third large eigenvalue through a transverse square, while two hubs are the rank-two case and are bounded.

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2608.14802, 'Dynamical Gibbs-non-Gibbs transitions for finite-alphabet models on trees'] Let $i\in \{2,3\}$ and $\theta>4$. Define the sequence $(l^{(i)}_n(t))_{n\in \N_0}$ recursively by $l^{(i)}_0(t):=l$ and $l^{(i)}_{n+1}(t):=g_t^{[i]}(l_n^{(i)}(t))$ for all $n\in \N_0$. Then there exists a time $t_B< \infty$ such that for every $t\geq t_B$, the sequence has the following properties:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\alph*)]
      \item The limit $l^{(i)}(t):=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}l^{(i)}_n(t)$ exists and is a fixed point of $g_t^{[i]}$.
      \item There exist neighborhoods $U_2$ and $U_3$ of the unperturbed $f$-stable fixed points $l_+^{(2)}$ and $l_+^{(3)}$, respectively, as defined in Lemma \ref{lem: Fixed points normalized simplex Potts model}, such that the limiting fixed points $l^{(2)}(t)$ and $l^{(3)}(t)$ from part a) satisfy $l^{(i)}(t)\in U_i$ for $i\in \{2,3\}$.
Moreover, for every $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and every $i\in\{2,3\}$, the corresponding time-dependent inhomogeneous recursion satisfies $G_t^{[j]}\left((U_i)^{2}\right)\subset U_i.$
      \item The neighborhoods $U_2$ and $U_3$ can be chosen such that the corresponding root conditional probabilities \eqref{eq: Root marginals recursive description} are uniformly separated. More precisely, there exists $C>0$ such that
      \begin{equation}
          \inf_{\substack{l^{(1)},l^{(2)},l^{(3)}\in U_2\\
          \widetilde{l}^{(1)},\widetilde{l}^{(2)},\widetilde{l}^{(3)}\in U_3}}\left|R_{t,2}(l^{(1)},l^{(2)},l^{(3)})-R_{t,2}(\widetilde{l}^{(1)},\widetilde{l}^{(2)},\widetilde{l}^{(3)})\right|\geq C\mathrm{exp}\left(-\frac{3t}{2}\right) 
      \end{equation}
      where $R_{t,2}$ is defined in \eqref{eq: Definition R_t,k and H_a(l)} in the \hyperref[Appendix: Lipschitz bound for root marginals]{Appendix B}.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, in the study of dynamical systems, the Hartman–Grobman theorem or linearization theorem is a theorem about the local behaviour of dynamical systems in the neighbourhood of a hyperbolic equilibrium point.         \max_{u,v\in V(\mathcal C_1)}\Reff^{\mathcal C_1}(u,v)&\le B_{A,\eta} n^{1/3},
\end{align*}
and there are disjoint vertex sets $A_n,B_n\subseteq V(\mathcal C_1)$ such that
\[
        \pi(A_n),\pi(B_n)\ge \alpha_{A,\eta},
        \qquad
        \Reff^{\mathcal C_1}(A_n,B_n)\ge b_{A,\eta} n^{1/3}.
\]

body:
Let A be an m by n random matrix with independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian entries of proxy at most K. Then with probability at least 1 - 2 exp(-c t^2), the operator norm satisfies ||A|| <= C K (sqrt(m) + sqrt(n) + t), with absolute constants c, C. In particular ||A|| is of order sqrt(m) + sqrt(n) with high probability - the correct scale, matching the Bai-Yin limit for iid fourth-moment entries.

[Prop 16 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] For $\delta >0$, 
let $(X_t, \mathscr{J}_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ be a weak limit in $\mathcal{C}([0,T], \mathcal{H}^{-1}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})\times \mathcal{H}^{-(3+\delta)}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}))$  of the couple of processes $\{(X_t^{(h)},\mathscr{J}_t(X^{(h)}))_{0 \le t \le T}\}_{ h \in T/{\mathbb N}^*}$ when $h\searrow 0$. 
Let $\phi\in \mathcal{H}^{(3+\delta)}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})\cap \mathcal{U}^2(\mathbb{S})$

and $\varepsilon >0$. 
Then, 
with probability one, 
for all $0\leq s<t\leq T$, 
\begin{align}
	\langle \phi, \mathscr{J}_{t}- \mathscr{J}_{s}\rangle \geq  \frac{1}{2}\int_s^t\int_{\mathbb{S}}\frac{\phi'(\mathbf{x})}{E_{\varepsilon}(\mathbf{x})+ D_{\mathbf{x}}{X}_{r}(\mathbf{x})}\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}\mathrm{d}r,
\end{align}
where $E_\varepsilon(\mathbf{x})$ is given by \eqref{eq:varepsilon}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 35 (Boundary trace of the free bulk evolution) of arXiv:2609.01826, 'An extension theory for fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory'] Let $I=[0,T]$ with $T<\infty$, and let $q,r$ be as in
Theorem~\ref{T:memory-wp}. Let $U_0\in L_a^2(\RN)$. If $0\le a<1$, then
\[
\mathbb T_a^\star(U_0)\in C^b_z\bigl([0,\infty);L_t^q(I;L_x^r(\Rd))\bigr);
\]
in particular $z\mapsto\mathbb T_a^\star(U_0)(\cdot,z,\cdot)$ extends
continuously to $z=0$ as an $L_t^q(I;L_x^r)$-valued map. If $-1<a<0$, the same
conclusion holds for the weighted free evolution
$k(z)\,\mathbb T_a^\star(U_0)$, in the mixed-norm framework of
\cite[Theorem~2.4]{GS2}; since $k(z)=1$ for $0\le z\le1$, this yields the same
boundary trace in $L_t^q(I;L_x^r)$.

body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\beta_1:=\frac{1}{2k(d-1)+1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s:=\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}.
\]
Then, for every pair of mappings $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ with
$f_j,g_j\in \mathcal{P}_d(\gamma)$,
\[
\int_E \Delta_f\,d\gamma\ge a,
\quad
\int_E \Delta_g\,d\gamma\ge a,
\]
and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(f_j)\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(g_j)\le b,
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_1)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1k^{3/2}d\,(\beta_1-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, if $d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2k^{3/2}d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^{\beta_1},
\end{equation}
where $C_2>0$ is an absolute constant.

More generally, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$, setting
\[
\beta_r:=\frac{1}{2rk(d-1)+1},
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_r)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1(r,k)\,d\,(\beta_r-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_r(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$. Moreover, if $d_r(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2(r,k)\,d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_r(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_r(f,g)^{\beta_r},
\end{equation}
where $C_2(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$.

[Corollary 12 (Parametrization of the unique toroidal limit) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Assume the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:classification} and suppose that
$\Var_T\neq0$ and $\spt\Var_T$ has genus one.  Then there exists a
uniformly conformal bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism
\[
 f\in W^{2,2}(\Sigma,\R^4)\cap W^{1,\infty}(\Sigma,\R^4),
 \qquad
 f\colon\Sigma\longrightarrow M:=\spt\Var_T,
\]
and there are a smooth zero-scalar-curvature, unit-volume metric
$g_{\mathrm{poin}}$ on $\Sigma$ and a function $u\in L^\infty(\Sigma)$
such that
\begin{equation}
 
 f^*g_{\mathrm{euc}}=e^{2u}g_{\mathrm{poin}}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 
 \Var_T=v(M,1),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 
 \lVert\Var_T\rVert
 =f_\#\mu_{f^*g_{\mathrm{euc}}}
 =\mathcal H^2\llcorner M.
\end{equation}
In particular, formula \eqref{eq:limit-measure} is independent of the sequence
used to construct the parametrization $f$.

[Proposition 28 (Poisson-tail estimate {\cite[Remark~3) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] {DFP}}]
Let \(t=t(\lambda)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) satisfy \(t/\lambda=o(1)\). Then
\[
1\le \frac{F_\lambda(t)}{p_\lambda(t)}
\le \sum_{j=0}^{t}\Bigl(\frac{t}{\lambda}\Bigr)^j
\le \frac{1}{1-t/\lambda}
=1+o(1).
\]
In particular,
\[
F_\lambda(t)=(1+o(1))\,p_\lambda(t).
\]

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2604.05999, 'Branching Process in a Varying Environment: How to Grow Like the Product of Means'] Assume the Spitzer condition
$$
\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{n} {\bf P}(S_k>0)\to \rho\in (0,1),\ n\to\infty
$$
i) Let for some $\beta\in (0,1]$ 
$$\widehat{\zeta}_i:=\ln {\bf E}_{\boldsymbol\eta} U_i^{1+\delta}, i\ge 1,
$$
be a.s. finite r.v., such that 
$$
{\bf E}\widehat{\zeta}_1<+\infty.
$$

ii) Let for some $\beta>1$, $\delta_0\in (0,1)$ 
$$\widetilde{\zeta}_i:={\bf E}_{\boldsymbol\eta} U_i \log^{\beta/\rho+\delta_0}\left(1+U_i\right), i\ge 1,
$$
be a.s. finite r.v., such that
$$
{\bf E}\widetilde{\zeta}_1^{1/(\beta-1)}<+\infty,\quad 
{\bf E}V(\xi_1) \widetilde{\zeta}_1^{\rho/(\beta-1)}<+\infty,
$$
where $V(\cdot)$ is defined by (1.4) of~\cite{AGKV}. 

Then~(\ref{P+ZnConv}) is true. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Berlowertails of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] There exist absolute positive constants $C$, $C_1$, $C_2\geq 1$
such that the following holds.   Let $n$ be a large enough integer and 
$C\log n \leq d \leq n/2$.  Let 
     $\mathcal{B}_{n}$ be an $n \times n$ random matrix having i.i.d. Bernoulli$(d/n)$ entries. Let $z\in \mathbb{C}$ 
     satisfy  $|z| \leq \sqrt{d}\, \log \log d$. Then 
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(s_n(\mathcal{B}_{n}-z\mathbf{I}_{n}) \leq n^{-\beta}) 
    \leq \frac{C_1}{\sqrt{d}},
    \]
     for some $\beta \in   (2,  C_2 \log \log n]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \((N,R_{+},R_{-},\gamma)\) be a sutured manifold and \(S\) be a properly embedded surface in \(N\).
We call \(S\) a \emph{decomposition surface} for \((N,\gamma)\) if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any sutured torus \(T\), the intersection \(S\cap T\) is either empty or a collection of essential simple closed curves, all of which represent the same homology class in \(H_{1}(T)\).
\item For any sutured annulus \(A\), \(S\cap A\) is either empty, a simple closed curve with the same homology class as the suture \(A\cap s(\gamma)\), or a properly embedded nonseparating arc.
\item No component of \(\partial S\) bounds a disc in \(R(\gamma)\) and no component of \(S\) is a disc \(D\) with \(\partial D\subset R_{+}\cup R_{-}\).
\end{enumerate}

Let pi be a prior probability, let L(theta)=log p(D|theta) be finite pi-almost-surely, and let I be an open interval of positive inverse temperatures. Let q_lambda=e^(lambda L)pi/Z(lambda), with 0<Z(lambda)<infinity for lambda in I. Let f be a real measurable function independent of lambda. Explicit sufficient regularity for the source differentiation step is: for each compact K contained in I there is a pi-integrable H_K dominating e^(lambda L)(1+|f|)(1+|L|^2) for all lambda in K. Then d/dlambda E_q_lambda f=Cov_q_lambda(f,L). In particular the total-data Gibbs objective J(q_lambda)=-E_q_lambda L satisfies Jprime(lambda)=-Var_q_lambda(L)<=0. For the per-example objective Ghat=J/n, the derivative is -(1/n)Var_q_lambda(L). These two normalizations must not be interchanged. This is the AppendixA Eq14 quotient-rule identity with sufficient differentiation regularity made explicit; no globally strict decrease is asserted when the variance vanishes.

[Defn 9 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] [See \cite[Definitions~3.8, 3.9 and 3.11]{Ya}.]
A pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra
\[
\sA^*=(A^*,d,F,\alpha:L\to A^0,\delta:L\to A^1)
\]
over $\sR$ is \emph{saturated} if its underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra is
saturated in the sense of \cite[Definition~3.4.1]{BLM}. Let
\[
i_A\colon A^*\longrightarrow\Sat(A^*)
\]
be the saturation map of the underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra. We equip
$\Sat(A^*)$ with the same monoid $L$ and with maps
\[
\alpha_{\rm sat}:=i_A^0\circ\alpha,
\qquad
\delta_{\rm sat}:=i_A^1\circ\delta.
\]
The resulting pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra is denoted by $\Sat(\sA^*)$.

A saturated pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra is \emph{strict} if its
underlying saturated Dieudonn\'e algebra is strict in the sense of
\cite[Definition~3.5.6]{BLM}. If
\[
\rho_A\colon A^*\longrightarrow W(A^*)
=
\varprojlim_r A^*/\mathrm{Fil}^rA^*
\]
is the strictification map of the underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra, we
equip $W(A^*)$ with the same monoid $L$ and with maps
\[
\alpha_W:=\rho_A^0\circ\alpha,
\qquad
\delta_W:=\rho_A^1\circ\delta.
\]
We write $W(\sA^*)$ for the resulting strict pre-log Dieudonn\'e
algebra and set
\[
\WSat(\sA^*):=W(\Sat(\sA^*)).
\]

[Prop u11 of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] Assume that the existence condition~(equation intro:existence of the paper) is satisfied and that the drift $\mu$ is non-zero.
Denote by $\mu_1^{-}$ and $\mu_2^{-}$ the negative parts of the drift components (defined by $\mu_i^-=\max(-\mu_i,0)$). 
The process $Z$ is transient if and only if
\begin{equation}
\mu_1 + r_{2}\mu_2^{-} > 0 
\quad \text{or} \quad 
\mu_2 + r_{1}\mu_1^{-} > 0,

\end{equation}
and recurrent if and only if
\begin{equation}
\mu_1 + r_{2}\mu_2^{-} \le 0 
\quad \text{and} \quad 
\mu_2 + r_{1}\mu_1^{-} \le 0.

\end{equation}
In the latter case, the process is positive recurrent and admits a unique stationary
distribution if and only if
\begin{equation}
\mu_1 + r_{2}\mu_2^{-} < 0 
\quad \text{and} \quad 
\mu_2 + r_{1}\mu_1^{-} < 0,

\end{equation}
and is null recurrent if and only if
\[
\mu_1 + r_{2}\mu_2^{-} = 0 
\quad \text{or} \quad 
\mu_2 + r_{1}\mu_1^{-} = 0.
\]
In this case, the invariant measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure and we denote by $\pi$ its density. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Recurrence and transience criterion

[Proposition prop:nondeg-NS of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] Consider this periodic-torus specialisation of the stochastic 2D Navier--Stokes equation (equation eq:NS-full of the paper) with additive noise $\mathcal{B} = Q^{1/2}$ where $Q$ excites finitely many eigenmodes of $A$, and write $g_k := Q^{1/2}f_k$ for the forcing directions. Suppose the noise satisfies the H\"ormander bracket condition of Hairer--Mattingly [hairer2011hormander]. Setting $\mathcal{A}_0 := \{g_k\}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{n+1} := \mathcal{A}_n \cup \{\widetilde{B}(h_1, h_2) : h_1, h_2 \in \mathcal{A}_n\}$ with $\widetilde{B}(h_1,h_2) := B(h_1,h_2) + B(h_2,h_1)$ the symmetrised nonlinearity, the linear span of $\mathcal{A}_\infty := \bigcup_{n \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_n$ is dense in $H$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
  \item \textup{(Finite-dimensional projected logarithmic derivatives)} For each $N \geq 1$, the projection $\Pi_N X(t)$ admits a smooth, everywhere strictly positive Lebesgue density on $H_N := \mathrm{ran}(\Pi_N) = \mathrm{span}\{e_1, \ldots, e_N\}$, with smooth, globally defined logarithmic derivative $\nabla\log p_N: H_N \to H_N$, by the Mattingly--Pardoux theorem for the 2D torus [mattinglypardoux2006malliavin] (smoothness and everywhere strict positivity of all finite-dimensional projected densities, for all $t > 0$, under viscosity-independent conditions), the torus instance of the general Hairer--Mattingly H\"ormander framework [hairer2011hormander] applied to the projection $\Pi_N\gamma_t\Pi_N$. The projected logarithmic derivative is given by the abstract Bismut--Fomin theorem (Theorem~(thm:abstract-bismut-fomin of the paper)) applied to $F = \Pi_N X(t)$ on the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $H_N$, with the compression $\Gamma_N = \Pi_N\gamma_t\Pi_N$ as its Malliavin covariance.
 \item \textup{(Admissible direction space for full $H$-directional logarithmic derivatives)} Define the \emph{admissible direction space}
  \begin{align*}
    \mathcal{H}^{\sharp}_t &\;:=\; \bigl\{h \in H : \text{Assumption~(ass:nondeg of the paper) holds for } h\bigr\} \\
    &\;=\; \bigl\{h \in H : h \in \operatorname{Ran}(\gamma_t) \text{ a.s.,}\;\; \mathbb{E}[\norm{\gamma_t^{\dagger}h}_H^q] < \infty \\
    &\qquad\qquad \text{ at the H\"older-triangle exponent } q, \\
    &\qquad\qquad\;\; \text{Cameron--Martin compatibility}~(equation eq:CM-compat-limit of the paper)\text{--}(equation eq:CM-compat-dominator of the paper)\bigr\}.
  \end{align*}
  Then for every $h \in \mathcal{H}^{\sharp}_t$ for which the domain hypothesis $v_h \in \operatorname{Dom}(\delta_U)$ of Theorem~(thm:main of the paper), Part~I, additionally holds, sufficient conditions being those of Remark~(rem:domain-vh-suffic of the paper), the full-$H$-directional Bismut--Fomin identity $\partial_h \mu_t = \beta_h\,\mu_t$ applies, with $\beta_h(X(t)) = -\mathbb{E}[\delta_U(v_h)\mid X(t)]$. If the further fixed-Tikhonov and raised structural hypotheses of Part~II hold, the explicit decomposition~(equation eq:skorokhod-decomp of the paper) applies as well.
  \item \textup{(Scope of (2))} The space $\mathcal{H}^{\sharp}_t$ is a deterministic subset of $H$, cut out by almost-sure and expectation conditions on $\gamma_t$. Verification of $h \in \mathcal{H}^{\sharp}_t$ for any specific $h$ is a separate quantitative input (verification of clauses~(i)--(ii)--(iii) of Assumption~(ass:nondeg of the paper) for the specific direction). The denseness of $\mathcal{H}^{\sharp}_t$ in $H$ is genuinely subtle and is open in full generality under H\"ormander's bracket condition alone; see Remark~(rem:nondeg-NS-gap of the paper) for the obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\medskip\noindent The Mattingly--Pardoux/Hairer--Mattingly bounds control cone-restricted quadratic forms of $\gamma_t$ (all unit $\phi$ with a definite component in a fixed finite-dimensional range), and in particular the compressed matrices $\Pi_N\gamma_t\Pi_N$; for each fixed nonzero $\phi$ in the reachable span (dense under the bracket condition) they give $\langle \gamma_t \phi, \phi\ran (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:contraction-with-cascade-coefficients-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let 
\(
q\in(1,2)
\),
\(r\ge2\), and let \(G\) be a finite set. Fix \(m\ge0\).
Suppose that the family
\[
(Z_u)_{\lvert u \rvert=m}
\]
is independent of \(\mathcal F^X_m\), that the vectors \(Z_u\) are independent
and coordinatewise mean zero, and that all \(Z_u\) have the same distribution
as a random vector \(Z\) with
\[
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q<\infty.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\left\|
\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u Z_u
\right\|_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\middle|\mathcal F^X_m
\right]
\le
C_q r^{q/2}
\left(\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u^q\right)
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\left\|
\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u Z_u
\right\|_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\right]
\le
C_q r^{q/2}\rho(q)^m
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q.
\end{equation}

body: [Lemma 48 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Let $a_2<a_1<0$. [Theorem thm:cross-sign of arXiv:2602.19192, 'Bakry--\'Emery Curvature of the Fractional Laplacian\\ via Fractional Brownian Covariance'] For $n,m > 0$:
\begin{equation}
  \Psi_\gamma(n,-m) = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(n^\gamma + m^\gamma
  - (n+m)^\gamma\bigr).
\end{equation}
This vanishes identically if and only if $\gamma = 1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item At $\gamma = 1$: $\Psi_1(n,-m)
  = \tfrac{1}{2}(n + m - (n+m)) = 0$ for all $n,m > 0$.
\item For $\gamma < 1$: $\Psi_\gamma(n,-m) > 0$
  (subadditivity of $|\cdot|^\gamma$).
\item For $\gamma > 1$: $\Psi_\gamma(n,-m) < 0$
  (superadditivity of $|\cdot|^\gamma$).
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Let $F_t = e^{tL}$ be a strongly continuous bounded semigroup on a Banach space $(B,\|\cdot\|_B)$:
        \[
            \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{B \to B} \leq e^{\bar m t}.
        \]
        
        Let $L$ be the generator of $F_t$, and let $D \subset \operatorname{dom} L$ be another Banach space with $\|\cdot\|_D \geq \|\cdot\|_B$ such that
        \[
        \|Lf\|_B \leq l \|f\|_D \, \forall f \in D.
        \]
        Assume also that $F_t$ is bounded in $D$:
        \[
        \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{D \to D} \leq e^{m t},
        \]
        for some $m \geq 0$.
        
        
        Let $U_h$ be a family of linear bounded operators in $B$ with 
        \[
          \| U_h \|_{B \to B} \leq e^{q h},
          \qquad q\ge0,
        \]
        and let
        \begin{align} 
        \left\| \left( \frac{U_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \epsilon_h \|f\|_D, \\
        
        \left\| \left( \frac{F_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \chi_h \|f\|_D, 
        \end{align}
        where $\epsilon_h,\chi_h>0$ are monotone and tend to zero as $h\to0$.
        
        Then
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t} \left\| (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f - F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{ms + q (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{\bar m t} h (l + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}
        \end{equation}

        For the killed semigroups with rate $c>0$,
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t}
            \left\| e^{-c\lfloor s/h\rfloor h } (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f
            - e^{-cs} F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{(m-c)s + (q-c) (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{(\bar m - c) t} h (l + \epsilon_h + c) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}
        \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 21 of arXiv:2605.31471

[Definition def:averagecase of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \\ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] Let $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ be a metric Polish probability space. Given $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\epsilon > 0$ and $r>0$, we say that $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is \emph{$(n,\epsilon,r)$-average-case approximable} if, whenever $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are i.i.d.\ with distribution $\mu$ on a probability space $(\Psi,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, there is an event of $\mathbb{P}$-probability at least $1-\epsilon$ on which one has
    \[
    \bigg|\int\!f(x)\,\mu(dx) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nf(X_i)\bigg|\leq r\cdot\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\|f\|_{\text{Lip},B(X_i,r)}
    \]
    for all Lipschitz functions $f:\mathfrak{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$. Given $\epsilon,r:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$ which vanish as $n\rightarrow\infty$, we say that $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is \emph{asymptotically average-case approximable with rate $(\epsilon,r)$} if, for all $n$ sufficiently large, $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is $(n,\epsilon(n),r(n))$-average-case approximable.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Pair-balanced factual identities under partial verification

T379-C015 v2, proof (unaudited). Both exact verification suites PASS;
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending.
Targets 1 and 2. This is a conditional data-regime result, not a global
expected minimax claim. The unresolved unequal-sibling-count regime is
the hardest missing piece; C010 shows why its ordering cannot be assumed.

## Model and data region

Use the paired VC-d experiment: d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K integers;
one A and one S per pair, all remaining contexts known S. S has K true
candidates, A has an independent uniform r-subset. The source p chooses
contexts uniformly, then true candidates uniformly. Observe n>=0 iid
factual context/candidate samples without orientation tags. Independently
a perfect verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each
variable context, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Let C_x be the union of
distinct observed and verified candidate identities in context x.

Condition on any positive-probability data outcome for which every pair
has |C_left|=|C_right|=h_j<=r. The actual identities may differ. Thus no
orientation is logically excluded, and every one of 2^d orientations
is compatible. Counts and likelihoods of repeated observations can be
unequal: uniform orientation weights below are an ARTIFICIAL proof
distribution, not the actual Bayesian posterior. Under a chosen
orientation, the A support ranges uniformly over r-subsets containing
C_A. Put D_h=#{j:h_j=h}, ell<=h<=r.

Define

 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N),
 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)),
 M_h=(D_h/N)*(2-h/r-h/K),
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

Over ALL generators, with source Mis_infinity<=c required in every
compatible world (including every compatible A support), the proposed
exact conditional worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V_D(c)=tau_ell*(T_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h=ell+1}^r (tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.       (1)

All formulas allow missing D_h and c in [0,1]. Exact score bins define
source Mis_infinity=TV(g,p_Pi), with p uniformly coarsened in each bin.

## Lower bound across arbitrary mixed bins

Average orientations fairly and A supports uniformly conditional on
containing their known identities. Let mu be the resulting mean law.
Every known true atom in a variable context has density

 a=(1/r+1/K)/(2N).

probability tau_h under this artificial prior. Their total mu mass is
M_h across the D_h pairs. Known S atoms have density 1/(NK).

with count at least h, consists of lower-density atoms than its entire
complement. For ANY partition Pi, uniform coarsening increases its mass:

its complement, so replacing both means by the cell mean transfers
mass into E_h. This proves the assertion per bin, not merely globally.

[Lemma 70 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $\nu$ be a compactly-supported signed measure on $\amsmathbb{A}$ with density $\mathscr{L}^2(\amsmathbb A)\cap \mathscr{L}^1(\amsmathbb A)$, and such that
\[
\forall e \in [\mathfrak{e}]\qquad \mathfrak r_e\big((\nu([\hat a'_h,\hat b'_h]))_{h = 1}^H\big) = 0.
\]
Then there exists $C>0$ depending only on the constants of Assumption
 \ref{Assumptions_Theta}, such that for any function $f$ with finite $|\!|f|\!|_{\frac{1}{2}}$ we have
 \[
 \biggl|\int_{\amsmathbb R} f(x) \nu(x)\dd x \biggr|^2 \leq C\,\D[\boldsymbol{\nu},\boldsymbol{0}]\, |\!|f|\!|^2_{\frac{1}{2}}.
 \]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2511.01245, 'A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain'] For the binary Burnside process on $C_2^n$, we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \binom{n}{2k} \left(\frac{1}{2^{4k}} \binom{2k}{k}^2\right)^{2\ell}$.
    \item Take any $\varepsilon > 0$. If $\ell \le (1-\varepsilon) \frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$, then $\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Meanwhile, if $\ell \ge (1+\varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$, then $\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Therefore, there is some sequence of starting states $x^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ such that $\chi_{x^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ even after $(1 - \varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$ steps, while all starting states $x$ have $\chi_x^2(\ell) \to 0$ after just $(1 + \varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$ steps. 
    \item Let $x^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ be any sequence of states such that $cn \le |x^{(n)}| \le (1 - c)n$ for some $c \in (0, 1)$ (where $|x|$ denotes the number of ones in $x$). Then $\chi_{x^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ for $\ell = \Theta_c\left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)$ (that is, after order $\frac{n}{\log n}$ steps with constant depending only on $c$). 
    \item In particular, let $y^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ be the states with $\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor$ zeros followed by $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$ ones. Then $\chi_{y^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ for $\ell \le (1-\varepsilon) \frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 34 ($h$-adic saturation) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every $z\in Z_h$ and every $m\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \hc_h(z)\in h^mU_h^0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 z\in h^mZ_h.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\hc_h$ is injective.

Candidate inference to be tested: rapid decay of the truncated particle-density two-point function, together with fast empty-disk probabilities, implies quantitative alpha mixing of full point-process restrictions in separated windows. This inference is refuted by the accompanying stationary Cox process. A density pair function is a second-order statistic; alpha mixing controls all measurable local events. Neither a Gibbs specification nor ergodicity of that counterexample is claimed.
Stationarity, simplicity, finite positive intensity, and fast void tails.
No independent process-mixing hypothesis may be silently substituted by a density pair bound.
title: Rejected route: density pairs determine process mixing

[Corollary cor:deterministiclimit of arXiv:2608.21931, 'Interacting Urn Schemes on Finite Ancestral Directed Acyclic Graphs'] Suppose that Assumption~(asm:deterministiclimit of the paper) holds. Then the entire
system $\{\U{n}{v}:n\ge0,\ v\in V\}$ converges almost surely to a
deterministic limit $\{\us{}{v}:v\in V\}$; that is,
\[
\U{n}{v}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\us{}{v},
\qquad
\text{as }n\to\infty,\ \forall v\in V.
\]

For the sum-reinforcement scheme, the limiting proportions are
characterized as follows. For each generator $g\in G$, the limit
$\us{}{g}$ is the normalized Perron--Frobenius eigenvector of
$R^{(g,g)}$. For $v\in V\setminus G$,
\begin{equation}
\us{}{v}:=
\begin{cases}
\U{0}{v}, & \text{if }v\in S,\\[0.25cm]
\displaystyle
\frac{1}{b_v}
\sum_{p:p\rightsquigarrow v}
\us{}{p}R^{(p,v)},
& \text{if }v\in V\setminus(G\cup S),
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
where
\[
b_v:=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{p:p\rightsquigarrow v}r\big((p,v)\big),
& \text{if }v\in V\setminus S,\\[0.25cm]
1, & \text{if }v\in S,
\end{cases}
\]
is referred to as the \emph{total balance} of the vertex $v$.

For the average-reinforcement scheme, the limiting proportions are
obtained from (equation 11 of the paper) by replacing each reinforcement matrix
$R^{(p,v)}$ with $R^{(p,v)}/d_v^{\mathrm{in}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textbf{Strong convergence for irreducible generators}

[Theorem Important Estimates of arXiv:2411.04631, 'Existence of Martingale Solutions to Stochastic Constrained Heat Equation'] Suppose $u_{n}(t)$ solves (equation faedo after Qn of the paper) then\\
\begin{align}
    \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{E} \left(\sup_{s \in [0,T]}||u_{n}(t')||^{2}\right) \leq C_{1},\\
    \sup_{n\geq 1} \mathbb{E} \left(\sup_{s \in [0,T]}|u_{n}(t')|^{2n}_{{L^{2n}}}\right) \leq C_{2},\\
    \sup_{n\geq 1}\mathbb{E}\left(\int_{0}^{T} |u_{n}(t')|^{2}_{\mathcal{E}}dt'\right) \leq C_{3},
\end{align}
for some constants $C_{1},C_{2},C_{3}>0$.
title: Theorem Important Estimates of arXiv:2411.04631

Own work draft, proof (unaudited), conditional on C012 and C007; no independent PASS and no novelty assertion. In the noiseless isotropic Gaussian teacher model with an independently specified probe at fixed theta in (0,pi/2], let E(alpha,theta) be the infimum of fixed-threshold max-margin limiting errors at retained aspect alpha, including no pruning f=1, with dimension limit first. For alpha>=1, sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*alpha)<=E(alpha,theta)<=1/alpha, so its large-alpha log-log exponent is -1. The lower bound is the retained-label latitude/counting argument C012, independent of original-pool size. For the upper bound keep all data: the classical Vapnik support-vector leave-one-out bound, reproduced in Burges 1998 Sec.7.4 Eq.(93), says expected risk of an m-point SVM is at most the expected support-vector fraction in m+1 iid points. Folded Gaussian rows have full density on the teacher half-space and affine general position, so a homogeneous minimum-norm hard-margin classifier has at most d active constraints almost surely, giving expected error<=d/(m+1). C007 and bounded convergence give unpruned limiting error<=1/alpha. The classical bound itself is not new; this is an unaudited application combined with C012. The constants leave a gap as theta->0. An exact crossover, initial exponential regime and optimal retained fraction are not established.
C012 v2 retained-budget lower envelope accepted
C007 unpruned max-margin limit accepted
Noiseless isotropic Gaussian teacher; independent fixed probe angle theta>0
Homogeneous linear max-margin with no fitted intercept
Retained aspect alpha>=1; no-pruning endpoint included in envelope
Each threshold fixed before dimension limit; infimum afterwards
title: Draft: imperfect-probe inverse-retained-budget envelope via Vapnik SVM leave-one-out bound (w694 C014; unaudited)

Let (X, Y1, Y2) be jointly Gaussian with S11 = Cov(Y1), S12 = Cov(Y1, Y2), S22 = Cov(Y2), C1 = Cov(X, Y1), C2 = Cov(X, Y2), possibly singular, with Moore-Penrose inverses; let m1 and K1 be the conditional mean and covariance of X given Y1 = y1, T = S22 - S12^T S11^+ S12, D = C2 - C1 S11^+ S12, and w = y2 - mu2 - S12^T S11^+ (y1 - mu1) the innovation of the second observation. For compatible (y1, y2), the conditional law of X given Y1 = y1 and Y2 = y2 has mean m12 = m1 + D T^+ w and covariance K12 = K1 - D T^+ D^T, which coincide with the one-shot pseudoinverse formulas for the stacked observation (Y1, Y2). The second update must use the innovation w, not the raw deviation y2 - mu2.

[Proposition cor: technical on graphs of arXiv:2512.18435, 'Indistinguishability for recurrent clusters'] Let $G$ be a Cayley graph of a finitely generated group $\Gamma$, $\eta$ an invariant labelling of $G$ and $\omega$ an $\eta$-measurable percolation process such that $(\eta,\omega)$ is jointly $\Gamma$-invariant.

       Let $(\eta',\omega')$ be an identically distributed copy of $(\eta,\omega)$, $x$ and $x'$ two vertices, $E$ an $(\eta,\eta')$-measurable event on which the clusters $K$ of $x$ in $\omega$ and $K'$ of $x'$ in $\omega'$ are infinite, and assume that, conditionally on $E$, $\eta$ and $\eta'$ only differ in a finite set $S$ such that $K\setminus S$ and $K'\setminus S$ share at least one infinite connected component $K_0$.

    Let $\mathscr A$ be a component property. Then, conditionally on $E$, $x$ has type $\mathscr A$ in $\eta$ if and only if $x'$ has type $\mathscr A$ in $\eta'$ (up to a probability 0 event). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition cor: technical on graphs of arXiv:2512.18435

Then, $F$ is the restriction to $U$ of a function, say $F_0$, analytic in $\mathbb C_r$ and such that $K_{F_0,t}(z,w)$ is positive definite in $\mathbb C_r$ if and only if the

Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables with values in [0,1], let X = sum_i X_i and mu = E[X]. Then for every delta > 0, P(X >= (1 + delta) mu) <= ( e^{delta} / (1 + delta)^{1 + delta} )^{mu} <= exp( - delta^2 mu / (2 + delta) ), and for every delta in (0,1), P(X <= (1 - delta) mu) <= ( e^{-delta} / (1 - delta)^{1 - delta} )^{mu} <= exp( - delta^2 mu / 2 ). The two tails have DIFFERENT constants and the upper-tail exponent degrades from delta^2 mu/3 for delta <= 1 to roughly delta mu log delta for large delta; quoting the lower-tail constant 1/2 for the upper tail is a common error. The bounds hold with mu replaced by any upper bound on E[X] in the upper tail, and by any lower bound in the lower tail, which is how they are usually applied. The variables need only be independent and [0,1]-valued, not identically distributed and not Bernoulli. [standard; e.g. Mitzenmacher and Upfal, Probability and Computing, 2nd ed., Theorems 4.4 and 4.5]
X_1, ..., X_n independent with values in [0,1]
mu = E[X] (or an upper bound for the upper tail, a lower bound for the lower tail)
delta > 0 for the upper tail, delta in (0,1) for the lower tail

body:
[Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Fix $n\in \Z_{\geq 1}$ and a set $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda_0(n)\subset \Lambda\subset \Lambda_1(n)$ (see Section \ref{subsection:coarsemapproper}). 
    Let $G$ be a closed subgroup of $\rmB(n)$.
    Then the composition $\mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G : G\to \R^{ \Lambda}$ is coarse.
    Here, $G$ is equipped with the LR-coarse structure, $\R^{\Lambda}$ is equipped with the bounded coarse structure (see Example \ref{example:coarse}) and $\iota_G$ is the inclusion map from $G$ to $\rmB(n)$.
    In particular, for closed subgroups $L,H$ of $G$, 
    if the pair $(\mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G(L), \mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G(H))$ is asymptotically disjoint in $(\R^{ \Lambda},\mathcal{E}_d)$, 
    the natural $L$-action on $G/H$ is proper (see Corollary \ref{corollary:coarsemapproper}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.25785

body:
[Lemma pointwise-criterion of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $F\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ be a $T$-functor. Then $F$ admits a right adjoint if and only if $F_A\colon{\mathcal{C}}(A)\to{\mathcal{D}}(A)$ admits a right adjoint $G_A$ for every $A\in T$ such that these right adjoints satisfy the \emph{Beck--Chevalley condition}: for every $f\colon A\to B$ in $T$ the Beck--Chevalley map $f^*G_B\to G_Af^*$ associated to the naturality equivalence $f^*F_B\simeq F_Af^*$ is an equivalence. 
    
    Moreover, in this case the functor $F_X\colon{\mathcal{C}}(X)\to{\mathcal{D}}(X)$ admits a right adjoint $G_X$ more generally for any $X\in\PSh(T)$, and the Beck--Chevalley condition holds more generally for all maps in $\PSh(T)$.\qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Cor 14 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $d = o(\sqrt n)$. Let $\mathbf X\sim \Inv_2(R)$.  If $\frac{1}{n^{d}}\E(R^{2d}) \to 1$ and $\frac{1}{n^{2d}}\Var(R^{2d}) \to 0$, then we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 24 (Tree-graph inequality) of arXiv:2510.23423, 'One-arm exponents of the high-dimensional Ising model'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a subgraph of $\mathbb Z^d$ and $\beta\geq 0$. Then, for every $x,y,z\in V$,
\begin{equation}
	\phi_{G,\beta}^0[x\connect{}y,z]\leq \sum_{u,u'\in V: \: u\sim u'}\phi_{G,\beta}^0[x\connect{}u']\phi_{G,\beta}^0[u'\connect{} z]\phi^0_{G,\beta}[u\connect{}y].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tree-graph inequality

body: [Thm 23 of arXiv:2604.24189, 'Malliavin calculus and densities for chaos-driven stochastic differential equations'] Let $Z^{H,q}=(Z^{H,q,1},\ldots,Z^{H,q,m})$ be the $m$-dimensional Hermite process of order $q\geq 1$ and self-similarity parameter $H\in \left(\frac{1}{2},1\right)$ defined in \eqref{eqn:defofmultihermitekernel}. Then $Z^{H,q}$ satisfies hypothesis $\mathbf{(H_5)}$.
title: Thm 23 of arXiv:2604.24189

[Lemma lem:OY-dressing of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Suppose the gauged kernels $K_a$ are trace class on $H$
and the resolvents $(I+K_a)^{-1}$ exist on the Darboux
stencil.  Then $K_a$ is dressing compatible with
$(\Psi_a, \Phi_a)$ in the sense of
Definition~(def:dc-clean-dressing of the paper):
\begin{align}
\partial_rK_a&=\Psi_a\Phi_a,
\\
\partial_\tau K_a
&=
\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl((\partial_r\Psi_a)\Phi_a
-\Psi_a(\partial_r\Phi_a)\bigr),
\\
K_{S_Ia}-K_a&=\Psi_a\Phi_{S_Ia}.

\end{align}

		In particular, if $\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0$, then
		\[

body: [Definition 2.4 of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let G be a generator family of proper convex sets. The dual Radon number r⊤ G is the least integer m such that every m-element family F ⊆G has a nontrivial partition F = F1 ˙∪F2 satisfying conv \ F1 ∪ \ F2  ̸= X. If (X, C) is finite and G = B is its basis, then r⊤ B is exactly the Radon number of the dual convexity space.

Method: Integrator-authored exact special-case argument and failure analysis after checking the incoming source Result: If H2 is spanned by a unit vector u and H1 has finite rank, monotone-couple A with law P_H1 inside C with law P_H. Their deterministic sizes differ by one, so C minus A is a singleton B. At any coordinate e, P(B={e})=P(e in C)-P(e in A)=(P_H)ee-(P_H1)ee=|u(e)|^2. Thus B has precisely P_H2 and (A,B) gives the required coupling in this special case. For higher rank, the same subtraction determines only one-point intensities of C minus A; its higher inclusion probabilities are not fixed. The finite problem can be written as nonnegative weights w(A,B) on disjoint pairs with the three required marginals, but setting up this transportation problem does not prove it feasible. Check: The rank-one masses sum to ||u||^2=1 and each difference indicator equals 1_(e in C)-1_(e in A). A random pair of same-size subsets can have matching one-point intensities yet different two-point probabilities, showing why the rank-one calculation does not generalize by intensity matching alone. Obstruction: No general coupling construction. Earlier floating-point LP claims are retained only in the frozen incoming record, not counted as exact certificates.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0462-disjoint-coupling-of-orthogonal-projection-processes

body:
[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2606.14038, 'Trivariate Hypergeometric Series Formulas\\ for Pure Partition Functions of Multiple $3$-S'] Both  $\sum_{\u n\in\N_0^2} A^0_{\u n} \u r^{\u n}$ and $\sum_{\u n\in\N_0^2} B^0_{\u n} \u r^{\u n}$ converge locally uniformly in $ (-1,1)^2$. Let $F_0$ and $G_0$ denote the limit functions, respectively. Then they are analytic and symmetric and satisfy equation (\ref{rainbow1'''}) for any distinct $j,k\in [2]$ and
\BGE \beta r_1\pa_1 F_0+\beta r_2\pa_2 F_0+\beta^2 F_0=-(1-r_1r_2) G_0. \EDE
Moreover, $F_0>0$ on $(-1,1)^2$ and is given by the   Horn $G_2$ function (\cite{Horn}) with parameters $(\beta,\beta;1-2\beta,1-2\beta)$:
\BGE F_0(r_1,r_2)= G_2^{\mathrm{Horn}}(\beta ,\beta ;1-2\beta ,1-2\beta;-r_1,-r_2).\EDE
In addition, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item [(i)] Suppose $\beta>1/3$. Then for any $n_1\in\N_0$, $A^{\Sigma}_{n_1}:=\sum_{n_2=0}^\infty A^0_{(n_1,n_2)}$ converges absolutely, and
\BGE A^{\Sigma}_{n_1} =\frac{\Gamma(2\beta)\Gamma(3\beta-1)}{\Gamma(\beta)\Gamma(4\beta-1)}\cdot \frac{(\beta)_{n_1}(1-\beta)_{n_1}}{(1)_{n_1}(2\beta)_{n_1}}.\EDE
Moreover, for any $L\in (0,1)$,
\BGE \sum_{n_1=0}^\infty \sum_{n_2=0}^\infty |A^0_{(n_1,n_2)}| L^{n_2}=\sum_{n_1=0}^\infty \sum_{n_2=0}^\infty |A^0_{(n_1,n_2)}| L^{n_1}<\infty.\EDE
In this case, $F_0 $ is continuous and positive on $[0,1]^2\sem\{(1,1)\}$ with
\BGE  F_0(x,1)=F_0(1,x)=
\frac{\Gamma(2\beta)\Gamma(3\beta-1)}{\Gamma(\beta)\Gamma(4\beta-1)} \cdot f_\beta (x),\quad x\in [0,1).\EDE
\item [(ii)]  If $\beta>1/2$, then $F_0$ extends continuously to a positive function on  $[0,1]^2$ with
\BGE F_0(1,1) = \frac{\Gamma(2\beta)^2\Gamma(2\beta-1)}{\Gamma(\beta)^2 \Gamma(4\beta-1)}.\EDE

\end{enumerate}

body: [Lemma lem:regularity of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] When $d\ge 2$, for any $h\in C^{0,1}$ let $f_h$ denote the solution to the multivariate Stein equation $\Delta f_h(x) - x^{\top}\nabla f_h(x)=h(x)-\mathbb{E}[h(Z)]$ for any $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, where $Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)$. Then $f_h\in C^{2,\delta}$ and $[\nabla^2 f_h]_{\operatorname{Lip},\delta} \lesssim \frac{1}{1-\delta}$ for any $\delta\in(0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.20169, 'THEORY OF UNCERTAIN PROBABILITY:\\ CAN WE DERIVE THE PROBABILITY DENSITY FUNCTION OF UNCER'] If $\left(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U}\right)$ is an arbitrary measurable space, a function $\mathbb{X}$: $\Pi\rightarrow\mathcal{U}$ is a measurable map from $\left(\Pi, \mathbb{F}\right)$ to $\left(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U}\right)$ if 

$\mathbb{X}^{-1}(U)\equiv\left\{\boldsymbol{\pi}:\mathbb{X}(\boldsymbol{\pi})\in U\right\}\in\mathbb{F}$ for all $U\in\mathfrak{U}$.

If $(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U})=(\mathcal{R},\mathfrak{R})$, $\mathbb{X}$ is called an uncertain random variable.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.20169

[Lemma lem:HS-curvature-full of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] On a Riemann surface the Hitchin--Simpson curvature is of type $(1,1)$ and is
\begin{equation}
 R_{D_h}
 = R_h
  +[\theta,\theta_h^{*}].
\end{equation}
In particular,
\(
 \mathrm{tr}_E[\theta,\theta_h^{*}]=0
\), so
\(
 \mathrm{tr}_E R_{D_h}=\mathrm{tr}_E R_h
\).

body: [Theorem thm:infinite-counterexamples of arXiv:2609.03184, 'On uniquely colorable Cayley graphs'] For every prime $p \ge 5$, the graph $G_p = \mathrm{ICG}_{12p}(\{2, p\})$ is a uniquely $3$-colorable circulant graph with clique number $\omega(G_p) = 2$. Consequently, there exists an infinite family of uniquely colorable circulant graphs where $\chi(G) \neq \omega(G)$, providing a negative answer to Problem 3.6 in [Klotz-2017].
title: Theorem thm:infinite-counterexamples of arXiv:2609.03184

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2606.15432, 'A Concavity Theorem for the Parisi PDE'] Let \(h_1,h_2\in \Hoelder{\alpha/2}([0,1])\).
Then, for all $(s,x)\in [0,1]\times \R$,
\begin{equation*}

D^2\Psi^\gamma[h_1,h_2](s,x)
=
-
\int_s^1
\iint_{[s,\sigma]^2}
h_1(\rho_1)h_2(\rho_2)
A^{\gamma,s,\sigma,x}(\rho_1\wedge\rho_2)
\dd\rho_1\dd\rho_2\dd{\sigma},
\end{equation*}
where
\begin{equation}
    
    A^{\gamma,s,\sigma,x}(\rho)
    =
    \frac12
    P_{s,\rho}^\gamma[L_\rho^\gamma w_{\rho,\sigma}^\gamma](x)
    +
    \frac{1}{4}
    \int_s^\rho
    P_{s,\tau}^\gamma
    \Bigl[
        \gamma(\tau)\tau 
        \partial_x P_{\tau,\rho}^\gamma[v^\gamma(\rho,\,\cdot\,)]
        \partial_x w_{\tau,\sigma}^\gamma
    \Bigr](x)
    \dd{\tau}
\end{equation}
with $\rho\in [s,\sigma]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2606.15432

body: In mathematical measure theory, for every positive integer n the ham sandwich theorem states that given n measurable "objects" in n-dimensional Euclidean space, it is possible to divide each one of them in half (with respect to their measure, e.g. volume) with a single (n − 1)-dimensional hyperplane. This is possible even if the objects overlap.
title: Ham sandwich theorem

[Lemma lem:zxk-ineq of arXiv:2607.14993, 'Sharp phase transition for percolation with short-range dependencies'] Let $x \in \mathbb Z^d, 1 \leqslant k \leqslant N$ and $n \in \mathbb N^*$ as well as $\beta \in \mathbb R_+^*$. Let $l_0 \in \llbracket 1, M \rrbracket$ such that for all $s, t \in \llbracket 1, N \rrbracket$ we have $(\zeta(s, t) \geqslant 1) \wedge (s \geqslant k) \implies \zeta(s, t) \geqslant l_0$. Then
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb P(Z_{x, k} \text{ pivotal for } A_n) \leqslant \frac {(2d-1)(1-p_{l_0})} {\mathbb P(Z_{x, k} = 1) (1 - h_M)^{2d}} \sum\limits_{y \in \mathcal N(x)} \mathbb P(Y_{\{x, y\}, l_0} \text{ pivotal for } A_n) .
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:zxk-ineq of arXiv:2607.14993

For standard-zero-moment ordinary bias-corrected diagonal two-coordinate Adam with b=.9,d=.999,outside-sqrt epsilon and fixed positive eta,epsilon, suppose theta_h=eta*lambda_h/epsilon>38 and0<theta_l=eta*lambda_l/epsilon<=38. Active convergence to38 forces the low coordinate to its origin and the high coordinate to its origin or exact two-cycle, deriving both denominator limits. A persistent positive asymptotic top gap is equivalent to gradient norm tending to zero and squared high-gradient fraction tending to(38-theta_l)/(theta_h-theta_l). On the ENTIRE strict mixed range theta_h>38>theta_l>0, origin-rate separation makes this compensation impossible: active convergence to38 forces the high cycle and scaled top limit38. At theta_l=38, the top gap criterion remains vanishing gradient norm with high-gradient fraction tending to zero; the top limit is then theta_h. The gradient condition implies active convergence to38 and a positive top gap unconditionally under the stated assumptions; the reverse implication and orbit classification are conditional on012v2.
