[Lemma 9 (Series reduction) of arXiv:2609.02080, 'Logarithmic basis number of graphs'] Let $v$ be a degree-two vertex incident with two distinct non-loop edges $uv$ and $vw$, where possibly $u=w$.  Let $G'$ be obtained by suppressing $v$ and replacing those two edges by one edge $uw$ (a loop if $u=w$).  Then
\[
    \bn(G')=\bn(G)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \beta(G')=\beta(G).
\]

\sup_{\delta_0\leq |t|\leq T}\sup_j\|\mathcal L_{j,it}^L\|_*<1.

$$
\sup_{\delta_0\leq |t|\leq T}\|\mathcal L_{0,it}^n\|_*\leq Ce^{-cn}.
$$

[Theorem thm:fin-add-price-chain of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be a gamble space.
  For all measurable $X:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    
    \sup_{Q\in\Delta_{0,f}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_Q X
    \leq
    \sup_{Q\in\Delta_f(\Omega)} \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_Q[ X - Z]
    \leq
    \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \sup_{Q\in\Delta_f(\Omega)} \mathbb{E}_Q[ X - Z]
    =
    \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X~.
  \end{equation}
  If $X$ is additionally bounded, the first inequality is an equality when  $\mathcal{Z}$ is upward-scalable and contains zero, and the second when $\mathrm{dcl}(\mathcal{Z})$ is convex.

body:
[Proposition prop:HOMFLY width 1 of arXiv:2608.29986, 'Khovanov-Rozansky homology over $\F[U,V]$'] Let $K \subset S^3$ be a knot and $\widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ its reduced Khovanov-Rozansky homology. If the Rasmussen's $\mathfrak{sl}_1$ spectral sequence from $\widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathbb{F}} $ collapses after the first differential $d_1$, then $\mathit{CH}(K)$ splits as a direct sum of
\begin{itemize}[label=$-$]
    \item $C(1, -1, \dots, 1, -1)$ or $C(-1, 1, \dots, -1, 1)$, and
    \item some $1 \times 1$ squares.
\end{itemize}
One of the sides of each $1 \times 1$ square is decorated with a $-1$ and all other arrows are decorated with a $1$.

[Lemma l:local_smoothing_iteration_pressure of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $Q=Q_{\varrho}(t_0,x_0)$ be a parabolic cylinder of side $\varrho\in (0,1]$ and center $(t_0,x_0)\in {\mathbb R}\times {\mathbb R}^d$. 
Suppose that (equation eq:smoothness_coefficients_localized_SMR of the paper) holds. Fix $r\in (1,\infty)$ and $\eta\in (0,1)$.
Let $q_0\in [2,\infty)$ and $q_1\in (q_0,\infty)$ be such that $q_1-q_0\leq 1/d$. Then, for all local solutions $(v,\pi,(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n)$ to the stochastic Stokes system (equation eq:turbulent_Stokes_xi_linear of the paper) in $Q$ satisfying 
\begin{align}

F &\in L^r(\Omega;L^{2}(I;L^{q_1}(B))),\\

(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n&\in L^r(\Omega;L^{2}(I;H^{1,q_1}(B;\ell^2))),\\

\pi &\in L^r(\Omega;L^{2}(I;L^{q_0}(B))),
\end{align}
it holds that
$$
\pi \in L^r(\Omega;L^{2}(I;L^{q_1}(\eta B)))
$$
with a corresponding estimate depending only on the norms of $F$, $\pi$ and $(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n$ appearing in (equation eq:local_smoothing_iteration_pressure1 of the paper)-(equation eq:local_smoothing_iteration_pressure3 of the paper).

[Lemma calc of arXiv:2412.08334, 'Maker-Breaker on Galton-Watson trees'] Let $(S_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ be a left-continuous random walk with positive drift and $\pi_{-1}>0$, started in $S_0=0$. 
	Then the following hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item $\pi_{-1}+\theta+\sigma=1$
		\item $\sigma=\pi_{-1}\cdot \frac{1-\rho}{\rho}$ and $\theta=1-\frac{\pi_{-1}}{\rho}$

		\item $\theta_\mathrm{odd}=\frac{\pi_{-1}\,(1-\rho_\mathrm{odd})}{\rho\theta\,(2\rho_\mathrm{odd}-1)}$
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 13 (Fractional Sobolev--Morrey estimate) of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Let $T>0$, $1<p<\infty$, and
		\[
		0<r<1,
		\qquad
		r p>1.
		\]
		Let $f\in L^p(0,T)$ satisfy
		\[
		[f]_{W^{r,p}(0,T)}^p
		\triangleq
		\int_0^T\int_0^T
		\frac{
			|f(t)-f(t')|^p
		}{
			|t-t'|^{1+r p}
		}
		\,\mathrm dt'\,\mathrm dt
		<\infty.
		\]
		Then $f$ admits a representative, still denoted by $f$, belonging to
		\[
		C^{0,r-\frac1p}([0,T]).
		\]
		Moreover,
		\begin{equation*} 
			|f(t)-f(t')|^p
			\le
			C_{r,p}
			|t-t'|^{r p-1}
			[f]_{W^{r,p}(0,T)}^p,
			\qquad
			t,t'\in[0,T].
		\end{equation*}

body:
[Lemma lem:covering_number_in_jin of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] Let $\mathcal V$ denote a class of functions of the form
\[
V(\cdot)=\min\Bigl\{\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\bigl[w^\top\phi(\cdot,a)+\beta\sqrt{\phi(\cdot,a)^\top\Lambda^{-1}\phi(\cdot,a)}\bigr],H\Bigr\},
\]
where the parameters satisfy $\|w\|_2\le L$, $\beta\in[0,B]$, and $\lambda_{\min}(\Lambda)\ge \lambda$.
Assume $\|\phi(x,a)\|_2\le 1$ for all $(x,a)$.
Let $\mathcal N_\epsilon$ be the $\epsilon$-covering number of $\mathcal V$ under
$\mathrm{dist}(V,V')=\sup_x|V(x)-V'(x)|$.
Then
\[
\log \mathcal N_\epsilon
\le d\log\Bigl(1+\frac{4L}{\epsilon}\Bigr)
+d^2\log\Bigl(1+\frac{8\sqrt d\,B^2}{\lambda\epsilon^2}\Bigr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covering-number bound for optimistic value functions, Lemma D.6 in \cite{jin2020provably}

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Consider the situation of Lemma \ref{allinvariantmeasures0}. The following are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $G=\mathbf{P}_1$ is Hurwitz (so that $S$ is negative definite), and $\mu$ is an infinitesimally invariant measure for $\big (L^{A,\mathbf{P}}, C_0^{\infty}(\R^2)\big )$. 
\item[(b)] $\mu$ is a finite invariant measure for the semigroup associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,\mathbf{P}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ and its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}. 
\end{itemize}
Moreover, in either case (a) or (b), the following hold: 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
$\mu$ is the (up to a multiplicative constant) the unique finite invariant measure for the semigroup mentioned in (b), and the unique finite infinitesimally invariant measure for  $(L^{A,\mathbf{P}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2))$.
\item[(ii)]
If $\alpha_{2,0}\not =-\frac{\beta_{2,1}}{2}$ or $\beta_{2,2} \not=-\frac{\alpha_{2,1}}{2}$, then there is no SOHHD for $\tilde{\mathbf{P}}$.
\item[(iii)]
If $\alpha_{2,0}=-\frac{\beta_{2,1}}{2}$ and $\beta_{2,2} =-\frac{\alpha_{2,1}}{2}$ then
\eqref{OHHD2dim} is the unique OHHD for $\tilde{\mathbf{P}}$.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem thm:2sloseinmodified-stronger of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] Consider the modified variant of the two-stage bootstrap percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^2$.
    When $p$ and $q$ are both sufficiently small, for some constant $c > 0$, the following holds with probability at least $1 - cq^{41}$.
    In the final configuration of the dynamics, the origin is either not in state $2$, or is contained in a maximal connected set of state-$2$ vertices that has $\ell^\infty$-diameter at most $750$.

[Theorem 7 (van den Berg) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that $D$ is simply connected and that $\partial D$ is Minkowski nondegenerate with
Minkowski dimension $\msf d_M(\partial D)\in[1,2)$. That is,
\[0<\liminf_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}\leq
\limsup_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}<\infty,\]
where we define
\[\partial D_r=\left\{x\in\mbb R^2:\inf_{y\in\partial D}|x-y|<r\right\}.\]
There exists constants $c\in(1,\infty)$ and $\th>0$ such that
\begin{align}

c^{-1}t^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2}\leq\msf{A}(D)-\msf M_0(t)\leq ct^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2},\qquad t\in(0,\th).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For an odd prime p and integer a, the Legendre symbol (a/p) is 0 if p | a, +1 if a is a nonzero quadratic residue mod p (some x^2 = a), and -1 if a is a quadratic nonresidue. Euler's criterion gives (a/p) = a^{(p-1)/2} mod p; the symbol is completely multiplicative in a. It is the object of the law of quadratic reciprocity and generalizes to the Jacobi symbol for composite lower arguments.

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

[Theorem of arXiv:2411.17104, 'Two-barriers-reflected BSDE with Rank-based Data'] Under assumptions $\textbf{(A1)}-\textbf{(A3)}$, the game ((5.1 of the paper)) with $\xi := g(\widetilde{X}(T))$, $L(t):=L(t,\widetilde{X}(t))$ and $U(t):=U(t,\widetilde{X}(t))$ has the value $V(t)$, given by backward component $Y$ of the solution to (equation 5.1.1 of the paper) for all $0\leq t\leq T$, i.e.,
\[
V(t):=\underline{V}(t)=\overline{V}(t)=Y(t),\; a.s..
\]
Futhermore,  there exists a saddle-point $(\hat\lambda_{t},\hat\tau_{t})\in \mathcal{M}_{t,T} \times \mathcal{M}_{t,T}$,
\[
\hat\lambda_{t}:=\min\Big\{T,\inf\Big\{a\in[t,T)|Y(a)=U(a)\Big\}\Big\}, \]
\[
\hat\tau_{t}:=\min\Big\{T,\inf\Big\{a\in[t,T)|Y(a)=L(a)\Big\}\Big\},
\]
that is,
\[
\mathbb E\left[R_{t}(\hat\lambda_{t},\tau ) \mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right]\leq\mathbb E\left[R_{t}(\hat\lambda_{t},\hat\tau_{t} ) \mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right]=Y(t)\leq\mathbb E\left[ R_{t}(\lambda,\hat\tau_{t})\mid \mathcal{F}_{t}\right],\; a.s.,
\]
for point $(\lambda,\tau)$ in $\mathcal{M}_{t,T} \times \mathcal{M}_{t,T}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

   F_{N,\Des(\pi)},

 \Phi_N(h_{\boldsymbol m})

\end{equation}
Moreover, for every permutation \(\sigma\) of \([n]\),
$\Hom_{\boldsymbol m}(x,y)
 =\G_{m_{\sigma(n)}}\cdots
  \G_{m_{\sigma(1)}}(x)$.

Let $I:=\{i\in\{1,2,3\}:W_i<\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\}$ and define  $\textup{QT}(W_1, W_2, W_3)$ to be the law of the quantum surface $S$ constructed as follows. 
	    {Sample $(S_0, (S_i)_I)$ from $\textup{QT}(\tilde{W}_1, \tilde{W}_2, \tilde{W}_3) \times \prod_{i\in I} (1-\frac{2W_i}{\gamma^2})\mathcal{M}_2^{\textup{disk}}(W_i)$ where $\tilde{W}_i = \max (W_i, \gamma^2 - W_i)$. Let $(D, \phi, a_1, a_2, a_3)$ be an embedding of $S_0$. For each $i \in I$, identify the first marked point of $S_i$ with the vertex $a_i$ of $S_0$, and forget this marked point. Let $S$ be the resulting three-pointed quantum surface. }
title: Thin quantum triangles

body: [Theorem 2.6 (Maximum–entropy characterisation) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$, latent positions $U=(U_{i})_{i=1}^{n}\in(0,1)^{n}$, and a finite index set $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathbb{N}_{0}\times\mathbb{N}_{0}$. Let $\Omega:=\{0,1\}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ and identify $A\in\Omega$ with an undirected adjacency matrix by setting $A_{ji}:=A_{ij}$ and $A_{ii}:=0$. Using the statistics $S_{00}(A)$ and $S_{rs}(A,U)$ defined in Section 2.4, fix target moments $m_{00}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $(m_{rs})_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}$ and define $\mathcal{Q}(m):=\Bigl\{Q\text{ pmf on }\Omega:\;\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00},\;\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}\ \ \forall(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}\Bigr\}.$ Assume $\mathcal{Q}(m)\neq\varnothing$. (i) Existence and uniqueness. There exists a unique maximiser $Q^{\star}\in\mathcal{Q}(m)$ of Shannon entropy $H(Q):=-\sum_{A\in\Omega}Q(A)\log Q(A),$ where $\log$ is the natural logarithm and $0\log 0:=0$. (ii) Exponential-family characterisation (attainable moments). For $\theta=(c,(s_{rs})_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}})$ define $P_{\theta}(A\mid U):=\exp\Bigl\{c\,S_{00}(A)+\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)-\Psi_{n}(\theta;U)\Bigr\},$ with $\Psi_{n}(\theta;U):=\log\sum_{A\in\Omega}\exp\Bigl\{c\,S_{00}(A)+\sum_{(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)\Bigr\}.$ If there exists $\theta^{\star}$ such that $P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid U)\in\mathcal{Q}(m)$ (equivalently, $\mathbb{E}_{\theta^{\star}}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00}$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\theta^{\star}}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}$ for all $(r,s)\in\mathcal{I}$), then $Q^{\star}=P_{\theta^{\star}}(\cdot\mid U).$ In particular, if one restricts $\theta$ to the WL–ERG subfamily (e.g. by imposing symmetry constraints inherited from a symmetric coefficient matrix), then any moment-matching WL–ERG member must coincide with $Q^{\star}$ and hence is the unique maximum–entropy distribution under the constraints. The maximising distribution is always unique; the canonical parameter $\theta^{\star}$ is unique whenever the exponential family is minimal.

body: Question 5 of Hu and Sun's survey on Hunt's hypothesis (H) (arXiv:1908.06825) asks whether every pure-jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfies (H). The classical sufficient conditions bound Im psi by a multiple of 1 + Re psi; the oldest, Kanda-Forst, asks |Im psi(z)| <= M (1 + Re psi(z)) for all z. The driftless subordinator with Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}, x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}, has sum a_m x_m = 1 and sum a_m = infinity, and along z_m = 1/(m x_m) its exponent psi(z) = int (1 - e^{izx}) nu(dx) satisfies |Im psi(z_m)| / (1 + Re psi(z_m)) = 4m + O(1) (computed at high precision: 23.999 at m = 6, 32.000008 at m = 8), so the Kanda-Forst ratio is unbounded and the classical route to (H) is closed for it. It is not a counterexample to (H): an octave-by-octave estimate of the Kesten-Bretagnolle integral int Re(1/(1 + psi(z))) dz suggests the integral diverges, so points would be polar - a heuristic, not a proof. The example is atomic, outside the survey's type-(alpha, beta) density class, and the survey's Theorem 2.8 and Remark 2.21 anticipate processes of this kind, so it is an explicit witness with a computed rate rather than a new phenomenon.

[Definition Interval extension of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For the remainder of this section, an \textit{interval} is a closed interval with rational endpoints. An \textit{interval enclosure} of a variable $x$ is an interval $[x] := [\underline{x},\overline{x}] \ni x$. Its width is \(\operatorname{wd}([x])=\overline{x}-\underline{x}\). 
    For a real function $F(x_1,\dots,x_m)$, a function $[F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m])$ is said to be an \textit{interval extension} of $F$ if
    \[
        x_j\in[x_j]\quad (1\le j\le m)
        \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
        F(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in [F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m]).
    \]
    Interval extensions also naturally define operations on intervals. For example,
    \[
    I+J=[\underline I+\underline J,\overline I+\overline J],
    \qquad
    I/c=[\underline I/c,\overline I/c]\quad(c>0).
    \]
    We henceforth implicitly assume all interval operations are performed with ``outward'' rounding (lower endpoints rounded downward and upper endpoints upward) to maintain rationality of the endpoints.
title: Interval extension

[Theorem 5 (Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] For every \(C_0\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C=C(C_0)\) with the following property. Let
\[
A_i=B_i+L_i,
\qquad
i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
be self-adjoint matrices. Assume that \(B_i\in\mathcal A\) for a finite-dimensional \(C^*\)-algebra \(\mathcal A\) satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A\le C_0n$, and assume $\|B_i\|\le 1$, $\|L_i\|\le 1$, and $\|L_i\|_F^2\le \frac{n}{\log^3(en)}$ for every \(i\in[n]\). Then, there exist signs \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{\pm1\}\) such that
\[
\Bigl\|
\nlsum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i
\Bigr\|
\le
C(C_0)\sqrt n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families

[Lemma 57 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $\Ncal(m,C)$, $\Ncal(m_0, C_0)$ be two equivalent Gaussian measures on $\Hcal$. Then
	$\range(C^{1/2}) = \range(C_0^{1/2})$.

		&= \range(C_0^{1/2}).

[Lemma 39 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] For every \(a>1\), \(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{WH}}_a(0)=0\),
\(\left(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{WH}}_a\right)'(0)=0\), and
\begin{equation}

\left(\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{WH}}_a\right)''(0)
=
\frac{a-1}{2\pi^2(a+1)}\log a.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, as \(\theta\to0\) in every smaller strip \(S_{\theta_*}\),
\(0<\theta_*<\pi\),
\[
\mathcal{C}^{\operatorname{WH}}_a(\theta)
=
\frac{a-1}{4\pi^2(a+1)}(\log a)\theta^2
+
O(|\theta|^3).
\]

body:
[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $L\subset M_{n,m}(\R)$ and $K\subset \R^n$ be compact sets of positive volume whose convex hulls contain the (appropriate) origin in their interiors. Then, 
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n]((K^{\star,Q})_{\circ,Q})^m 
    \] 
    and 
    \[ 
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((L_{\circ,Q})^{\star,Q})\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m,
    \]
    with equality only for invariant sets (up to sets of Lebesgue measure zero). 
    
    In particular, the following two statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $K$ or $K^\circ$, has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m 
    \]
    with equality if and only if $K=E$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets; 
    \item  if $L_{\circ,Q}$ or $(L_{\circ,Q})^\circ$ has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m
    \]
    with equality if and only if $L=E^{\star,Q}$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset \R^n$ up to removal of null sets.
    \end{enumerate}

	Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a constant \(\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon} > 0\) such that for all \(\mu \in \mathcal{A}\)
	and \(\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{B}\), 
	\[
		d_{\text{BL},1}(\mu,\bar{\mu})\leq 2\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon} d_{\text{BL},\square}(\mu,\bar{\mu}) + \varepsilon.
	\]

[Lemma strong-approximations of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Assume the conditions of Lemma~(lemma:LIL of the paper) hold. If $ \mathbb{E}[x(1)^{\alpha}] < \infty $ for some $ \alpha > 2 $, then there exist two standard Brownian motions $ \check{B}' $ and $ \check{B}'' $ such that
	\[
	\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{1/\alpha}} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big\vert \sum_{i = 1}^{\lfloor t \rfloor} x(i) - t - c_{x} \check{B}'(t)\Big\vert \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{1/\alpha}} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \vert N(t) - t - c_{x} \check{B}''(t) \vert \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{=} 0.
	\]
	If $ \mathbb{E}[\exp(t x(1))] < \infty $ in a neighborhood of $ t = 0 $, then there exists a positive number $ C_{x} $ such that
	\begin{align*}
		\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log T} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \Big\vert \sum_{i = 1}^{\lfloor t \rfloor} x(i) - t - c_{x} \check{B}'(t)\Big\vert & \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{<} C_{x},\\
		\limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log T} \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \vert N(t) - t - c_{x} \check{B}''(t) \vert & \overset{\mathrm{a.s.}}{<} C_{x}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma strong-approximations of arXiv:2505.04942

[Theorem thm:existenceweaksolutions of arXiv:2608.16946, 'A diffusion model for time-dependent compositional data'] The SDEs (equation canonicalSDE of the paper), (equation adjustedSDE of the paper), and (equation truncatedSDE of the paper) have weak
solutions. Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}
\renewcommand{\alph{enumi}}{\alph{enumi}}

\item Given a probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with support contained in $\mathcal{S}$, there exist weak
solutions for SDEs  (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper) such that $X(0)$ has the 
prescribed distribution, and $X(t)\in\bar\mathcal{S}$ for all $t\geq0$, $P$-a.s.
\item Given a probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$ with support contained in $\mathcal{S}^-$, there exists a weak
solution for SDE (equation truncatedSDE of the paper) such that $X^-(0)$ has the 
prescribed distribution, and $X^-(t)\in\bar\mathcal{S}^-$ for all $t\geq0$, $P$-a.s.
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, these solutions are unique in distribution, and they are equivalent, in the sense that:
\begin{enumerate}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\renewcommand{\alph{enumi}}{\alph{enumi}}

\item Any weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) is a solution for (equation adjustedSDE of the paper) and viceversa.
\item If $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X(t)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ is a weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper),
then $((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\allowbreak\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X^-(t))$ is a weak solution for (equation truncatedSDE of the paper).
\item If $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},W(t),X^-(t)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ is a weak solution for (equation truncatedSDE of the paper),
then $((\Omega,\mathcal{F},P),\{\mathcal{F}_t\},\allowbreak W(t),X^+(t))$ is a weak solution for (equation canonicalSDE of the paper) and (equation adjustedSDE of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:existenceweaksolutions of arXiv:2608.16946

[Corollary of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{cor:anchored_isop_dim}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J: V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel with $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d\alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (1,2)$.
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$. 
    
    Then the infinite cluster $K_{\infty}$ has anchored isoperimetric dimension at least $1/(\alpha-1)$ almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let $p \in (1, \infty)$ and $N \in \N$. Let $0 \leq \xi_N(x) \leq 1$ be a sequence of finitely supported functions on $\Z$, such that 
$$\xi_N (x)  \rightarrow 1, \quad x \in \Z, \quad \operatorname{and} \quad \sup_{N \in \N} \mathcal{M}_{p, \sigma, \alpha}(\xi_N) < \infty.$$ 
Then there exists a finitely supported sequence $0 \leq e_N (x) \leq 1$, converging pointwise to $1$, such that 
$$
\mathcal{M}_{p, \sigma, \alpha} (e_N) \rightarrow 0 \quad \text{as} \quad N \rightarrow \infty.
$$

body: In probability theory and mathematical physics, a random matrix is a matrix-valued random variable—that is, a matrix in which some or all of its entries are sampled randomly from a probability distribution. Random matrix theory (RMT) is the study of properties of random matrices, often as they become large. RMT provides techniques like mean-field theory, diagrammatic methods, the cavity method, or the replica method to compute quantities like traces, spectral densities, or scalar products between eigenvectors. Many physical phenomena, such as the spectrum of nuclei of heavy atoms, the thermal conductivity of a lattice, or the emergence of quantum chaos, can be modeled mathematically as problems concerning large, random matrices.
title: Random matrix

[Theorem 5.4 (Chen, Theorems 2.3.2 and 2.4.1; Matsuda, Theorem 3.7) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186']

Let $x\in\mbb R^2$ and $t>0$ be fixed,
and suppose that $Z$ is either $B^x$ or $B^{x,x}_t$.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item Let $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$.
There exists a random variable $\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)$ such that
\[\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)
\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
there exists a random variable $\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)$ such that
\[\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\Big(\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)-\mbf E\Big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)\Big]\Big)
\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 57 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Suppose that we are given a family of $M-1$ ASEPs $(\eta^{(i)}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for $i\in \lbr M-1\rbr$ on the same graph $G=(V,E)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \eta^{(M-1)}_0 \succeq  \eta^{(M-2)}_0 \succeq \dots \succeq \eta^{(2)}_0 \succeq \eta^{(1)}_0 
\end{equation} according to the basic coupling $\mathbf{P}$. Then we define the \textbf{colored ASEP} $(\zeta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for all $t \geq 0$ by
\begin{equation}
\zeta_t(i) := 1+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1} \big(1-\eta^{(j)}_t(i)\big)  
\end{equation}  for all $t \geq 0$ and $i \in  V$. We refer to the particles of colors $1,2,\dots,M-1$ as \textbf{first class particles}, \textbf{second class particles}, and so on, as well as to type $M$ particles as \textbf{empty sites}.

body:
[Thm 3 of arXiv:2511.18861, 'Correlation Decay for Maximum Weight Matchings on Sparse Graphs'] Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree at most $3$. Suppose that the edge weights are i.i.d.\ exponential random variables with mean $1$. Let $e\in E(G)$. Then  for any $r\geq 1$ and for any $\varepsilon  \in (0, 1)$,
    \[
   \varrho_r(G, e)   \leq 6 \big((1-\varepsilon)^{r} + \varepsilon \big).
    \]
    In particular, setting $\varepsilon = \log{r}/r$, we obtain that 
    \[
    \varrho_r(G, e)  \leq  \frac{18\log{r}}{r} \quad \text{for all $r\geq 2$.}
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 38 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $G_i$ be a sequence of Lie groups and  $\phi _i : G_i \to G$ a sequence of good approximations. Assume $G$ is a Lie group and the sequence $G_i$ has the NSS property. Then $\mathfrak{g}$, the  Lie algebra of $G$, admits an ideal $\mathfrak{h} \trianglelefteq \mathfrak{g}$ with $\mathfrak{g}/ \mathfrak{h}$ nilpotent and 
    \begin{equation}
         \text{dim} (\mathfrak{h}) = \limsup_{i \to \infty} \text{dim} (G_i) .  
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Egorov's theorem states that on a FINITE measure space, almost everywhere convergence of measurable functions implies almost uniform convergence: for every eps > 0 there is a measurable E with mu(E) < eps such that the convergence is uniform on the complement of E. Finiteness cannot be dropped. On R with Lebesgue measure let f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}; then f_n -> 0 at every point, but for ANY set E of finite measure the complement meets [n, n+1] for infinitely many n, so sup over the complement of E of |f_n| equals 1 for infinitely many n and the convergence is not uniform off any set of small measure. What survives on a sigma-finite space is the LOCAL statement: for every measurable A with mu(A) < infinity and every eps > 0 there is E contained in A with mu(E) < eps and uniform convergence on A minus E; equivalently, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence on each set of finite measure. The converse implication holds in general: almost uniform convergence always implies convergence almost everywhere and in measure, on any measure space. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.33 and Exercise 2.39]
mu(Omega) < infinity for the global statement; a set of finite measure for the local statement
f_n measurable, f_n -> f mu-almost everywhere, all functions finite a.e.

body: Classical Schwarz lemma: if f maps the open unit disk holomorphically into itself and f(0)=0, then |f(z)|<=|z| and |f'(0)|<=1. Equality at a nonzero point or in the derivative bound forces f(z)=az with |a|=1. A distinct higher-dimensional result is Royden's Theorem1 (1980): let M be complete Kaehler with Ricci curvature at least k<=0, and N be Kaehler with holomorphic sectional curvature at most K<0. For a nonconstant holomorphic f:M->N, let nu be the maximal complex rank of df. In the paper's curvature convention, ||df||_op^2 <= Lambda(f) <= (2nu/(nu+1)) k/K, where Lambda(f)=trace_g(f*h) is the sum of squared singular values. Constant maps satisfy zero derivative directly. Trace energy and squared operator norm are distinct when rank exceeds one. This note does not assert the same conclusion for arbitrary Hermitian targets or remove the rank factor from the trace bound.
title: Schwarz lemma and Royden bound with hypotheses

[Lem compound of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] Let $(\Gamma_0, \omega_0)$ be a weighted planar network with associated weight matrix $M_0$ such that the weight matrix  $M^\prime_0$ of  $(\Gamma_0, 
 \lvert \omega_0\rvert )$ strictly dominates, i.e. $$\beta M^\prime_0 \geq  \lvert M_0 \rvert$$ for some $0<\beta <1$. 
 Then if $(\Gamma, \omega)$ is a concatenation of planar networks including $m$ copies of   $(\Gamma_0, \omega_0)$, its weight matrix $M$ and the weight matrix $M^\prime$ of  $(\Gamma, \lvert \omega\rvert)$ satisfy the strict domination $$\beta^m M^\prime \geq \lvert M \rvert.$$

body:
[Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}=\{R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $1$, with drift $-\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$, for each $i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$.
We consider the O'Connell-Yor polymer partition function (see [OYbb]) across $\{\mathcal{B}_i\}_{i=1}^{2k}$, defined as
\[
Z_{\mathcal{B}}(x,i;y,j) = \idotsint_{x=x_i\le \cdots \le x_j \le x_{j+1}=y} \exp\left( \sum_{i'=i}^j \mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'+1})-\mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'}) \right) dx_{i+1}\cdots dx_j,
\]
for any $1\le i \le j \le 2k$, and $0\le x \le y$.

Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j\in\llbracketi, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of inverse gamma random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal{B}$, satisfying 
\[X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
1 & j =i,\\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_j-\gamma_i), \qquad &j\in\llbracket i + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i- \gamma_{2k + 1 -j}), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i+\alpha), \qquad &j =  2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
\[
R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in P[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; x, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in P[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x\ge 0,\\
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; |x|, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x< 0,
\end{cases}
\]
where $P[i,\ell]$ is the collection of all up-right paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(-i,i)$ to $(-1,\ell)$, and  
$\hat{P}[i,\ell]$ is the subset of such paths that intersect $\{(x,x+2k+1): x\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020

[Theorem 35 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Assume that Conditions ($\sH_\sigma^g$) and ($\sH_b$) hold. Let  $\gamma_n(f):=\sup_{r\in D_n}\|f\|_{\mL_\infty^q([r,r+1/n])}$. Let $X^n$ be the solution to  Eq. (\ref{EulerAPP3.81}) and let  $f\in \mL_{p}^q([0,1])$ and $h\in \mH_{1,p}^q([0,1])\cap \mL^{\infty}([0,1])$ for some $q\in [2,\infty)$ and $p\in(2(d/\beta\vee 1),\infty]$ satisfying $\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}<1$. Then for any $\bar{p}\in(0,p)$, there exists a constant $N=N(d,p,q,\bar{p})$ such that 
		\be 
		&&\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\int_{0}^{t}h(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})(f(\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr|\|_{L_{\bar{p}(\Omega)}}\no\\
		&\leq &N\bigg\{\|h\|_{\mL^{\infty}([0,1])}\gamma_n(f)(1/n)^{1-\frac{1}{q}}+[(1/n)^{\alpha/2}+(1/n)^{ 1-\beta/2}+(1/n)^{1/2}\log(n)]T(f,h)\bigg\},
		\ee
		where $$T(f,h)=(\|h\|_{\mL^{\infty}([0,1])}+\|h\|_{\mH_{1,p}^{q}([0,1])})\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}.$$
		Particularly 
		\be 
		&&\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\int_{0}^{t}(f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})-f(r,\widetilde{X}_{r_n}^{n}))dr|\|_{L_{\bar{p}(\Omega)}}\no\\
		&\leq &N\bigg\{\gamma_n(f)(1/n)^{1-\frac{1}{q}}+[(1/n)^{\alpha/2}+(1/n)^{ 1-\beta/2}+(1/n)^{1/2}\log(n)]\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}\bigg\}.
		\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 35 of arXiv:2607.18862

[Theorem 106 of arXiv:2507.07702, 'Observables of random spanning trees in random environment'] Let $pn = \log n + \lambda(n)$ for $\lambda(n) \rightarrow \infty$. Then for $n$ large enough

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2608.31145, 'Gauge-compatible tensors on statistical manifolds: splitting and submanifold geometry'] Let $M$ be a $\Theta$-CR submanifold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Assume
\[
\ker(F_{\Theta}|_{TM})=D_{\Theta}.
\]
Then $D_{\Theta}$ is $\nabla^{*}$-autoparallel if and only if
\begin{equation}
h(X,\Theta Y)
=
f_{\Theta}(h^{*}(X,Y))
\end{equation}
for all $X,Y\in\Gamma(D_{\Theta})$.

\item Assume
\[
\ker(P_{\Theta}|_{TM})=D_{\Theta}^{\perp}.
\]
Then $D_{\Theta}^{\perp}$ is $\nabla^{*}$-autoparallel if and only if
\begin{equation}
A_{\Theta V}U
+
t_{\Theta}(h^{*}(U,V))
=
0
\end{equation}
for all $U,V\in\Gamma(D_{\Theta}^{\perp})$.
\end{enumerate}

[Prop point to point contraction  wrp to sup norm of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $\lambda>0$ and let $\Delta\in \mathbb{N}$.
    Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a family of graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ that is closed under taking induced subgraphs and that satisfies VSSM with rate $\alpha\in [0,1)$ and constant $C'>0$ for the hard-core model at fugacity $\lambda$. 
    Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the family of self avoiding walk trees of graphs in $\mathcal{G}$.
    Let $K\subset B_{\lambda/2}(\lambda/2)$ be a compact set containing a neighbourhood of $[\ell_{\Delta}(\lambda),r_{\Delta}(\lambda)]$.
    Then there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $(T,v)\in \mathcal{T}$, $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $u\in S^*_T(v,n)$, and any vector $(r_{u'})\in [\ell_\Delta(\lambda),\lambda]^{S^*_T(v,n)\setminus \{u\}}$ we have
    \[
    \norm{F'_{T,n;u}}_{K}\leq C|\epsilon_u(T,n)|.
    \]

[Lemma of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] Let $\xi, \eta\in \partial X$ and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}, (\xi_n')_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and $(\eta_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}, (\eta_n')_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be sequences converging to $\xi$ and $\eta$ respectively. Then for $w,z \in X$
\[\limsup_{n,m \to \infty}(\xi_n,\eta_m)_w \leq \limsup_{n,m \to \infty}(\xi'_n,\eta'_m)_w +2\delta,\]
\[\limsup_{n,m \to \infty}(\xi_n,z)_w \leq \limsup_{n,m \to \infty}(\xi'_n,z)_w +\delta.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'

[Lemma compare_towers_final of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'] Let $s\geq r\geq 1$ be integers and let $a_1, \dots a_r$ and $ b_1,\dots, b_s>0$ be (strictly) positive real numbers.
	Let 
\begin{align}
	h_a(u)&=f(a_1f(a_2\dots f(a_r u)\dots))\\ h_b(u)&=f(b_1f(b_2\dots f(b_s u)\dots)).
\end{align}	
	Then if $r<s$, we have $h_a(u)\lll h_b(u)$. 
	The same is true if $r=s$ and if the largest $i\in [r]$ such $a_i\neq b_i$ is such that $a_i<b_i$ and $i>1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma compare_towers_final of arXiv:2603.28936

\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\hookrightarrow B_{p,2}^{k+1}(\Omega),
 \qquad 0<p<1.
\]
For every $0<q<2$,
\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\not\hookrightarrow B_{p,q}^{k+1}(\Omega),
\]
and for every $s>k+1$ and $0<q\leq\infty$,
\[
 \mathcal L_1(\D)\not\hookrightarrow B_{p,q}^s(\Omega).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.00680

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/1a/1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7c673ab1f544f0e3955fcd92879e554a7907834c68728a34330c1cedd7cbda10","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","bundle_id":"population.t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise-017","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_017.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Critical tanh: exact tangent kernel and its shared Wishart noise

20 October 2026. C050/C051; Target 3. Proof drafts, unaudited.
These are infinitesimal-angle one-step results, not a two-input tanh
diffusion theorem or an all-order cumulant expansion. No novelty asserted.

## C050: exact positive-variance kernel

Fix n>=2 and q>0. Let g,h be independent N(0,I_n) vectors. For two inputs
with equal preactivation variance q and angle theta, the next activated
vectors are exactly distributed as

    x = tanh(sqrt(q) g),
    y(theta) = tanh(sqrt(q)(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h)).

The independent Gaussian weight rows give these conditional marginals
given the present Gram matrix. The tanh critical weight variance is 1/n;
thus the next diagonal variance is K'=||x||^2/n and the radial multiplier
is M_q=||x||^2/(nq). There is no width-dependent shaping normalizer.

Set D=diag(sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i)), P_x=I-xx^T/||x||^2. Then the right-hand
derivative H_q of the angle between x and y(theta) at theta=0 is

    H_q^2 = q h^T D P_x D h / ||x||^2.

Proof: y(0)=x and y'(0)=sqrt(q)Dh. The derivative of y/||y|| is
sqrt(q)P_x Dh/||x||, whose norm is the nonnegative angular speed.
Almost surely x is nonzero and this speed is positive for n>=2.

Conditionally on g, Q_q=h^T D P_x D h is a sum of n-1 independent
chi-square_1 variables with positive weights equal to the nonzero
eigenvalues lambda_j of D P_x D. These satisfy

    d_min^2 <= lambda_j <= 1,
    d_min = min_i sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i).

Indeed these nonzero eigenvalues equal those of P_x D^2 P_x restricted
to x-perp, whose Rayleigh quotients lie in that interval. Both M_q and
the conditional weights depend on the same g. In particular the exact
positive-q model must retain this conditioning; replacing Q_q by an
independent chi-square is a different kernel. Even the radial sum
||x||^2/q is bounded above by n/q, unlike a chi-square variable.

For fixed n, q decreases to zero gives jointly, almost surely under the
original (g,h) coupling,

    M_q -> S/n,      H_q -> sqrt(R/S),
    S=||g||^2 ~ chi-square_n,
    R=h^T P_g h ~ chi-square_(n-1),  R independent of g and hence of S.

The independence follows because the conditional law of R given g is
the same chi-square_(n-1) law for every nonzero g. The SAME S appears in
the radial multiplier and angular denominator. For n=1 the tangent
speed is zero, so logarithmic angular statements below exclude n=1.

## C051: uniform leading noise at the critical variance scale

For every fixed C<infinity, uniformly over 0<q<=C/n, define

    A_q=log M_q,       B_q=log H_q.

As n increases,

    n Cov((A_q,B_q)) -> [[2,-1],[-1,1]].

Here Cov is centered covariance. Equivalently, replacing B_q by the
logarithmic reciprocal-angle multiplier -B_q changes both off-diagonal
entries to +1. This only identifies one-step noise, not a drift limit.

### Coupling and quantitative error

Draw g and, independently, eta_1,...,eta_(n-1) iid standard normals.
Use a measurable ordering of the eigenvalues above and put

    Q_q^* = sum_j lambda_j(g) eta_j^2,
    R^* = sum_j eta_j^2,       S=||g||^2.

The pair (M_q, sqrt(q Q_q^*/||x||^2)) has EXACTLY the required joint
law (M_q,H_q), by the conditional quadratic-form law. Also S and R^*
are independent chi-squares with the stated degrees of freedom.
Thus this construction verifies both coupled marginals. No pointwise
comparison with the original h projection is being asserted.

For z>=0, sech^2(z) <= tanh(z)/z <= 1, with the continuous value at zero.
Consequently, with Z=max_i |g_i|,

    d_min^2 <= ||x||^2/(qS) <= 1,
    d_min^2 <= Q_q^*/R^* <= 1.

Since log(cosh z)<=z^2/2, this yields the deterministic coupling bounds

    |A_q-log(S/n)| <= 2q Z^2,
    |B_q-(1/2)log(R^*/S)| <= q Z^2.

A Gaussian union bound P(Z^2>r)<=min(1,2n exp(-r/2)), integrated as
E Z^4=integral_0^infinity 2r P(Z^2>r)dr, gives
||Z^2||_2 <= C_0 log(2n). Hence each logarithmic error has L2 norm at
most C_1 q log(2n), without deleting any event or inverse tail.

### Covariance calculation

Let A_0=log(S/n), B_0=(log R^*-log S)/2. Gamma integration gives

    Var A_0 = psi_1(n/2),
    Cov(A_0,B_0) = -(1/2)psi_1(n/2),
    Var B_0 = (psi_1((n-1)/2)+psi_1(n/2))/4.

The trigamma series psi_1(z)=sum_(k>=0)(z+k)^(-2) and integral comparison
give psi_1(z)=1/z+O(z^-2). These identities can alternatively be obtained
by differentiating E S^t=2^t Gamma(n/2+t)/Gamma(n/2) at t=0.
The displayed baseline covariance therefore has the claimed limit
after multiplying by n, and its centered L2 norms are O(n^-1/2).

For centered random variables, covariance perturbation by L2 errors e
has size at most C(n^-1/2 ||e||_2 + ||e||_2^2); centering an error costs
no more than its L2 norm. After multiplying by n, our bound is

    O(sqrt(n) q log(2n) + n q^2 log(2n)^2)
       = O_C(log(2n)/sqrt(n) + log(2n)^2/n),

uniformly over 0<q<=C/n. This tends to zero and proves C051.

## Scope left open

The limits are: first the angle derivative at zero for fixed n,q,
then n -> infinity with q<=C/n. C051 does not justify exchanging the
infinitesimal-angle limit with a finite-angle network evolution, does
not give the order-1/n drift, and does not establish that actual tanh
input correlations approach one. The scalar critical-tanh diffusion
and cumulant-rate work remain separate claims C026-C027 and C044-C047.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:22c6d532d863fd81ef53240a00570657817f6c17e8e5fb0515c76a33cfbda523","revision_digest":"sha256:fc88eab43dde02de84f288e293b9f37cf1114c075d6075db6c02f0a27cabfd4e","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C051:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T13:53:12.705197","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: [Theorem 3.11 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,k,N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ be partial permutations, let $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, let $Y$ be the matrix resulting from the partial trace evaluation $(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{k}})(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})$, and let $q=\sum_{j=1}^{k}(m-|D(\sigma_{j})|)$ with $D(\sigma_{j})$ the domain of $\sigma_{j}$, so that $Y$ acts on a space of dimension $N^{q}$. For every $p\in\mathbb{N}$, $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\mathrm{Tr}((YY^{*})^{p})\leq N^{2pC(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}.$ (3.2) Moreover, for any configuration $\bm{\pi}_{0}$ with $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};\bm{\pi}_{0})=M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$, it holds that $Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*}=N^{2M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}I_{N^{q}},\qquad\mathrm{Tr}((Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*})^{p})=N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\quad(p\in\mathbb{N}).$ Thus, the tuple $(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})=(E_{\pi_{1}},\ldots,E_{\pi_{m}})$, which is independent of $p$, attains every lower moment bound $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}$. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:concave_profile_contract}
Let \(P_t\) have curvature at least \(\kappa\).
If an increasing concave function \(\psi:[0,D]\to[0,\infty)\) controls the increments of \(H\), then
\[
\|P_tH(x)-P_tH(y)\|_{\op}\le \psi((1-\kappa)d(x,y))
\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in\Omega.
\]

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] The localisation $p^l\colon \cal{C} \to \cal{B}^l$ admits a left calculus of fractions, that is, for $x,y \in \cal{C}$ the map
\[ \colim_{[y \mono y'] \in y\rtimes \cal{A}}\Map_{\cal{C}}(x,y') \to \Map_{\cal{B}^l}(p(x),p(y)) \]
is an equivalence, where $y\rtimes \cal{A} \subseteq \cal{C}_{y/}$ is the full subcategory spanned by the inclusions $y \mono y'$ with cofibre in $\cal{A}$. 
In particular, if $f\colon x \to y$ is a map in $\cal{B}^l$ then for every $\tilde x\in \cal{C}$ lifting $x$ we can lift $f$ to a map $\tilde f\colon \tilde x \to \tilde y$ with domain $\tilde x$. Dually, the localisation $p^r\colon \cal{C} \to \cal{B}^r$ admits a right calculus of fractions and every map in $\cal{B}^r$ admits a lift in $\cal{C}$ given any prescribed lift of its codomain.

[Lemma lem:complete-collision of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] In a fresh Kac frame put $\mathsf P_i=a_ia_i^*$ and
$W_i=\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W$.  Before any ancillary boundary routing, the intact
coordinate-plane average obeys, for arbitrary real
$|\epsilon_i|\le1$,
\[
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i\epsilon_iW_i\right\|_\mathrm{op}\le\frac2N.
\tag{3.2.10f}
\]
The exact scalar identities are
\[
 W_i^2=\left(1-\frac2N\right)W_i+\frac{N-1}{N^2}I,
 \qquad [A_i,\mathsf P_i]=0.
\tag{3.2.10g}
\]
If a passive map separates equal labels, then
\[
 \mathsf P_iT\mathsf P_i=\langle a_i,Ta_i\rangle \mathsf P_i;
\tag{3.2.10h}
\]
this expression remains in the intact collision block and is not replaced
by a scalar unless $T$ itself is scalar.  Relative to the Jacobi
coefficients $1,\gamma$, the only naked finite-$N$ residuals in (eq:3.2.10g of the paper)
are $-2N^{-1}W_i$ and $-\gamma N^{-1}I$.  The first child remains
time-indexed.  The second is formed only after the $m-1$ collision labels
have been summed; before residual temporal components are defined it is
removed from the temporal word, with $\gamma$ retained in the
monomer--dimer ledger and the remaining $N^{-1}$ kept as a favorable
scalar coefficient carrying no time, gap, anchor, or translation.

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \((M^{n},g)\), \(n\geq4\), be a closed, connected, oriented,
locally conformally flat manifold with scalar curvature
\(\mathrm{Sc}_{g}\geq n(n-1)\). Identify
\(\Gamma:=\pi_1(M)\) with its holonomy Kleinian group, and suppose that
\(\Gamma\) is elementary. If there exists a smooth distance-nonincreasing (i.e.,
\(1\)-Lipschitz) map
\(
f\colon(M^n,g)\to (S^{n},g_{st})
\)
of nonzero degree, then \(f\) is a Riemannian isometry.

body:
[Corollary cor: double well of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Under the same conditions as the previous theorem,
let $d=1$, and consider the choice of confinement potential of the form
\begin{equation}

 V(x)
 =
 \frac{x^4}{4} - \lambda\frac{x^2}{2}
 ,\qquad
 x,y,\lambda\in\R,
\end{equation}
or more generally suppose  that $V$ is in the GHS class, i.e.~satisfies Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper) below.
Then for any $T>T_c$ (defined in (equation eq_def_beta_c of the paper)), 
the measure $m^N_T$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with a constant independent of $N$.  
Moreover, the log-Sobolev constant vanishes  linearly at $T_c$: 
\begin{equation} 	
\limsup_{N\to\infty} \gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	
\leq 
c_1 (T-T_c)
,\qquad
\gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	\geq 
c_2 (T-T_c)
,\quad 
N\geq 1,
\end{equation}
for some  constants $c_1, c_2>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Double well confinement potentials

$$|S_\pi(N)|\leq N^{t(G^\pi)}\prod_{i=1}^m ||D_i||.$$

body:
[Corollary 15 (Weighted stable representation) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $0<p\le q$, and let $V_{p,q}$ be the unique factor of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Then, for every bounded measurable $h:\R\to\R$,
\[
\E h(X_p)=\E h(V_{p,q}X_q).
\]
If $p<q$, put $a=1/p$, $b=1/q$, let $S_{p/q}$ be independent of $X_q$, and set
\[
W_0=S_{p/q}^{-b}.
\]
Then
\[
\E W_0=\frac{\Gamma(a)}{(p/q)\Gamma(b)}=\frac{a\Gamma(a)}{b\Gamma(b)}<\infty,
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\E h(X_p)=\frac{\E\left[W_0 h\left(2^{a-b}W_0X_q\right)\right]}{\E W_0}.

\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\varkappa:=\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}.
\]
Then, for every mapping $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ with $f_j\in \mathcal{P}_d(\gamma)$, satisfying
\[
\int_E \Delta_f\,d\gamma \ge a
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(f_j)\le b,
\]
and for every $\alpha\in(0,\varkappa)$, one has
\[
\sigma_f(t)
\le
C_1kd(\varkappa-\alpha)^{-\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}}
\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)^\alpha
\quad \forall t>0,
\]
where $C_1>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, optimizing over $\alpha$, we obtain
\[
\sigma_f(t)
\le
C_2kd
\bigl(1+\bigl|\ln\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)\bigr|\bigr)^{\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}}
\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)^\varkappa
\quad \forall t>0,
\]
for some absolute constant $C_2>0$.

[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.03361, 'Grassmann--Pl\"ucker Parametrization of Convolutional Filter Subspaces:\ Regularity and Cl'] Let $\cK=\CC^k$, let $H=\Hom(E,F)$, and let
$\cC:\cK\to H$ be the linear map induced by the finite-stride convolution in
Definition~\ref{def:convolution}. For every $1\leq q\leq k$, the parametrization
\[
  \Phi=\Pl_H\circ\Gamma_{\cC}:
  \Gr(q,\cK)\longrightarrow\PP(\wedge^qH)
\]
is a closed embedding. If $X=\Gr(q,\cK)$ and $Y=\Phi(X)$, then
$\Phi:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ is an isomorphism. In particular, $\Phi$ is finite
and birational onto its image, $\#\Phi^{-1}(y)=1$ for every $y\in Y$, and
\[
  \dim Y=q(k-q),\qquad \Sing(Y)=\varnothing.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main theorem

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two. Verification as the source words it: both bounds are uniform over the whole admissible range of R (measured max F(0) = 0.099010, min F(a) = 0.129901), so this is a proof and not a numerical observation; and a control both ways - on the three cases where the authors' Theorem 4.4 applies (alpha = 1, beta = 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3) the same root counter returns at most 2 roots at t = 1.01 D and t = 10 D, agreeing with their proved theorem. Prior art not cleared. nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2, supported on [1/10, 10] sigma_t the free positive multiplicative Brownian motion t >= 5 pi

\right\rangle^{\bullet,\,\mathcal C'/(Q'\cup\{p\})}_{d}

=

specialized to \(\mathcal C'\) and \(\mathcal C_0\), respectively, and the sign \((-1)^{\epsilon(N',N_0)}\) is fixed in terms of the parity of insertions so that we formally have \[\prod_{i\in N}\gamma_i=(-1)^{\epsilon(N',N_0)}\prod_{i\in N'}\gamma_i\prod_{i\in N_0}\gamma_i,\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    \[
        \mathbb{E}^x\left[f(X_t);t\leq \sigma \right]=\int_E p^-_\sigma(t,x,y)f(y)\mu(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall t>0,x\in E, f\in \mathrm{b}\mathscr{B}(E).

In particular, 
\[

\]
provides a decomposition of transition density function into the contributions before and after $\sigma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] Let $g_0$ be a stretching morphism from some capacity $\lambda$ on an interval $I$ to the constant capacity 1, and fix $x_0\in\overline I$. This means that for $z_0:=g_0(x_0)\in\overline\R$, $g_0$ is a $\mathcal C ^1$-diffeomorphism from $I$ to $\R$ of the form $g_0 : x\in I \mapsto z_0+\int_{x_0}^x {\dd r} / \lambda(r) \in \R $ (understood as a limit when $z_0=\pm\infty$). Let $(D_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ be a continuous process with strictly increasing quadratic variation, taking values in $\overline \R = \R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ (defined up to time-change) and verifying the following two conditions.

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(i) Well-posedness of the flow.}
For every $x\in I$, the integral equation
$$g_t(x)=g_0(x)+\int_0^t\1_{(z_0,g_s(x))}(D_s)\dd[D]_s$$
admits a unique solution until time $T(x):=\inf\{t\geq 0, g_t(x)=\pm\infty\}$, and the map
$(t,x)\mapsto g_t(x)$
is continuous on its domain $\{(t,x), x\in I, 0\le t < T(x)\}$. 

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(ii) Jointly continuous local times along the flow.}
For $x\in I$, assume that the family of processes $(R_t^x)_{0\leq t <T(x)} :=(D_t-g_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(x)} $ admits jointly continuous local
times: namely, assume that there exists a nonnegative field
$(L_t^x(a))_{x\in I,a\in\R,\, 0\leq t<T(x)}$, jointly continuous (at least in a neighborhood of $a=0$)
in $(t,x,a)$, such that for every $x\in I$, every $0\leq t<T(x)$,
and every bounded Borel function $f$,
$$\int_0^t f(R_s^x)\dd[R^x]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(a)L_t^x(a)\dd a.
$$

\ms

Write   
$L_t(x):=L_t^x(0).$ For $0\leq t \leq T$, let $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$, and finally let us define for such a process $D$ its final time $T(D) := \inf\{s\leq T,\, \mathring I_s=\emptyset\}\wedge T $.
Then the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $0 \leq t < T(D)$, the map $x\mapsto g_t(x)$ is an increasing $C^1$-diffeomorphism from the open interval $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$ to $\R$, with
$$\partial_x g_t(x)=({\exp(L_t(x))}) / {\lambda(x)}.$$

\item  The process $X$ defined for $0\leq t< T(D)$ by
$X_t:=g_t^{-1}(D_t)\in \overline I_t$
is continuous and admits a bicontinuous local time $(\Lambda_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(D),\,x\in I}$, where
$\Lambda_t(x)=\lambda(x)\left(1-\exp\bigl(-L_t(x)\bigr)\right)$, i.e.\ for every bounded Borel function $f$, 
$$\int_0^t f(X_s)\dd[X]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Lambda_t(x)\dd x.
$$
\end{enumerate}

$t<\zeta$ if and only if $\delta$ is constant. In this case $\delta\equiv\Delta\neq0$ and $dP_t=\Delta P_t(1-P_t)\,d\overline W_t$,  $t<\zeta$.

[Lemma 30 (Lyapunov drift for the forward and adjoint chains) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:U} and~\ref{ass:whole-space-growth}.  Write
$\calL_\eps^{(+)}=\calL_\eps$ and
$\calL_\eps^{(-)}=\calL_\eps^*$.  Equivalently,
\[
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)} f
    =
    \sigma p\cdot\nabla_\theta f
    +\left(-\sigma L^{-1}\nabla U(\theta)+\sigma\gamma r\right)
        \cdot\nabla_p f
    +(-\sigma\gamma p-\gamma r)\cdot\nabla_r f
    +\frac{\gamma\eps}{L}\Delta_r f,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\]
There exist constants $\kappa,\alpha,\eta,C_V,c,C>0$, with
$\eta=\kappa\alpha$, such that the functions
\[
    V_\sigma(\theta,p,r)
    =
    C_V+H(\theta,p,r)+\eta H(\theta,p,r)^2
    +\alpha K_\sigma(\theta,p,r),
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\},
\]
where
\[
    K_\sigma
    =
    \sigma\theta\cdot p+\theta\cdot r
    +\frac{2\sigma}{\gamma}p\cdot r
    +\frac{\gamma}{2}|\theta|^2,
\]
are nonnegative, have compact sublevel sets, and satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)}V_\sigma
    \le
    -c\left(U(\theta)+|p|^2+|r|^2+H(\theta,p,r)|r|^2\right)+C,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every
\[
    R\ge \frac{C+1}{c},
\]
the compact set $\mathsf K_R$ defined in
\eqref{eq:whole-space-lyapunov-set} satisfies
$\calL_\eps^{(\sigma)}V_\sigma\le -1$ on
$\mathsf K_R^c$ for both signs $\sigma$.

body:
[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The fixed-domain perturbation formulas used later are collected here.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}, so that the principal eigenvalue is simple in the positive cone. Let $h\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $h\ge0$ and $h\not\equiv0$. Then $\Lp(\cA_\R+h)<\Lp(\cA_\R)$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $b\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $b\ge0$ and $b\not\equiv0$, and assume that the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore} hold for every operator $\cA_\R+rb$ under consideration. Then $r\longmapsto\Lp(\cA_\R+rb)$
is strictly decreasing and locally Lipschitz. If there exist $r_-<r_+$ such that the two values have opposite signs, there is a unique $r_*$ with $\Lp(\cA_\R+r_*b)=0$.

\textup{(iii)} Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be fixed. Let
\[
\cA_\tau u=d\int_\Omega\big(J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)\big)u(y)\,dy+\big(q(x)+\tau r(x)\big)u'(x)+\big(b(x)+\tau h(x)\big)u(x),
\]
where $q,r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$, $b,h\in C(\overline \Omega)$ and $H\in C(\overline \Omega^2)$.  We restrict $\tau$ to a real interval on which the drift is bounded away from zero and the kernels $J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)$ are nonnegative and satisfy a common positivity condition in a neighborhood of the diagonal. Let $\lambda(\tau)=\Lp(\cA_\tau)$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized principal eigenfunction are real analytic in $\tau$ on that interval. If $\phi,\phi^*>0$ are the direct and adjoint principal eigenfunctions at $\tau=0$, normalized by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*\,dx=1$,
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda'(0)={}&-d\int_\Omega\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)H(x,y)\phi(y)\,dy\,dx\\
&-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx
-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for a potential perturbation alone,
\[
\lambda'(0)=-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]

\textup{(iv)} On a fixed bounded interval let
\[
\cA_{d,c}u=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+c\,r(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
where $d>0$, $c$ ranges in an interval on which $cr(x)$ has a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and $r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Normalize the direct and adjoint eigenfunctions by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized eigenfunction are real analytic in $(d,c)$ on every connected parameter region on which $d>0$ and $cr$ keeps a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and
\[
\partial_d\Lp=-\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)\phi(y)\,dy-\phi(x)\right)dx,
\]
\[
\partial_c\Lp=-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]
No sign is asserted for these derivatives in general.

\textup{(v)} For the scaled operator
\[
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}u=\frac1{\sigma^m}\left(\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+q(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
put $\rho=\sigma/L$ and $v(\xi)=u(L\xi)$. Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\Lp\left(L^{-m}\rho^{-m}(\mathcal J_\rho-I)+L^{-1}q(L\cdot)\partial_\xi+a(L\cdot),(-1,1)\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal J_\rho v(\xi)=\int_{-1}^{1}J_\rho(\xi-\eta)v(\eta)\,d\eta.
\]

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] The Klein geometry $\operatorname{Euc}(n)/O(n)$ is first-order and reductive. More precisely, under the identification \eqref{eq:euc-quotient-on},
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Ad}}(A)(v)=Av,
\qquad A\in O(n),\quad v\in\mathbb{R}^{n},
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak{euc}(n)=\mathfrak{o}(n)\oplus\mathfrak{t},
\qquad
\mathfrak{t}:=
\left\{
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0\\
v&0
\end{pmatrix}: v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
\right\},
\]
with $\mathrm{Ad}(O(n))(\mathfrak{t})\subset\mathfrak{t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Main2 3 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Let $p\ge2$ and let $S_w(0)\subseteq\mathbb Z_p^m$ be a set of vectors of Hamming weight $w$. There exists an embedding
$f:S_w(0)\hookrightarrow S^{(p-1)m-1}\subset\mathbb R^{(p-1)m}$
such that if $b\le m$ is an integer satisfying
$\frac{w}{m}<J_p\!\left(\frac{b}{m}\right)$
and $\mathcal C$ is any subset of $S_w(0)$ that satisfies $d(x,y)\ge b$ for all distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C$, then

\begin{enumerate}
\item For all distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C$, $\langle f(x),f(y)\rangle<0$, where $\langle \,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denotes the Euclidean inner product; and
\item $|\mathcal C|\le\min\left\{(p-1)m+1,\gamma(p,b,w,m)\right\}$,
where \begin{equation}
\gamma(p,b,w,m)
:=
\floor{\frac{b}{\,b-mJ_p^{-1}(\frac{w}{m})\,}}.
\end{equation}.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth exponents in the spatial city-formation model structural calculation Result: A rigorous one-sided bound supports the balanced exponent when0<alpha<1 and beta>2alpha. Write d=beta/2-alpha>0. A union bound over influence disks gives area{I(y,t)>u}<=pi*c0^(2/beta)*u^(-2/beta)*M_t^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta), using concavity of the population power. Thus the conditional founding probability is at least1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*M_t^d)], K=(2pi)^(beta/2)*c0. Put theta=(1-alpha)/(1+d) and m=floor(kappa*t^theta). Until M reaches m, each of the last floor(t/2) arrivals has founding chance at least p=1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*m^d)]. Choose kappa small so this Bernoulli count has mean at least2m. A stopped coupling and Chernoff then give P(M_t<m)<=exp(-c*m) for large t. Check: The disk estimate is valid even at the square boundary because clipping only reduces area. Sum_i N_i^(2alpha/beta)<=M^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta). On the event M_t<m the threshold has never been reached, so domination by independent Bernoulli(p) increments throughout the half-interval is legitimate. The exponent identity theta*(1+d)=1-alpha makes the mean comparable to m. Obstruction: This proves a lower city-count growth bound in the balanced regime, not the matching upper bound, comparable populations, unbalanced regime, or alpha1 logarithmic law. The upper bound requires control of spatial clustering and influence overlap that the union bound does not supply.

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.04143, 'The Geometry of Real Anisotropic Bohnenblust--Hille Constants'] Let $\mathbf q$ be an $m$-linear Bohnenblust--Hille exponent. Write
\[
 q_{\min}:=\min_i q_i,\qquad q_{\max}:=\max_i q_i,
\]
let $d=d(\mathbf q)$, and set
\[
 \varepsilon=d+\frac{2}{m+1}.
\]
Assume $\varepsilon\le2/3$ and define
\begin{equation}
 k=\left\lfloor\frac{2}{\varepsilon}\right\rfloor-1.
\end{equation}
Then $2\le k\le m$, $p_k\le q_{\min}$, and
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}\le
 A_{p_k}^{-(m-k)}B_{\R,k}^{\mult}.
\end{equation}
If $\varepsilon\le1/4$, then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathbf q}^{(m)}\le
 M\left(\frac{2}{\varepsilon}\right)^\vartheta
 \exp\left(\frac{m\varepsilon}{4(1-\varepsilon)}\right).
\end{equation}

[Lem \cite{SY78}, Lemme 1 of arXiv:2412.05698, 'Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles'] Let $X$ be a function on $U \times \mathbb{R}_+
  \times \Omega$ such that:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item[a)] For all $u \in U$, the process $X^u$ is indistinguishable from a
    c{\`a}dl{\`a}g process.
    
    \item[b)] For all $t \in \mathbb{R}_+$, there exists a function $H_t$ on
    $U \times \Omega$, measurable with respect to $\mathfrak U \otimes
    {\mathfrak F}$, such that: $\forall u \in U, X^u_t (\cdot) = H_t (u,
    \cdot)$ almost surely $P$-a.s.
  \end{itemize}
  Then there exists a $\mathfrak U$-measurable function $Y$ on $U \times \mathbb{R}_+ \times
  \Omega$, indistinguishable from $X$, such that for all $u$, the trajectories
  of $Y^u$ are all c{\`a}dl{\`a}g. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 26 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] A module \(M\in {}_S\mathcal{M}^{\mathsf{DG}}\) is said to be \emph{cellular} if it satisfies the following additional conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{(S\arabic*)},ref=S\arabic*,nosep,labelsep=.5em,align=left]
\item For each $ 0 \leq q \leq n $, there is a decomposition \( M^q=\bigoplus_{\tau\in S_q} M(\tau)\), where each $M(\tau)$ is finite-dimensional over \(\Bbbk\), and, for $\tau= [v_0,\ldots,v_q],$ \( M(\tau)\subseteq M_{v_0}=M_{s(\tau)}.\) Moreover, \(M^q=0\) for \(q>n\). We write \[ \iota_\tau : M(\tau) \hookrightarrow M^q, \qquad
\pi_\tau : M^q\twoheadrightarrow M(\tau) \] for the natural inclusions and projections, respectively. 
\item For each $\tau\in S_q$, $\zeta\in S_{q+1}$, let \(D_{\tau\rightarrow\zeta} \coloneq \pi_\zeta\circ d_M\circ \iota_\tau.\) Then
\[d_M\big\lvert _{M(\tau)}=\sum_{i=0}^{q+1} \sum_{\substack{\zeta\in S_{q+1}\\ d_i\zeta=\tau }}
D_{\tau\rightarrow \zeta}.\]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 4 (Peskun--Tierney optimality of the $N$-vote rule) of arXiv:2609.00905, 'When Metropolis and Hastings Meet Bradley and Terry: Exact MCMC From Preference Voting'] Fix a proposal kernel $q$ and a comparison budget $N\geq 1$. Among all exact acceptance rules satisfying detailed balance with respect to $\pi$, that use the same proposal kernel and only the outcomes of exactly $N$ judge
queries per proposal, the $N$-vote rule Peskun--Tierney dominates every
competitor. Equivalently, for every proposed move $x\to x'$, we have 
$\mathbb P_{\text{$N$-vote}}(\textup{accept }x'\mid x,x'\textup{ proposed})
\geq
\mathbb P_{\text{competitor}}(\textup{accept }x'\mid x,x'\textup{ proposed}).
$

The proof is given in Appx. \ref{app:optimality-proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Peskun--Tierney optimality of the $N$-vote rule

        \item  $\E X_1^2 = 1$,
        \item  $\frac{1}{n^{4d}}\E\nm{\mathbf X}_2^{8d} \to 1$, and

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] If \(Z\) is uniform on the \(p\)-th roots of unity and
\(W=|\Impart Z|\), then
\[
 \E W^2=\frac12,\qquad \E W\geq\frac12,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(W)\leq\frac14.
\]
Consequently, for independent copies \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\),
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\left\{\sum_{j=1}^N W_j<N/4\right\}\leq\frac4N.
\end{equation}
All these bounds are independent of \(p\).

[Lem lA1Delta of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let $r\in[2,\infty)$. Then, for any $\gamma\in [0,1]$
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[t_k,t_{k+1})}\mathbf{E}^{(N)}_{t_1,\dots,t_N}\Big[\|\Delta_t^n\|^r\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t_k}\Big]
\leq_C \|\Delta_{t_k}^n\|^r
&+h_n^{r\gamma +1}(1+\|X_{t_k}^{(n)}\|^{r\gamma\chi+r}) +h_n^{r\gamma }(1 + \|X^n_{t_k}\|^{r\gamma\chi+r})\\
&+h_n  (U_{t_k}^n)^r
+ h_n^{r\gamma+1} (U_{t_k}^n)^{r\gamma\chi}  + h_n
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
for $n$ large enough uniformly over

[Defn Infinitesimal holonomy of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a cooriented $C^0$-foliation on $M$, and $\gamma : S^1 \rightarrow L$ be a smooth closed curve tangent to a leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$, inducing a holonomy map 
    $$h : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \rightarrow (-1,1)$$
    for some $\varepsilon > 0$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ has \textbf{infinitesimal attracting holonomy} around $\gamma$ if for every open interval $\{0\} \subset I \subset (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$, there exists a smaller open interval $\{0\} \subset J \subset I$ such that 
    $$\overline{h(J)} \subset J.$$
title: Infinitesimal holonomy

[Theorem 22 (Empirical Fourier CLT) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] There is a $\lambda_d$-conull set $E_\eta\subset\bR^d$ such that, for every
$\xi\in E_\eta$, every $m\geq1$, and every
$h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C_c^\infty(\bR^d;\bC)$,
\begin{equation}

    \bigl(Z_R(\xi;h_1),\ldots,Z_R(\xi;h_m)\bigr)
    \dto \bigl(G_\xi(h_1),\ldots,G_\xi(h_m)\bigr)
    \qquad\text{in }\bC^m,
\end{equation}
where the vector on the right is complex Gaussian with mean zero and
\begin{align}

    \E\!\left[G_\xi(h_a)\overline{G_\xi(h_b)}\right]
    &=s_\eta(\xi)
      \int_{\bR^d}h_a\overline{h_b}\,d\lambda_d,\\

    \E\!\left[G_\xi(h_a)G_\xi(h_b)\right]&=0.
\end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation}

    Z_R(\xi;h)
    \dto \mathcal{CN}\bigl(0,s_\eta(\xi)\|h\|_2^2\bigr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Empirical Fourier CLT

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \( (M^n,g) \), \(n\geq5\), be a closed, connected, oriented, locally conformally flat Riemannian manifold with positive scalar curvature and infinite fundamental group. Then \(M\) can be realized as a quotient \(\Omega/\Gamma\), as described above, with \(\Gamma\cong\pi_1(M)\). There exists an integer
$i \geq \Big\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \Big\rfloor + 1$
such that $\pi_i(M^n) \neq 0$.

If, in addition, \( H_1(M^n;\mathbb{Z}) = 0 \), then \( \Gamma \) is non-elementary.

If, moreover, \(\Gamma\) is torsion-free, then the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set satisfies
\[
1 < \dim_{\mathcal H}\Lambda(\Gamma) < \frac{n-2}{2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02267

[Theorem 4 (The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $u \in \R^n$. Let $f \in \mathcal{F}(\conbodI)$. Then, for every measurable function $g:\R^n\to\R_+$ and measurable, non-increasing function $\Omega : (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that 
    \[
    f(x)g(y) \leq \Omega^2(\langle x, y \rangle), \qquad \forall \,\,x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } \langle x,y \rangle>0,
    \] 
    it holds
    \begin{equation}
    
        \left(\int_{\R^n} f(x) \langle x,u \rangle^2 dx \right) \left(\int_{\R^n} g(y) \langle y,u \rangle^2 dy \right) \leq \left(\int_{\R^n} \Omega(|z|^2) \langle z,u \rangle^2 dz \right)^2.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality

[Definition see, e.g., \cite{wijesekera_constructive_1990, simpson_proof_1994} of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For an f-model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, we define an \emph{intrinsic satisfaction relation} $\Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M}$ on $W \times \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ by:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, (x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi     \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, \forall y' \sqsupset x'\, (y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, \exists y' \sqsupset x'\, (y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item The other cases are identical to the classical $\Vdash_\mathfrak{M}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We write $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^i \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(i-)valid in} $\mathfrak{M}$'') to mean $\forall x \in W\,(x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$,
  and $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^i \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(i-)valid on} $\mathfrak{F}$'') to mean that $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^i \varphi$ for every $\mathfrak{M}$ based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
title: see, e.g., \cite{wijesekera_constructive_1990, simpson_proof_1994}

Then there exists \(C=C(u,S,r)>0\) such that, for every \(M\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
\|g-\Pi_{\le M}g\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}
\le
\rho C r^M
+

\end{equation}
If, in addition, \(h\in\mathcal D(N^\beta)\) for some \(\beta>0\), then
\begin{equation}
\|g-\Pi_{\le M}g\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}
\le
\rho C r^M
+
(M+1)^{-\beta}
\|N^\beta h\|_{L^2(\gamma_d)}.

\end{equation}

Let γ : [α,β] → C be a closed piecewise C^1 curve and let a be a point not on the trace of γ. The winding number (index) of γ about a is n(γ,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ dz/(z - a). It is always an integer; as a function of a it is constant on each connected component of the complement of the trace of γ, and it is 0 on the unbounded component. The definition extends additively to cycles (finite formal integer combinations of closed curves) and, via continuous branches of the argument, to merely continuous closed curves. A cycle γ lying in an open set U is called null-homologous in U (homologous to zero) if n(γ,w) = 0 for every w in C minus U. An open connected U ⊂ C is simply connected if and only if every cycle in U is null-homologous in U, if and only if the complement of U in the Riemann sphere is connected. The homology form of Cauchy's theorem reads: if f is holomorphic on U and γ is a cycle null-homologous in U, then ∫_γ f(z) dz = 0 and n(γ,z) f(z) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ - z) dζ for every z in U off the trace of γ.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.26953, '2608.26953'] Let \(A\) be a \(\Bbbk\)-algebra. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item \(A\) admits a universal connected FODC \((\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A),d_{\mathrm{uni}})\) given by
\[
\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)  \coloneq  \ker(\mu)\subseteq A\otimes_\Bbbk A,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{uni}}(a)=1_A\otimes a -a\otimes 1_A, \quad \forall a\in A, \]
where \(\mu\colon A\otimes_\Bbbk A\rightarrow A\) denotes the algebra multiplication.
\item Any FODC \(\Omega^1_A\) is isomorphic to a quotient \(\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)/N\), for some sub-bimodule \(N\subseteq\Omega^1_{\mathrm{uni}}(A)\), with differential induced by \(d_{\mathrm{uni}}\).

[Proposition prop:tilted_gen_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $k\in\mathbb{R}$ and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold, in particular, 
assume additive noise $D=\sigma\sigma^\top/2$. The semigroup
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t \geq 0}$ is a strongly continuous semigroup on $L^2(\mu)$ whose
infinitesimal generator acts on $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ as
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J
  &=
  b \cdot (\nabla + kU)
  +
  (\nabla + kU) \cdot D(\nabla + kU),
  
\end{align}
or equivalently, expanding for $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ yields
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J f
  &=
  \mathcal{L}f
  +
  k\bigl(b \cdot U + \nabla \cdot DU\bigr) f + 2kU \cdot D \nabla f
  +
  k^2(U \cdot DU)f.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 24 (Joint fixed-index distributional and moment limit) of arXiv:2606.29635, 'Extremality and Limit Laws for the Siblings of the Coupon Collector'] Fix $J\ge2$ and set $a_{N,j}=(\log N)^{j-1}/(j-1)!$. In the equal-probability model,
\[
        \left(\frac{U_2^N}{a_{N,2}},\frac{U_3^N}{a_{N,3}},\ldots,\frac{U_J^N}{a_{N,J}}\right)
        \Rightarrow (W,W,\ldots,W),\qquad W\sim\Exp(1).
\]
For every fixed nonnegative integer vector $\mathbf m=(m_2,\ldots,m_J)$,
\[
        \E\prod_{j=2}^J\left(\frac{U_j^N}{a_{N,j}}\right)^{m_j}
        \to (m_2+\cdots+m_J)!.
\]
For $J=2$ this recovers the Papanicolaou--Doumas limit theorem \cite{PapanicolaouDoumas}.

[Lemma lem:recovery-nonempty of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Fix $t>0$ and set $\bar F:=\bar A^{-1}\bar\gamma$. Suppose (lem:hk_ss_finite of the paper) holds. Then there exists a sequence $(\psi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset C_b^\infty(\bar E;\mathbb{R}^n)$ such that

\begin{equation}
  \int_{\bar E}\bar u(t,x)\,
  \big(\psi_k(x)-\bar F(x)\big)^\top\bar A(x)\big(\psi_k(x)-\bar F(x)\big)\,d\bar\pi(x)
  \longrightarrow 0,
\end{equation}
and $\|\psi_k\|_{L^\infty}\le k$ for all $k$. In particular, the set of recovery sequences in (ass:locking of the paper) is nonempty.

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2506.12632, 'Point process convergence of extremes in $K$-symmetric exclusion'] Suppose that $\alpha : \Z^2 \to \R$ is symmetric, and let $\beta : \Z \to \R$. Then for $n \ge 2$, 
\[
	\sum_{\bx \in \Z^n} \sum_{\{i,j\} \subset [n]} \alpha(x_i,x_j) \prod_{k \in [n] \setminus \{i,j\}} \beta(x_k) = {n \choose 2} \bigg( \sum_{\bx \in \Z^{(2)}} \alpha(x_1,x_2) \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{x \in \Z} \beta(x) \bigg)^{n-2}. 
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 18 of arXiv:2506.12632

[Theorem thm:ZIMcompelete of arXiv:2607.29409, 'The Zombie Infection Model'] Consider the ZIM on $K_{N}$ and let $\Delta = \{1,\dots
		,M\}$ with $M<N$. Then, as $N\rightarrow \infty$, the distribution of
		${\mathcal{Z}}_{\infty}/N$ converges under $\BP^{\ZIM}_{\lambda,K_N,\Delta}$ to $0$

		$X\sim \Bernoulli{1-\frac{1}{\lambda^{M}}}$ when $\lambda>1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
