[Theorem 35 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] Suppose that \(p\ge2\), \(F\in C^2(\mathbb R)\), \(F''\) is
non-decreasing, and for all $x \in \R$,
       $ |F(x)|
        \le
        C\left(1+|x|^p\right)
       $.
Then there exists a constant \(C_F<\infty\) such that for all $x \in \R$,
$$
        |F''(x)|
        \le
        C_F\left(1+|x|^{p-2}\right),\
        |F'(x)|
        \le
        C_F\left(1+|x|^{p-1}\right).
$$

Let f: U -> R^n be C^1 on an open set U containing an equilibrium x* of y' = f(y) (f(x*) = 0), and suppose x* is hyperbolic: A = Df(x*) has no eigenvalue with zero real part. Then there are a neighborhood V of x* and a homeomorphism h: V -> h(V) in R^n with h(x*) = 0 that conjugates the nonlinear flow phi_t near x* to the linear flow exp(tA): h(phi_t(x)) = exp(tA) h(x) for x in V and every t with phi_s(x) in V for s between 0 and t, so orbits go to orbits with the direction of time kept. The discrete-time analogue holds for a diffeomorphism g with a hyperbolic fixed point x* (Dg(x*) has no eigenvalue of modulus 1): g is locally topologically conjugate near x* to Dg(x*).
f is C^1 near the equilibrium x*
x* is hyperbolic: Df(x*) has no purely imaginary eigenvalue (resp. Dg(x*) has no eigenvalue of modulus 1 in the discrete-time case)

body: Seifert-Van Kampen theorem: Let X be a topological space written as X = U union V, where U and V are open and path-connected and the intersection U intersect V is nonempty and path-connected, and choose a basepoint x_0 in U intersect V. Let i and j denote the homomorphisms pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(U, x_0) and pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(V, x_0) induced by inclusion. Then pi_1(X, x_0) is the pushout of i and j, i.e. the free product with amalgamation pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0) modulo the normal subgroup generated by all elements i(g) j(g)^{-1} with g in pi_1(U intersect V, x_0). In particular, if U intersect V is simply connected then pi_1(X, x_0) is the free product pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0). This lets one compute fundamental groups of spaces built from simpler pieces.
title: Seifert–Van Kampen theorem

body: [Lemma lem:component_jordan_domain of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $z \in \mathbf{H}$ and let $U$ be the connected component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus {\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ containing $z$. Then $\mathbf{F}(z)$ is a.s. the union of a simple curve $\eta_a$ from $0$ to $x(U)$, two simple curves $\eta_L$ and $\eta_R$ from $x(U)$ to $y(U)$ which form, respectively, the clockwise and counterclockwise boundary arcs of $\partial U$ from $x(U)$ to $y(U)$, and a simple curve $\eta_b$ from $y(U)$ to $\infty$. The curves $\eta_a, \eta_L, \eta_R$ and $\eta_b$ do not intersect except at $x(U)$ and $y(U)$, and the boundary conditions of $h$ given $\mathbf{F}(z)$ are those of the left (resp.\ right) side of a flow line of angle $\theta(U)$ on the left (resp.\ right) side of each of these curves.

\]
then $D$ is a type-A $p$-cover. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

 \Psi_{\bmtheta}(x)=k

 \bigl[\tfrac{k}{K},\tfrac{k+1}{K}

 \quad k=0,\ldots,K-1.
\end{equation}
All parameters depend only on $(K,\delta)$.

contains nonnegative channels from which the address is obtained by a fixed
affine readout.  Consequently, this readout may be omitted and merged into a
following fixed affine layer.

[Lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] Let $\mu_t$ be the distribution after running stochastic localization with the $\Id$ driving matrix for time $t$ initialized at $\mu_{H_N}$.
    Then $\mu_t$ arises as the Gibbs distribution of the Hamiltonian $H_{N,t}(\sigma)$:
    \[
        H_{N,t}(\sigma) = H_N(\sigma) + \angles*{\by_t, \sigma}\mcom
    \]
    where 
    \[
        (H_N, \by_t) \stacker{law}{=} (H_N, t\bx + \sqrt{t} \bg)\mcom
    \]
    where $\bx \sim \ScS_N$, $H_N \sim \mu_{\pl}(\cdot | \bx)$, and $\bg\sim\calN(0,\Id_N)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sam'

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $\msp \in X$ be a point, $Z_1, \dots, Z_k$ irreducible closed subsets of $X$ such that $\msp \in Z_i$ and $\dim Z_i > 0$ for any $i$, and let $g_1, \dots, g_m \in R$ be homogeneous polynomials.
Suppose that $X$ is quasismooth at $\msp$ and that $\{g_1, \dots, g_m\}$ isolates $\msp$.
We set $G_i \coloneq (g_i = 0)_X$, and we set
\[
\mu \coloneq \min \Set{ \frac{\omult_{\msp} (G_i)}{\deg g_i} | 1 \le i \le m}.
\]
Then, there exists an effective $\mbQ$-divisor $T \sim_{\mbQ} A$ such that $\omult_{\msp} (T) \ge \mu$ and $T$ does not contain any $Z_i$ in its support.
In particular, there exists an effective $\mbQ$-divisor $T' \sim_{\mbQ} d A$, where
\[
d \coloneq \max \Set{ \deg (g_i) | 1 \le i \le m},
\]
such that $\omult_{\msp} (T') \ge 1$ and $T'$ does not contain any $Z_i$ in its support.

body:
Let k be an algebraically closed field and R = k[x_1, ..., x_n]. Weak form: every proper ideal I of R has a common zero, that is, V(I) = {a in k^n : f(a) = 0 for all f in I} is nonempty; equivalently every maximal ideal of R has the form (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n). Strong form: for every ideal I, the ideal of polynomials vanishing on V(I) is the radical of I: if g in R vanishes on V(I) then g^m in I for some m >= 1. Hence V and I give an inclusion-reversing bijection between radical ideals of R and algebraic subsets of k^n.
k algebraically closed (over R, for example, x^2 + 1 has no zero and the weak form fails)

[Proposition 19 (Critical local linear BSDE) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Let \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), and \(r\) be progressively measurable on
\(\Omega\times I\), with values in \(\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb R^m\), and
\(\mathbb R\), respectively.  Assume that \(\beta\mathbin{\cdot}W\in
\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb P;I)\), and let
\[
 L_t^\beta
 :=\exp\left(
  \int_u^t\beta_s\,dW_s
  -\frac12\int_u^t\lvert\beta_s\rvert^2\,ds
 \right),\qquad
 \frac{d\mathbb Q}{d\mathbb P}\bigg|_{\mathcal F_v}=L_v^\beta .
\]
Thus \(L_u^\beta=1\).  Suppose the BMO--Girsanov constants are those of
Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-bmo-girsanov}.  Let
\(r_A>1\), set \(p_A=r_A/(r_A-1)\), and assume
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\tau\in\mathcal T_I}
 \left\|
  \mathbb E_\tau^{\mathbb Q}
  \exp\left(r_A\int_\tau^v\alpha_s^+\,ds\right)
 \right\|_\infty
 \leq K_A<\infty .
 
\end{equation}
Assume also that \(\int_u^v\lvert\alpha_s\rvert ds<\infty\) almost surely,
\(\eta\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_v)\), and
\(r\in\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)\).  Then
\eqref{eq:critical-linear-bsde} has a unique solution in
\(\mathbb S^\infty(I)\times\mathbb H^2_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb P;I)\), and
\begin{equation}
 \|R\|_{\mathbb S^\infty(I)}
 \leq K_A^{1/r_A}
 \left(
  \|\eta\|_\infty+
  \|r\|_{\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)}
 \right).
 
\end{equation}
Under \(\mathbb Q\), one admissible BMO bound is
\begin{equation}
 \|S\mathbin{\cdot}W^{\mathbb Q}\|_{
       \mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb Q;I)}^2
 \leq
 \|\eta\|_\infty^2
 +\frac{2\|R\|_\infty^2}{r_A}\log K_A
 +2\|R\|_\infty
   \|r\|_{\mathfrak R_{p_A}(\mathbb Q;I)}.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, \eqref{eq:bmo-norm-equivalence} gives a deterministic bound
for \(S\mathbin{\cdot}W\) under \(\mathbb P\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Critical local linear BSDE

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Given $V\in\cC^{7}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ a $0$-regular potential (see Definition \ref{definition:kregular}), and $f\in\cC^{0}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$. Let $Y^N$ be a multimatrix model with potential $V$ (see Definition \ref{def:randompot}). Then, almost surely, 
$$ \lim_{N\to\infty} \norm{f(Y^N)} = \norm{f\circ T^0(x)}, $$
where $x$ is a $d$-tuple of free semicircular variables, and $T^0$ is the map from Theorem \ref{mainthm}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:cone of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] For any $u_1>1$, we choose a small constant $d_0>0$ and a large constant $n_1>64\, d_0^2$ such that the following construction is possible for all $n>n_1$ and $1\le m\le n$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$]
        \item On the unit sphere, we pick $n$ unit vectors $(v_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ such that $|v_i-v_{i'}|>12\,d_0\,n^{-1/2}$ for any $1\le i<i'\le n$. Let $S_i:=\mathsf{C}(v_i,d_0/\sqrt n)$, $1\le i\le n$, be $n$ disjoint cones.
        \item On each surface $S_i\cap\partial \mathcal{B}_0$, we further pick $m$ points $v_{i,j}$ along an arc such that the following properties hold.
        Let $c_0$ and $c_1$ be two small positive constants. Consider two smaller cones
        \[
        T_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},u_1^{-n}) \quad \text{and} \quad V_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},c_0m^{-1}n^{-1/2}).
        \]
        For any $i,j$, we have $T_{i,j}\subseteq V_{i,j}\subseteq S_i$, $\mathrm{dist}(v_{i,j},\partial S_i)\ge c_1\, n^{-1/2}$, and $V_{i,j}\cap V_{i,l}=\varnothing$ if $j\neq l$. Moreover, if $1\le j<l\le m$, then $ |z/|z|-v_{i,l}|\geq c_1|j-l|/(m\sqrt n)$  for every $z\in V_{i,j}$.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition prop:two_r of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l')
\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Then, for each $1 \le s \le n$, the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} |r_{ss}|^2 \bigr]
\]
 vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\begin{align*}
&\alpha_1 ! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow (m+1)} n^{\uparrow (l+1)}} \\
& \qquad \times
\begin{cases}
 ( (n+m)(n+l) -(\alpha_s+1)(2n+m+l) +(\alpha_s+1)(\alpha_s+2) ) & \text{if $s<n$},
\\
 ( n +(m-\alpha_n)(l-\alpha_n) + \alpha_n ) & \text{if $s=n$},
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
where $\alpha_k:=\mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j}\sqcup\bm{i}')$
for all $k=1,2,\dots, n$.

[Theorem 42 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Assume that $\Gamma_{\mu}$ is strongly irreducible 
and that the image of $\Gamma_{\mu}$ in the projective linear group 
${\rm PGL}(V)$ is not contained in any compact subgroup of ${\rm PGL}(V)$. 
Assume also that $\mu$ admits a finite exponential moment \eqref{Exponential-moment}. 
Let $f$ be a compactly supported continuous function on $\bb R$. 
Then, uniformly in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,   
\begin{align*}
\upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  \bb E  \Big( f (\log \|g_n \cdots g_1 \| - n \lambda_{\mu} - w_n)  \Big) 
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  \int_{\bb R} f(u) du. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 42 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2506.09333, 'On the Dimension-Free Concentration of Simple Tensors via Matrix Deviation'] Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_N$ be i.i.d. copies of a mean-zero subgaussian isotropic random vector $Z$, and let $T\subset \R^d$ be a bounded set. Then, for any integer $p\ge 2$, we have
    $$
    \E\sup_{v\in T}\abs*{\sum_{i=1}^N \ip{Z_i}{v}^p - N \E \ip{Z}{v}^p} 
    \lesssim_{K,p} \gamma(T)^p + \sqrt{N}\gamma(T)\rad(T)^{p-1},
    $$
    where the sign $\lesssim_{K,p}$ hides factors that depend only on $K$ and $p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 6 (Aldous' criterion for tightness {\cite[Theorem~16.10) of arXiv:2604.21143, 'Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model'] {Billingsley1999}}]
		Let $T > 0$, and let $\{X^n\}$ be a sequence of c\`adl\`ag $\Rd$-valued processes on $[0,T]$.
		If the following two conditions hold, then $\{X^n\}$ is tight in $D([0,T]; \Rd)$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every $t \in [0,T]$, the family of laws of $\{X^n_t\}$ is tight in $\Rd$.
			\item For every $\eta > 0$ and every sequence of stopping times $\{\tau_n\}$ bounded by $T$,
			\[
			\lim_{\delta \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le \theta \le \delta} \P\left( |X^n_{(\tau_n + \theta) \wedge T} - X^n_{\tau_n}| \ge \eta \right) = 0\,.
			\]
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix any $\delta\in(0,1)$, and set
$
\tilde{\varepsilon}:=\frac{\delta}{20\tau},
\bar\varepsilon:=\frac{\tilde{\varepsilon}}{4.4\tau},
\varepsilon:=\frac{\bar\varepsilon}{4\tau}
$.
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\bm d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)
$
denote its degree sequence. Suppose that $v_1,\dots,v_{\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil}$ are vertices with degrees greater than $n^{2\tilde\varepsilon}$. Let $\tilde A$ denote the event that, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$, the vertex $v_a$ has at least $\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$ pairwise distinct neighbors
$
u_1^{(a)},\dots,u_{\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil}^{(a)}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{u_b^{(a)}:1\le a\le \lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil ,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct, and have degrees between $n^{\bar\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\bar\varepsilon}
$. Moreover, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$ and each $b=1,\dots, \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$, the vertex $u_b^{(a)}$ has at least $ \lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil$ distinct neighbors
$
w_{a,b,1},\dots,w_{a,b,\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{w_{a,b,m}:1\le a\le\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil,\ 1\le m\le\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct and have degrees between
$n^{\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\varepsilon}$. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\tilde A\mid \bm d)\ge 1-\exp(-n^{\bar\varepsilon(\tau-2)/2})-\exp(-n^{\varepsilon/2}), \qquad \text{on the event $D_{\varepsilon}$ defined in \eqref{eq_D}. }
\end{equation}

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that the hypotheses in Theorem \ref{Theorem: Main}
hold, and that $\msf T_0(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion in \eqref{Equation: Smooth Heat Trace}.
Let $t_1>t_2>\cdots>0$ be a vanishing sequence of positive numbers.
The following holds for any fixed $\ka>0$:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1/2-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}2\pi t_n\,\msf T_\ka(t_n)=\msf{A}(D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}4\sqrt{2\pi t_n}\left(\tfrac{\msf{A}(D)}{2\pi}t_n^{-1}-\msf T_\ka(t_n)\right)=\msf{L}(\partial D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:ub of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] In the setting of (thm:1 of the paper), fix $n\geq 1$ and $K>0$, let $\rho_n(x)$ be the maximum vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ above $x+(\frac{L}2,0)$ for $-N_n^{2/3} \leq x\leq N_n^{2/3}$,
and set $\sigma^2>0$ as per (def:sigma of the paper). 
Then every weak limit point $\mathbf{Y}_n(t)$ of the process $Y_n(t):=N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$ ($t\in[-K,K]$), as $L\to\infty$, satisfies
\[ \mathbf{Y}_n \preceq \mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,. \]
Moreover, for every fixed $m$, every weak limit point $({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ of the processes $(Y_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ satisfies
\[ ({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n)_{n\leq m} \preceq \bigotimes_{n\leq m}\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:ub of arXiv:2509.04333

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.10051, 'Ergodicity of the voter model with dynamic anti-voter bonds'] Consider a Markov chain with a countable state space~$\mathcal{S}$ and~$Q$-matrix~$\{q(x,y): x,y \in \mathcal S\}$ that satisfy~\eqref{eq_q_finite}. Given~$t \in (0,\infty)$ and~$\epsilon>0$, there exists a finite~$s_0$ so that for any~$z \in \mathcal S$, there exists a coupling on~$\Prob$ of two Markov chains~$(Z^1_s)_{s \ge 0}$ and~$(Z^2_s)_{s \ge 0}$ with~$Q$-matrix~$\{q(x,y): x,y \in \mathcal S\}$ started both from~$z$ such that
$$ \Prob( Z^1_s = Z^2_{s+t} \text{ for all } s \ge s_0 ) > 1-\epsilon. $$

[Theorem thm:compregime of arXiv:2606.01866, 'Phase Transition of a Semiflexible Membrane in Two Dimensions'] For $d=2$, let $\{\phi_x\}_{x\in V_N}$ be the centered Gaussian interface, zero outside $V_N$, whose covariance is $G_N$. For each fixed $\lambda\in[0,2]$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, the following holds for $x,y\in V_N^\delta\coloneq V_{\lfloor (1-\delta)N\rfloor}$: As $N\to\infty$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item(Long-range covariance) If $\|x-y\|\gtrsim N^{\lambda/2}$, then
        \[\operatorname{Cov}(\phi_x,\phi_y)=\operatorname{Cov}^\nabla_N(\phi_x,\phi_y)+O(1).\]

    \end{enumerate}
    The asymptotic notation such as $\gtrsim$ or $\ll$ is defined later; see (ch:notation of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Theorem1.1 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Let $\zeta$ be a mean 0, variance 1 random variable with a subgaussian tail. We also assume that $\zeta$ has a finite Log-Sobolev constant.

Let $A_n$ be an $n\times n$ symmetric random matrix with upper-diagonal entries $\{A_{i,j}\}_{1\leq i\leq j\leq n}$ being independent and identically distributed with distribution $\zeta$, and $A_{ij}=A_{ji}.$

Fix two positive numbers $\kappa>0$ and $\Delta>0$, and consider two locations $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in[-(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n},(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n}]$ such that $|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|\geq \Delta n^{1/2}$. 

Then there exist constants $C>0,c>0$ depending only on the random variable $\zeta$ and the constants $\kappa,\Delta$ such that for any $\delta_1,\delta_2\geq 0$, we have the following singular value estimate jointly at $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$:
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbb{P}\left(\sigma_{min}(A_n-\lambda_1 I_n)\leq\delta_1 n^{-1/2},\sigma_{min}(A_n-\lambda_2 I_n)\leq\delta_2 n^{-1/2}\right)\leq C\delta_1\delta_2+2e^{-cn}. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Theorem1.1 of arXiv:2504.15992

An elementary probability control, not an FPP counterexample. If J is uniform on {1,...,m} and A_i={J=i}, each deterministic event has probability 1/m, while P(union_i A_i)=1. Equivalently, each threshold indicator has mean 1/m and their maximum is always one. Therefore an estimate for every deterministic pair of endpoints does not automatically control a pair chosen after observing the environment. For the square boundary S_n in Z^2 there are 8n sites and at most 64n^2 ordered endpoint pairs; a raw union bound needs a per-pair bound o(n^-2) to vanish. Qualitative midpoint decay supplies no such conclusion. Independence of the resampled edge from its outside environment is valid; multiplying success probabilities for correlated endpoint capacities or selected corridors needs an additional justified filtration or independence argument.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item For every $u \in \mathcal{V}$ and $j \geq 2$,
\begin{align}
K(Tu) - K(u) &= \Psi(Tu)\Phi(Tu),
   \\
\partial_1 K(u) &= \Psi(Tu)C_1(u)\Phi(u),
   \\
K(S_j u) - K(u)
  &= \Psi(Tu)C_j(u)\Phi(S_j u).
  
\end{align}
\item There exists $z \in \mathbb{F}$ such that the resolvent
exists at every vertex:
\[
R(u) \vcentcolon= (I - zK(u))^{-1} \in \mathrm{End}(H),
\qquad u \in \mathcal{V}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 3 (Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] Let \(f\in C(\mathbb R^n)\).

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\le\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has \(u(x_0)\le0\) or
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\le0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if \(u\ge0\) in \(\mathbb R^n\) and, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\ge\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\ge0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity solution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.
title: Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.30400, 'What to Expect When You're Expecting'] Let \(n\ge2\). For \(1\le k\le n\), say that the extended expectation of the sum is determined by \(k\)-marginals if the following holds: whenever \(X=\left(X_1,\ldots,X_n\right)\) and \(Y=\left(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\right)\) are random vectors in \(\R^n\) such that \(\left(X_i\right)_{i\in S}\stackrel{d}=\left(Y_i\right)_{i\in S}\) for every \(S\subseteq\left[n\right]\) with \(\lvert S\rvert\le k\), and both \(\E\sum_{i=1}^nX_i\) and \(\E\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\) are defined, then
\[
\E\sum_{i=1}^nX_i=\E\sum_{i=1}^nY_i.
\]
We term the least such \(k\) the marginal degree of sums in dimension \(n\) and denote it by \(\sigma\left(n\right)\).
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.30400

  \right\}.
  
\end{align}

[Proposition pro: Wasserstein-$p$ bound without exchangeability final version of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Let $X\in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a random vector, and $T: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function. Suppose $T(X)$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[|T(X)|^p] < \infty$ for some $p > 1$. We assume Assumptions (assumption: Stein identity final version of the paper), (assumption: Kramers-Moyal expansion final version of the paper) and (assumption: integrability of Kramers-Moyal coefficients final version of the paper)
     hold for $X$ with operator $\mathcal{A}$ and mapping $T$. Then for any $t_0 > 0$, we have the following upper bound for Wasserstein-$p$ distance between $\mathcal{L}(T(X))$ and $\mathcal{L}(Z')$, 
    \begin{align}
        W_p(\mathcal{L}(T(X)), \mathcal{L}(Z')) &\leq g_0(t_0,p) + \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - a_{k}^{\mathcal{L}_{OU}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &= g_0(t_0,p) + g_1(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[| a_{1}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) + T(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &+ g_2(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{2}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - 1|^p]^{1/p} + \sum_{k=3}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p}, 
    \end{align}
    where $Z'\sim N(0,1)$ and the coefficients $g_k(t_0,p)$ for $k\ge 0$
are continuous in $(t_0,p)$ and are given explicitly in (equation eq: W-p bound final of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wasserstein-$p$ bound via generator comparison

[Proposition prop:basic-facts-zero of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let gamble space $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be given.
  Then we have
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}\, 0 \geq 0$ if and only if $\mathcal{Z}$ is arbitrage-free.

  \end{enumerate}

[Proposition propE3 of arXiv:2411.04238, 'Holomorphic jump-diffusions'] (Theorem 2.4.1, Theorem 6.2.14, Theorem 6.2.4 and Theorem 11.1.2 in [B:11] and  Theorem 19.3 in [Rudin:86])
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Order and type of an entire function do not change under differentiation. 
    \item  Non-constant entire functions of order strictly smaller than 1 are unbounded on lines.
    \item Let $\tau\in (0,\infty)$ and let
$B_\tau$ be the set of  
 all entire functions of exponential type  $\tau$, which are bounded on the real axis.  Then  $h\in B_\tau$ implies 
 $$|h(z)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)| \exp(\tau |\Im(z)|).$$
 Moreover, in this case we also have that $h'\in B_\tau$, 
$\sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h'(x)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)|\tau$
for all $z\in \mathbb C$, and thus in particular 
 $$|h'(z)|\leq \sup_{x\in \mathbb R}|h(x)| \tau \exp(\tau |\Im(z)|).$$
 \item {\textbf{Paley--Wiener theorem}} Let $h\in H(\mathbb C)$ be an entire function of exponential type $\tau$ such that 
 $$\int_{\mathbb R}|h(x)|^2dx<\infty.$$
 Then there exists $g\in L^2(-\tau,\tau)$ such that
 $h(z)=\int_{-\tau}^\tau g(t)e^{itz}dt$ for each $z\in \mathbb C$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition propE3 of arXiv:2411.04238

body: [Proposition 4.5 of arXiv:2510.05566, 'Domain-Shift-Aware Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models'] relates the conservativeness term πn+1 to the effective sample size neff. When the estimated weights are reasonably balanced, neff is large and the upper bound shows that the extra mass placed on ∞is small, so the upper bound in Theorem 4.4 stays close to the target level. Conversely, when only a few calibration points receive most of the weight, neff becomes small.

[Corollary 42 (Self-improvement) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A} and put
$\XX^{(n)} := \{ x \in \XX : T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi \}$ for $n \in \N$. Then
$\XX^{(n)} \subseteq \XX^{(n+1)}$ for every $n \in \N$. Hence the condition
``for every $x \in \XX$ there is a number $n \in \N$ with
$T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi$'' already implies ``for every $x \in \XX$ there is a
number $n_{0}(x) \in \N$ such that $T^{n}_{x} \sim \pi$ for \emph{every}
$n \ge n_{0}(x)$''.

[Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Let $a_n$ be a sequence such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$. Let $(\xi^{n,k})_{k\in{\mathbb N}}$ be a sequence of  $i.i.d.$ random vectors in  ${\mathbb R}^d$. Suppose that their moments satisfy:
  $${\mathbb E} \xi^{n,1}=m+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  and $${\mathbb E}(\xi^{n,1}_i-m_i)(\xi^{n,1}_j-m_j)=\sigma_{ij}+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  for some $m\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and some covariance matrix $C=(\sigma_{ij})_{d\times d}$. Let $b_n\in{\mathbb R}^d$ be a sequence such that $|b_{n}|=O\left(\sqrt{n}+a_n^2\right)$.
  Suppose that there exists $R>0$ such that for all $\eta\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and $|\eta|<R$, $\sup_n\log {\mathbb E}\exp(\eta\cdot \xi^n)<\infty$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item   Let $N(\lambda_n n)$ be an independent Poisson process with $\lambda_n=\lambda+O(\frac{1}{n})$. The sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N(\lambda_n n)}\xi^{n,k}-\lambda m n+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, (C+mm^T)l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C+mm^T$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals  
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,(C+mm^T)^{-1}x\>.}$$
    \item For any $\lambda>0$ and $u\in{\mathbb R}$, the sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\xi^{n,k}-(\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n})m+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, C l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,C^{-1}x\>.}$$
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471

[Prop Meromorphic continuation and difference equation of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] The function $\widehat \pi_1$ admits a meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ and satisfies the difference equation
\[
\widehat \pi_1(y(s+(\mu_1+\mu_2)))=\widehat G(s)\,\widehat \pi_1(y(s)),
\]
where
\[
\widehat G(s):=\frac{k_1(s)\,k_2(\zeta s)}{k_2(s)\,k_1(\zeta s)}
=\frac{(s-s_1)(s+s_2+\mu_2)}{(s-s_2)(s+s_1+\mu_2)}.
\]
Moreover, the functional equation and the invariance properties by $\widehat\eta$ and $\widehat\zeta$ extend to the whole complex plane $\mathbb{C}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] Let $A,B\subset\bR^d$ be bounded Borel sets with
$\lambda_d(\partial A)=\lambda_d(\partial B)=0$. Then
\begin{equation}

    \Cov_\eta\bigl(\mathbb S\ind_A,\mathbb S\ind_B\bigr)
    =\int_{\bR^d}\widehat{\ind}_A(\xi)
       \overline{\widehat{\ind}_B(\xi)}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi).
\end{equation}
In particular, $\Var_\eta(\mathbb S\ind_A)$ is obtained by taking $A=B$.
For every $g\in\mathcal S(\bR^d)$, one also has the mixed identity
\begin{equation}

    \Cov_\eta\bigl(\mathbb S\ind_A,\mathbb S g\bigr)
    =\int_{\bR^d}\widehat{\ind}_A(\xi)
      \overline{\hat g(\xi)}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi).
\end{equation}
Consequently, the Bartlett covariance identity holds on the linear span of
Schwartz functions and indicators of bounded Borel sets with boundary of
Lebesgue measure zero. Moreover, for every $\xi\in\bR^d$, the centered statistic
$M(\ind_A\chi_\xi)$ has Koopman spectral measure
\begin{equation}

    d\varsigma_{M(\ind_A\chi_\xi)}(\lambda)
    =\bigl|\widehat{\ind}_A(\lambda-\xi)\bigr|^2
      \,d\sigma_\eta(\lambda).
\end{equation}

body:
[Definition 12 of arXiv:2607.02434, 'A Topological Formula for \\ Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations'] The $i$-dimensional \textbf{plaquette random cluster model (PRCM)} with free boundary conditions on a finite cell complex $X$ with parameters $p\in\brac{0,1}$ and $q\in\N_{\geq 2}$ is the random $i$-complex $P$ with the following distribution:
$$\mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{X}\paren{P} = \mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{X,p,q}\paren{P} \propto p^{\abs{P}}\paren{1-p}^{\abs{X^{i}} - \abs{P}}\abs{H^{i-1}\paren{P;\Z_q}}$$
where $\abs{X^{\paren{i}}}$ and $\abs{P}$ denote the number of $i$-faces $X$ and $P.$

Moreover, if $\Lambda=\brac{-N,N}^d\subset \Z^d$ is a box, the PRCM with wired boundary conditions on $\Lambda$ is the measure
$$\mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Lambda}\paren{P} = \mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Lambda,p,q}\paren{P} \propto p^{\abs{P}}\paren{1-p}^{\abs{\Lambda^{\paren{i}}} - \abs{P}}\abs{H^{i-1}\paren{P\cup \partial \Lambda;\Z_q}}\,.$$
The weak limits of these measures as $\Lambda\nearrow \Z^d$ exist by standard stochastic monotonicity arguments and are denoted by $\mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{\Z^d,p,q}$ and $\mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Z^d,p,q}.$
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2607.02434

body: [Lemma lem:FKG-CLE of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a deterministic simply connected domain and let $\Gamma_U$ be a non-nested $\CLE_4$ in $U$. Let $F, G \colon \BR^{U_\BQ \times U_\BQ} \to \BR_{\ge 0}$ be non-negative measurable mappings. Suppose that $F(d) \ge F(d^\prime)$ and $G(d) \ge G(d^\prime)$ for all $d, d^\prime \in \BR^{U_\BQ \times U_\BQ}$ with $d(x, y) \ge d^\prime(x, y)$ for all $x, y \in U_\BQ$. Then $\BE\lbrack F(D_{\Gamma_U}^U) G(D_{\Gamma_U}^U)\rbrack \ge \BE\lbrack F(D_{\Gamma_U}^U)\rbrack \BE\lbrack G(D_{\Gamma_U}^U)\rbrack$. The same is true for any pair of non-negative measurable functionals of $(\Gamma_U, D_{\Gamma_U}^U)$ which are a.s.\ non-increasing under the merging operation of (lem:monotonicity of the paper), and in particular for the indicator functions of the events $\{D_{\Gamma_U}^U(A, B) > \varepsilon\}$, where $A, B \subseteq \overline U$ are deterministic and $\varepsilon > 0$.

[Thm 43 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $M$ be a matroid. Suppose $F$ is a flat of $M$ minimal for the property that $M$ is a non-trivial modular join over $F$. Choose flats $F_0, F_1$ with $F = F_0 \cap F_1$ such that $M = P_F(F_0, F_1)$. 
Then $M$ is supersolvable if and only if $M_0 \deq M|_{F_0}$ and $M_1 \deq M|_{F_1}$ are both supersolvable and at least one of them has a full modular flag passing through $F$.

[Lemma cutoff of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] Let $\tau,j_0,\alpha$ be as above. Let $U=\frac{\mathcal{L}^n}{\mathcal{L}^n(Q_{j_0,\alpha})}\in {\mathcal M}_+(\mathbb{R}^n)$

        \item $\| \dive \left(j_0 \left(\eta \tau + (1-\eta)U\right)\right) \|_{\mathrm{KR}} \leq C|j_0|\alpha$,
    \end{enumerate}
where $C$ depends only on $R$ and $n$.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] \phantom{ }
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Under Assumptions (assu:space of the paper) and (assu:noise of the paper), for any $p\ge 2$, any $T>0$, and for any initial datum $u_0\in L^p(\Omega,\mathcal{F}_0,\mathbb{P};L^2(U,\rho))$, there exists a unique $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. continuous and $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\in [0,T]}$-adapted
$L^2(U,\rho)$-valued strong solution $u(t)$, $t\in [0,T]$ of (equation eq:gen_model of the paper), and there exists a constant $C_{p,T}>0$, such that
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}(\|u(t)\|^p_{L^2(U,\rho)})\leq C_{p,T}\left(1+\mathbb{E}\|u_0\|^p_{L^2(U,\rho)}\right),\quad t\in[0,T].
\end{align*} 
\item
Under Assumptions (assu:space of the paper), (assu:noise of the paper), (assu:hat of the paper), and (assu:inv of the paper), there exists a non-trivial compactly embedded linear subspace $H_1\subset L^2(U,\rho)$, such that for every initial datum $v\in H_1$, there exists a sequence of real numbers $T_n\ge 1$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $T_n\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$, and a probability measure $\mu^v$ on the Borel sets of $(L^2(U,\rho))$ which is invariant for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$, and the following convergence holds
\[\frac{1}{T_n}\int_0^{T_n}\mu_{u}(t,v)\,dt\rightharpoonup \mu^v\quad\text{as}\;\;n\to\infty,\]
in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
\item Under Assumptions (assu:space of the paper), (assu:noise of the paper), (assu:hat of the paper), (assu:inv of the paper), and (assu:ergo of the paper), there exists a unique probability measure $\mu$ on the Borel sets of $(L^2(U,\rho))$ with second moments which is invariant for the exponentially ergodic and exponentially mixing semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$, and, in particular,
\[\mu_{u}(t,v)\rightharpoonup \mu\quad\text{as}\;\;t\to\infty,\]
for every $v\in L^2(U,\rho)$ in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
In particular, there exist constants $\hat{C}\ge 0$ and $\lambda\in (0,2\alpha)$, such that for any $v\in H$, and any $t\ge 0$,
\[\left|\mathbb{E}[\varphi(u(t,v))] - \int_{L^2(U,\rho)}\varphi(z)\, \mu(dz) \right|\le 2\operatorname{Lip}(\varphi)\left(\|v\|^2_{L^2(U,\rho)}+\hat{C}\right)e^{-(2\alpha-\lambda)t},\]
for any bounded and Lipschitz continuous function $\varphi:L^2(U,\rho)\to\mathbb{R}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2505.14012

body: Let mu and nu be probability measures on a measurable space (S, S), and let (X, Y) be any coupling of mu and nu, meaning X and Y are random variables defined on a common probability space with X distributed as mu and Y distributed as nu. body: [Lem 12 of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $\phi_i: G_i \to G$ be good approximations with $A_i \subset G_i$, $A\subset G$ as regular neighborhoods, and assume $G$ is metrizable. Then for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and any sequence $g_i \in A_i ^n$, after passing to a subsequence, there is $g \in \overline{A^n}$ with $\phi_i (g_i) \to g$. Moreover, if $g_i \in \partial A_i$ for all $i$, then $g \in \partial A$.
title: Lem 12 of arXiv:2608.30990

DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. On the path o--a2--b--a1 with three independent Bernoulli(1/2) bonds, order A=(a1,a2). Let F2 mean that a2 is the first member of A connected to o in this order. Then P(F2)=3/8 and P(F2 and a2 connects to b)=1/8, so P(a2 connects to b | F2)=1/3, whereas min_(a in A)P(a connects to b)=1/2. The first-reached event contains a decreasing exclusion, so FKG does not justify the pointwise conditional lower bound. The Kozma--Nitzan global inequality P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_(a in A)P(a connects to b) is nevertheless an equality here (both sides 1/4). This refutes the conditional proof premise, not the global conjecture.

body:
[Openquestion 33 (Multiple winner flips for a fixed pair) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix two patterns $A,B$ and use \emph{random tie-break} with identical independent coins $\Pr(\mathrm{H})=p$.
Can the advantage function
\[
g_{A,B}(p):=\Pr(A\!>\!B)-\tfrac12
\]
have \emph{two or more distinct zeros} in $(0,1)$ (equivalently, can the winner $A$ vs.\ $B$ flip more than once as $p$ varies)?
If so, what is the smallest length pair $(|A|,|B|)$ for which this happens?

More generally, for fixed lengths $(L_1,L_2)$, what is the largest possible number of winner flips
(i.e.\ the largest possible number of sign changes of $g_{A,B}(p)$ on $(0,1)$)
over all pairs with $|A|=L_1$, $|B|=L_2$? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Multiple winner flips for a fixed pair

body: Let (mu_n) be a sequence of probability measures and mu a probability measure on a metric space S with its Borel sigma-algebra. The following are equivalent: (i) mu_n converges weakly to mu, meaning integral of f d mu_n converges to integral of f d mu for every bounded continuous f: S -> R; (ii) limsup_n mu_n(F) <= mu(F) for every closed set F; (iii) liminf_n mu_n(G) >= mu(G) for every open set G; (iv) mu_n(A) converges to mu(A) for every Borel set A with mu(boundary of A) = 0. [standard, e.g. Billingsley, Convergence of Probability Measures]

body:
[Thm 5 (Stability of compensated jump functionals under quadratic variation convergence) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let \(X\) and \(\{X^n\}_{n\ge 1}\) be real-valued càdlàg processes on
\([0,t]\), with jump measures \(\mu\) and \(\mu^n\), and predictable
compensators \(\nu\) and \(\nu^n\), respectively. Assume that 
\[
        [X^n-X]_t \longrightarrow 0
        \quad\text{in probability.}
\]

Let \(f\) and \(f_n\), \(n\ge 1\), be predictable functions on
\(\Omega\times[0,t]\times\mathbb R\), 
such that the compensated jump integrals
\[
        M_t
        :=
        \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
        f(s,x,\omega)(\mu-\nu)(ds,dx),
\]
and
\[
        M^n_t
        :=
        \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
        f_n(s,x,\omega)(\mu^n-\nu^n)(ds,dx)
\]
are well-defined purely discontinuous local martingales.
Assume that $\P\left(\exists s\le t: \Delta X_s(\omega)\in \mathrm{disc}(f(s,.,\omega))\right)=0$.
Assume moreover that, for every \(a>0\), there exists a nonnegative
predictable process \(C^a\), locally bounded on \([0,t]\), such that, for
all \(n\ge1\),
\[
|f_n(s,x,\omega)|+|f(s,x,\omega)|
\le C^a_s(\omega)|x|,
\qquad s\le t,\ |x|\le a .
\]
Assume also that there exists a set \(\Omega_0\in\mathcal F\) with
\(\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that, for every \(\omega\in\Omega_0\), every
\(s\leq t\), and every compact set \(K\subset\mathbb R\),
\[
        \sup_{x\in K}|f_n(s,x,\omega)-f(s,x,\omega)|\longrightarrow 0 .
\]

Then
\[
        M^n \longrightarrow M
        \quad\text{ucp on }[0,t].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stability of compensated jump functionals under quadratic variation convergence

[Theorem 1 (Liu--Tang--Zhang) of arXiv:2609.04069, 'Positive and Negative Square Energies of $2$-Connected Graphs'] If $F$ is a connected graph, then
$$
 \min\{\spen(F),\sneg(F)\}\geq |V(F)|-1.
$$
In particular, both square energies are at least $|V(F)|-1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem T:MainTheorem of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] (Mean field large-population limit) Let $0<T<\infty$ be given and let Assumptions (A:molarBdd of the paper)-(A:AssumptionMomentFiniteness of the paper) hold. Then, the sequence of measure-valued processes $\{\bm{\mu}_{t}^{\zeta}\}_{t \in[0, T]} \in \mathbb{D}_{\otimes_{j=1}^{J} M_{F}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})}([0, T])$ is relatively compact in $\mathbb{D}_{\otimes_{j=1}^{J} M_{F}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})}([0, T])$ and it converges in distribution to $\{\boldsymbol{\xi}_t\}_{t \in [0,T]} \in C_{\otimes_{j=1}^{J} M_{F}(\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d})}([0, T])$ as $\zeta \rightarrow 0$, where each $\xi_t^j$ is the unique solution to
\begin{align}
   &\left\langle  f, \xi_{t}^{j}\right\rangle = \left\langle f, \xi_0^{j}\right\rangle + \int_0^t \left\langle (\mathcal{L}_{j}f)(x,v), \xi_{s}^{j}(dx,dv)\right\rangle ds\notag\\
      &\phantom{=} + \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\int_0^t \int_{\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{(\ell)} \otimes \tilde{\mathbb{V}}^{(\ell)}}\frac{1}{\bm{\alpha}^{(\ell)}!}K_\ell(\bm{x},\bm{v})\biggl(-\sum_{r=1}^{\alpha_{\ell j}}f\left(x_r^{(j)},v_r^{(j)}\right)+\int_{\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)}}\left(\sum_{r=1}^{\beta_{\ell j}}f\left(y_r^{(j)},{v'}_{r}^{(j)}\right)\right)\\
      &\phantom{=}\times m_{\ell}\left(\bm{y},\bm{v'}|\bm{x},\bm{v}\right)d\bm{y}d\bm{v'}\biggr)\lambda^{(\ell)}[\xi_{s}](d\bm{x}, d\bm{v}) ds.\notag
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem T:MainTheorem of arXiv:2606.03079

[Definition def:graph-matrix-for-shape of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Given a shape \(\tau\), its graph matrix \(M_\tau\) is indexed by boundary labelings.
For boundary labelings \(S\) of \(U_\tau\) and \(T\) of \(V_\tau\), define
\[
    \mathsf{M} _{\tau}[S,T]
    =
    \sum_{\substack{
        \sigma:\,V(\tau)\to \mathbb N \\
        \sigma \text{ is a mapping of } \tau \\
        \sigma(U_\tau)=S,\ \sigma(V_\tau)=T
    }}
    \prod_{e\in E(\tau)}
    \chi_{t(e)}\bigl(G[\sigma(e)]\bigr).
\]
Here, if \(e=\{x,y\}\) is an edge between a square vertex and a circle vertex, then
\(G[\sigma(e)]\) denotes the corresponding entry \(G[\sigma(x),\sigma(y)]\).
title: Graph matrix of a shape

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \((T_L)_{L\geq1}\) be positive trace-class contractions on a Hilbert space. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(\sup_{L\geq1}L^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(T_L)<\infty\);
\item there is a measurable \(r:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) with \(r\in L^1(0,\infty)\) such that, for every \(m\geq1\),
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{tr}(T_L^m)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_0^\infty r(\xi)^m\,\mathrm{d}\xi.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then, for each \(t>-1\),
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{1}{L}\log\det(\operatorname{Id}+tT_L)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_0^\infty \log\bigl(1+t\,r(\xi)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\xi,
\]
locally uniformly for \(t\) in compact subsets of \((-1,\infty)\).

[Theorem 22 of arXiv:2606.26496, 'Homeomorphism of the Revuz correspondence under Dynkin class assumptions'] Let ${\sf A}^n,{\sf A}\in\mathbf{A}_c^+$. Denote by $\mu_n$, $\mu$ their Revuz measures in ${\sf S}$ for each $n$. Assume that $\mu \in {\sf S}_{L\!D}$ and $\{\mu_n\}$ is of uniformly local Dynkin. For any compact set $K \subset E$, if the resolvent kernel $R_1(x,y)$ is continuous on $E\times E$. Then, $R_1 \mu^K,R_1\mu_n^K \in C_b(E)$ and the following conditions are equivalent:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[{\rm (i)}] $\mu_n$  converges to $\mu$ weakly on $K$.
			\item[{\rm (ii)}] $U_1 \mu^K_n$  converges to $U_1 \mu^K$ strongly in $\mathcal{E}_1$-norm.
			\item[{\rm (iii)}] $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to \infty}\mathbb{E}_x\left[ \sup_{0\leq t\leq T} \left|  (1_K{\sf A}^n)_t - (1_K{\sf A})_t \right|  \right] =0  \text{ for any }T>0\text{ and any }\  x\in E.$
			\item[{\rm (iv)}] $R_1 \mu_n^K$  converges to $R_1 \mu^K$ uniformly on $E$.
		\end{itemize}

[Prp 11 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For a boundedly compact metric space $(X,d^X)$ and $\rho_X\in X$, we have the following.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item [$\mathrm{(i)}$]The function $d^{X,\rho_X}_{\BL^{\kappa}}$ is a well-defined complete, separable metric on $\calM(X)$.
    \item [$\mathrm{(ii)}$]The topology of $(\calM(X),d^{X,\rho_X}_{\BL^{\kappa}})$ is independent of $\rho_X$ 
    and the convergence with respect to this topology is equivalent to vague convergence.
    \item [$\mathrm{(iii)}$]Let $(Y,d^Y)$ be a $\bcm$ space and fix an isometric embedding $f:X\to Y$.
  Then $\calM(X)\ni \mu\mapsto \mu\circ f^{-1}\in \calM(Y)$ is isometric 
  with respect to $d^{X,\rho_X}_{\BL^{\kappa}}$ and $d^{Y,f(\rho_X)}_{\BL^{\kappa}}$. 
   \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prp 11 of arXiv:2605.23308

[Dfn 3. dfn: functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Functor}] 
  We call $\tau$ a \textit{functor} on $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ if it satisfies the following.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      For every $ (S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$,
      one has a metric space $(\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}), d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}})$
      where $\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$ is a set and $d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}}$ is a metric on it.
      We simply write $\tau(S) \coloneqq \tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$.
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      one has a distance-preserving map $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$.
    \item 
      For any two root-and-distance-preserving maps $f :S_{1} \to S_{2},\, g : S_{2} \to S_{3}$,
      it holds that $\tau_{g \circ f} = \tau_{g} \circ \tau_{f}$.
    \item 
      For any $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$, 
      it holds that $\tau_{\id_{S}} = \id_{\tau(S)}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Similarly, we call $\tau$ a functor on $\mathfrak{M}$ if it satisfies the same conditions 
  not for $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ but for $\mathfrak{M}$.
title: Dfn 3. dfn: functor of arXiv:2412.08236

For any non-negative integer n, the rising factorial x^{\overline{n}} = x(x+1)...(x+n-1) is the generating polynomial for the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind: x^{\overline{n}} = sum_{k=0}^n [n atop k] x^k.

[Theorem thm:rmulmc_discretization of arXiv:2506.23062, 'Shifted Composition IV\@: \\ Toward Ballistic Acceleration for Log-Concave Sampling'] Let $\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}'$ denote the kernels for~(eq:rm-ulmc of the paper) and~(eq:ULMC of the paper) respectively, and let $\boldsymbol{P}$ denote the kernel for~(eq:ULD of the paper) run for time $h$.
    Assume that $-\beta I \preceq \nabla^2 V \preceq \beta I$, $\gamma \leqslant \sqrt{32\beta}$, and $h = \widetilde O(\frac{\gamma}{\beta} \wedge \frac{\gamma^{1/3}}{\beta^{5/6} T^{1/3}})$.
    Then, for $T \coloneqq Nh$ and $C_{\chi^2} \coloneqq \log(1+\chi^2(\bs\mu\mathbin{\|}\bs\pi))/d$,
    \begin{align*}
        \KL(\bs\mu\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}^{N-1}\hat{\boldsymbol{P}}{}' \mathbin{\|} \bs\mu \boldsymbol{P}^N) = \widetilde O\Bigl( (1+C_{\chi^2})\,(1 + \beta^{1/2} T)\,\frac{\beta^2 dh^3}{\gamma} \Bigr)\,.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {\ref{eq:rm-ulmc} discretization bound}

[Prop stat of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] Let $\rho_0$ be a Hitchin representation and let $\rho \neq \rho_0$ be a quasi-Hitchin representation in its bending fiber. There exist constants $0<\alpha<1$ and $0<\lambda<1$ such that, for all sufficiently large $L$, at least an $\alpha$-proportion of the curves in $\mathcal S(L)$ satisfy
\[
\ell_\rho^H(\gamma)\leq\lambda\ell_{\rho_0}^H(\gamma).
\]
Moreover, when $\rho_0$ is $n$-Fuchsian, the analogous statistical domination holds for the translation length. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Statistical domination of lengths

body:
[Theorem thm:singularity of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}\cap C^{3}$ have a regularly varying right
		tail in the smooth sense:
		$f^{(j)}(x) = (-1)^{j}(p)_{j}\,c_{0}\,x^{-p-j}(1+o(1))$ for
		$j = 0, 1, 2$, with $p > 1$. If $p \neq 2$, then
		\begin{equation}
			R \;\sim\; \frac{p(2-p)}{2c_{0}^{2}}\,x^{2p-2}:
			
		\end{equation}
		the curvature at the boundary of the support diverges to $+\infty$
		for $1<p<2$ and to $-\infty$ for $p>2$; for exponential or faster
		tails, again in the smooth sense, $R \to -\infty$. At $p = 2$ the
		leading divergence cancels and regularity is decided at second
		order: if
		\begin{equation}
			f(x) = c_{0}x^{-2}\big(1 + b\,x^{-\alpha} + o(x^{-\alpha})\big),
			\qquad 0 < \alpha < 2,\ \alpha \neq 1,\ b \neq 0,
			
		\end{equation}
		in the smooth sense, then
		\begin{equation}
			R \;\sim\; \frac{\alpha b(\alpha - 1)}{c_{0}^{2}}\,x^{2-\alpha},
			
		\end{equation}
		which still diverges. Hence a quadratic leading tail is necessary
		for the curvature to remain bounded at the boundary of rank, but
		not sufficient: every second-order correction of order $x^{-\alpha}$
		with $0 < \alpha < 2$, $\alpha \neq 1$, forces divergence, while
		corrections of order two and faster, again in the smooth sense,
		leave the curvature bounded. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Singularity theorem

Every set can be well-ordered: for every set X there exists a total (linear) order on X in which every nonempty subset of X has a least element. Over ZF the well-ordering theorem is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to Zorn's lemma.

Consider the set P of pairs (W, r) where W is a subset of X and r is a well-ordering of W. Order P by end-extension: (W_1, r_1) <= (W_2, r_2) when W_1 is an initial segment of (W_2, r_2) and r_2 restricted to W_1 equals r_1. P is nonempty (the empty set with the empty order, or any singleton). Every chain in P has an upper bound: take the union of the domains with the union of the orders; end-extension makes this a well-defined linear order, and it is a well-order because any nonempty subset meets some member W of the chain, and its least element within that W remains least overall, since later members of the chain only add elements above all of W. By Zorn's lemma P has a maximal element (W*, r*). If W* were not all of X, pick x in X outside W* and place it above every element of W*: this yields a well-ordering of W* union {x} that properly end-extends (W*, r*), contradicting maximality. Hence W* = X and X is well-ordered. (Conversely, a well-ordering of a union of a family of nonempty sets yields a choice function by selecting least elements, so the well-ordering theorem implies AC.)","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:81845b66a64fd9e8baa9830788af1d24ccfa7255e76ef65a7c1032858629b23b","revision_digest":"sha256:fdf48816b2f29bc209d59710653ec93725cf49f1621dab9e2c47d1f24218a909","source_id":"wikipedia:Well-ordering_theorem","source_revision":"as-read-2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma lem6.3 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $(y_1, y_2, y_3, \dots)$ and $(z_1, z_2, z_3, \dots)$
are each a sequence of elements of the set $\{-1,0,1\}$.
Suppose that (i) there exists $m \in \mathbb N$ such that
$y_k = z_k = 0$ for all $k > m$, and
(ii) there exists $k \in \mathbb N$ such that $y_k \neq z_k$.

   Suppose $r_1, r_2, r_3, \dots$ is a sequence of positive numbers 
such that $r_{k+1}/r_k \geq 3$ for every $k \in \mathbb N$.

   Then each of the sums $\sum_{k=1}^\infty r_ky_k$ and 
$\sum_{k=1}^\infty r_kz_k$ has at most finitely many non-zero summands 
(and therefore trivially converges absolutely); and these sums satisfy 
$\sum_{k=1}^\infty r_ky_k \neq \sum_{k=1}^\infty r_kz_k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem6.3 of arXiv:2411.03528

[Dfn 37 (Sub-exponential class) of arXiv:2609.02398, '\textbf{Convex Order Comparisons for Sub-Gamma Random Variables}'] Let $\sigma, \alpha > 0$. A random variable $X$ belongs to the class
$\SE(\sigma^2, \alpha)$ if
\begin{align}
    \E\left[e^{\lambda X}\right]
    \leq \exp\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2}{2}\right)
    \qquad \text{for all } |\lambda| \leq \frac{1}{\alpha} \, .
    
\end{align}
title: Sub-exponential class

[Thm 1d-upper-and-lower of arXiv:2411.14336, 'Finding the root in random nearest neighbor trees'] There exist $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that the following holds for the 1-NN model for all $n \in \mathbf{N}$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$. 
There exists a $O(n^2 + \log^2(1/\varepsilon))$-time embedded root finding algorithm that returns $H(\varepsilon, n)$ of size satisfying $|H(\varepsilon, n)|\log |H(\varepsilon, n)| \leq c_1 \log(1/\varepsilon)$. Additionally, it is information-theoretically impossible to provide a confidence set whose size satisfies $|H(\varepsilon, n)| \log |H(\varepsilon,n)| < c_2 \log(1/\varepsilon)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop discretize of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Given a strong solution $t\mapsto \text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}\in\mathbb{R}^N$ to the SDE

    \begin{align*}
{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}=\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}){\rm d} t+\sigma{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(t)}
\end{align*}

    on $\mathbb{R}^N$ for some function $\text{\boldmath $a$}:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^N$ and constant diffusion coefficient $\sigma$, along with a step
    size $\delta\in(0,1)$, consider the Euler-Maruyama scheme
    $\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(0)},\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(1)},\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(2)},\ldots$ defined recursively by
    $\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(0)}=\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(0)}$ and

    \begin{align*}
\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n+1)}=\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n)}+\delta
\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n)})+\sigma(\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(\delta(n+1))}-\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(\delta n)}).
\end{align*}

    Suppose that, for some positive constants $K_1,K_2,K_3$, we have that
    $\mathbb{E}[\|\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(0)}\|^2]\le K_1N$, $\| \text{\boldmath $a$}({\boldsymbol 0})\|^2\le K_2N$, and
    $\| \text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $u$})-\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $v$})\|\le K_3\|\text{\boldmath $u$}-\text{\boldmath $v$}\|$ for all $\text{\boldmath $u$},\text{\boldmath $v$}\in\mathbb{R}^N$,
    i.e. the initial condition is bounded in $L^2$ and the drift
    coefficient is Lipschitz and bounded at the origin. Then there
    exists a constant $L$ depending only on $K_1,K_2,K_3$ such that
    for all $\delta>0$ and $T\in\delta\mathbb{N}$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[\|\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(T)}-\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(T/\delta)}\|^2]\le Le^{LT}\delta N.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop discretize of arXiv:2608.06500

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $p\ge 2k$, let
\[
q:=\frac{p}{p-2k+1},
\]
let $\varkappa\in(0,q)$, and let $a,b>0$. For $r\in\mathbb{N}$, set
\[
\beta_r:=
\frac{p\varkappa}{p(r+\varkappa)+\varkappa r(2k-1)}.
\]
Then, for every pair of mappings $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ with
$f_j,g_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$,
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|g_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\]
and
\[
\gamma(\Delta_f\le \varepsilon)\le a\varepsilon^\varkappa,
\quad
\gamma(\Delta_g\le \varepsilon)\le a\varepsilon^\varkappa
\quad \forall\, \varepsilon>0,
\]
one has
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
2^{14}k^{7/2}(q-\varkappa)^{-1}(a+b^p+1)\,
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^{\beta_1}.
\]
More generally, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C(r,k)(q-\varkappa)^{-1}(a+b^p+1)\,
d_r(f,g)^{\beta_r},
\]
where
$C(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$.

[Lemma lem:descent_curves of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let~$(x,y)\in \mathcal D_c^\circ$ lie in a phase region, and let~$\zeta_0=\zeta_*(x,y)$. If~$(x,y)\in \mathcal F_{(\alpha,\beta)}$, where~$(\alpha,\beta)\subset A_0$ is the interval between consecutive angles~$\alpha,\beta$, assume that~$(x,y)\notin \bm l_{e(\alpha)}\cup \bm l_{e(\beta)}$. Then we may choose orientations of~$C_{(x,y),\mathrm{desc}}$ and~$C_{(x,y),\mathrm{asc}}$ such that, for all sufficiently large~$n$ and all
\(
\mathsf b_n\in B(\mathsf C_n),
\mathsf w_n\in W(\mathsf C_n),
\)
the curve~$C_{(x,y),\mathrm{desc}}$ is {homologous} to~$C(I_{\mathsf b_n})$ in
\[
\Sigma\setminus \bigcup_{e\in I_{\mathsf b_n,-}} \bm\alpha_e,
\]
and the curve~$C_{(x,y),\mathrm{asc}}$ is {homologous} to~$C(I_{\mathsf w_n})$ in
\[
\Sigma\setminus \bigcup_{e\in I_{\mathsf w_n,+}} \bm\alpha_e.
\]

[Theo Approximation of arXiv:2411.19543, 'Feller property and convergence for semigroups of time-changed processes'] Let $F_n,\, F$ be the fine supports of $\mu_n,\mu_\infty$, respectively. Assume that $F_n,\, F,\, n\in\mathbb{N}$ are closed. Let $\Pi_n : C_0(F)\to C_0(F_n),\;\, u\mapsto (P_F u)|_{F_n}$. Then for all $u\in C_0(F)$ it holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)] 
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in F_n} \left|\check{T}_t^n \Pi_n u(x) - \Pi_n \check{T}_t^\infty u(x) \right| = 0
\]
locally uniformly in $t\in [0,\infty)$.
\item[\rm(2)] For all $\alpha>0$
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in F_n} \left|V_\alpha^n \Pi_n u(x) - \Pi_n V_\alpha^\infty u(x) \right| = 0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 38 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$. Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be a fixed bounded interval, and let $\cB_{\sigma,\Omega}$ denote the centered operator in Proposition~\ref{thm:conjugation} with the integral restricted to $\Omega$. For fixed $0\le m<2$, put
\[
\eta_\sigma=
\begin{cases}
\sigma,&0\le m<1,\\
\sigma^{2-m},&1\le m<2.
\end{cases}
\]
There are $\sigma_0>0$ and $C_\Omega>0$, independent of $\sigma$, such that

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(H\leq G\), let \(K\) be a \(G\)-field, and let \(\chi:H\to K^\times\) satisfy the \(1\)-cocycle condition
  \[
    \chi(h_1h_2)=\chi(h_1)\,h_1\bigl(\chi(h_2)\bigr)\quad(h_1,h_2\in H).
  \]
  Choose a section
  \[
    \rho:G/H\longrightarrow G,\quad \rho(H)=1,
  \]
  and put
  \[
    \alpha(\gamma,\lambda):=\rho(\gamma\lambda)^{-1}\gamma\rho(\lambda)\quad(\gamma\in G,\ \lambda\in G/H).
  \]
  If the elements \(z_\lambda\), \(\lambda\in G/H\), are algebraically independent over \(K\), then the formulas
  \begin{equation}
    \gamma(z_\lambda):=\rho(\gamma\lambda)\bigl(\chi(\alpha(\gamma,\lambda))\bigr)z_{\gamma\lambda}
  \end{equation}
  extend the given action on \(K\) to a \(G\)-field structure on the purely transcendental extension
  \[
    E:=K\bigl(z_\lambda:\lambda\in G/H\bigr).
  \]
  In particular,
  \[
    h(z_H)=\chi(h)z_H\quad(h\in H).
  \]

  Moreover, let \(D\trianglelefteq G\) satisfy \(D\subseteq H\) and \(\chi|_D=1\).
  If \(D\) acts trivially on \(K\), then it acts trivially on \(E\).

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton structural argument Result: If the offspring distribution has finite support bounded by D, each coordinate of the distributional map is a polynomial of degree at most D in the color probabilities. Fixed points are therefore a compact real algebraic subset of the probability simplex. In contrast with one variable, polynomial equations may have curves of zeros, so analyticity alone cannot prove finiteness. Check: For example, the algebraic system x-y=0 in a square has a whole line of zeros; this illustrates the logical gap without asserting that this system comes from an automaton. Obstruction: The nonnegative multinomial coefficients and deterministic count assignments constrain which algebraic sets can occur. Neither an admissible positive-dimensional example nor a general exclusion is obtained.

[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2607.22470, 'A Logarithmic Fluctuation Hierarchy for Sequential Interacting Diffusions'] Let \(n_1,\ldots,n_q,k_1,\ldots,k_r\ge0\), and let
\(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_q,\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_r\in
C_c^\infty(\R^d)\). Then, as \(N\to\infty\), the following convergences hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The initial vector
\[
\bigl(\langle Y_0^{N,n_a},\varphi_a\rangle\bigr)_{a=1}^q
\]
converges weakly in \(\R^q\) to the centered Gaussian vector with covariance
\eqref{eq:limit-initial-covariance}.

\item[(ii)] The martingale vector
\[
\bigl(M^{N,k_b}(\psi_b)\bigr)_{b=1}^r
\]
converges weakly in \(C([0,T];\R)^r\) to the centered continuous Gaussian
martingale with covariations \eqref{eq:limit-martingale-covariance}.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition cor:minibatch-variable-range-eb of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Fix deterministic integers $t_0 \ge 1$ and $b \ge 1$, and let $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t \ge t_0-1}$ be a filtration. For every $t \ge t_0$, let $H_t^{(1)}, \ldots, H_t^{(b)}$ be integrable, $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable random variables that are conditionally independent given $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$ and have a common conditional mean $m_t \coloneqq \mathbb{E}\left[H_t^{(i)} \mid \mathcal{F}_{t-1}\right]$, for $i = 1, \ldots, b$. Let $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ be an almost surely finite,\footnote{As in Theorem~(thm:variable-range-eb of the paper), no uniform upper bound on the process $\{c_t\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is assumed.} nonnegative predictable process such that $\left|H_t^{(i)}\right| \le c_t$ almost surely for every $t \ge t_0$ and $i = 1, \ldots, b$. Define
\[
    \overline H_{t_0-1}^{\mathrm{MB}}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    \overline H_t^{\mathrm{MB}}
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s=t_0}^t
    \left(
        \frac{1}{b}
        \sum_{i=1}^b
        H_s^{(i)}
        -
        m_s
    \right),
\]
and
\[
    W_{t_0-1}^{\mathrm{MB}}
    \coloneqq
    0,
    \qquad
    W_t^{\mathrm{MB}}
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{s=t_0}^t
    \sum_{i=1}^b
    \left(H_s^{(i)}\right)^2,
    \qquad
    C_t
    \coloneqq
    \max_{t_0 \le s \le t}
    c_s.
\]
Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        \overline H_t^{\mathrm{MB}}
        \le
        \frac{1}{b}
        \mathfrak B_\alpha\left(
            W_t^{\mathrm{MB}},
            C_t
        \right)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem_1 of arXiv:2607.11469, 'Breuer-Major-Donsker invariance principle'] Let $\{ G_k \}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a centered stationary Gaussian sequence 
with $\rho_G(0)=1$. Let $\mathcal{F}_k = \sigma\{ G_j: j\leq k \}$,
 $Y_k = \mathbb{E}[ G_k | \mathcal{F}_{k-1}]$, and $\varepsilon_k = G_k - Y_k$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$.
Then the following results hold. 

\smallskip

\noindent
{\rm (i)}  $\{ Y_k \}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is a  centered stationary Gaussian sequence 
with $\rho_Y(0)  = 1 -\nu^2$ with $\nu = \| G_0 - Y_0\|_2$.
Moreover, $\varepsilon_k$, $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, are i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0, \nu^2)$.
 
\smallskip

\noindent
{\rm (ii)}  If $\rho_G\in\ell^d(\mathbb{Z})$ for some $d\geq 2$, then $\rho_Y\in\ell^d(\mathbb{Z})$ as well. 

\smallskip

\noindent
{\rm (iii)} Suppose $\nu^2 < 1$ and define 
$
Z_k:=\frac{Y_k}{\sqrt{1-\nu^2}}.
$
Then, 
for each $k\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\begin{equation}
\qquad\qquad\qquad
\mathbb{E}[\varphi(G_k)\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}]
=
P_\tau\varphi(Z_k)
\quad\text{with  
$e^{-\tau}=\sqrt{1-\nu^2}
$.}
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lem_1 of arXiv:2607.11469

body: [Theorem 5.1 ([13]) of arXiv:2511.20698, 'On the Role of Hidden States of Modern Hopfield Network in Transformer'] The norm of the residual of attention-only network ${\textrm{AttnNet}}(\bm{X})$ decays as $\displaystyle\|\textrm{Res}\left({\textrm{AttnNet}}(\bm{X})\right)\|_{1,\infty}\leq\left(rC\right)^{\frac{3^{L}-1}{2}}\|\textrm{Res}\left(\bm{X}\right)\|_{1,\infty}^{3^{L}},$ (13) where $r=\frac{8H}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}$ and $C$ is certain constant. This suggests the double exponential decay of the rank.

body: Let tau be a stopping time with respect to a filtration (F_t)_{t in T} (that is, {tau <= t} is in F_t for every t). The sigma-algebra of events prior to tau, denoted F_tau, is defined as the collection of all A in F such that A intersect {tau <= t} is in F_t for every t in T. F_tau is itself a sigma-algebra, tau is F_tau-measurable, and if sigma and tau are stopping times with sigma <= tau almost surely then F_sigma is a subset of F_tau. [standard, e.g. Karatzas and Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus]
title: The Stopping-Time Sigma-Algebra F_tau

[Lemma lem:shape-monotonicity of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Let $X_\theta\ge0$ have CDF $G_\theta$ and density $g_\theta$.  Put
\[
        W(\theta)=\operatorname{Var}(X_\theta)-\mathbb E X_\theta,
        \qquad
        \mu_\theta=\mathbb E X_\theta.
\]
Assume that $\operatorname{Var}(X_\theta)\ge \mathbb E X_\theta$ and that
\[
        w_\theta(x):=-\partial_\theta G_\theta(x)
\]
is nonnegative, locally integrable, and satisfies
$0<\int_0^\infty w_\theta(x)\,d x<\infty$.  Assume also that differentiation under the tail integrals below is justified.  If
\begin{equation}
        \frac{w_\theta(x)}{xg_\theta(x)}
\end{equation}
is increasing in $x$, then $W'(\theta)>0$.

body: [Definition def:crossing_cluster of arXiv:2506.07158, 'The diffusivity of supercritical Bernoulli percolation is infinitely differentiable'] We say that a cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ is crossable if each of the $d$ pairs of opposite $(d-1)$-dimensional faces of the cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ is joined by an open path in ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$. We say that a cluster $\mathscr{C}\subseteq {\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ is a crossing cluster for ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ if $\mathscr{C}$ intersects each of the $(d-1)$-dimensional faces of ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$.
title: Crossability and crossing cluster

[Thm 228 (\textbf{main result for symmetrized projection pursuit}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The following holds in the Ising (resp. spherical) cases.
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item 
        
        If $\mu \in \ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ (resp. $\ocM^{\sph,\sym}(\alpha)$), for any $\iota > 0$ there exist $L$ large enough and $c$ small enough such that for sufficiently large $N$, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm that $(\iota,1-e^{-cN})$-symmetrically attains $\mu$.
        \item 
        
        For any $\fq \in [1,2)$ and $\iotamsr > 0$, there exists small $\iotasol > 0$ such that the following holds.
        For any $L$, there exists small $c>0$ such that for sufficiently large $N$, all $L$-Lipschitz algorithms are $(\fq, \iotamsr,\iotasol,1-e^{-cN})$-symmetrcally confined to $\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textbf{main result for symmetrized projection pursuit}

Assumptions: Independent Gaussian zero-bias ReLU rows/layers, hybrid normalized/ordinary Gram self-loop kernel of C039, n sufficiently large, fixed T. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:4fa172f7326b7cf343a5dab2ef18c188e23a118bb2655d2c8fd721ca7b379026","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/4f/4fa172f7326b7cf343a5dab2ef18c188e23a118bb2655d2c8fd721ca7b379026.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:98724c8e7c4c4475db5c666bd81d25ff0417c42dc077cf1ae14f24f3ad7d26fa","bundle_entry_key":"relu-all-state-weak-defect","bundle_id":"population.t244-logarithmic-bounded-weak-rate-015","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-relu-all-state-weak-defect","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C042-C043: bounded-observable logarithmic finite-width bias

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target 1, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
All claims below depend on the preceding unaudited C032-C041 calculations
as specified. They require the reviewer's independent check. This is a
bounded-observable result, not an expansion of the infinite raw exact
reciprocal mean. Literature novelty is not asserted.

Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and

    A=(2u+a)D+u^2 D^2,
    B=(10u+6a/5+b/u)D+(11u^2+12au/5+a^2/2)D^2
                                +(4u^3+au^2)D^3+(u^4/2)D^4,
    C=B-A^2/2=(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2.

Let P_s be the semigroup of dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)V dW, and f(u)=1-exp(-u).
Use C039's global hybrid Gaussian/ReLU kernel Q_n for the reciprocal
U=1/(n theta). Fix theta0 in (0,pi], T<infinity.

## C042: accumulated local weak defect, with no reciprocal upper cutoff

For any deterministic v_k in [0,T], put g_k=P_(v_k)f. Uniformly in
N<=Tn, with U_k the hybrid chain started at U0=1/(n theta0),

    sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E| (Q_n-P_(1/n))g_k(U_k)
                                          -Cg_k(U_k)/n^2 |
                                             <=C_(theta0,T)/n. (1)

The v_k need not be monotone. This is a local-defect estimate along the
chain, sufficient for telescoping bounded tests. It contains no stopping
boundary correction and uses no finite raw reciprocal moment of the exact
network.

### Weighted semigroup derivative bounds

The affine solution V_v^u=V_v^0+uJ_v, J_v=exp(v+sqrt(2)W_v), gives

    D^j g_v(u)=(-1)^(j+1) E[J_v^j exp(-V_v^0-uJ_v)], j>=1.

For every nonnegative integer r and positive integer j,

    sup_(0<=v<=T,u>=0) u^r |D^j g_v(u)| < infinity.             (2)

For r=0 use E J_v^j. For r>0 use (uJ_v)^r exp(-uJ_v)<=r^r exp(-r)
and the finite lognormal moment E J_v^(j-r), uniform for v in [0,T].
Also 0<=g_v<=1. These are uniform all-state bounds, stronger than merely
bounded unweighted derivatives on fixed reciprocal compacts.

### The small-angle expansion with constants uniform in u

Fix the small-angle threshold epsilon of the hybrid kernel and set
theta=1/(nu)<=epsilon, allowing arbitrarily large u. In C032's normalized
concentration box, T_theta(z)=theta/output_angle is between fixed positive
constants, with uniformly bounded coordinate derivatives of every fixed
order needed below. By the chain rule and (2),

    |D_z^ell [g_v(uT_theta(z))]|<=C_T min(u,1), 1<=ell<=5.     (3)

For u<=1 every term contains u^j with j>=1 and a bounded derivative.
For u>=1 use (2) with r=j and the positive lower bound on T_theta.
The same bounds apply to the further finitely many weighted derivatives
needed for the theta-expansion coefficients and their mean-coordinate
variation. No derivative of g_v of order zero is asserted to decay.

Repeat C032's fourth-order centered sample-average expansion, retaining
(3). Its scaled Taylor remainder is C_T min(u,1)n^(-3/2). Freezing the
third- and fourth-moment coefficient at theta=0 costs at most
C_T min(u,1)sqrt(theta)/n. The covariance and coordinate multiplier
second-order theta remainders cost C_T min(u,1)theta^2. Deleted bounded
test terms cost C_T n exp(-cn), uniformly in u. Their polynomial Taylor
terms have the same exponential control by uniform row moments and (3).

The baseline zero-angle coefficients remain precisely C030's terms,
uniformly in u, by the same Taylor expansion and (3). The deterministic
map has displacement

    u theta/F(theta)-u=a/n+b/(n^2 u)+O(1/(n^3 u^2)),

which is O(1/n) uniformly for theta<=epsilon. Its scalar test Taylor
remainder after scaling is bounded by C_T(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2, exactly as
in C036. Thus the identical explicit operators A,B satisfy

    | n(Q_n-I)g_v(u)-Ag_v(u)-Bg_v(u)/n |
      <=C_T[n^(-3/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2+n exp(-cn)],
                                      theta=1/(nu)<=epsilon.  (4)

In simplifying, min(u,1)/sqrt(u)<=1 and
min(u,1)theta^2<=C(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2 were used. The constants in (4)
are independent of any upper cutoff on u. This uniformity is the new
step beyond C036; it is justified by the derivative decay in (2).

### The diffusion step and the large-angle step

The functions Ag_v,A^2g_v,A^3g_v are uniformly bounded by (2), since
their coefficients are polynomials multiplying positive-order derivatives.
Their Ito martingale coefficients are bounded as well, using the bounds
on u times their first derivatives. Iterated Dynkin identities therefore
give, with h=1/n,

    P_h g_v=g_v+hAg_v+h^2 A^2g_v/2+O_T(h^3),                 (5)

uniformly for all u>=0. One can first localize the nonexplosive linear SDE
and then remove the localization by boundedness; no assertion of a
globally analytic semigroup is needed. Combining (4)-(5) proves the
pointwise small-angle defect bound

    |(Q_n-P_h)g_v-Cg_v/n^2|
       <=C_T[n^(-5/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^3+exp(-cn)].           (6)

If theta>epsilon, then u<=1/(n epsilon). The hybrid ratio U_next/u is
bounded, so |Q_n g_v-g_v|<=C_T u<=C_T/n by the bounded first derivative.
Also |P_hg_v-g_v|<=h||Ag_v||_infinity<=C_T/n. From the displayed formula
for C and 1/u=n theta<=n pi, |Cg_v(u)|/n^2<=C_T/n on this range.
Consequently the defect is at most C_T/n for large angles.              (7)

### Sum the defects

C039 gives E theta_k^p<=C_(p,T)/(k+1)^p, and on every hybrid state
1/U_k=n theta_k. Sum (6) at the small-angle states, using the full
positive moment bounds as upper bounds. The resulting terms are

    C_T n^(-3/2), C_T/n^2,
    (C_T/n^2)sum_(k<N)1/(k+1)<=C_T log(n+1)/n^2,
    (C_T/n)sum_(k<N)1/(k+1)^2<=C_T/n,
    C_T n exp(-cn).

For (7), C039 at p=2 bounds the expected number of large-angle visits
by epsilon^(-2)sum E theta_k^2<=C_T. Its total contribution is C_T/n.
All displayed smaller terms are O(1/n), proving (1).

## C043: the terminal bounded-observable rate

For fixed t>0, N=floor(nt), let theta_N be the exact width-n Gaussian
zero-bias ReLU angle with fixed theta0 in (0,pi]. Define its observable
to be f(1/(n theta_N)) on nondegenerate paths and zero after killing.
Then, as n tends to infinity,

    E[f(1/(n theta_N));alive]
       =E[f(V_t^0)] + (D_t/(2pi))log(n)/n+O_(theta0,t)(1/n),   (8)

where

    D_t=D P_t f(0)=E[exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t-V_t^0)]>0.

Any other fixed bounded cemetery value changes (8) only exponentially
through time N, by the same hybrid coupling. In particular the leading
bounded-observable bias is positive and is of order log(n)/n, rather
than a pure c(t)/n expansion. The O(1/n) coefficient is not identified.

Proof. Set t_n=N/n and G_k=P_((N-k)/n)f. The exact semigroup relation
G_k=P_(1/n)G_(k+1) and the Markov property of the hybrid chain give

    E f(U_N)-P_(t_n)f(U0)
      =sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E[(Q_n-P_(1/n))G_(k+1)(U_k)].          (9)

All tests are bounded. Apply (1) to conclude that (9) equals

    (1/n^2)sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E[(C G_(k+1))(U_k)]+O(1/n).      (10)

The k=0 term is O_(theta0,t)(1/n): its singular part is bounded by
C/(n^2 U0)=C theta0/n, and the other terms are smaller. For k>=1,
C041's proof applies also to the one-step shifted test G_(k+1).
Explicitly, its first derivative differs from D_t by at most
C_t[(k+1)/n+u], because |t_n-t|<=1/n. Multiplying by theta_k and
using theta_k U_k=1/n and E theta_k<=C/(k+1) shows a bounded total
weighted error after summation. C040 gives

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E theta_k=(1/a)log(n)+O_(theta0,t)(1).

Thus the singular part of (10) is
(b/a)D_t log(n)/n+O(1/n). The remaining parts of C contribute O(1/n),
by bounded first and second test derivatives and the hybrid reciprocal
moment bounds (4) in C040. Since b/a=1/(2pi), this identifies (10).

Finally U0=1/(n theta0). Bounded D P_s f and bounded Af imply

    |P_(t_n)f(U0)-P_t f(0)|<=C_(theta0,t)/n.

This includes the initial-angle and fractional-layer effects at the
remainder order. The global hybrid coupling through N steps fails with
probability at most C_t n exp(-cn). Since f and its cemetery value are
bounded, transfer to the exact chain changes the expectation by that
order, which is smaller than 1/n. This proves (8).

## Scope and review priority

No exact-chain raw reciprocal moment is claimed or used. The proof
performs its martingale estimates on a finite-moment regularization,
then transfers bounded observables. The estimate is for the specified
smooth bounded test, not a total-variation, Wasserstein, joint-output or
full-path quantitative rate. Independent review should check (4)'s
uniformity in unbounded u, the hybrid coupling, and the covariance
calculation underlying B before accepting (8).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:48d5412d05f2566420246d906fe5e2cb5ea63da0a7aee9e2d7460ec5d88ae3f3","revision_digest":"sha256:fe4020fda7ee8bb5bc64e7c9222149cf2937451449a472e5282436a82c485792","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C042:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Fix 0<rho<1 and independent standard normal Z_0,...,Z_m. Let X_i=sqrt(rho)*Z_0+sqrt(1-rho)*Z_i and M_m=max_i X_i. Coordinates have variance one and distinct covariance rho. Var(M_m)>=rho, so the field is not superconcentrated. Nevertheless the number of coordinates at deficit at most delta_m=(log m)^(-1/4) from M_m tends to infinity in probability. Thus growing near-peaks with pairwise covariance merely bounded away from one, even at vanishing absolute deficit, are insufficient for superconcentration. This does not refute a criterion requiring overlaps to tend to zero.
Independent standard Gaussian coordinates
Fixed positive common covariance rho
Candidate uses overlap bounded away from one, not overlap tending to zero
