body:
[Lem 60 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The set $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$, as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}, is a singleton set consisting of the standard gaussian measure:
$\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)=\{\cN(0,1)\}$.
\begin{proof}
    Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$. By the definition \eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}, this means that for any $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $L>0$ and a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_{N_j})_{j\ge 1}$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        &\WERR(\cA_{N_j}, \mu)
        =\max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big( \mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu \Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j}), \cP(\{\pm 1\}) \Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon\,, \\
        &q_0(j) \equiv \chi_{\cA_{N_j}}(0) 
        = \frac{\|\bbE \bsig_j\|_2^2}{N_j} 
        \stackrel{j\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 1
        \,,
    \end{align*}
where we abbreviate $\bsig_j\equiv \cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. 
    Define the perturbed (deterministic) algorithm $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ by setting 
    \[
        \tilde{\bsig}_j
        \equiv \tilde\cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux) 
        = \frac{\bbE\bsig_j}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} \,.
    \]
This clearly satisfies $\bbE[\|\tilde{\bsig}_j\|_2^2]  = N_j$, so $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ is a $0$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.
Since $\tilde{\bsig}_j$ is a deterministic vector in $N_j$ dimensions of norm $(N_j)^{1/2}$, we have $\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1)$.
    Note that
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\bbE[
            \|\bsig_j - \tilde{\bsig}_j\|^2]}{N_j} 
        &= \frac{1}{N_j} \bbE\bigg[ \bigg\|
            \bigg(\frac{1}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} - 1 \bigg) 
            	(\bbE\bsig_j)
            - (\bsig_j - \bbE\bsig_j)
        \bigg\|^2 \bigg] \\
        &= \Big(1 - q_0(j)^{1/2}\Big)^2 + \Big(1 - q_0(j)\Big)
        \le 2\Big(1-q_0(j)\Big)\,,
    \end{align*}  
again using that inequality $|x^{1/2}-y^{1/2}| \le |x-y|^{1/2}$ for $x,y\ge0$.
    Then, by Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.approx}, with constants $c_0$, $C_1(\alpha)$, $C_2(\alpha,L)$ as defined therein, we have
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j}),
        	\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1) 
	\Big)
        \le \bigg\{
        C_1(\alpha) 2(1-q_0(j)) + C_2(\alpha,L) e^{-c_0N_j} \bigg\}^{1/2}\,.
    \]
Combined with the assumption that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu) \le \epsilon$ for all $j$, we find $\bbW_2(\mu,\cN(0,1)) \le \epsilon$.
    Since this holds for all $\epsilon > 0$, we conclude $\mu = \cN(0,1)$.
    We have thus shown $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1) \subseteq \{\cN(0,1)\}$.
    The reverse inclusion $\cN(0,1) \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$ is witnessed by the (sequence of) deterministic algorithms
    \[
        \cA_N(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) = (1,\ldots,1) \in \bbR^N\,, 
    \]
    which are $0$-Lipschitz with $\mu(\cA_N) = \cN(0,1)$, $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N) = \delta_1 \in \cP(\{\pm 1\})$, and $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 1$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 4 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Let $L(x,{\d} y)$ be a kernel on $E\times\mathscr{B}(E)$. Suppose that the jumping measure $J$ satisfies $J({\d} x{\d} y)\leq D_2L(x,{\d} y)\m({\d} x)$ for some $D_2>0$.
Let ${\sf d}$ be a distance function on $E$ consistent with the given topology. Assume that there exists $\beta\in]0,+\infty[$ such that 
\begin{align*}
M_{\beta}:={\m}\text{\rm-ess-sup}_{x\in E}\int_E(1\land {\sf d}(x,y)^{\beta})L(x,{\d} y)<\infty.
\end{align*} 
Then, for $p\in[1,+\infty]$, {\rm(}resp.~$p\in[2,+\infty]${\rm)}, 
we have 
 $D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})\subset D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}^{\diamond}$ 
and $D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})\subset D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}$ {\rm(}resp.~$D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})\subset D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}^{\dag}$ 
and $D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}\cap L^p(E;{\m})\subset D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\dag}${\rm)}.

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] The function \(K_{\nu,C}\) is a finite positive semidefinite kernel on
\(G\times J\).  It satisfies
\begin{align}
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((ar,j),(as,k)\bigr)
&=
\chi_\alpha(a)^{-1}
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,j),(s,k)\bigr),
\\
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,j),(r,j)\bigr)
&=
\chi_\alpha(r)^{-1}p_j.

\end{align}
If further  \(\mathsf T\) acts on \(J\), with the action denoted by
\((u,j)\mapsto uj\), \(\nu\) is \(B\)-invariant  and  
\[
C_{uj}=B^uC_j,
\qquad u\in\mathsf T,\quad j\in J,
\]
then
\begin{equation}

K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,uj),(s,uk)\bigr)
=
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,j),(s,k)\bigr).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:relu_samples of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$. 
Let $\ell(y,y') = (y-y')^2$ be the quadratic loss function.
Suppose that the $y$-marginal of $\mu$ has a finite fourth moment, i.e., $\EE[|y|^4] <\infty$. 
Then there exists an algorithm that agnostically learns $\cH_\mathsf{ReLU}$ with accuracy $\varepsilon$ and confidence $1-\delta$ using i.i.d. samples of size 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \(\tilde{O}\left(\varepsilon^{-3} d^{O((1/\varepsilon)^r)} \log(1/\delta)\right)\) under \(r\)-strictly sub-exponential input $\mu_x$;
    \item \(\tilde{O}\left(\varepsilon^{-3} d^{O(\exp{O(\varepsilon^{-1})})} \log(1/\delta)\right)\) under sub-exponential input $\mu_x$. lip
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let us consider a probability mass function $\eta: \mathbb{N}_{>0} \to [0,1] $ and an $\mathbb{N}_{>0}$-valued random variable $\mathcal{L}$ satisfying $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{L}=\ell)=\eta(\ell), \, \ell \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$. 
	We call the distribution of $\mathcal{L}$ the length distribution of the worms. Let us also consider a nearest neighbour simple random walk $(X(t))_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ on the vertices of $G$ starting from $X(0)=o$, independent of $\mathcal{L}$.
	Let us define the probability measure $\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}$ on $\mathcal{H}_{o}$ by 
	\begin{equation}
		
		\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}(H) := P_{o}( \{ X(0), X(1), \ldots, X(\mathcal{L} - 1) \} = H )
	\end{equation}
	for each $H \in \mathcal{H}_{o}$.
	Given any $\lambda >0$, the Poisson zoo $\mathcal{N}_{\eta}^{\lambda} := \mathcal{N}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^{\lambda}$ built upon this measure via Definition (def:poisson_zoo of the paper) is called the random length worms model at level $\lambda$, and the corresponding random set $\mathcal{S}_{\eta}^\lambda := \mathcal{S}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^\lambda$ is the random length worms set at level $\lambda$.
title: Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145

[Definition def:RBGshell of arXiv:2510.13733, 'Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation \\ with Critical Branching Random Walks'] Fix an initial (integer) radius $R_0$ and
an initial particle configuration $\eta_0$ with support on 
 $\partial B_{ R_0}$.
Let $N_0 := \sum_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d} \eta_0(x)$ be the total number of particles at time zero. 
At each step $t \in \mathbb{Z}_+$,
given the step $t-1$, 
we set
$
R_t := R_{t-1} +   H_t,$
where 
\begin{equation}
H_{t}   : = \Big   \lceil  \,     \Big(  \kappa \,  N_{t-1}  \,   \big( \log (N_{t-1} + 1) \big)^{\beta}  \Big )^{ \frac{1}{d}}  \, \Big \rceil
\end{equation}
with $\beta= 1$ if $d=3$ and $\beta=0$ if $d > 3$. Here $\kappa>0$  is a large enough constant depending only on the dimension.
We start a RBG with radii $R_{t-1}$ and $R_t$ from the  particle configuration 
$\eta_{t-1}$ 
(which has support in $\partial B_{R_{t-1}})$
and let $\eta_t$ be the escaping particle configuration of such process 
(which has  support
in $\partial B_{R_t}$,  recall Definition (def:RBG of the paper)).
We then move to the next step $t+1$ and repeat the procedure. 
Define for any $\alpha >0$ the  stopping time (with the convention that $\inf \emptyset = + \infty$)
\begin{align}

T^{(\alpha)} & : = \inf \{ t  \geq 0  \, : \, N_t  > \alpha  N_0  \} . 
\end{align}

Let M(X) be the essential supremum of the density of X (M = infinity if there is no bounded density). (Thm 1) For independent random vectors X_1,...,X_n in R^d: M(X_1+...+X_n)^{-2/d} >= (1/e) sum_k M(X_k)^{-2/d}. (Cor 2) If M(X_k) <= M for all k and sum a_k^2 = 1, then M(sum a_kX_k) <= e^{d/2} M. (Closing remark, from Rogozin's theorem and Ball's cube slicing) For real X_k: M(S_n)^{-2} >= (1/2) sum_k M(X_k)^{-2}, and 1/2 is best possible (two independent uniforms on intervals of equal length give equality). 1/e is the dimension-free constant; for fixed d >= 2 the sharp constant is Gamma(1+d/2)^{2/d}/(1+d/2) (Madiman-Melbourne-Xu), which decreases to 1/e as d -> infinity.

Assumes: independence; random vectors in R^d (Thm 1, Cor 2); real variables (the 1/2 remark)

body:
Author-proved reduction awaiting independent review. In a proper strictly positive weighted graph, if a bigeodesic gamma uses an edge e of weight t_e, replacing only that weight by s in (0,t_e) preserves the entire bigeodesic. A finite straddling segment decreases by Delta=t_e-s; a simple competitor decreases by either Delta if it uses e or zero if it avoids e. Thus every e-avoiding competitor has new excess cost at least Delta. A subsegment on one side stays minimizing because it sits inside a minimizing straddling segment. In iid nonatomic positive FPP, positive probability of a bigeodesic through e implies positive probability of such a uniformly pinned bigeodesic under the same iid law: choose a<b<c with F(b)>0 and P(A_e,t_e>=c)>0, where a is the essential infimum, then independently resample s with law F. The event has probability F(b)*P(A_e,t_e>=c)>0 and penalty at least c-b. This multiplication uses exactly the fresh independent coordinate. No planar exclusion of these pinned paths is proved.
proper strictly positive metric for deterministic preservation
iid positive nonatomic finite edge law for the probability reduction

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.29761, '2608.29761'] For each $L>0$ there exists a constant $C=C(L)$ so that for every $\delta>0$ the following holds. 
Suppose $\alpha,\beta$ are geodesic arcs in $\Ha^n$ of length at least $L$, and whose endpoints are at most $\delta$ apart. If $u_j(\alpha)$ and $u_j(\beta)$, $j=1,2$, are the initial and the terminal tangent vectors at $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively then 
$$
\dis_{\TB}(u_j(\alpha),u_j(\beta))\leq C\delta.
$$

body: [Lemma 52 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Let $\beta_1,\beta_2<Q$ and $\beta_3\in(-\infty,Q)\cup\{Q^-\}$. Let $D_0$ be a deterministic neighborhood of $[-1,0]$. Let $\psi\sim\LF_\bbH^{(\beta_1,0),(\beta_2,\infty),(\beta_3,-1)}$, and let $S=S(\psi)\subseteq \bbH$ be a bounded random set measurable with respect to $\psi$ such that $\ol S \cap D_0=\emptyset$. Suppose for any open set $U\subseteq\bbH$, the event $\{(\bbH\backslash S)\subseteq U\}$ is measurable with respect to $\psi|_U$. Then conditioned on $(S,\psi|_S)$ and $\{S\neq\emptyset\}$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn: conditioning Markov kernel definition}, we have $\psi|_S \overset{d}{=} h+\mathfrak{h}$  where $h$ is a GFF on $S$ with zero (resp.\ free) boundary conditions on $\partial S \cap \bbH$ (resp.\ $\partial S \cap \bbR$), $\mathfrak h$ is the harmonic extension of $\psi|_{\bbH \backslash S}$ to $S$ with normal derivative zero on $\partial S \cap \bbR$.

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): (S12 sec.5.) Treat A = e_0 as the incoming boundary coordinate and the B_i = e_i as private. Projection of R = span{L_u} to the private space sends L_u |-> B_u and is injective, hence R cap span{A} = {0} (eq (16)). Thus the selector space creates NO new boundary-only residual direction and the connector-absorption clause holds for every ancestor residual space. Conditioning on the root sign leaves a uniform independent-set fibre, so L_{B|A} = n - H(B|A) = n - log_2 L_n = ell(A_n) (eq (17)). Together with (15) this is a conditional linear certificate with constant 1/log_2(4/3) and NO connector surcharge. Notes: The constant here (2.4094) is better than S14's cycle constant 2, but it is the ROOT-CONDITIONED statement; S14 (2) proves the stronger target-uniform version over an arbitrary junction basis W containing A.

body: In mathematics, the Borel sets of a topological space are a particular class of "well-behaved" subsets of that space. For example, whereas an arbitrary subset of the real numbers might fail to be Lebesgue measurable, every Borel set of reals is universally measurable. Which sets are Borel can be specified in a number of equivalent ways. Borel sets are named after Émile Borel.

body:
Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); D0007-C004 v1; audits w668:PASS. Every probability law F with bounded support, absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and symmetric about its mean is n-completely mixable for all sufficiently large n. No density floor or unimodality is assumed. A positive-measure density level set A on the positive half-line supplies a bounded odd-order zero-sum reserve by convolving differences until they reach A; global sign and coordinate permutation give a symmetric dominated marginal. The residual is symmetric and pairs, so the odd-order reserve lemma applies. The threshold depends on F; the nonsymmetric case is not resolved.
F absolutely continuous
F has bounded support
F symmetric about its mean

Status: proof (unaudited). Special case of D0007; novelty not yet cleared.

Statement. Let F be an absolutely continuous probability law with bounded support, symmetric about its mean mu. Then there is a finite N(F) such that F is n-CM for every integer n>=N(F). No pointwise lower bound on its density, no support interval without gaps, and no unimodality are assumed.

We will construct one odd-order symmetric reserve H with bounded density dominated by a positive multiple of f, and apply D0007-C002. The main open piece of D0007 is the nonsymmetric case, for which the residual-pair argument is unavailable.

1. Normalize mu=0. Write f for a symmetric version of the density, so f(-x)=f(x) almost everywhere. Choose M>0 bounding the support. Since F is absolutely continuous, it has no atom at zero and its mass in (0,M] is 1/2. There are eps>0 and a measurable set A subset (0,M] of positive Lebesgue measure a such that f(x)>=eps almost everywhere on A and also on -A. For example some level set {x in (0,M]:f(x)>=1/j} has positive measure, since the union of these sets carries all positive-half mass. Put u(x)=1_A(x)/a. This is a bounded probability density.

2. Let v=u*tilde(u), with tilde(u)(x)=u(-x). It is the density of Y-Y' for independent Y,Y' with density u. It is continuous and v(0)=1/a>0. To justify continuity directly, v(t)=|A intersect (A+t)|/a^2, and the absolute difference of v(t) and v(s) is bounded by ||1_A(.-t)-1_A(.-s)||_1/a^2. Translations are continuous in L1 for every finite-measure measurable set: approximate 1_A in L1 by finite linear combinations of bounded-interval indicators, whose translation continuity follows from the interval symmetric-difference bound, and use the triangle inequality. Thus choose delta>0 and c>0 with v(t)>=c for |t|<=delta.

3. Choose an integer k>=1 with k delta>M. The k-fold convolution v^{*k} is strictly positive at every t in (-k delta,k delta). Indeed v>=c 1_{[-delta,delta]}, so v^{*k}>=c^k (1_{[-delta,delta]})^{*k}; the latter is strictly positive in that open interval. For k>=2 this follows by integrating over a small open neighborhood of the first k-1 coordinates equal to t/k, leaving the last also within (-delta,delta); k=1 is immediate. Consequently

    Z=integral_A u(y) v^{*k}(y) dy

is positive. It is finite since every convolution density here is bounded above by ||u||_infinity=1/a.

4. An exact zero-sum probability vector. Draw a vector (Y_1,...,Y_{2k}) with joint density

    [ product_{i=1}^{2k} u(y_i) ] u(s(y)) / Z,
    s(y)=sum_{i=1}^k y_i - sum_{i=k+1}^{2k} y_i.

It integrates to one because s under the unweighted product law has density v^{*k}, and E[u(s)]=Z. Set Y_0=s(Y). The weight u(s) forces Y_0 in A, while all Y_i are in A almost surely. Form the odd vector W of length m=2k+1 with entries

    (Y_1,...,Y_k, -Y_{k+1},...,-Y_{2k}, -Y_0).

Its sum is exactly zero.

5. Each magnitude marginal has a bounded density on A. For any i from 1 to 2k, integrate the displayed joint density in every other variable. Conditional on y_i, the integral of u(s) over the remaining independent variables is at most ||u||_infinity=1/a. Thus the marginal density q_i(y) is <=u(y)/(aZ)<=1_A(y)/(a^2 Z). For Y_0, its density is q_0(y)=u(y)v^{*k}(y)/Z, with the same bound because ||v^{*k}||_infinity<=1/a. The sign in W changes support to -A where appropriate, without changing the bound.

6. Multiply W by an independent equiprobable sign, then apply an independent uniform permutation. The resulting vector has sum zero and identical symmetric marginals H. Their common density h is supported on A union -A and satisfies

    h(x)<=1/(2a^2 Z) almost everywhere on A union -A.

The factor 1/2 follows because A and -A are disjoint, and each globally randomized coordinate is a symmetric magnitude law with density q_i(|x|)/2. Averaging over coordinates preserves the bound. Hence H is symmetric and m-CM.

7. Set p=min(1/2,eps*a^2*Z)>0. Then p h<=eps/2<=f on A union -A, and p h=0 elsewhere. The residual density g=(f-ph)/(1-p) is a symmetric probability density with bounded support. Apply D0007-C002: F is n-CM for all even n and for every odd n with n>=m and np>=m. Thus N(F)=ceil(m/p) is a valid finite threshold. Translate all coordinates back by mu.

Proof checks: Z is positive by actual convolution mass on A, not by a conditional event claimed to have positive probability; the zero-sum law is defined by an explicit normalized density on 2k free coordinates. No conditioning on a zero-probability event is used. body: [Proposition completudemetricaJacobi of arXiv:2609.03909, 'Conic Pseudo-Finslerian Mechanical Systems'] Let $L$ be a Finslerian metric and $\tilde{L} = (\Phi \circ \pi) L$ be a Jacobi metric of $L$. [Lemma 13 (Robust separated batch) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] Suppose that for some $\eta>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \min\{\theta-x,\ x+a-\theta,\ \theta-(x+a-b)\}\ge\eta.
 
\end{equation}
Use the separated supports above, but let the actual initial left voltage
and aggregate input magnitudes be $x'$, $A\ge0$, and $B\ge0$.  Suppose that
under both orderings the continuous drift rate before a first hit has
magnitude at most $L_{\rm dr}$ and that
\begin{equation}
 |x'-x|+|A-a|+|B-b|+4L_{\rm dr}\varepsilon<\eta,
 \qquad 4\varepsilon<\rho.
 
\end{equation}
Then the target fires exactly once in the excitatory-first system and does
not fire in the inhibitory-first system on $[0,4\varepsilon]$.

[Definition Agnostic learning of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta\in (0,1)$. 
Let $\ell:\RR\times\RR\to \RR^+$ be a loss function.
Suppose that $\mu$ is a distribution over $\RR^d \times \RR$ and $\cH$ is a hypothesis class where each element $h\in \cH$ is a function from $\RR^d$ to $\RR$.  
And let $\cD = \{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i\in [n]}$ be a dataset with i.i.d. samples drawn from $\mu$. 
We say that an algorithm $\cA$ that takes $\cD$ as input and outputs a hypothesis $f:\RR^d\to \RR$ learns $\cH$ agnostically, if with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the draw of $\cD$, it holds that
\begin{align}
    \EE_{\mu}\big[\ell(y,h(x))\big] &\le \mathrm{opt}_{\cH} + \varepsilon, \text{ where } \mathrm{opt}_{\cH} = \inf_{f\in \cH} \EE_{\mu}\big[\ell(y,f(x))\big].  
\end{align}
title: Agnostic learning

body:
[Theorem 57 (Sharp quadratic phase diagram on polynomial-growth groups) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $\Gamma$ be an infinite finitely generated group of polynomial growth
degree $D$.  Fix $1\le r<\infty$, $a,b\ge0$,
$0<\sigma\le D/2$, and $c_x=\langle x\rangle^{-\sigma}$.
Then $(T_{2,N}^{a,b}(c))_N$ is Cauchy in
$L^2(\Omega;\Sch_r)$ if and only if
\begin{equation}

 \frac D4<\sigma\le\frac D2
\end{equation}
and, with $\beta=D-2\sigma$,
\begin{equation}

 a>\beta,\qquad b>\beta,\qquad
 a+b>\beta+\frac Dr.
\end{equation}
Whenever these conditions hold, all the $L^p$-convergence, deviation,
almost-sure convergence, and quantitative cutoff-rate conclusions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:second-order-singular-transfer} hold.  At the logarithmic
endpoint $\sigma=D/2$, the three conditions become
\[
 a>0,\qquad b>0,\qquad a+b>\frac Dr.
\]
If $\sigma\le D/4$, no choice of $a,b\ge0$ yields
$L^2(\Omega;\Sch_r)$ convergence.

body:
[Defn Schottky double of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let $\Omega \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ be a simply connected domain in $\mathbb{C}$ with $\Gamma=\partial \Omega$ consisting of prime ends. Take copy $\tilde{\Omega}$ of $\Omega$ and weld $\Omega$ and $\tilde{\Omega}$ together along $\Gamma$ so that a compact topological surface $\Omega^{Double}=\Omega \cup \Gamma \cup \tilde{\Omega}$ is obtained. If $z \in \Omega$ let $\tilde{z}$ denote the corresponding point on $\tilde{\Omega}$. Then an involution $j$ on $\Omega^{Double}$ is defined by
$$
\begin{array}{ll}
j(z)=\tilde{z} & \text { and } \\
j(\tilde{z})=z & \text { for } z \in \Omega, \\
j(z)=z & \text { for } z \in \Gamma .
\end{array}
$$

The conformal structure on $\tilde{\Omega}$ will be the opposite to that on $\Omega$, which means that the function $\tilde{z} \mapsto \overline{z}$ serves as a local variable on $\tilde{\Omega}$, and $j$ becomes anti-analytic. 

For $p\in \partial \Omega$, let $\phi:U\subset \overline{\Omega} \rightarrow \phi(U)$ be a local boundary chart at $p$, 
let $\tilde{U}$ be the corresponding subset in $\tilde{\Omega}$, 
then $\tilde{\phi}:\tilde{U} \subset \tilde{\Omega} \rightarrow \overline{\phi}(\tilde{U})$ is a local chart at $\tilde{p}$.
Then we can define a local chart $\tau$ for $\Omega^{Double}$ at boundary point $p$ by 
$$ \tau(z)=\left\{
\begin{aligned}
&\phi(z), z \in U \\
& \overline{\phi(z)}, z \in \tilde{U}.
\end{aligned}
\right.
$$

Thus, the conformal structure on $\Omega^{Double}$, inherited from $\mathbb{C}$, extends in a natural way across $\Gamma$ to a conformal structure on all of $\Omega^{Double}$. This makes $\Omega^{Double}$ into a symmetric Riemann sphere.

For example, we identify $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ with the Schottky double of $\mathbb{H}$ or that of $\mathbb{D}$. Then the corresponding involution $j$ is $j_{\mathbb{H}}: z \mapsto z^*=\bar{z}$ for $\Omega=\mathbb{H}$ and $j_{\mathbb{D}}: z \mapsto z^*=1 / \bar{z}$ for $\Omega=\mathbb{D}$.
title: Schottky double

[Theorem HALFGODHALFSOUVLAKI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$
  and $0 < \theta < 1$. Assume that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^{\theta}} \log \mathbb{E} [H
    \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N
    (A))] = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then, for every $k \in
  \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th moment of the random measure $N^{- \theta} \sum_{i =
  1}^N \delta \left( N^{- 1} \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges, as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in
  probability to $\Psi^{(k)} (0) / (k - 1) !$.

[Thm 5 (Crandall--Rabinowitz) of arXiv:2608.30796, 'Tumor boundary instability induced by pressure feedback'] Let \(W\) and \(Z\) be real Banach spaces, and let
\(\mathcal F:W\times\mathbb R\to Z\) be a \(C^k\) mapping,
\(k\geq3\), in a neighborhood of \((0,\mu_0)\). Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(\mathcal F(0,\mu)=0\) for \(\mu\) near \(\mu_0\);
\item
\(\ker \mathcal F_w(0,\mu_0)=\operatorname{span}\{w_0\}\);
\item \(\operatorname{Range}\mathcal F_w(0,\mu_0)\) is closed and has
codimension one in \(Z\);
\item
\(\mathcal F_{w\mu}(0,\mu_0)w_0\notin
\operatorname{Range}\mathcal F_w(0,\mu_0)\).
\end{enumerate}
Then the nontrivial solutions of \(\mathcal F(w,\mu)=0\) near
\((0,\mu_0)\), together with the bifurcation point, form a
\(C^{k-2}\) curve \((w(\epsilon),\mu(\epsilon))\) satisfying
\[
w(\epsilon)=\epsilon w_0+o(\epsilon),
\qquad
\mu(0)=\mu_0.
\]
Locally, every solution lies either on this curve or on the trivial
branch \((0,\mu)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Crandall--Rabinowitz

[Theorem 49 of arXiv:2608.09700, 'A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs'] Suppose that $\mcZ=(Z_\tau)$ is an admissible collection of stochastic fields and that $u$ can be be developed in the paracontrolled system up associated with \eqref{eq_gPAM} to order $\gamma$,.
For any smooth function $h$ depending on $v_* = (\partial^k_{*} u)_{k \in A}$ where $A$ is a finite subset of $\N^{d+1}$ such that $r_h<\gamma$ with $r_h =\sup \{ |k|,k\in A\} $, one has 
			$$
			h(v_*) = \sum_{n\geq 0}\sum_{\substack{\tau=  X^r \prod_{i=1}^{n}\mcI^+_{a_i}(\tau_i)^{\beta_i}\in\mcT^+ \\ |\tau|<\gamma-r_h}} \frac{1}{ r!}\P\Big( \partial^r \prod_{i=1}^n D_{a_i}^{\beta_i} h(v_*) \prod_{j=1}^{n} \frac{u_{\tau_j}^{\beta_j}}{\beta_j!} \, ,Z_\tau\Big)  + h(v)^\#,
			$$
			where the $ \mathcal{I}_{a_i}(\tau_i) $ are pairwise disjoint. One has $h(v)^\#\in C^{\gamma-r_h}$, and that $\bm{u}\in\mcD^\gamma_\P(\mcZ) \mapsto h(v_*)^\#\in C^{\gamma-r_h}$ is local Lipschitz.

[Lem 4 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] Let $\beta_{k}^n(c):=\prod_{j=k}^n \left(1+\frac{c}{j+1}\right)$, where $c<0$. We have
\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
\item For any $n\ge 1$ and $\left(-2c-1 \right)\vee 1 \le k\le n$, we have
\beq
\exp\left(-\frac{c^2}{\left(-2c-1 \right)\vee 1}\right) \left(\frac{n+1}{k}\right)^c\le \beta_{k}^n(c)\le\left(\frac{n}{k+1}\right)^c.
\deq

\item For $c<-1/2$, we have
\beq
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\left(\sum_{k=0}^n (k+1)^{-2} \left(\beta_{k}^n(c)\right)^2\right)^{-1}}{(-2c-1)n}=1.
\deq

\end{enumerate}

 \mathcal R^{-1}(K_r\mathcal Y)=\mathscr D_rM^*,

body: [Lemma prop:bounded_cle_crossings of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $\overline{\Gamma}$ be a nested $\CLE_4$ on $\BD$, let $F \subseteq \BD$ be a compact set,  and set $d \defeq \dist(F ,  \partial \BD)>0$.  Then,  there exists a universal constant $b_0 \in (0,1)$ such that the following is true.  For each $\epsilon \in (0,1)$,  there exists $\delta \in (0,1)$ depending only on $\epsilon$ and $d$ such that for all $z \in F$ and all $0 < r_1 < r_2 < d/2$ with $r_1 / r_2 \leq \delta$,  the probability that there are at least four crossings of $B_{r_2}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{r_1}(z)}$ made by loops in $\overline{\Gamma}$ is at most $(r_1 / r_2)^{2 - \epsilon}$.  Also,  the probability that there are more than four crossings of $B_{r_2}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{r_1}(z)}$ made by loops in $\overline{\Gamma}$ is at most $(r_1 / r_2)^{2 + b_0}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let G be a finite group and let p be a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p; equivalently, G has a subgroup of order p. The number of such elements is a multiple of p - 1, and the number of subgroups of order p is congruent to 1 modulo p.
G finite
p prime with p | |G|

[Theorem thm:full HOMFLY complex of arXiv:2608.29986, 'Khovanov-Rozansky homology over $\F[U,V]$'] Let $K \subset S^3$ be a knot. There is a $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $-graded finitely generated free chain complex $(\mathit{CH}(K), \partial)$ over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{F}} [U,V]$ such that
\begin{enumerate}

    \item $H_*(\mathit{CH}(K) \otimes_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{F}} [U,V]} \ensuremath{\mathbb{F}} ) \cong \widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ as $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \oplus\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} $-graded vector spaces where $\widehat{\mathit{H}}(K)$ denotes the reduced Khovanov-Rozansky homology.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:causal-reweighting of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Suppose that Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) holds.
Let $I=(r_0,r_1)$ and let $w_1,w_2$ be regular weights for the same reference
diffusion.  If $w_2/w_1$ is nondecreasing on $I$, then
\begin{equation*}
 C_{w_2,I}(X)\leq C_{w_1,I}(X).
\end{equation*}
In particular, the assertion is understood in $[0,\infty]$, with no prior
finiteness assumption on either side.

Let alpha > 0. A random variable X is called sub-Weibull with parameter alpha (denoted Sub-Weibull(alpha)) if its Orlicz norm with Young function psi_alpha(x) = exp(x^alpha) - 1 is finite: ||X||_{psi_alpha} = inf { c > 0 : E[exp(|X| / c)^alpha] <= 2 } < infinity. Sub-Weibull(2) corresponds to sub-Gaussian, and Sub-Weibull(1) corresponds to sub-exponential.
alpha > 0
X is a real random variable
title: Sub-Weibull Random Variable

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose Assumptions \ref{assump:X} and \ref{assump:dynamics} hold with $f=-U'$,
the lower bound $\alpha>0$ in \eqref{eq:Uconvexity} satisfies
$\alpha>\Lambda_{\max}$, and Assumption \ref{assump:convergence} holds. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item The Gibbs measure $\mu_\Gibbs$ is well-defined, and there exist deterministic almost sure limits
\begin{equation}
v_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \|\btheta\|_2^2 \rangle,
\qquad q_*=\lim_{n \to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\langle \btheta^\top \btheta' \rangle.
\end{equation}
\item For each fixed $\tau \in \R$, there exists a limit
$c_\theta(\tau)=\lim_{s \to \infty} C_\theta(s+\tau,s)$. This defines a
symmetric positive-semidefinite function
$c_\theta:\R \to \R$ satisfying, for some $C,c>0$ and
all $s,t \geq 0$ and $\tau \in \R$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
c_\theta(0)=v_*, \qquad \lim_{\tau \to \infty} c_\theta(\tau)=q_*,\\
|C_\theta(t,s)-c_\theta(t-s)|\leq Ce^{-c\min(s,t)},
\qquad |c_\theta(\tau)-q_*| \leq Ce^{-c|\tau|}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\item For each fixed $\tau \geq 0$, there exists a limit
$r_\theta(\tau)=\lim_{s \to \infty} R_\theta(s+\tau,s)$. This defines a
function $r_\theta:[0,\infty) \to \R$ satisfying, for some $C,c>0$
and all $t \geq s \geq 0$ and $\tau \geq 0$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
|R_\theta(t,s)| \leq Ce^{-c(t-s)}, \qquad
|r_\theta(\tau)| \leq Ce^{-c\tau},\\
|R_\theta(t,s)-r_\theta(t-s)| \leq Ce^{-cs}, \qquad
\int_0^t |R_\theta(t,s)-r_\theta(t-s)| \d s \leq Ce^{-ct}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\item $c_\theta$ is continuous on $\R$, smooth on $(0,\infty)$,
and has a right derivative $c_\theta'(0^+)=\lim_{\tau \to 0^+} c_\theta'(\tau)$
at $\tau=0$. We have the fluctuation-dissipation relation
\begin{equation}
r_\theta(\tau)={-}c_\theta'(\tau) \text{ for } \tau>0,
\qquad r_\theta(0)={-}c_\theta'(0^+)=1.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, for all $\tau>0$, we have
\[c_\theta(\tau) \geq 0,
\qquad r_\theta(\tau) \geq 0, \qquad r_\theta'(\tau) \leq 0.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 13 of arXiv:2607.10102

body:
[Proposition t.randomfieldCLT-new of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ be a random field in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with values in a Polish space
$\mathbb {M} $ and $\zeta: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb {M}  \to \mathbb{R}$ a  measurable function. 
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d $,
independent of the random field $M$. 
Consider empirical random measures $(\hat{\sigma}_{n}^{\zeta(M)})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ as in (equation linearstatBsigma of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
Assume that $\mathcal{P}$ has fast mixing correlations 
as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper). Assume that either (a) the random field $M$ satisfies the fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing condition of Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper) or (b) 
$M$  satisfies the fast \textnormal{BL}-mixing condition of Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.BL-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper)
and $\zeta(x,\cdot)$ is Lipschitz. If $\zeta$ satisfies the $p$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with respect to $M$ for all $p>1$ then the central limit theorem holds for
    $(\hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, i.e., as $n \to \infty$

\[   ({\rm Var} \, \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) )^{-1/2}\Big( \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
  \]
for $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$,  provided
${\rm Var} \, {\hat{\sigma}_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f)} = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item  
Suppose the random field~$M$ and the point process~$\mathcal{P}$ are stationary 
(necessarily jointly so, due to their independence) with~$\mathcal{P}$ having intensity~$\rho$, 
and suppose that~$\zeta$ is translation invariant, 
i.e., $\zeta(x,\cdot) = \zeta(\cdot)$. Also assume $\zeta$ satisfies the $(1+\epsilon)$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with respect to $M$ for some $\epsilon > 0$.
Then the mean empirical field satisfies for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$
\begin{equation}
n^{-1} \, \mathbb{E}  \, \hat\sigma_n^{\zeta(M)}(f)
= \rho\, \mathbb {E}  \, \zeta(\0,M(\0)) \int_{W_1} f(x)\, \mathrm{d} x, \quad n\in\mathbb{N},
\end{equation}
which holds  without assuming mixing conditions on~$\mathcal{P}$ and~$M$ nor  Lipschitz conditions on $\zeta$. Moreover, under either of the mixing assumptions (a) or (b) of part~(i.CLT-infinite-zeta-field-mixing of the paper) we obtain for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1} {\rm Var} \, \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f)
= \sigma^2(\zeta) \int_{W_1} f(x)^2\,\mathrm{d} x,
\]
where
\begin{align}  
\sigma^2(\zeta) 
&:= \rho\, \mathbb {E}  \, \zeta^2(\0,M(\0)) \\
&\quad + \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} 
\Big( 
\mathbb {E} [\zeta(\0,M(\0))\, \zeta(x,M(x))]\, \rho^{(2)}(\0,x)
- \rho^2\, \mathbb {E} [\zeta(\0,M(\0))]\, \mathbb {E} [\zeta(x,M(x))]  
\Big)\, \mathrm{d} x \in [0, \infty) \nonumber
\end{align}
provided that~$\zeta$ satisfies the $(2+\epsilon)$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) for some $\epsilon > 0$.
\item  Let
$\boldsymbol{\zeta} := (\zeta_1, \ldots, \zeta_m)$ be a vector of translation-invariant, real-valued measurable functions 
on $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb {M} $, with each $\zeta_i$ satisfying the $(2+\epsilon)$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with respect to $M$ for some $\epsilon > 0$.

Let N be an eps-net of the unit sphere of R^n with eps in (0, 1/2), and A any m by n matrix. Then ||A|| <= (1 - eps)^{-1} sup over x in N of ||A x||; for a symmetric matrix, ||A|| <= (1 - 2 eps)^{-1} sup over x in N of |<A x, x>|. The sphere admits an eps-net of size at most (1 + 2/eps)^n, so suprema over the sphere reduce to maxima over exponentially many fixed points - the standard first step of random matrix norm bounds.

body:
[Lem 241 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,\iota > 0$ and $\fq\in [1,2)$ there exists $\epsilon = \epsilon(\alpha,\iota,\fq) > 0$ such that 
	\[
	\max\bigg\{
	\bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) 
	: \mu\in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)
	\bigg\}
	\le \iota\,.
	\]
The same statement holds with
$\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ and
$\cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ in place of $\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)$
and $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$. (The sets mentioned above specified by Definition~\ref{d:achievable-msrs}, \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L}, and \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L.SYM}.)

\begin{proof} Let
$\cA_N$ be an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm. 
If $\mu \in \cP_2(\R)$ satisfies $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_N),\mu) \le \epsilon$, then Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound} gives, for $N$ large enough,
	\[
	\|\mu\|_{L^2} 
	\le 
	\|\mu(\cA_N)\|_{L^2} 
	+ \bbW_2(\mu(\cA_N),\mu)
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l2}}{\le} 
	C(\alpha)^{1/2} + \epsilon
	\le (2C(\alpha))^{1/2}\,,
	\]
where the last bound holds for $\epsilon$ small enough. For such $\epsilon$, it follows by recalling \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L} and \eqref{e:cM.Lip} that 
	\[\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon) 
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L}}{=}
	\bigcup_{L>0}
		\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))\,.
	\]
For $\iota > 0$, define the set
	\[
		S_\iota = \Big\{\mu \in \cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha)) : \bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) \ge \iota\Big\}\,.
	\]
	Now suppose for contradiction that $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ intersects $S_\iota$ for all $\epsilon > 0$.
	Recall from Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq} that the $\cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))$
	endowed with the $\bbW_\fq$ metric
	 is compact.
	The set $S_\iota$ is closed with respect to this metric. Thus, for any sufficiently small $\epsilon > 0$, the set
	\[
		S_\iota \cap \overline{\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)}
	\]
	(where the overline now denotes closure with respect to the $\bbW_\fq$ metric) is a nonempty closed subset of $\cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))$ indexed by $\epsilon$, hence also compact.
	These sets form a nested family of nonempty compact sets, so their intersection is also nonempty.
	However, their intersection is
	\beq
		S_\iota \cap \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \overline{\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)}
		\subseteq  
		S_\iota \cap \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;2\epsilon)
		\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip}}{=} 
		S_\iota \cap \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha)
		\stackrel{\textup{Thm.~\ref{thm:control.problems.main}}}{=} S_\iota \cap \ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)
		= \emptyset\,,
	\eeq
which yields a contradiction.
This proves that there exists $\epsilon$ such that $\bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) \le \iota$ for all $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$.
	The analogous claim for $\cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ and $\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ is proved similarly, using Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.sym} in place of Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.main} in \eqref{e:confinement.cM.lip.to.nbd.of.ideal}.
\end{proof}

[Corollary 57 (Failure of Euclidean rigidity without the
additional hypotheses) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Fix $n\geq4$, and let $K$, $M=S^n\setminus K$, and
$(g^{(t)})_{t\in(-m_0,\infty)}$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:counterexample-psc}.  The
manifold $M$ is connected, smooth, open, and simply connected, and
\(\widetilde H_i(M;\mathbb Z)=0\) for \(i\geq0\).
For every $t\geq0$, the metric $g^{(t)}$ is complete and locally
conformally flat, with
$\mathrm{Sc}_{g^{(t)}}\geq0$.  Moreover, the inclusion
$\iota:M\hookrightarrow S^n$ may be chosen as a developing map of
$(M,g^{(t)})$.  The omitted set, and also the topological boundary of
the developing image, is
$\Lambda:=S^n\setminus\iota(M)=\partial\iota(M)=K$,
which is a nondegenerate continuum.  Nevertheless, $M$ is not
homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^n$.

Consequently, the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:intro-E}\textup{(ii)} can fail
when its two additional topological hypotheses are omitted
simultaneously.  The disjunction of conditions
\textup{(i)}--\textup{(v)} in Corollary~\ref{Contractible for} likewise
cannot be omitted, even if its conclusion is weakened from conformal
equivalence to homeomorphism.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] There exist admissible minimal disks $\Gamma_0\prec\Gamma_1$, constants
	$0<t_0<t_1$, and a smooth function $v$ on the closure of the component of
	$M\setminus\Gamma_0$ containing $\mathcal E_+$. The function satisfies
	$v\to\infty$ along $\mathcal E_+$, its level sets are minimal disks, and
	\[
	 \Gamma_i=\{v=t_i\},\qquad i=0,1.
	\]
	On the component of $M\setminus\Gamma_0$ containing $\mathcal E_+$,
	\begin{equation}
	\operatorname{div}\left(
	\frac{\bar\nabla v}{|\bar\nabla v|}
	\right)=0,
	
	\end{equation}
	and on its lateral support boundary,
	\begin{equation}
	-\frac{\bar\nabla v}{|\bar\nabla v|}\cdot\nu_S>\tanh t_0.
	
	\end{equation}
	Moreover, $v$ and its minimal level-set foliation extend smoothly across $\Gamma_0$ to the side away from $\mathcal E_+$.

For fixed 0<=b<1 and n>=2, take Z_n Bernoulli with p_n=n^{-2(1-b)}, F_1=F_2=n(2-Z_n), G_1=G_2=2n. The G_i are independent constants, n<=F_i<=G_i<=2n, the errors are nonnegative and <=n, and F_i=G_i except on probability p_n->0. Nevertheless Var F_i=n^{2b}(1-p_n) and Var(F_1-F_2)=0. This refutes the abstract inference from vanishing departure probability to decoupling; it is not an iid FPP construction or a KPZ counterexample.

[Proposition 29 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let
\(
  E(t):=\mathcal E_{u_0}(x_t).
\)
Then
\begin{equation}
  E'(0)
  =
  \frac12\int_M
  \operatorname{tr}_g\bigl(u^*k\bigr)\,d\mu_g,
  
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  E''(0)
  =
  \frac12\int_M
  \operatorname{tr}_g\bigl(u^*l\bigr)\,d\mu_g
  -
  \mathcal I_u(W,W).
  
\end{equation}
Then \(W\) is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal J_uW=S_k.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  E''(0)
  =
  \frac12\int_M
  \operatorname{tr}_g\bigl(u^*l\bigr)\,d\mu_g
  -
  \bigl\langle
    S_k,\mathcal J_u^{-1}S_k
  \bigr\rangle_{L^2}.
  
\end{equation}
Here
\(
  \langle A,B\rangle_{L^2}
  :=
  \int_M h(A,B)\,d\mu_g
\)
for sections \(A,B\in\Gamma(u^*TS)\).

body:
[Prop 32 of arXiv:2608.13727, 'Hitting-time mixing for the star transposition shuffle'] Let \(s\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), let \(s_n=\lfloor n\log n\rfloor\), and suppose \(s=s_n+nc_n^\star(s)\), where
    \(|c_n^\star(s)|\le \tfrac12\log\log n-4\log\log\log n\).
    Let \(T_n\subseteq[n]_\star\) satisfy \(|T_n|\le(\log n)^2\), and let \(Y_s^{\,T_n}\) denote the random variable \(Y_s\) conditioned on \(\mathcal F(T_n)\).
    Let \(\mu^{T_n}\) be the probability measure on \(\mathfrak S_n\) obtained by embedding the uniform distribution on \(\mathfrak S_{[n]\setminus T_n}\) into \(\mathfrak S_n\) via the natural inclusion.
    Then
    \[ d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(\mathcal L(Y_s^{\,T_n}),\mu^{T_n}\right) \le n^{-1/2+o(1)}, \]
    uniformly over all such \(T_n\).

$$\{ [t,u,v,w]\in \mathbb{CP}_3~|~ t^4 + u^4 + v^4 + w^4 =0\}.$$
Then any Einstein metric $g$ on $K3$ is Ricci-flat  and hyper-K\"ahler, in the sense that it is K\"ahler with respect to 
an $S^2$-family of orientation-compatible   integrable complex structures 
 on $K3$.  As a consequence, the moduli space $\mathscr{E} (K3)$ is therefore connected. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:ub-h1-Lns of arXiv:2411.10419, 'Lower bounds on the top Lyapunov exponent for linear PDEs driven by the 2D stochastic Navi'] Let $\varrho$ be a solution to (equation e:main of the paper) with $L[u] $ satisfying
(equation e:form-PSA of the paper) or (equation e:form-LNS of the paper). Then for any $\gamma\in (2,3)$ and $0\leqslant s \leqslant t$, there exists a $C(\gamma)>1$ such that: for the projective process $\pi=\varrho/\|\varrho\|$ we have 
\[
\|\pi_{t} \|_{H^{1}}\leqslant C(\gamma) \exp\left(C(\gamma)\int_{s}^{t} \|u_{r}\|_{H^{\gamma}}\mathrm{\,d} r \right)\left(\|\pi_{s}\|_{H^{1}}+ (t-s)
\sup_{s\leqslant r \leqslant t}\|u_{r}\|_{H^{\gamma +1}}\right)\;.
\]
Therefore, for any $\mathbf{r} \geqslant 1 $ there exists a $C(\mathbf{r},t)>0$ such that 
\[
\mathbb{E} \left[ \| \pi_t\|_{H^{1}}^{\mathbf{r}} \right] \leqslant C(\mathbf{r},t) \mathbb{E} \left[\| \pi_{s}\|_{H^{1}}^{2\mathbf{r}} +1\right]^{\frac{1}{2}} V_{\mathbf{r}}^{\frac{1}{2}}(u_{0})\;,
\] 
where $V_{\mathbf{r}}$ is defined in (equation e:lyap-sns of the paper).

body:
[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let $a$ and $b$ be the real-valued functions determined locally by
\begin{equation}
  u_t
  =
  ta+\frac{t^2}{2}b+O(t^3).
  
\end{equation}
Then, on $X_0\setminus Z(q)$,
\begin{align}
  (\Delta_0-2)a
  &=
  \mathcal D_q\log\lambda,
  
  \\
  (\Delta_0-2)b
  &=
  4\left(
    \mathcal D_q a+a^2-1
  \right).
  
\end{align}
Consequently, for every compact set
$K\Subset X_0\setminus Z(q)$ and every $k\ge 0$,
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  \widetilde\sigma_t
  ={}&
  \sigma_0
  +
  2t\left(
    B_q+a\sigma_0
  \right)
  \\
  &+
  t^2
  \left[
    \left(
      2+b+2a^2
    \right)\sigma_0
    +
    4aB_q
  \right]
  +
  O_{C^k(K)}(t^3).
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{align}
  \dot{\widetilde\sigma}_0
  &=
  2B_q+2a\sigma_0,
  
  \\
  \ddot{\widetilde\sigma}_0
  &=
  \left(
    4+2b+4a^2
  \right)\sigma_0
  +
  8aB_q.
  
\end{align}

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2609.03881, 'Eulerian insertion operators and an Eulerian form of the Pieri rule'] For \(a,b\geq0\),
\[
 \G_a\G_b
 =\sum_{j=0}^{\min(a,b)}(-1)^j
   \frac{(a+b-j)!}{(a-j)!(b-j)!j!}\,
   (y-x)^j\G_{a+b-j},
\]
where \((y-x)^j\) acts by multiplication.

If the function \(\Phi_x\) of (equation def_phi of the paper) is non-decreasing on \((-x,\infty)\), then  immediate stopping is optimal for every \(y\in I_x\), and
    \(
        U_x(y)=k_x(y),\, y\in I_x.
    \)

    Suppose, on the other hand, that the one-interval regime (equation one_interval_phi_geometry of the paper) holds. Let \(q_x\) be the unique solution of (equation eq_main_balancing_condition of the paper), and \(a_x,b_x,R_x\) be defined by (equation def_ax_bx_fixed_x of the paper), (equation def_Rx_fixed_x of the paper). Then
    \(
        \mathcal C_x=(a_x,b_x)
    \)
    is the continuation region; the value function is given by
    \begin{equation}
        U_x(y)
        =
        \begin{cases}
            k_x(y), & -x\le y\le a_x,\\[0.3em]
            q_xG(y)+R_x-cyG(y), & a_x<y<b_x,\\[0.3em]
            k_x(y), & y\ge b_x;
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    and the stopping time
    \[
        \tau_x^*
        \coloneqq
        \inf\{t\ge0:Y_y(t)\notin(a_x,b_x)\},
    \]
    with the convention \(\tau_x^*=0\) when \(y\notin(a_x,b_x)\), is optimal.

body:
[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $\Phi \in H^{1,2}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $c_{ij}=-c_{ji}\in H^{1,2}_{loc}(\R^d)\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d),\ 1\le i,j\le d$, and $\mu=\rho\,dx$, where $\rho=\exp(2 \Phi)$. Set 
$$
\overline{\mathbf{B}}:= C^T\nabla \Phi.
$$ 
(i) We have the following equivalences:
$$
\mathrm{div}_{\mu}(\mathrm{div}C)= 0 \ \Leftrightarrow \  \mathrm{div}_{\mu}(\overline{\mathbf{B}})= 0 \ \Leftrightarrow\ \big \langle \mathrm{div} C, \nabla \Phi\big \rangle=0\ \Leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{div}_{dx}(\overline{\mathbf{B}})= 0.
$$ 
(ii) Let $k_1, k_2 \in \mathbb{R}$ be constants. Then, we have:
\begin{enumerate}
\item [(a)] If either one of the four equivalent conditions in (i) holds, then 
\[
\mathbf{G} =  \nabla \Phi+ k_1C^T\nabla \Phi+ k_2\mathrm{div} C
\]
is an OHHD.
\item [(b)] If either $k_1\neq 0$ or $k_2 \neq 0$, and $\mathbf{G} =  \nabla \Phi+ k_1C^T\nabla \Phi+ k_2\mathrm{div} C$ is an OHHD, then one of the four equivalent conditions of (i) is satisfied.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:HJ CLT of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] {tree-CLT}}]
Let $\mathcal{T}_k$ be a random BST on $k$ nodes, and let $f$ be a function mapping unlabeled fringe trees to $[0,1]$. Define the following $\mathcal{T}$-measurable random quantity:
\[
    F_k := \sum_{v\in V(\mathcal{T}_k)} f\pa{(\mathcal{T}_k)_v}.
\]

body:
Let T be a closed symmetric operator on a complex Hilbert space H, with deficiency subspaces K_+ = ker(T* − i), K_- = ker(T* + i) and deficiency indices n_± = dim K_±. Then: (1) D(T*) = D(T) ⊕ K_+ ⊕ K_-, a direct sum which is orthogonal for the graph inner product ⟨x, y⟩ + ⟨T*x, T*y⟩. (2) The closed symmetric extensions of T correspond bijectively to partial isometries from a closed subspace of K_+ into K_-; the self-adjoint extensions correspond bijectively to unitary operators U: K_+ → K_- (onto), via D(T_U) = {x + φ + Uφ : x ∈ D(T), φ ∈ K_+} and T_U(x + φ + Uφ) = Tx + iφ − iUφ. (3) Hence T has a self-adjoint extension iff n_+ = n_-; T is self-adjoint iff n_+ = n_- = 0; if n_+ = n_- = n with 1 ≤ n < ∞, the self-adjoint extensions form a family parametrized by the unitary group U(n); if exactly one of n_± is 0 and the other is not, T is maximal symmetric and has no self-adjoint extension. (4) If there is a conjugation C (antiunitary, C² = I) with C D(T) ⊂ D(T) and TC = CT, then n_+ = n_- (von Neumann's conjugation criterion; e.g. real differential operators with real coefficients). (5) If T is bounded below, n_+ = n_- (and a self-adjoint extension with the same lower bound exists, the Friedrichs extension).
H is a complex Hilbert space
T is closed and symmetric (densely defined)
for (4): a conjugation C commuting with T and preserving D(T)
for (5): T is bounded below

[Definition see, e.g., \cite{bozic_models_1984} of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For an f-model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, we define an \emph{extrinsic satisfaction relation} $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ on $W \times \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ by:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall x' \geq x\, (x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall y \sqsupset x \, (y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \exists y \sqsupset x\, (y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item The other cases are identical to the classical $\Vdash_\mathfrak{M}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We write $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^e \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(e-)valid in} $\mathfrak{M}$'') to mean $\forall x \in W\,(x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$,
  and $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi$ (``$\varphi$ is \emph{(e-)valid on} $\mathfrak{F}$'') to mean that $\mathfrak{M} \vDash^e \varphi$ for every $\mathfrak{M}$ based on $\mathfrak{F}$.

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2604.11489, '2604.11489'] Let $\{X_n, n\ge 1\}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables with common nonuniform distribution $\{p_i, i\ge 1\}$ satisfying
$\ee|\ln p(X_1)|^{2+\delta} < \infty$. Assume that there exist an integer valued function $K(n)$  and $0< \delta< \frac{1}{2}$ such that
\beq
K(n)\le n^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta},\ \ n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\ln n\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i \leq C,
\ \ -n^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}\sum_{i=K(n)}^{\infty}p_i\ln p_i\leq C,
\deq
then we have
\beq
\sup_x\left|\pp\left(\frac{\sqrt{n}(\hat{H}_{MM}-H)}{\sigma}<x\right)-\Phi(x)\right|
 \leq Cn^{-\frac{\delta}{2}},
\deq
where $\Phi$ denotes the standard normal distribution function and $\sigma^2=\Var(\ln p(X_1))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 31 of arXiv:2608.19065, 'Boundedly exchangeable graphs'] Let
\[
    \widehat{\mu}_n
    \coloneqq
    \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\widehat p_n(k)\,\delta_k
\]
denote the empirical degree distribution on $\nbb_0$, where $\widehat p_n(k)$ is defined as in Proposition~\ref{PropConvDegDist}, and let $\pi \coloneqq \operatorname{Poisson}(\delta V_t)$.
Then
\[
    d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\widehat{\mu}_n,\pi)
    \xrightarrow{\pbb}0.
\]
If, in addition, \eqref{CondSummable} holds, then this convergence holds almost surely.

Known supporting comparison; proof (unaudited), no novelty claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:251a81781266638cf433fe2502cf13691ee3345ca3055e4a09442677a9b8c28c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/25/251a81781266638cf433fe2502cf13691ee3345ca3055e4a09442677a9b8c28c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:8c192f261b687d35b3c29a423144e220abb97e50e2555adbe984d3f3cd3b48fa","bundle_entry_key":"spherical-moments-bilinear-disagreement","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-spherical-moment-gaussian-metric-proof","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-spherical-fourth-moment-proof-gaussian-bilinear-disagreement-metric","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Direct Gaussian disagreement metric comparison

Target2 verification supplement for LOW-003 v2. Known geometric comparison, not a new frontier move. Status: proof (unaudited). This source-independent derivation removes one imported step from the existing lower audit; it does not prove the packing or the sample lower bound.

For d>=2 and U,V in O(d), let rho be the disagreement probability of sign(a^T U b) and sign(a^T V b), with independent standard Gaussian a,b. Then

    ||U-V||_F/(pi sqrt(3d)) <= rho <= ||U-V||_F/(2sqrt(d)).

The zero matrix case U=V is included. No small-angle, large-dimension or asymptotic hypothesis is needed.

## Angle and chord

For b!=0 put u=b/||b||. Conditional on b, the Gaussian a gives disagreement theta(u)/pi, where theta is the angle in [0,pi] between Uu and Vu. For linearly independent normals, this follows by the uniform angular distribution of the two-dimensional Gaussian projection; coincident and opposite normals give respectively0 and1. Thus the formula remains valid at the endpoints without dividing by an angle or by a cross product. The event b=0 is null.

Let X=||(U-V)u||. Since both vectors are unit, X=2sin(theta/2). For theta in [0,pi], sin(x)<=x and the concavity chord bound sin(x)>=2x/pi for x in [0,pi/2] give

    X <= theta <= (pi/2)X.

Consequently EX/pi <=rho<=EX/2. It remains to compare EX with the normalized Frobenius norm.

## Exact spherical moments

More generally let M be any real d-by-d matrix, S=M^T M, and X=||Mu|| for uniform u on the unit sphere. Put s1=tr(S)=||M||_F^2 and s2=tr(S^2). Rotational invariance and diagonalizing the symmetric positive-semidefinite S yield

    EX^2=s1/d,
    EX^4=(s1^2+2s2)/(d(d+2)).

Here is a direct derivation of all tensor constants. Symmetry gives E u_i^2=1/d. Let A=E u_1^4 and B=E u_1^2 u_2^2. Coordinate sign symmetry kills odd monomials. Invariance under the 45-degree rotation in the first two coordinates gives A=(2A+6B)/4, hence A=3B. Squaring sum_i u_i^2=1 gives dA+d(d-1)B=1, hence B=1/[d(d+2)] and A=3/[d(d+2)]. These denominators are positive for every d>=2. Expanding the square of sum_i lambda_i u_i^2 gives the displayed formula. Since all eigenvalues lambda_i>=0, s2<=s1^2. Therefore

    EX^4 <=3(EX^2)^2.

If s1=0 then M=0, so X=0 everywhere and the asserted comparison is immediate. Otherwise EX^2 and EX^4 are positive. All moments are finite because X<=||M||_op on the compact unit sphere.

Two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities give

    (EX^2)^2 <= EX * EX^3,
    EX^3 <=sqrt(EX^2 * EX^4).

Combining and dividing by the positive latter square root yields

    EX >= (EX^2)^(3/2)/(EX^4)^(1/2) >=sqrt(EX^2/3).

Also EX<=sqrt(EX^2) by Cauchy-Schwarz. Thus

    ||M||_F/sqrt(3d) <= EX <=||M||_F/sqrt(d).

Apply M=U-V to finish the theorem. No integral limit or infinite-sum interchange occurs.

## Application and limits

The lower half supplies an explicit absolute Gaussian-metric constant for LOW-003 v2 section1. It makes the use of the metric comparison in Li-Zhang-Arora arXiv:2010.08515v2 LemmaD.4 independently transparent. The orthogonal packing and common-rotation entropy estimate still require independent audit. This is an elementary proof of a known comparison, with no novelty claim and no new score asserted.

Boundary examples: U=V gives rho=0 and both norm bounds0. V=-U gives rho=1, normalized difference2, and upper bound1 exactly. In d=2 a fixed plane rotation by t in [0,pi] gives rho=t/pi and normalized Frobenius difference2sin(t/2), consistent with both estimates. Repeated/singular eigenvalues of S cause no problem: diagonalization and nonnegative eigenvalues are all that is used. Dropping orthogonality of U,V would break the unit-normal chord identity (positive scalar multiples of U have the same classifier), so that hypothesis is essential.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:db9a7a1a1e0cd92f7ce6de2ee596b67790d2a11cff63093a7f9b4e6da5b5b49b","revision_digest":"sha256:ff15e789de4337e43bcd7b747eb0687a594f1f595e58ebc92384ace7b8268277","source_id":"own-work:w693:T407-METRIC-010:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T12:23:32.414765+03:00; v1; known comparison self-contained derivation, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem thm:upper_bound_comono_tech of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)\setminus\{1\}$, $\bm{X}$ and $\bm{Z}$ be as above and Assumptions~(\nameref{asm:S}) \& (\nameref{asm:C}) hold. Then, for every $q\in(0,1]$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus B_{\bm{0}}(1)}|\bm{w}|^q\nu_{\bm{X}}^{\mathrm{d}}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w})<\infty$ 
we have $\mathds{E}\big[\sup_{s\in[0,1]} |\bm{R}^t_s|^q\big] = \mathcal{O} \big(t^{1-q/\alpha}G(t)^{-q}\big)$ as $t\downarrow 0$ and, if $p\ne\alpha-1$ and $q\in (0,\alpha)\cap(0,1]$ satisfy $q\notin\{\alpha/(p+1),\alpha/(\alpha\delta+1)\}$, we have, as $t \downarrow 0$,
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{W}_2\big(\bm{M}^{\bm{S}^t},\bm{M^Z}\big)
&=\mathcal{O}\big(G_2(t)+(1+G(t)^{p})t^{\min\{p/\alpha,\delta\}}\big),\\
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{L}^{\bm{S}^t}, \bm{L}^{\bm{Z}}\big) 
&= \mathcal{O} \big( G_2(t)^q
    + (1+G(t)^{pq})(1+G_1(x))^{q(1+p)}
        t^{\min\{pq/\alpha,q\delta,1-q/\alpha\}}\big), \qquad \text{ and }\\
|\bm{\varpi}_{\bm{S}^t}-\bm{\varpi}_{\bm{Z}}|
        &=\begin{dcases}
            \mathcal{O}\big(G_2(t)+t^{1-1/\alpha}G(t)^{-1} 
    +(1+G_1(t))t^{\min\{1-1/\alpha,\delta\}}\\
    \qquad +G(t)^{p}(1+G_1(t))^{1+p}t^{\min\{1-1/\alpha,p/\alpha\}}\big), & \alpha \in (1,2),\\
    \mathcal{O}\big(G_2(t)+t^{p/\alpha}G(t)^{p} +t^{\delta}\big), & \alpha \in (0,1).
        \end{dcases}
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 21 (\cite{ConSet2023}) of arXiv:2506.12632, 'Point process convergence of extremes in $K$-symmetric exclusion'] Fix $K = 1$ and $x \in \R$. 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]

\item If $L\big(\frac{\log t}{t}\big)^{1/2} \to \psi \in (0,\infty]$ as $t \to \infty$, then 
\[
	\lim_{t\to\infty} 
	\mu_t^L \circ v_t^{-1}(x, \infty) = \sigma(1 - e^{-\psi/\sigma})e^{-x}. 
\]

\item If $L\big(\frac{\log t}{t}\big)^{1/2} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$, then 
\[
	\lim_{t\to\infty} 
	\mu_t^L \circ v_{t,L}^{-1}(x, \infty) = e^{-x}. 
\]

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), leftmargin=2.4em, itemsep=0pt, topsep=1pt]
    \item If $C_{k,j}\notin anc_k^{\rblk}(C_{k,i})$, then for $\forall u\in C_{k,j}$ and $v\in C_{k,i}$, we have $u\notin anc_k(v)$.
    \item If $C_{k,j}\in pa_k^{\rblk}(C_{k,i})$, then there $\exists u\in C_{k,j}$ and $v\in C_{k,i}$ such that $u\in pa_k(v)$.

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'] Let 	$1\leq r \leq p \leq m$ and let $m_1,\dots,m_p\geq 1$, $p_1,\dots,p_r\geq 1$ with $m_1+\dots+m_p=m$ and $p_1+\dots+p_r=p$. Let $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_p)$ be a permutation of $[p]$. Let $\mathcal{P}=(P_1,\dots, P_R)$ be a random partition of $[p]$ and $\Pi=(R;|P_1|,\dots,|P_r|;\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is the valid ordering associated to $\mathcal{P}$.
Then we have
	\begin{align}
		\mathbb E\left[\mathbf{1}_{\Pi= (r;p_1,\dots,p_r;\sigma)}\prod_{i=1}^{p}(\mathbf{I}_{V_i}-g_k(u\eta_k))^{m_i}\right]
	=O\left(\frac{1}{n^{p-\beta}} \right),
		\end{align}
where $s:= |\{j\in [r]: \sum_{i\in P_j} m_i=1 \}|$ and $\beta:= r-s$.
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'

body: [Defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] Let $G$ be a graph. On the vertices of $G$ fix an enumeration and let $v$ be one of the vertices of $G$. The tree of Self-Avoiding Walks $T_{\text{SAW}}(G,v)$ of $G$ rooted at $v$ is the tree of walks originating at $v$ that do not intersect themselves, except when the walk closes a cycle, at which point the walk ends. When that happens, the second copy of the twice-appearing vertex is fixed to be a $+$, if the edge closing the cycle is larger than the edge starting the cycle, and $-$ otherwise. In this case, comparing the edges really means comparing the respective vertices, with respect to the enumeration we initially fixed. It is easy to see that the degree of each vertex of $T_{\text{SAW}}(G,v)$ is at most $d$.
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the I'

\item Conversely, let $r_0,t_0, n>0$ be constants and $\epsilon \colon [r_0,\infty)\times [0,\infty) \to[0,\infty)$ a function with $\epsilon(t,x) \to0$ if $t\to\infty$ and monotone decreasing  for all $x\in [0,\infty)$, such that properties

such that ($FK_{c}(r_1)$) holds with  
dimension function 
\[

\]

body:
[Theorem thm:multit of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Choose $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, any real $C_1>0$, and a large enough $N\in \mathbb N$.
We take the $N$ dimensional DBM $\{Y_i(\tau)\}_{1\leq i\leq N, \tau>0}$ started from zero initial condition, and $\vec k \in \mathbb N^m$, $\tau_1\le \tau_2\le \dots \le \tau_m$ such that
\begin{equation}

|k_\ell-\mathbf k_\ell N^{2/3}|<C_1, \qquad \left|\frac{2}{\beta}N + \frac{2}{\beta}\boldsymbol{\tau}_\ell N^{2/3}-\tau_\ell\right|<C_1,\qquad  \text{for each }\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket.
\end{equation}
Then as $N\to\infty$, uniformly over the ($N$--dependent) choices of $\vec k$ and $\vec \tau$ satisfying (equation eq_x2 of the paper):
\[
 \mathbb E \left[ \prod_{\ell=1}^m \left(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^N \left(\frac{Y_i(\tau_\ell)}{\sqrt{2\beta\tau_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell}+\left(\frac{Y_i(\tau_\ell)}{\sqrt{2\beta\tau_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell+1}\right) \right]\to \mathbf L_\beta(\vec \mathbf k, \vec\boldsymbol{\tau}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:multit of arXiv:2411.10829

Let G be a finite connected graph with distinct edge weights, T its minimum spanning tree, and G_p its subgraph of edges of weight at most p. For each component C of G_p, the restriction T to C is a spanning tree and the T path between vertices of C stays in C. Therefore max_C diam_intrinsic(C)<=diam(T). A probabilistic lower bound on sublevel intrinsic component diameter transfers directly to the MST; this gives no MST upper bound or high-dimensional cluster estimate by itself.
Finite connected graph
Distinct edge weights
Graph distance counts edges
title: Sublevel component intrinsic diameter is a lower bound for MST diameter

[campaign status: unreviewed - the campaign's own argument plus a clean Lean file; author-checked, no independent referee] Let V be a xi-QSO on a type set partitioned into q blocks, in the sense of Rozikov's Problem 10 and his (12): a pair of types in the same block, and any pair containing the empty body 0, produces the empty body; cross-block pairs may produce anything. CLAIM: for every such V and every state x, 1 - V(x)_0 <= (1 - 1/q) (1 - x_0)^2. Consequently e_0 is the unique fixed point, 1 - x_0 decays quadratically and at least like (1 - 1/q)^n, and Theorem 5 of the source extends from two blocks to every partition. The cross-block coefficients are irrelevant. The constant is SHARP, attained when the block masses are equal and cross-block pairs never produce 0. READING CAVEAT recorded with the result: pairs containing 0 must produce 0, as in (12); otherwise the coordinate e_0 is not even fixed. Prior art: the xi^(s) and xi^(as)-QSO literature is a different notion, the literal Problem 10 was not found addressed, and novelty is small.
V is a xi-QSO in the sense of Rozikov (12): same-block pairs and pairs containing 0 produce 0
the type set is partitioned into q blocks, q >= 2

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9e7bac292193bea84acf2b1f3f3c43275b7fb8ae6348b57318056c45e3d17784","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/9e/9e7bac292193bea84acf2b1f3f3c43275b7fb8ae6348b57318056c45e3d17784.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3b2761a7c29a87f0ea620b851aac22586976a933ea436007cfb1e2edd8bf67b5","bundle_entry_key":"shared-zero-resonance","bundle_id":"population.resonant-shared-zero-obstruction-019","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"asymptotic recurrence methods","draft":"w706/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:analysis.asymptotics:resonant-shared-cosine-zeros-obstruct-full-weighted-curvature-interval","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-034 v1; kind route-failure; target1; proof (unaudited).

STATEMENT: A LIMITATION OF THE ASYMPTOTIC ROUTE, NOT AN ADAM ORBIT
Let 0<theta1<theta2, K>0, and s_t=t*omega+phi, with omega/pi irrational.
Define the exact leading modes h1(t)=cos(s_t), h2(t)=sqrt(K)*cos(3*s_t).
The weighted curvature
 Q_t=(theta1*h1(t)^2+theta2*h2(t)^2)/(h1(t)^2+h2(t)^2)
has accumulation set
 [theta1,(theta1+9*K*theta2)/(1+9*K)],
along defined times. Its upper endpoint is strictly less than theta2.
Thus positive nonzero oscillation amplitudes and a common decay rate
alone do not imply the whole interval between the two caps. One cannot
delete029's rational-independence assumption from its torus-density
step without additional frequency/phase analysis.

This is an exact fact about leading modes. No standard-initialization
Adam trajectory realizing these locked phases is constructed or claimed.
It does not refute the corresponding assertion about actual Adam orbits.
It is an auxiliary route obstruction and scores no frontier move.

PROOF
The identity cos(3s)=cos(s)*(4*cos(s)^2-3) gives, whenever cos(s)!=0,
 Q_t=F(z_t), z_t=(4*cos(s_t)^2-3)^2,
 F(z)=(theta1+K*theta2*z)/(1+K*z).
The range closure of z on the circle is [0,9]. Irrational rotation
has arbitrarily late visits to every open arc (the one-dimensional
Kronecker theorem), so its accumulation set is the entire interval.
Deleting times cos(s_t)=0 has no effect: there is at most one such
time, since two would make omega/pi rational. The expression F(z_t)
extends continuously through the deleted zeros. F'(z)=
K*(theta2-theta1)/(1+K*z)^2>0. Therefore its image interval has the
stated endpoints. The gap to theta2 is
 (theta2-theta1)/(1+9*K)>0.

COMPATIBILITY OF FREQUENCIES WITH THE SUBCRITICAL CAPS
For b=9/10, r=sqrt(b), choose any irrational omega/pi in (0,1/3),
and put theta_j=[1+b-2*r*cos(j*omega)]/(1-b), j=1,3.
Both lie in the strict complex-root cap interval of029 and theta3>theta1.
Hence the resonance is not ruled out by the possible linearized
frequencies. This frequency observation still says nothing about whether
the nonlinear standard-initialization curve produces the locked phase
relation phi3=3*phi1 modulo pi.

REMAINDERS AND THE UNPAID EXTENSION
For an actual Adam asymptotic expansion the remainders are geometric.
Away from shared leading zeros the quotient limit is legitimate. Near
shared zeros, dividing remainders by the leading amplitude requires a
quantitative lower bound or a higher-order recurrence argument. No such
bound is proved here. In particular, irrationality by itself supplies
no quantitative inhomogeneous approximation rate. Rationally independent
frequencies in029 avoid this issue by choosing subsequences with a
strictly positive limiting squared-weight sum and trapping all other
subsequences by the two caps.

SOURCE AND VERIFICATION
The trigonometric identity, monotonicity and weighted-quotient algebra
are proved above; scripts/check_resonant_extension.py checks five exact
polynomial/rational identities. Classical rotation density is the
one-dimensional Kronecker theorem (2404.00077v1 Section1, printedp1,
states the classical discrete version). This is not an independently
audited claim, a literature-newness claim, or a computer-assisted Adam
trajectory counterexample.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:77c3bddc7e6f19c3539229b7439cf6b082e473b9b6e07a0a036f16925e6589f0","revision_digest":"sha256:ff322d3a13f45255ff658c756386a79cf44de89e216a46086a1eca3e5b1652ed","source_id":"own-work:T421-W706-034","source_revision":"version 1; proof (unaudited); auxiliary route only","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 12 (Universality of the mean-field exponent; conditional on Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red}) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Suppose the offspring law of $N$ is aperiodic (generic, since $p_{d,d'}\in(0,1)$ gives full support on $\{0,\dots,\deg-1\}$) and $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{off}}<\infty$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:var}). Then at criticality $\rho(M)=1$,
\[
\Prob(|S|=n)\sim\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2_{\mathrm{off}}}}\,n^{-3/2},\qquad n\to\infty,
\]
and slightly off criticality, $\Prob(|S|=n)\sim C\,n^{-3/2}e^{-n/\xi}$ with $\xi=(1-\rho(M))^{-1}$. The exponent $3/2$ depends only on criticality and finiteness of the offspring variance --- not on the drifts, thresholds, or boundary structure.

[Definition 7 (Ewens fragmentation process $\Pp^{(n,\theta)}$) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $\theta>0$ and an integer $n\ge 1$.
We construct a random finite rooted tree $(\mathcal T_n , K)\in \Omega$ as follows.
Each vertex $u$ carries an integer mass $K(u)\in\{1,2,\dots\}$.
The root is denoted by $\varnothing$ and has mass
\[
K(\varnothing)=n.
\]

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{Splitting rule.}
Let $u$ be a vertex.
\begin{itemize}
\item If $K(u)=1$, then $u$ is declared a leaf and produces no children.
\item If $K(u)=k\ge 2$, set $m:=k-1$ and sample an $\mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$ partition with count vector
$(C^{(u)}_1,\dots,C^{(u)}_m)$ as in Definition~\ref{def:ewens}.
Let $(A^{(u)}_1 \ge A^{(u)}_2 \ge \cdots \ge A^{(u)}_{\delta(u)})$ be the corresponding partition of block sizes, i.e.
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{\delta(u)} A^{(u)}_i = m,\qquad
\#\{i: A^{(u)}_i=j\}=C^{(u)}_j.
\]
Then $u$ produces $\delta(u)$ children, denoted $(ui)_{1\le i\le \delta(u)}$, with masses
\[
K(ui):=A^{(u)}_i,\qquad i=1,\dots,\delta(u).
\]
\end{itemize}
All splitting variables at different vertices are sampled independently. We
denote $\Pp^{(n,\theta)}$ the probability measure on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$
corresponding to this procedure.
title: Ewens fragmentation process $\Pp^{(n,\theta)}$

body:
[Theorem thm:dgt4-many-limits of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $d\geq5$. There exists an i.i.d.\ scenery
	$(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ whose one-site law has mean zero, variance one,
	a strictly positive
	$C^\infty$ density, and
	\[
		\mathbb{E} e^{\theta|\zeta(0)|}<\infty,
		\qquad
		cr\leq-\log\mathbb{P}(\zeta(0)\leq-r)\leq Cr
	\]
	for some $c,C,\theta>0$ and every sufficiently large $r$.
	There is a sequence $R_k\uparrow\infty$ such that, for every
	$\kappa\in[3/2,2]$, there are indices
	$k_\ell\uparrow\infty$ such that, for all $T>0$ and
	$s>(d-4)/2$,
	\[
		R_{k_\ell}^{(d-4)/2}
		\left(
		u_{\lfloor TR_{k_\ell}^2\rfloor}
		-\mathbb{E} u_{\lfloor TR_{k_\ell}^2\rfloor}(0)
		\right)^{(R_{k_\ell})}
		\Longrightarrow
		\mathcal H_{\kappa,T}
		\qquad\text{in }H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\, .
	\]
	For $T>0$, the fields $\mathcal H_{\kappa,T}$ with
	$\kappa\in[3/2,2]$ have pairwise distinct laws.

[Prop approximating_G_with_G of arXiv:2506.10623, 'Polynomial slowdown in an angle-dependent 2d branching Brownian motion'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)$ and $\beta > 0$.
	Let $L>0$, $a> (1-\kappa)/(1-\frac{\kappa}{2}) = 1-\alpha/2$ and $b>1-\kappa$.
	Then, there exists $\varepsilon_0 = \varepsilon_0(\alpha,a,b) > 0$ such that for all $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0)$, there are $C,c>0$ such that for $s$ large enough, for any $t\geq s + s^\kappa$, any $x,y\in \mathbb{R}$ with $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lvertx\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rvert \leq s^{(\kappa + \varepsilon)/2}$ and $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lverty\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rvert \leq t^{(\kappa + \varepsilon)/2}$ and any function $f$ satisfying $f^-_{L,a,b} \leq f \leq f^+_{L,a,b}$, we have
	\begin{equation*}
	\widetilde{G}(s,x;t,y) = (1+o(1)) G(s,x;t,y),
	\end{equation*}
	where the $o(1)$ holds as $s\to\infty$, uniformly in $t,x,y,f$ (but depending on $\alpha,\beta,L,a,b,\varepsilon$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

suppose that $B_n$ is monotone increasing. Let $(Z_j)$ be a sequence of

[Lem tree-two-edge-residual of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] Let $1<p<2$, let $x_0,x_1\ge0$, let
$\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\{-1,1\}$, and let
$\rho=|\sigma_0x_0^{p-1}+\sigma_1x_1^{p-1}|$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 x_0^p\le(1+\varepsilon)x_1^p+C_p\varepsilon^{-1}
 \max\left\{\rho^q,
 \frac{\rho^2}{x_0^{p-2}+x_1^{p-2}}\right\},
 \qquad0<\varepsilon\le1,
\end{equation}
where, if $x_i=0$, we set $x_i^{p-2}=+\infty$ and interpret a finite
nonnegative number divided by $+\infty$ as zero.

[Lemma permutations of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $Y = (Y_1, \dots, Y_n)$ be a set of i.i.d.\ random variables on a measurable space $\mathcal{Y}$.
    Let $g_i \colon \mathcal{Y}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{+}$, $i \in [n]$, be measurable and integrable functions, such that each $g_i(y_1, \dots, y_n)$ does not depend on $y_i$ and
    \[
    \sum_{i \in [n]} g_i(Y) \le M~~\text{a.s.}
    \]
    Let $I \subset [n]$ and define
    \[
    \mathscr{F}_{I} \coloneqq \sigma\lr{\left\{Y_i: i \in I  \right\} }.
    \]
    Let $\varPi_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$. 
    Then it holds that
    \[
    \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\pi \in \varPi_n} \sum^n_{i=1} \E [g_{\pi(i)}(Y) | \mathscr{F}_{\pi([1, i-1])}] 
    \le \frac{n+1}{n} M~~\text{a.s.}
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma permutations of arXiv:2411.07878

[Proposition prop:campanato of arXiv:2608.16915, 'Exact mean--covariance dynamics of the Weber field in the stochastic Lagrangian representa'] If $\sup_{t}\left\lVert M(t)\right\rVert_{C^\alpha_x}\le K$ then
$\mathcal X_M(z_0,r)\le C_\alpha Kr^\alpha$ for all $z_0,r$. The temporal part is not
controlled by this hypothesis: for a constant matrix $B\ne0$ and
\[
  M(t,x)=\sin\Bigl(\frac1{T-t}\Bigr)B\qquad(t<T),
\]
one has $\sup_{t<T}\left\lVert M(t)\right\rVert_{C^\alpha_x}=\left\lvert B\right\rvert$ and
$\mathcal X_M((x_0,T),r)=0$ for every $r$, yet
\[
  \lim_{r\downarrow0}\mathcal Y_M((x_0,T),r)^2
  =\lim_{r\downarrow0}\mathcal T_M((x_0,T),r)^2=\frac{\left\lvert B\right\rvert^2}{2} .
\]

body:
[Cor Q<=>V of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] If $V$ is an ergodic upper probability on a measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ with respect to a measurable transformation $T:\Omega\to \Omega$, then 
	$\operatorname{core}(V)\cap \mathcal{ M}(T)=\operatorname{core}(V)\cap \mathcal{ M}^e(T)$
	has only one element, denoted by $Q$. Moreover, for any $A\in\mathcal{F}$, 
	\[Q(A)=0\text{ if and only if }V(A)=0.\]
	In particular, $V(A)=Q(A)$ for any $A\in\mathcal{I}$.

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let $\theta\in(0,1)$. A path $X:[0,T]\to \mathbb{R}^d$ is called \textit{$\theta$-H\"older rough} if there exists a constant $c>0$ such that for every $s\in[0,T]$, every $\varepsilon$ in $(0,T/2]$, and every unit vector $\zeta$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, there exists $t$ in $[0,T]$ such that $\varepsilon/2<|t-s|<\varepsilon$ and 
    $$
    |\langle\zeta,X_{s,t}\rangle|>c\varepsilon^\theta.
    $$
    The largest such constant is called the \textit{modulus of $\theta$-H\"older roughness} and is denoted as $L_\theta(X)$.

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2512.00570, 'Makeenko--Migdal equations for lattice Yang--Mills--Higgs'] Let $s$ be a collection of strings.

Fix an edge $e$.

One has
\begin{equs}
C_{G,s,e}\,\phi(s) =\sum_{\mO}  \mp q(\mO) \sum_{s' \in \mO^\pm_{e}(s)}\phi(s'),
\end{equs}
where the sum is over all operations in the first table,
and $C_{G,s,e}$ is a constant depending on $G,s,e$.

Fix  $x\in \Lambda$.

One has
\begin{equs}
C_{M,s,x}\,\phi(s) =\sum_{\mO}   q(\mO) \sum_{s' \in \mO_{x}(s)}\phi(s'),
\end{equs}
where the sum is over all operations in the second table,
and $C_{M,s,x}$ is a constant depending on $M,s,x$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Theorems 6 and 7 have been used in the determination of various star-critical Ramsey numbers involving cycles, fans, and other graphs.

body: Let X be a topological space. The Borel sigma-algebra B(X) is the smallest sigma-algebra of subsets of X containing every open set (equivalently, every closed set); its members are the Borel sets. It is the intersection of all sigma-algebras containing the topology, so it exists and is unique. On the real line, B(R) is generated equally by the open intervals, by the closed intervals, by the half-lines (-infinity, a] with a rational, or by any base of the topology; every open, closed, F_sigma (countable union of closed sets) and G_delta (countable intersection of open sets) set is Borel, and the Borel sets are stratified by the Borel hierarchy of countable length omega_1. B(R^n) equals the product sigma-algebra of n copies of B(R). Every continuous map between topological spaces is Borel measurable (preimages of Borel sets are Borel), as is every pointwise limit of a sequence of Borel measurable real functions; but the image of a Borel set under a continuous map need not be Borel - such images are the analytic sets (Suslin, 1917). B(R) has the cardinality of the continuum, 2^{aleph_0}, while the Lebesgue measurable sets number 2^{2^{aleph_0}} (every subset of the null Cantor set is measurable), so there exist Lebesgue measurable sets that are not Borel: Lebesgue measure on B(R) is completed by adjoining all subsets of Borel null sets. Every finite Borel measure on a Polish space is regular (inner regular by compact sets: a Radon measure), which is why Borel sets are the natural domain of measures on metric spaces.

body:
[Proposition 32 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Let \cref{ass:gaussian-stable-selected} hold. Then, for all sufficiently large
  $N$, the unique nonzero invariant law $\nu_{A,N}$ of $K_{A,N}$ satisfies
  \begin{equation}
    \int_0^1 q^{-\gamma N}\,\nu_{A,N}(\mathrm{d}q)
    \leq
    \frac{e^{bN}}{1-e^{-\kappa N}},
  \end{equation}
  where $R_0,\gamma,\kappa$ are as in
  \cref{prop:gaussian-near-zero-negative-moment}, and $b$ is the constant in
  \cref{lem:gaussian-outside-negative-moment} for this choice of $R_0,\gamma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
